# flak

> A fast, opinionated linter for YAML files.

`flak` catches syntax errors, style inconsistencies, and common pitfalls in YAML before they break your CI pipeline, Kubernetes deployment, or config loader.

```console
$ flak config/
config/app.yaml
  3:5   error    duplicate key "port"                         no-duplicate-keys
  12:1  warning  line exceeds 120 characters (134)            max-line-length
  18:9  warning  truthy value "yes" should be "true"          strict-booleans

config/db.yaml
  7:3   error    inconsistent indentation (expected 2, got 3) indentation

✖ 4 problems (2 errors, 2 warnings) in 2 files
```

---

## Features

- **Fast** – lints thousands of files in milliseconds
- **Zero config** – sensible defaults out of the box
- **Configurable** – enable, disable, or tune every rule
- **Auto-fix** – automatically fix many style issues with `--fix`
- **CI-friendly** – meaningful exit codes and machine-readable output (JSON, SARIF, GitHub Actions annotations)
- **Schema-aware** – optionally validate against JSON Schema

---

## Installation

### Homebrew (macOS/Linux)

```sh
brew install flak
```

### Cargo

```sh
cargo install flak
```

### npm

```sh
npm install --global flak-cli
```

### Prebuilt binaries

Download the latest release for your platform from the [Releases](https://github.com/your-org/flak/releases) page.

### Verify installation

```sh
flak --version
```

---

## Quick Start

Lint a single file:

```sh
flak docker-compose.yaml
```

Lint a directory recursively:

```sh
flak .
```

Lint using glob patterns:

```sh
flak "k8s/**/*.yaml" ".github/workflows/*.yml"
```

Automatically fix what can be fixed:

```sh
flak --fix .
```

Read from stdin:

```sh
cat config.yaml | flak -
```

---

## Usage

```
flak [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...

Arguments:
  [PATHS]...  Files, directories, or globs to lint (default: .)

Options:
  -c, --config <FILE>       Path to config file (default: auto-detect)
  -f, --format <FORMAT>     Output format: pretty, compact, json, sarif, github
                            [default: pretty]
      --fix                 Automatically fix problems where possible
      --fix-dry-run         Show fixes without writing them
  -r, --rule <RULE>         Enable only the specified rule(s)
      --disable <RULE>      Disable the specified rule(s)
      --max-warnings <N>    Exit with error if warnings exceed N
  -q, --quiet               Report errors only, suppress warnings
      --no-color            Disable colored output
      --ignore <PATTERN>    Ignore files matching the pattern
      --schema <FILE|URL>   Validate documents against a JSON Schema
      --list-rules          Print all available rules and exit
      --init                Generate a starter .flak.yaml config
  -h, --help                Print help
  -V, --version             Print version
```

---

## Configuration

`flak` looks for configuration in the following order:

1. Path given via `--config`
2. `.flak.yaml` or `.flak.yml` in the current directory or any parent
3. A `flak` key in `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`
4. Built-in defaults

Generate a starter config:

```sh
flak --init
```

### Example `.flak.yaml`

```yaml
# Extend a built-in preset: "recommended", "strict", or "relaxed"
extends: recommended

ignore:
  - "vendor/**"
  - "node_modules/**"
  - "**/*.generated.yaml"

rules:
  indentation:
    level: error
    spaces: 2
    sequences: indented   # indented | flush | consistent

  max-line-length:
    level: warning
    max: 120
    ignore-urls: true

  strict-booleans: error
  no-trailing-spaces: error
  document-start: off

  quoted-strings:
    level: warning
    style: double         # single | double | any
    only-when-needed: true

# Apply different settings to specific files
overrides:
  - files: [".github/workflows/*.yml"]
    rules:
      max-line-length: off
```

Each rule accepts a level of `off`, `warning`, or `error`, either directly or via the `level` key.

---

## Rules

| Rule | Default | Fixable | Description |
| --- | --- | :---: | --- |
| `syntax` | error | | Document must be valid YAML |
| `no-duplicate-keys` | error | | Disallow duplicate keys in a mapping |
| `indentation` | error | ✔ | Enforce consistent indentation |
| `no-tabs` | error | ✔ | Disallow tab characters for indentation |
| `no-trailing-spaces` | warning | ✔ | Disallow trailing whitespace |
| `newline-at-eof` | warning | ✔ | Require a newline at end of file |
| `max-line-length` | warning | | Limit line length |
| `strict-booleans` | warning | ✔ | Only allow `true`/`false` (flags `yes`, `on`, etc.) |
| `quoted-strings` | off | ✔ | Enforce a quoting style |
| `key-ordering` | off | ✔ | Require keys to be sorted alphabetically |
| `document-start` | off | ✔ | Require or forbid `---` at document start |
| `empty-values` | warning | | Flag keys with implicit `null` values |
| `no-anchors` | off | | Disallow anchors and aliases |
| `octal-values` | warning | | Flag ambiguous octal-like numbers (e.g. `0755`) |
| `comments-spacing` | warning | ✔ | Require a space after `#` |
| `brackets` | warning | ✔ | Enforce spacing inside `[]` and `{}` |

Run `flak --list-rules` for full details, or see [docs/rules.md](docs/rules.md).

---

## Inline Directives

Disable rules for specific lines or blocks with comments:

```yaml
# flak-disable-next-line max-line-length
description: "This is a very long line that would normally trigger a warning but is allowed here"

# flak-disable strict-booleans
legacy_flag: yes
other_flag: on
# flak-enable strict-booleans

# Disable everything for the entire file (must be on the first line)
# flak-disable-file
```

---

## Exit Codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | No errors (warnings may be present) |
| `1` | One or more errors found, or `--max-warnings` exceeded |
| `2` | Invalid usage, bad config, or internal error |

---

## CI Integration

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
name: Lint YAML
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  flak:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: your-org/flak-action@v1
        with:
          args: --format github .
```

The `github` format emits annotations that appear inline on pull requests.

### GitLab CI

```yaml
lint-yaml:
  image: ghcr.io/your-org/flak:latest
  script:
    - flak --format compact .
```

### pre-commit

Add to `.pre-commit-config.yaml`:

```yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/your-org/flak
    rev: v1.0.0
    hooks:
      - id: flak
        args: [--fix]
```

### Docker

```sh
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/src" -w /src ghcr.io/your-org/flak .
```

---

## Editor Integration

- **VS Code** – [flak-vscode](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/) extension
- **Neovim** – supported via [nvim-lint](https://github.com/mfussenegger/nvim-lint) and `none-ls`
- **Any LSP client** – run `flak lsp` to start the built-in language server

---

## Output Formats

| Format | Use case |
| --- | --- |
| `pretty` | Human-readable, grouped by file (default) |
| `compact` | One problem per line: `file:line:col: level: message [rule]` |
| `json` | Machine-readable output for scripting |
| `sarif` | GitHub Code Scanning and other security tools |
| `github` | GitHub Actions workflow annotations |

---

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome! To get started:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/your-org/flak.git
cd flak
cargo build
cargo test
```

Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening a pull request. Bug reports and feature requests go in [Issues](https://github.com/your-org/flak/issues).

### Adding a new rule

1. Create a file in `src/rules/`
2. Implement the `Rule` trait
3. Register it in `src/rules/mod.rs`
4. Add tests and fixtures under `tests/fixtures/<rule-name>/`
5. Document it in `docs/rules.md`

## License

Licensed under the [MIT License](LICENSE).
````

## Features

- **Fast**: lints thousands of files in parallel.
- **Helpful errors**: precise line/column positions with clear messages.
- **Auto-fix**: safely fixes many style issues with `--fix`.
- **Configurable**: enable, disable, or tune every rule.
- **Multi-document support**: handles `---` separated documents correctly.
- **Multiple output formats**: human-readable, JSON, SARIF, JUnit, and GitHub Actions annotations.
- **Zero dependencies at runtime**: ships as a single static binary.

---

## Installation

### Homebrew (macOS / Linux)

```sh
brew install your-org/tap/flak
```

### Go

```sh
go install github.com/your-org/flak/cmd/flak@latest
```

### Prebuilt binaries

Download the latest release for your platform from the [releases page](https://github.com/your-org/flak/releases), then add it to your `PATH`.

### Docker

```sh
docker run --rm -v "$(pwd):/work" -w /work ghcr.io/your-org/flak:latest .
```

### Verify installation

```sh
flak --version
```

---

## Quick Start

Lint the current directory:

```sh
flak .
```

Lint specific files:

```sh
flak docker-compose.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml
```

Automatically fix what can be fixed:

```sh
flak --fix .
```

Generate a starter config file:

```sh
flak init
```

---

## Usage

```
flak [options] [paths...]
```

If no paths are given, `flak` lints the current directory recursively. Files matching `*.yaml` and `*.yml` are included by default.

### Options

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `-c, --config <file>` | Path to config file (default: auto-discovered `.flak.yaml`) |
| `-f, --format <fmt>` | Output format: `pretty`, `json`, `sarif`, `junit`, `github` (default: `pretty`) |
| `--fix` | Automatically fix problems where possible |
| `--dry-run` | Show what `--fix` would change without writing files |
| `--strict` | Treat warnings as errors |
| `-q, --quiet` | Report errors only, suppress warnings |
| `--max-warnings <n>` | Fail if more than `n` warnings are found |
| `--ignore <glob>` | Ignore files matching the pattern (repeatable) |
| `--no-ignore` | Do not respect `.flakignore` or `.gitignore` |
| `--stdin` | Read YAML from standard input |
| `--stdin-filename <name>` | Filename to report when using `--stdin` |
| `-j, --jobs <n>` | Number of parallel workers (default: number of CPUs) |
| `--no-color` | Disable colored output |
| `--list-rules` | Print all available rules and exit |
| `-v, --version` | Print version and exit |
| `-h, --help` | Show help |

### Examples

```sh
# Fail CI on any warning
flak --strict .

# Lint YAML piped from another command
kubectl get deploy my-app -o yaml | flak --stdin --stdin-filename deploy.yaml

# Ignore generated files
flak --ignore "**/generated/**" .

# Preview fixes as a diff
flak --fix --dry-run charts/
```

---

## Configuration

`flak` looks for a configuration file in the following order, starting from the current directory and walking up to the filesystem root:

1. `.flak.yaml`
2. `.flak.yml`
3. `flak.config.yaml`

### Example `.flak.yaml`

```yaml
# Start from a built-in preset: "recommended", "strict", or "minimal"
extends: recommended

# Files to include and exclude
include:
  - "**/*.yaml"
  - "**/*.yml"
exclude:
  - "node_modules/**"
  - "vendor/**"

rules:
  indentation:
    level: error
    spaces: 2
    indent-sequences: true

  line-length:
    level: warning
    max: 120
    allow-urls: true

  truthy:
    level: error
    allowed-values: ["true", "false"]

  document-start: off

  quoted-strings:
    level: warning
    quote-type: double
    required: only-when-needed

# Override rules for specific paths
overrides:
  - files: [".github/workflows/*.yml"]
    rules:
      truthy: off   # GitHub Actions uses `on:` as a key
  - files: ["charts/**/templates/*.yaml"]
    rules:
      syntax: off   # Helm templates aren't valid YAML until rendered
```

Each rule accepts a `level` of `error`, `warning`, or `off`. Shorthand is supported:

```yaml
rules:
  trailing-spaces: error
  comments: off
```

### Ignore files

`flak` respects `.gitignore` by default. Add a `.flakignore` file to exclude additional paths using the same syntax:

```
dist/
**/fixtures/**
legacy-config.yaml
```

---

## Rules

Run `flak --list-rules` for the full list with descriptions. Rules marked 🔧 can be fixed automatically with `--fix`.

| Rule | Default | Fixable | Description |
|------|---------|:-------:|-------------|
| `syntax` | error | | File must be valid YAML |
| `no-duplicate-keys` | error | | Mapping keys must be unique |
| `indentation` | error | 🔧 | Consistent indentation width |
| `trailing-spaces` | warning | 🔧 | No trailing whitespace |
| `new-line-at-end-of-file` | warning | 🔧 | Files must end with a newline |
| `line-length` | warning | | Maximum line length |
| `truthy` | warning | 🔧 | Disallow ambiguous booleans like `yes`, `on`, `no` |
| `key-ordering` | off | 🔧 | Keys must be sorted alphabetically |
| `quoted-strings` | off | 🔧 | Enforce quoting style for strings |
| `empty-values` | warning | | Disallow keys with no value |
| `document-start` | off | 🔧 | Require or forbid `---` at the start |
| `comments` | warning | 🔧 | Require a space after `#` |
| `brackets` | warning | 🔧 | Spacing inside flow sequences `[ ]` |
| `braces` | warning | 🔧 | Spacing inside flow mappings `{ }` |
| `colons` | error | 🔧 | Spacing around colons |
| `hyphens` | warning | 🔧 | Spacing after list hyphens |
| `octal-values` | error | | Disallow implicit octal numbers like `0755` |
| `no-tabs` | error | 🔧 | Tabs are not allowed for indentation |
| `anchors` | warning | | Disallow unused or undefined anchors/aliases |

### Presets

- **`minimal`**: only syntax and correctness rules (`syntax`, `no-duplicate-keys`, `no-tabs`).
- **`recommended`** *(default)*: correctness plus sensible style rules.
- **`strict`**: everything in `recommended`, with all warnings promoted to errors and `key-ordering` and `document-start` enabled.

---

## Inline Directives

Disable rules directly in your YAML using comments:

```yaml
# flak-disable-file                     ← disable all rules for this file
# flak-disable-file line-length         ← disable one rule for this file

# flak-disable truthy
legacy_flag: yes
other_flag: no
# flak-enable truthy

url: https://example.com/a/very/long/path  # flak-disable-line line-length

# flak-disable-next-line no-duplicate-keys
key: override
```

---

## Output Formats

### `pretty` (default)

Human-readable, colorized output grouped by file.

### `json`

```sh
flak --format json . > report.json
```

```json
[
  {
    "file": "config/app.yaml",
    "line": 3,
    "column": 1,
    "severity": "error",
    "rule": "no-duplicate-keys",
    "message": "duplicate key \"database\"",
    "fixable": false
  }
]
```

### `sarif`

For GitHub Code Scanning and other SARIF-compatible tools.

### `junit`

For CI systems that display JUnit XML test reports.

### `github`

Emits [workflow commands](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/using-workflows/workflow-commands-for-github-actions) so problems appear as inline annotations on pull requests.

---

## Integrations

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
name: Lint YAML
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  flak:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: your-org/flak-action@v1
        with:
          args: --strict .
```

Or install and run it directly:

```yaml
      - run: go install github.com/your-org/flak/cmd/flak@latest
      - run: flak --format github .
```

### pre-commit

Add to `.pre-commit-config.yaml`:

```yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/your-org/flak
    rev: v1.0.0
    hooks:
      - id: flak
        args: [--fix]
```

### GitLab CI

```yaml
lint-yaml:
  image: ghcr.io/your-org/flak:latest
  script:
    - flak --format junit . > flak-report.xml
  artifacts:
    reports:
      junit: flak-report.xml
```

### Editors

- **VS Code**: install the [flak extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/) for real-time diagnostics.
- **Neovim**: supported via [nvim-lint](https://github.com/mfussenegger/nvim-lint) and [none-ls](https://github.com/nvimtools/none-ls.nvim).
- **Other editors**: use `flak --stdin --format json` with your editor's generic linter integration.

---

## Exit Codes

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `0` | No errors found (warnings may be present) |
| `1` | Lint errors found, or warnings exceeded `--max-warnings` / `--strict` |
| `2` | Invalid configuration or command-line usage |
| `3` | Internal error (e.g., unreadable file) |

# flak

> A fast, opinionated linter for YAML files.

[![CI](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/your-org/flak/ci.yml?branch=main)](https://github.com/your-org/flak/actions)
[![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/your-org/flak)](https://github.com/your-org/flak/releases)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

`flak` catches syntax errors, style inconsistencies, and common mistakes in YAML before they reach production. It works well on Kubernetes manifests, CI pipelines, Docker Compose files, Ansible playbooks, and any other YAML your project depends on.

```
$ flak .
config/app.yaml
  3:1    error    duplicate key "database"                    no-duplicate-keys
  12:5   warning  wrong indentation: expected 2 but found 4   indentation
  18:22  warning  trailing whitespace                         trailing-spaces

deploy/service.yml
  7:10   error    truthy value "yes" should be "true"         truthy

✖ 4 problems (2 errors, 2 warnings) in 2 files
```

## Features

- **Fast**: lints thousands of files in seconds
- **Clear output**: precise line and column numbers with readable messages
- **Configurable**: enable, disable, or tune every rule
- **Auto-fix**: fixes many style issues automatically with `--fix`
- **CI-friendly**: meaningful exit codes and machine-readable output formats
- **Zero dependencies**: ships as a single static binary

---

## Installation

### Homebrew (macOS / Linux)

```sh
brew install flak
```

### Cargo

```sh
cargo install flak
```

### Prebuilt binaries

Download the latest release for your platform from the [releases page](https://github.com/your-org/flak/releases), then place it somewhere on your `PATH`.

```sh
curl -sSL https://github.com/your-org/flak/releases/latest/download/flak-linux-x86_64.tar.gz | tar xz
sudo mv flak /usr/local/bin/
```

### Docker

```sh
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/work" -w /work ghcr.io/your-org/flak .
```

Verify the installation:

```sh
flak --version
```

---

## Quick Start

Lint a single file:

```sh
flak config.yaml
```

Lint a directory recursively:

```sh
flak ./k8s
```

Lint the current project:

```sh
flak .
```

Automatically fix what can be fixed:

```sh
flak --fix .
```

Generate a starter config file:

```sh
flak init
```

## Usage

```
flak [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...
```

If no paths are given, `flak` lints the current directory. It picks up files ending in `.yaml` and `.yml` and respects `.gitignore` by default.

### Options

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `-c, --config <FILE>` | Path to a config file (default: auto-discovered `.flak.yaml`) |
| `-f, --format <FORMAT>` | Output format: `pretty`, `compact`, `json`, `github`, `sarif` (default: `pretty`) |
| `--fix` | Automatically fix problems where possible |
| `--diff` | Show the changes `--fix` would make without writing them |
| `-s, --strict` | Treat warnings as errors |
| `-q, --quiet` | Report errors only and suppress warnings |
| `--no-ignore` | Don't respect `.gitignore` or `.flakignore` |
| `--exclude <GLOB>` | Exclude matching paths (repeatable) |
| `--stdin` | Read YAML from standard input |
| `--stdin-filename <NAME>` | Filename to use in reports when reading from stdin |
| `--list-rules` | Print all available rules and exit |
| `--no-color` | Disable colored output |
| `-h, --help` | Print help |
| `-V, --version` | Print version |

### Examples

```sh
# Lint only Kubernetes manifests, excluding Helm templates
flak k8s/ --exclude 'k8s/charts/**/templates/**'

# Pipe content from another tool
helm template ./chart | flak --stdin --stdin-filename rendered.yaml

# Fail CI on any warning
flak --strict .

# Produce JSON for downstream tooling
flak --format json . > flak-report.json
```

---

## Configuration

`flak` looks for a config file in the current directory and its parents, in this order:

1. `.flak.yaml`
2. `.flak.yml`
3. `flak.yaml`

Run `flak init` to generate one with sensible defaults.

### Example `.flak.yaml`

```yaml
# Start from a built-in preset: "default", "relaxed", or "strict"
extends: default

# Files to skip, in addition to .gitignore
ignore:
  - "vendor/**"
  - "**/*.generated.yaml"

rules:
  indentation:
    level: error
    spaces: 2
    indent-sequences: consistent

  line-length:
    level: warning
    max: 120
    allow-urls: true

  truthy:
    level: error
    allowed-values: ["true", "false"]

  document-start: off

  comments:
    min-spaces-from-content: 1

# Per-path overrides
overrides:
  - files: [".github/workflows/*.yml"]
    rules:
      truthy: off        # GitHub Actions uses `on:` as a key
  - files: ["docs/**"]
    rules:
      line-length: off
```

Each rule accepts a `level` of `error`, `warning`, or `off`. You can also set a rule to the level directly as shorthand, for example `line-length: off`.

### Presets

| Preset | Description |
|---|---|
| `default` | Balanced rules suitable for most projects |
| `relaxed` | Syntax and correctness checks only, with minimal style enforcement |
| `strict` | Every rule enabled at `error` level |

---

## Rules

| Rule | Default | Fixable | Description |
|---|---|:---:|---|
| `syntax` | error | | Invalid YAML that cannot be parsed |
| `no-duplicate-keys` | error | | The same key appears twice in a mapping |
| `indentation` | warning | ✔ | Inconsistent or incorrect indentation |
| `trailing-spaces` | warning | ✔ | Whitespace at the end of a line |
| `line-length` | warning | | Lines longer than the configured maximum |
| `truthy` | warning | ✔ | Ambiguous booleans such as `yes`, `no`, `on`, `off` |
| `new-line-at-end-of-file` | warning | ✔ | File doesn't end with a newline |
| `empty-lines` | warning | ✔ | Too many consecutive blank lines |
| `document-start` | off | ✔ | Require or forbid `---` at the top of documents |
| `key-ordering` | off | | Mapping keys must be sorted alphabetically |
| `quoted-strings` | off | ✔ | Enforce a consistent quoting style |
| `comments` | warning | ✔ | Spacing and formatting of comments |
| `brackets` | warning | ✔ | Spacing inside flow sequences `[ ]` |
| `braces` | warning | ✔ | Spacing inside flow mappings `{ }` |
| `anchors` | warning | | Undefined, duplicate, or unused anchors and aliases |
| `octal-values` | error | | Implicit octal numbers such as `0777` |
| `float-values` | off | | Restrict forms like `.5`, `1e3`, `.inf`, `.nan` |

Run `flak --list-rules` for full details and options for each rule.

### Inline suppression

You can disable rules for a specific line or block with comments:

```yaml
password: hunter2  # flak-disable-line

# flak-disable-next-line line-length
description: "a very long line that you really don't want to wrap for some reason ..."

# flak-disable truthy
legacy_flag: yes
other_flag: no
# flak-enable truthy
```

To skip an entire file, add this comment anywhere in it:

```yaml
# flak-disable-file
```

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | No errors found (warnings may be present unless `--strict` is set) |
| `1` | One or more lint errors were found |
| `2` | Invalid usage, bad config, or an internal error |

rules:

    level: error

      - files: ".github/workflows/*.yml"

```
$ flak config/

  3:1   error    duplicate key "database"                 no-duplicate-keys

  18:22 warning  trailing whitespace                      no-trailing-spaces

## Features

- **Fast**: lints thousands of files in milliseconds
- **Sensible defaults**: works out of the box with zero configuration
- **Configurable**: enable, disable, or tune every rule
- **Auto-fix**: automatically repairs many style issues with `--fix`
- **Multiple output formats**: human-readable, JSON, SARIF, GitHub annotations, JUnit
- **Multi-document support**: handles `---` separated documents correctly
- **Schema-aware** (optional): validates against JSON Schema

## Installation

### Homebrew (macOS / Linux)

```sh
brew install flak
```

### Cargo

```sh
cargo install flak
```

### npm

```sh
npm install --global flak-cli
```

### Pre-built binaries

Download the latest release for your platform from the [releases page](https://github.com/your-org/flak/releases).

### Docker

```sh
docker run --rm -v "$(pwd):/work" ghcr.io/your-org/flak .
```

Verify the installation:

```sh
flak --version
```

---

## Quick Start

Lint a single file:

```sh
flak config.yaml
```

Lint a directory recursively:

```sh
flak .
```

Automatically fix what can be fixed:

```sh
flak --fix .
```

Generate a starter config file:

```sh
flak init
```

## Usage

```
flak [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...
```

If no paths are given, `flak` lints the current directory.

### Options

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `-c, --config <FILE>` | Path to config file (default: auto-discovered `.flak.yaml`) |
| `-f, --format <FORMAT>` | Output format: `pretty`, `compact`, `json`, `sarif`, `github`, `junit` |
| `--fix` | Automatically fix problems where possible |
| `--fix-dry-run` | Show what `--fix` would change without writing files |
| `--strict` | Treat warnings as errors |
| `-q, --quiet` | Report errors only, suppress warnings |
| `--max-warnings <N>` | Fail if more than `N` warnings are found |
| `--ignore <PATTERN>` | Glob pattern of files to ignore (repeatable) |
| `--rule <RULE=LEVEL>` | Override a rule's level, e.g. `--rule line-length=off` |
| `--stdin` | Read YAML from standard input |
| `--stdin-filename <NAME>` | Filename to report when using `--stdin` |
| `--no-color` | Disable colored output |
| `--list-rules` | Print all available rules and exit |
| `-h, --help` | Print help |
| `-V, --version` | Print version |

### Examples

```sh
# Lint only Kubernetes manifests
flak k8s/**/*.yaml

# Lint from stdin
cat docker-compose.yml | flak --stdin --stdin-filename docker-compose.yml

# Fail CI on any warning
flak --strict .

# Disable a rule for a single run
flak --rule document-start=off .
```

---

## Configuration

`flak` looks for a configuration file in the current directory and its parents, in this order:

1. `.flak.yaml`
2. `.flak.yml`
3. `flak.config.yaml`
4. A `flak` key in `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

### Example `.flak.yaml`

```yaml
# Start from a built-in preset: "recommended", "strict", or "relaxed"
extends: recommended

# Files and directories to skip
ignore:
  - node_modules/
  - vendor/
  - "**/*.generated.yaml"

# File extensions to lint
extensions:
  - .yaml
  - .yml

rules:
  indentation:
    level: error
    spaces: 2
    indent-sequences: true

  line-length:
    level: warning
    max: 120
    allow-urls: true

  strict-booleans: error
  no-trailing-spaces: error
  document-start: off

  quoted-strings:
    level: warning
    style: double     # "single", "double", or "consistent"
    required: only-when-needed

# Override rules for specific paths
overrides:
  - files: [".github/workflows/*.yml"]
    rules:
      strict-booleans: off   # GitHub uses `on:` as a key
```

### Rule levels

Each rule can be set to one of:

- `off`: disable the rule
- `warning`: report, but do not fail (unless `--strict`)
- `error`: report and exit with a non-zero code

---

## Rules

Run `flak --list-rules` for the full list. Rules marked 🔧 can be fixed automatically with `--fix`.

### Correctness

| Rule | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `syntax` | error | File must be valid YAML |
| `no-duplicate-keys` | error | Mapping keys must be unique |
| `no-anchor-undefined` | error | Aliases must reference a defined anchor |
| `no-tabs` 🔧 | error | Tabs are not allowed for indentation |
| `strict-booleans` 🔧 | warning | Use `true`/`false` instead of `yes`/`no`/`on`/`off` |
| `octal-values` | warning | Flag ambiguous octal-like numbers (e.g. `0755`) |

### Style

| Rule | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `indentation` 🔧 | warning | Enforce consistent indentation |
| `line-length` | warning | Limit line length |
| `no-trailing-spaces` 🔧 | warning | Disallow trailing whitespace |
| `final-newline` 🔧 | warning | Require a newline at end of file |
| `empty-lines` 🔧 | warning | Limit consecutive blank lines |
| `document-start` 🔧 | off | Require (or forbid) a leading `---` |
| `key-ordering` | off | Require keys to be sorted alphabetically |
| `quoted-strings` 🔧 | off | Enforce a quoting style for strings |
| `comments-spacing` 🔧 | warning | Require a space after `#` |
| `colons` 🔧 | warning | Control spacing around colons |
| `brackets` 🔧 | warning | Control spacing inside `[ ]` and `{ }` |

---

## Inline Directives

Disable rules directly in your YAML files with comments:

```yaml
# flak-disable-file line-length

key: value  # flak-disable-line strict-booleans
enabled: yes

# flak-disable-next-line no-duplicate-keys
name: first
name: second

# flak-disable indentation
legacy:
    weird:   indent
# flak-enable indentation
```

Omitting the rule name disables **all** rules for that scope.

---

| Format | Use case |
|---|---|
| `pretty` | Default; human-readable, grouped by file |
| `compact` | One problem per line: `file:line:col: level: message (rule)` |
| `json` | Machine-readable output for tooling |
| `sarif` | GitHub Code Scanning and other SARIF consumers |
| `github` | Inline annotations in GitHub Actions |
| `junit` | CI systems that consume JUnit XML |

```sh
flak --format json . > flak-report.json
```

```yaml
name: Lint YAML
on: [push, pull_request]

| `0` | No errors found |

| Command        | Description                                   |

| `lint`         | Lint files or directories (default command)   |
| `init`         | Create a `.flak.yaml` config in the current directory |
| `rules`        | List all available rules and their defaults   |

### Options

| Option                  | Description                                                    |
|-------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
| `-c, --config <FILE>`   | Path to a config file (default: auto-discovered `.flak.yaml`)  |

### Examples

```sh

```

## Configuration

`flak` looks for a config file in the current directory and walks up to the filesystem root. Recognized names:

- `.flak.yaml`
- `.flak.yml`
- `flak.yaml`

### Example `.flak.yaml`

```yaml
# Start from a preset: "default", "relaxed", or "strict"

  - "vendor/**"
  - "node_modules/**"
  - "**/*.generated.yaml"

    level: warning
    max: 120
    allow-urls: true

    allowed-values: ["true", "false"]

  document-start: off

  comments:
    min-spaces-from-content: 1

  - files: [".github/workflows/*.yml"]

Each rule accepts a `level` of `error`, `warning`, or `off`.

| Rule                  | Default  | Fixable | Description                                           |
|-----------------------|----------|:-------:|-------------------------------------------------------|
| `syntax`              | error    |         | YAML must parse correctly                             |
| `no-duplicate-keys`   | error    |         | Mapping keys must be unique                           |

| `-q, --quiet` | Only report errors |
| `--no-color` | Disable colored output |
| `--list-rules` | Print all available rules and exit |
| `-h, --help` | Print help |
| `-V, --version` | Print version |

### Examples

```sh
# Lint specific files
flak docker-compose.yml .github/workflows/*.yml

# Lint from stdin
cat values.yaml | flak - --stdin-filename values.yaml

# Fail CI on any warning
flak --strict .

# Preview auto-fixes as a diff
flak --fix --dry-run k8s/

# Machine-readable output
flak --format json . > flak-report.json
```

## Configuration

`flak` looks for a config file in the current directory and its parents, in this order:

1. `.flak.yaml`
2. `.flak.yml`
3. `flak.config.yaml`
4. A `flak` key in `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

### Example `.flak.yaml`

```yaml
# Start from a built-in preset: "recommended" (default), "strict", or "relaxed"
extends: recommended

# Files to ignore (in addition to .gitignore)
ignore:
  - "vendor/**"
  - "**/generated/*.yaml"
  - "charts/**/templates/**"   # Helm templates aren't valid YAML

# Additional file patterns to lint
include:
  - "**/*.yaml.tmpl"

rules:
  indentation:
    level: error
    spaces: 2
    indent-sequences: consistent

  line-length:
    level: warning
    max: 120
    allow-urls: true

  truthy:
    level: error
    allowed-values: ["true", "false"]

  document-start: off

  quoted-strings:
    level: warning
    quote-type: double
    required: only-when-needed

# Per-path overrides
overrides:
  - files: [".github/workflows/*.yml"]
    rules:
      truthy: off   # GitHub Actions uses the `on:` key
  - files: ["k8s/**"]
    rules:
      line-length:
        max: 160
```

Each rule accepts a `level` of `error`, `warning`, or `off`. A bare level (`document-start: off`) is shorthand for `{ level: off }`.

---

## Rules

Run `flak --list-rules` for the full list with descriptions. ✅ = enabled in `recommended`, 🔧 = auto-fixable.

| Rule | Description | ✅ | 🔧 |
| --- | --- | :-: | :-: |
| `syntax` | File must be valid YAML | ✅ | |
| `no-duplicate-keys` | Disallow duplicate keys in a mapping | ✅ | |
| `indentation` | Enforce consistent indentation | ✅ | 🔧 |
| `trailing-spaces` | Disallow trailing whitespace | ✅ | 🔧 |
| `new-line-at-end-of-file` | Require a final newline | ✅ | 🔧 |
| `new-lines` | Enforce line ending type (`unix` / `dos`) | ✅ | 🔧 |
| `no-tabs` | Disallow tab characters for indentation | ✅ | 🔧 |
| `truthy` | Disallow ambiguous booleans like `yes`, `on`, `Y` | ✅ | 🔧 |
| `line-length` | Limit line length | ✅ | |
| `empty-lines` | Limit consecutive blank lines | ✅ | 🔧 |
| `colons` | Enforce spacing around colons | ✅ | 🔧 |
| `commas` | Enforce spacing around commas in flow collections | ✅ | 🔧 |
| `comments` | Require a space after `#` | ✅ | 🔧 |
| `brackets` | Enforce spacing inside `[ ]` | | 🔧 |
| `braces` | Enforce spacing inside `{ }` | | 🔧 |
| `document-start` | Require or forbid `---` at document start | | 🔧 |
| `document-end` | Require or forbid `...` at document end | | 🔧 |
| `quoted-strings` | Enforce quote style for strings | | 🔧 |
| `key-ordering` | Require keys to be sorted alphabetically | | |
| `octal-values` | Disallow implicit octal values like `0755` | ✅ | |
| `float-values` | Disallow ambiguous floats like `.5` or `1e3` | | |
| `anchors` | Disallow unused anchors and undefined aliases | ✅ | |
| `empty-values` | Disallow keys with empty values | | |

---

## Inline Directives

Disable rules directly in your YAML using comments:

```yaml
# flak-disable-file                    # skip this entire file

# flak-disable line-length
very_long_key: "a value that would otherwise exceed the configured line length..."
# flak-enable line-length

enabled: yes  # flak-disable-line truthy

# flak-disable-next-line no-duplicate-keys
name: override
```

Omitting a rule name disables all rules for that scope.

---

## Output Formats

| Format | Use case |
| --- | --- |
| `pretty` | Default; grouped, colored, human-readable |
| `compact` | One problem per line: `file:line:col: level: message (rule)` |
| `json` | Programmatic consumption |
| `sarif` | GitHub Code Scanning and other SARIF tools |
| `junit` | CI test report dashboards |
| `github` | Inline PR annotations in GitHub Actions |

---

## Exit Codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | No errors found |
| `1` | Lint errors found (or warnings, with `--strict` / `--max-warnings`) |
| `2` | Invalid usage, bad config, or internal error |

---

## Integrations

### GitHub Actions

```yaml

on: [push, pull_request]

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

```

      - id: flak
        args: [--fix]
```

    - flak --format junit . > flak-report.xml
  artifacts:
    reports:

```

- 🧩 **Configurable.** Enable, disable, or tune every rule.
- 🎯 **Precise.** Reports exact line and column positions.
- 🔧 **Auto-fix.** Fixes many style issues automatically with `--fix`.
- 📦 **CI-friendly.** Uses meaningful exit codes and supports JSON, SARIF, and GitHub Actions output.
- 📄 **Multi-document support.** Handles `---` separated documents correctly.

## Installation

```sh

```

```

## Quick Start

flak config.yaml

Lint a whole directory recursively:

```sh
flak .

Fix what can be fixed automatically:

```sh
flak --fix .
```

```sh

## Usage

```
flak [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...
```

If no paths are given, `flak` lints the current directory.

### Options

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-c, --config <FILE>` | Use a specific config file |
| `--fix` | Automatically fix problems where possible |
| `--check` | Report fixable problems without changing files |
| `-f, --format <FORMAT>` | Output format: `pretty` (default), `compact`, `json`, `sarif`, `github` |
| `--strict` | Treat warnings as errors |

### Examples

```sh
# Lint only Kubernetes manifests
flak k8s/**/*.yaml

# Pipe content in from another tool
helm template ./chart | flak --stdin --stdin-filename chart.yaml

# Machine-readable output
flak --format json . > flak-report.json

# Fail CI on any warning
flak --strict .

## Configuration

`flak` looks for a config file in the current directory and then in each parent directory, in this order:

1. `.flak.yaml`
2. `.flak.yml`
3. `flak.toml`
4. A `[tool.flak]` section in `pyproject.toml`

### Example `.flak.yaml`

```yaml
# Start from a preset: "recommended", "strict", or "relaxed"
extends: recommended

# Files and directories to skip
ignore:
  - node_modules/
  - vendor/
  - "**/*.generated.yaml"

# File extensions to lint
extensions: [".yaml", ".yml"]

rules:
  indentation:
    level: error
    spaces: 2
    indent-sequences: consistent

  line-length:
    level: warning
    max: 120
    allow-urls: true

  no-implicit-truthy:
    level: error
    allowed: ["true", "false"]

  document-start: off

# Per-path overrides
overrides:
  - files: [".github/workflows/*.yml"]
    rules:
      no-implicit-truthy: off   # GitHub uses `on:` as a key
  - files: ["charts/**/templates/*.yaml"]
    rules:
      syntax: off               # Helm templates are not valid YAML before rendering
```

Each rule accepts a `level` of `error`, `warning`, or `off`. As a shorthand, you can set the level directly: `line-length: off`.

---

## Rules

Run `flak --list-rules` to see the full list along with each rule's defaults.

| Rule | Default | Fixable | Description |
| --- | --- | :---: | --- |
| `syntax` | error | | File must be valid YAML |
| `no-duplicate-keys` | error | | Mapping keys must be unique |
| `indentation` | error | ✅ | Indentation must be consistent |
| `no-tabs` | error | ✅ | Tabs are not allowed for indentation |
| `no-implicit-truthy` | warning | ✅ | Values like `yes`, `no`, `on`, and `off` must be quoted |
| `no-implicit-octal` | warning | | Catches numbers like `0755` that may be parsed as octal |
| `trailing-whitespace` | warning | ✅ | Lines must not end with whitespace |
| `final-newline` | warning | ✅ | File must end with a single newline |
| `line-length` | warning | | Lines must not exceed the maximum length |
| `empty-lines` | warning | ✅ | Limits consecutive blank lines |
| `key-ordering` | off | | Keys must be sorted alphabetically |
| `quoted-strings` | off | ✅ | Enforces a consistent quote style |
| `document-start` | off | ✅ | Requires or forbids `---` at the start of a file |
| `comments` | warning | ✅ | Requires a space after `#` and before inline comments |
| `anchors` | warning | | Flags undefined, unused, or duplicate anchors |
| `braces` / `brackets` | warning | ✅ | Controls spacing inside flow collections |

### Inline suppression

You can disable rules for a single line or a whole file with comments:

```yaml

name: example
password: yes  # flak-disable-line no-implicit-truthy

# flak-disable-next-line no-duplicate-keys

```

## Exit Codes

| `0` | No errors found |
| `1` | Lint errors found (or warnings found with `--strict`) |

        with:

- **Others:** any editor that supports external linters can call `flak --format compact --stdin`.

## FAQ

**How is flak different from yamllint?**
`flak` focuses on speed, auto-fixing, and modern CI output formats such as SARIF and GitHub annotations. Its rule names and config format will feel familiar if you are migrating from yamllint.

**Does flak validate against a schema (e.g., Kubernetes or JSON Schema)?**
Not yet. Schema validation is on the [roadmap](https://github.com/your-org/flak/issues). For now, `flak` checks syntax and style only.

**Why is `on:` flagged in my GitHub workflow?**
In YAML 1.1, `on` is parsed as the boolean `true`. GitHub handles this case specially, so you can disable `no-implicit-truthy` for workflow files with an override, as shown in the [Configuration](#configuration) example.

# flak

> A fast, opinionated linter for YAML files.

`flak` catches syntax errors, style inconsistencies, and common pitfalls in YAML files before they reach production. It works on CI configs, Kubernetes manifests, Ansible playbooks, Docker Compose files, and any other YAML.

```
$ flak config/
config/app.yaml
  12:3   error    duplicate key "timeout"                    no-duplicate-keys
  18:1   warning  trailing whitespace                        trailing-spaces
  24:9   warning  truthy value "yes" should be "true"        truthy

config/db.yaml
  7:15   error    found tab character in indentation         no-tabs

✖ 4 problems (2 errors, 2 warnings) in 2 files
```

---

## Features

- **Fast**: lints thousands of files in seconds
- **Sensible defaults**: useful out of the box with zero configuration
- **Configurable**: enable, disable, or tune every rule
- **Auto-fix**: automatically repairs many style issues with `--fix`
- **CI-friendly**: exit codes and machine-readable output formats (JSON, SARIF, GitHub Actions annotations)
- **Multi-document support**: handles `---`-separated documents in a single file

---

## Installation

### Homebrew (macOS / Linux)

```sh
brew install flak
```

### Cargo

```sh
cargo install flak
```

### Prebuilt binaries

Download the latest release for your platform from the [Releases](https://github.com/your-org/flak/releases) page and place the binary somewhere on your `PATH`.

### Verify the installation

```sh
flak --version
```

---

## Quick Start

Lint a single file:

```sh
flak deploy.yaml
```

Lint a directory recursively:

```sh
flak .
```

Automatically fix what can be fixed:

```sh
flak --fix .
```

Read from stdin:

```sh
cat deploy.yaml | flak -
```

---

## Usage

```
flak [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...
```

### Options

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `-c, --config <FILE>` | Path to a config file (default: auto-discovered `.flak.yaml`) |
| `--fix` | Automatically fix problems where possible |
| `--format <FORMAT>` | Output format: `pretty` (default), `compact`, `json`, `sarif`, `github` |
| `--strict` | Treat warnings as errors |
| `--quiet` | Report errors only; suppress warnings |
| `--rule <RULE>=<LEVEL>` | Override a rule's level for this run (e.g. `--rule line-length=off`) |
| `--exclude <GLOB>` | Exclude matching paths (repeatable) |
| `--list-rules` | Print all available rules and exit |
| `--no-color` | Disable colored output |
| `-h, --help` | Show help |
| `-V, --version` | Show version |

### Exit Codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | No errors found |
| `1` | One or more errors found (or warnings, with `--strict`) |
| `2` | Invalid usage or configuration |

---

## Configuration

`flak` looks for a configuration file in the current directory and its parents, in this order:

1. `.flak.yaml`
2. `.flak.yml`
3. `flak.yaml`

### Example `.flak.yaml`

```yaml
# Start from a built-in preset: "default", "relaxed", or "strict"
extends: default

# Files and directories to ignore
ignore:
  - node_modules/
  - vendor/
  - "**/*.generated.yaml"

rules:
  indentation:
    level: error
    spaces: 2
    indent-sequences: consistent

  line-length:
    level: warning
    max: 120
    allow-urls: true

  truthy:
    level: warning
    allowed-values: ["true", "false"]

  document-start: off

  comments:
    min-spaces-from-content: 2
```

Each rule accepts a `level` of `error`, `warning`, or `off`. Setting a rule directly to a level (e.g. `document-start: off`) is shorthand for `{ level: off }`.

---

## Rules

| Rule | Default | Fixable | Description |
|---|---|:---:|---|
| `syntax` | error | | File must be valid YAML |
| `no-duplicate-keys` | error | | Mappings must not contain duplicate keys |
| `no-tabs` | error | ✓ | Tabs are not allowed in indentation |
| `indentation` | error | ✓ | Enforce consistent indentation width |
| `trailing-spaces` | warning | ✓ | Disallow trailing whitespace |
| `line-length` | warning | | Limit maximum line length |
| `truthy` | warning | ✓ | Disallow ambiguous booleans like `yes`, `on`, `no` |
| `empty-values` | warning | | Flag keys with no value |
| `key-ordering` | off | | Require mapping keys in alphabetical order |
| `quoted-strings` | off | ✓ | Enforce a consistent quoting style |
| `document-start` | warning | ✓ | Require or forbid `---` at file start |
| `new-line-at-end` | warning | ✓ | Require a newline at end of file |
| `comments` | warning | ✓ | Enforce spacing around comments |
| `anchors` | warning | | Flag undefined or unused anchors and aliases |

Run `flak --list-rules` for the full, up-to-date list with details.

---

## Inline Directives

Disable rules for specific lines or blocks with comments:

```yaml
# Disable a rule for the next line
# flak-disable-next-line line-length
description: "This is a very long line that would normally trigger a warning but is fine here"

# Disable rules for a block
# flak-disable truthy
legacy_flag: yes
other_flag: on
# flak-enable truthy

# Disable all rules for the entire file (must be on the first line)
# flak-disable-file
```

---

## CI Integration

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
name: Lint YAML
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  flak:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

4. Document it in the Rules table above

| Command        | Description                                        |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `init`         | Create a `.flak.yaml` config in the current directory |
| `rules`        | List all available rules and their defaults        |
| `explain <rule>` | Show detailed documentation for a rule           |

### Options

| Option                    | Description                                                    |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-c, --config <FILE>`     | Path to a config file (default: auto-discovered)               |
| `-f, --format <FORMAT>`   | Output format: `pretty`, `compact`, `json`, `sarif`, `github`, `junit` |
| `--fix`                   | Automatically fix problems where possible                      |
| `--fix-dry-run`           | Show fixes as a diff without writing changes                   |
| `-s, --strict`            | Treat warnings as errors                                       |
| `-q, --quiet`             | Only report errors, suppress warnings                          |
| `--max-warnings <N>`      | Fail if more than `N` warnings are found                       |
| `--enable <RULE>`         | Enable a rule (repeatable)                                     |
| `--disable <RULE>`        | Disable a rule (repeatable)                                    |
| `--ignore <GLOB>`         | Ignore files matching a pattern (repeatable)                   |
| `--stdin`                 | Read YAML from standard input                                  |
| `--stdin-filename <NAME>` | Filename to use in reports when reading from stdin            |
| `--no-color`              | Disable colored output                                         |
| `-j, --jobs <N>`          | Number of parallel workers (default: number of CPUs)           |
| `-h, --help`              | Print help                                                     |
| `-V, --version`           | Print version                                                  |

### Examples

```sh
# Lint only files matching a glob
flak "k8s/**/*.yaml"

# Lint from stdin
cat docker-compose.yml | flak --stdin --stdin-filename docker-compose.yml

# Fail CI on any warning
flak --strict .

# Use a specific config and output JSON
flak -c ci/flak.yaml -f json . > report.json

# Preview fixes without modifying files
flak --fix-dry-run .
```

By default, `flak` checks files ending in `.yaml` and `.yml` and respects `.gitignore`.

---

## Configuration

`flak` looks for a config file in the current directory and its parents, in this order:

1. `.flak.yaml`
2. `.flak.yml`
3. `flak.yaml`
4. A `[tool.flak]` section in `pyproject.toml`

### Example `.flak.yaml`

```yaml
# Start from a built-in preset: "recommended", "strict", or "minimal"
extends: recommended

# Files and directories to skip
ignore:
  - node_modules/
  - vendor/
  - "**/*.generated.yaml"

# Additional file extensions to lint
extensions:
  - .yaml
  - .yml
  - .yaml.tmpl

rules:
  indentation:
    level: error
    spaces: 2
    indent-sequences: consistent

  line-length:
    level: warning
    max: 120
    allow-urls: true

  truthy:
    allowed-values: ["true", "false"]
    check-keys: false

  document-start: off

  quoted-strings:
    quote-type: double
    required: only-when-needed

# Override settings for specific paths
overrides:
  - files: [".github/workflows/*.yml"]
    rules:
      truthy: off # GitHub Actions uses `on:` as a key

  - files: ["k8s/**/*.yaml"]
    schema: kubernetes
```

### Rule levels

Each rule can be set to one of:

| Level     | Meaning                                     |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `error`   | Reported as an error; causes non-zero exit  |
| `warning` | Reported as a warning; exit 0 unless `--strict` |
| `off`     | Rule is disabled                            |

You can use the shorthand `rule-name: error` or a full object with `level:` plus options.

---

## Rules

Run `flak rules` for the full list, or `flak explain <rule>` for details on any single rule.

| Rule                  | Default   | Fixable | Description                                          |
| --------------------- | --------- | :-----: | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `syntax`              | error     |         | YAML must parse correctly                            |
| `no-duplicate-keys`   | error     |         | Mappings must not contain duplicate keys             |
| `indentation`         | warning   | ✅      | Enforce consistent indentation width                 |
| `no-tabs`             | error     | ✅      | Disallow tab characters for indentation              |
| `trailing-spaces`     | warning   | ✅      | Disallow trailing whitespace                         |
| `line-length`         | warning   |         | Limit line length                                    |
| `new-line-at-eof`     | warning   | ✅      | Require a newline at the end of the file             |
| `empty-lines`         | warning   | ✅      | Limit consecutive blank lines                        |
| `truthy`              | warning   | ✅      | Disallow ambiguous booleans like `yes`, `on`, `Y`    |
| `key-ordering`        | off       | ✅      | Require mapping keys to be sorted                    |
| `quoted-strings`      | off       | ✅      | Enforce a quoting style for strings                  |
| `document-start`      | off       | ✅      | Require or forbid `---` at the start of documents    |
| `document-end`        | off       | ✅      | Require or forbid `...` at the end of documents      |
| `comments`            | warning   | ✅      | Require a space after `#` and before inline comments |
| `colons`              | warning   | ✅      | Enforce spacing around colons                        |
| `commas`              | warning   | ✅      | Enforce spacing around commas in flow collections    |
| `brackets`            | warning   | ✅      | Enforce spacing inside `[ ]`                         |
| `braces`              | warning   | ✅      | Enforce spacing inside `{ }`                         |
| `anchors`             | warning   |         | Disallow undefined or unused anchors and aliases     |
| `octal-values`        | warning   |         | Flag implicit octal values like `0755`               |
| `float-values`        | off       |         | Flag ambiguous floats like `.5`, `NaN`, `inf`        |
| `empty-values`        | off       |         | Disallow keys with null/empty values                 |
| `schema`              | off       |         | Validate documents against a JSON Schema             |

### Presets

- **`minimal`**: syntax and duplicate key checks only
- **`recommended`** *(default)*: catches bugs and enforces broadly accepted style
- **`strict`**: enables nearly every rule at `error` level

---

## Inline Directives

Disable rules directly in your YAML using comments.

```yaml
# Disable a rule for the next line
# flak-disable-next-line line-length
description: "This is a very long line that would normally trigger the line-length rule, but it's fine here"

# Disable a rule on the same line
enabled: yes  # flak-disable-line truthy

# Disable rules for a block
# flak-disable indentation, trailing-spaces
legacy:
    weird:   formatting
# flak-enable

# Disable all rules for the whole file (must be in the first comment block)
# flak-disable-file
```

Omitting rule names disables all rules for that scope.

---

## Output Formats

| Format    | Use case                                              |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `pretty`  | Default; grouped, colored, human-readable output      |
| `compact` | One problem per line: `file:line:col: level: message [rule]` |
| `json`    | Machine-readable output for custom tooling            |
| `sarif`   | GitHub Code Scanning and other SARIF consumers        |
| `github`  | GitHub Actions inline annotations                     |
| `junit`   | CI systems that understand JUnit XML                  |

Example `json` output:

```json
[
  {
    "file": "config/app.yaml",
    "line": 3,
    "column": 1,
    "level": "error",
    "rule": "no-duplicate-keys",
    "message": "duplicate key \"database\"",
    "fixable": false
  }
]
```

---

## Integrations

### pre-commit

Add to `.pre-commit-config.yaml`:

```yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/your-org/flak
    rev: v1.0.0
    hooks:
      - id: flak
        args: [--fix]
```

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
name: Lint YAML
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  flak:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: your-org/flak-action@v1
        with:
          args: --strict --format github .
```

### GitLab CI

```yaml
flak:
  image: ghcr.io/your-org/flak:latest
  script:
    - flak --format junit . > flak-report.xml
  artifacts:
    reports:
      junit: flak-report.xml
```

### Editors

- **VS Code**: install the [flak extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/) from the Marketplace
- **Neovim**: supported via [nvim-lint](https://github.com/mfussenegger/nvim-lint) and `none-ls`
- **Any LSP client**: run `flak lsp` to start the built-in language server

---

## Exit Codes

| Code | Meaning                                                      |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `0`  | No errors found (warnings may be present)                    |
| `1`  | One or more errors found, or warnings with `--strict` / `--max-warnings` exceeded |
| `2`  | Invalid usage, bad config, or internal failure               |

---

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome! To get started:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/your-org/flak.git
cd flak
cargo build
cargo test
```

Please:

1. Open an issue to discuss significant changes before submitting a PR.
2. Add tests for new rules or bug fixes.
3. Run `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy` before committing.
4. Lint the repo's own YAML with `flak .` (of course).

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for full guidelines and [docs/writing-rules.md](docs/writing-rules.md) for a guide to adding new rules.

---

## License

`flak` is licensed under the [MIT License](LICENSE).
````

**Notes for customizing:**
- Replace `your-org` with your actual GitHub org or username.
- The installation section assumes a Rust implementation (Cargo). Adjust it if `flak` is written in Go, Python, or another language.
- Trim the rules table and integrations to match what you've actually implemented.

runs.prompt: Write a README.md for a CLI tool called 'flak' that lints YAML files.
runs.output:
# flak

> A fast, opinionated linter for YAML files.

[![Build Status](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/your-org/flak/ci.yml?branch=main)](https://github.com/your-org/flak/actions)
[![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/your-org/flak)](https://github.com/your-org/flak/releases)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

`flak` catches syntax errors, style inconsistencies, and common mistakes in YAML files before they reach production. Use it on Kubernetes manifests, CI pipelines, Ansible playbooks, Docker Compose files, or any other YAML.

```console
$ flak config/
config/app.yaml
  3:5    error    duplicate key "port"                         no-duplicate-keys
  12:1   warning  line exceeds 120 characters (134)            line-length
  18:9   warning  truthy value "yes" should be "true"          truthy

config/db.yaml
  7:3    error    inconsistent indentation (expected 2, got 3) indentation

✖ 4 problems (2 errors, 2 warnings) in 2 files
```

---

## Table of Contents

- [Features](#features)
- [Installation](#installation)
- [Quick Start](#quick-start)
- [Usage](#usage)
- [Configuration](#configuration)
- [Rules](#rules)
- [Inline Directives](#inline-directives)
- [Output Formats](#output-formats)
- [Exit Codes](#exit-codes)
- [CI Integration](#ci-integration)
- [Editor Integration](#editor-integration)
- [Contributing](#contributing)
- [License](#license)

---

## Features

- **Fast** – lints thousands of files in seconds
- **Zero config** – sensible defaults out of the box
- **Configurable** – enable, disable, or tune every rule
- **Auto-fix** – automatically fix many style issues with `--fix`
- **Multiple output formats** – human-readable, JSON, SARIF, GitHub annotations, JUnit
- **Multi-document support** – handles `---` separated documents
- **Inline suppressions** – ignore specific lines or rules with comments
- **CI-friendly** – meaningful exit codes and machine-readable output

---

## Installation

### Homebrew (macOS / Linux)

```sh
brew install flak
```

### Prebuilt binaries

Download the latest binary for your platform from the [Releases page](https://github.com/your-org/flak/releases), then place it on your `PATH`:

```sh
curl -sSL https://github.com/your-org/flak/releases/latest/download/flak-linux-amd64 -o /usr/local/bin/flak
chmod +x /usr/local/bin/flak
```

### From source

```sh
git clone https://github.com/your-org/flak.git
cd flak
make install
```

### Docker

```sh
docker run --rm -v "$(pwd):/work" -w /work your-org/flak .
```

Verify the installation:

```sh
flak --version
```

---

## Quick Start

Lint a single file:

```sh
flak deployment.yaml
```

Lint a directory recursively:

```sh
flak .
```

Fix what can be fixed automatically:

```sh
flak --fix .
```

Generate a starter config file:

```sh
flak init
```

---

## Usage

```
flak [options] [paths...]
```

If no paths are given, `flak` lints the current directory. Files matching `*.yaml` and `*.yml` are included by default.

### Options

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `-c, --config <file>` | Path to config file (default: auto-discovered `.flak.yaml`) |
| `-f, --format <fmt>` | Output format: `pretty`, `json`, `sarif`, `github`, `junit`, `compact` |
| `--fix` | Automatically fix problems where possible |
| `--dry-run` | Show what `--fix` would change without writing files |
| `--strict` | Treat warnings as errors |
| `-q, --quiet` | Report errors only, suppress warnings |
| `--no-color` | Disable colored output |
| `--exclude <glob>` | Exclude files matching glob (repeatable) |
| `--rule <name>=<level>` | Override a rule's level from the command line (repeatable) |
| `--stdin` | Read YAML from standard input |
| `--stdin-filename <name>` | Filename to use in reports when reading from stdin |
| `--list-rules` | Print all available rules and exit |
| `-v, --version` | Print version and exit |
| `-h, --help` | Show help |

### Commands

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `flak init` | Create a `.flak.yaml` config in the current directory |
| `flak explain <rule>` | Show documentation and examples for a rule |

### Examples

```sh
# Lint only Kubernetes manifests, skipping vendored files
flak k8s/ --exclude "k8s/vendor/**"

# Fail CI on warnings too
flak --strict .

# Pipe from another command
helm template ./chart | flak --stdin --stdin-filename rendered.yaml

# Temporarily disable a rule
flak --rule line-length=off .
```

---

## Configuration

`flak` looks for a config file in the current directory and walks up parent directories until it finds one. Supported filenames:

- `.flak.yaml`
- `.flak.yml`
- `flak.config.yaml`

### Example `.flak.yaml`

```yaml
# Start from a preset: "recommended" (default), "strict", or "minimal"
extends: recommended

# Files to lint
include:
  - "**/*.yaml"
  - "**/*.yml"

# Files to skip
exclude:
  - "node_modules/**"
  - "vendor/**"
  - "**/*.generated.yaml"

rules:
  indentation:
    level: error
    spaces: 2
    indent-sequences: consistent

  line-length:
    level: warning
    max: 120
    allow-urls: true

  truthy:
    level: warning
    allowed-values: ["true", "false"]

  document-start: off

  quoted-strings:
    level: warning
    quote-type: double
    required: only-when-needed

# Per-path overrides
overrides:
  - files: [".github/workflows/*.yml"]
    rules:
      truthy: off   # GitHub Actions uses `on:` as a key
```

Each rule accepts a level of `error`, `warning`, or `off`. Rules with options use the object form shown above.

---

## Rules

Run `flak --list-rules` for the full list, or `flak explain <rule>` for details.

| Rule | Default | Fixable | Description |
|------|---------|:-------:|-------------|
| `syntax` | error | | Reports invalid YAML (always enabled) |
| `no-duplicate-keys` | error | | Disallows duplicate keys in a mapping |
| `indentation` | error | ✅ | Enforces consistent indentation |
| `no-tabs` | error | ✅ | Disallows tab characters for indentation |
| `trailing-spaces` | warning | ✅ | Disallows trailing whitespace |
| `line-length` | warning | | Limits line length |
| `truthy` | warning | ✅ | Restricts ambiguous booleans like `yes`, `on`, `off` |
| `new-line-at-end-of-file` | warning | ✅ | Requires a final newline |
| `empty-lines` | warning | ✅ | Limits consecutive blank lines |
| `colons` | warning | ✅ | Enforces spacing around colons |
| `commas` | warning | ✅ | Enforces spacing around commas in flow collections |
| `brackets` | warning | ✅ | Enforces spacing inside `[ ]` |
| `braces` | warning | ✅ | Enforces spacing inside `{ }` |
| `comments` | warning | ✅ | Requires a space after `#` |
| `document-start` | off | ✅ | Requires or forbids `---` at document start |
| `key-ordering` | off | | Requires keys to be sorted alphabetically |
| `quoted-strings` | off | ✅ | Enforces a quoting style for strings |
| `octal-values` | warning | | Flags implicit octal values like `0755` |
| `anchors` | warning | | Reports undefined aliases and unused anchors |
| `float-values` | off | | Restricts float formats like `.5` or `1e3` |

---

## Inline Directives

Suppress rules directly in your YAML using comments:

```yaml
# Disable a rule for the next line
# flak-disable-next-line line-length
description: "This is a very long line that would normally trigger the line-length rule but we need it"

# Disable a rule on the same line
enabled: yes  # flak-disable-line truthy

# Disable rules for a block
# flak-disable no-duplicate-keys, key-ordering
legacy:
  a: 1
  a: 2
# flak-enable

# Disable all rules for the entire file (must be the first comment)
# flak-disable-file
```

---

## Output Formats

| Format | Use case |
|--------|----------|
| `pretty` | Default; grouped, colored, human-readable |
| `compact` | One problem per line: `file:line:col: level: message (rule)` |
| `json` | Machine-readable output for scripts and tooling |
| `sarif` | GitHub Code Scanning and other SARIF consumers |
| `github` | Inline annotations in GitHub Actions |
| `junit` | CI systems that consume JUnit XML (Jenkins, GitLab) |

Example JSON output:

```json
[
  {
    "file": "config/app.yaml",
    "line": 3,
    "column": 5,
    "level": "error",
    "rule": "no-duplicate-keys",
    "message": "duplicate key \"port\"",
    "fixable": false
  }
]
```

---

## Exit Codes

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `0` | No errors found (warnings may be present unless `--strict`) |
| `1` | Lint errors found |
| `2` | Invalid usage, bad config, or internal error |

---

## CI Integration

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
name: Lint YAML
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  flak:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install flak
        run: |
          curl -sSL https://github.com/your-org/flak/releases/latest/download/flak-linux-amd64 -o flak
          chmod +x flak
      - name: Run flak
        run: ./flak --format github .
```

### GitLab CI

```yaml
lint-yaml:
  image: your-org/flak:latest
  script:
    - flak --format junit . > flak-report.xml
  artifacts:
    reports:
      junit: flak-report.xml
```

### pre-commit

Add to `.pre-commit-config.yaml`:

```yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/your-org/flak
    rev: v1.0.0
    hooks:
      - id: flak
```

---

## Editor Integration

- **VS Code** – install the `flak` extension from the Marketplace
- **Neovim** – supported via [nvim-lint](https://github.com/mfussenegger/nvim-lint) or `null-ls`/`none-ls` using `--format json`
- **Any editor** – use `--stdin --format compact` for easy integration with generic linting plugins

---

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome! To get started:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/your-org/flak.git
cd flak
make test
```

1. Fork the repository and create a feature branch
2. Add tests for your change
3. Run `make lint test` to make sure everything passes
4. Open a pull request with a clear description

To propose a new rule, please open an issue first describing the problem it solves, with examples of YAML that should pass and fail.

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for more details.

---

## License

runs.output:
# 🐾 paw

**Tiny, accessible React UI primitives.**

`paw` is a small React component library with 12 unstyled-by-default (but nicely styled when you want them) UI primitives. Each one does one job, ships with sensible accessibility defaults, and stays out of your way.

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/paw.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/paw)
[![bundle size](https://img.shields.io/bundlephobia/minzip/paw)](https://bundlephobia.com/package/paw)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/paw.svg)](./LICENSE)

---

## ✨ Features

- **12 focused primitives.** No sprawling API surface.
- **Accessible by default.** WAI-ARIA patterns, keyboard support and visible focus states.
- **Tiny.** About 6 kB min+gzip for the whole library, and tree-shakeable per component.
- **Themeable.** Built on CSS custom properties, with no CSS-in-JS runtime.
- **TypeScript-first.** Fully typed props, with every component forwarding refs.
- **SSR-friendly.** Works with Next.js, Remix and Vite out of the box.

---

## 📦 Installation

```bash
npm install paw
# or
pnpm add paw
# or
yarn add paw
```

**Peer dependencies:** `react >= 18` and `react-dom >= 18`.

Import the base styles once at the root of your app:

```tsx
import "paw/styles.css";
```

> Prefer to bring your own styles? Skip the import. Every component renders semantic markup with predictable `paw-*` class names and `data-*` state attributes.

---

## 🚀 Quick Start

```tsx
import { Button, Input, Switch } from "paw";
import "paw/styles.css";

export default function App() {
  const [enabled, setEnabled] = React.useState(false);

  return (
    <form>
      <Input label="Email" type="email" placeholder="you@example.com" />
      <Switch checked={enabled} onCheckedChange={setEnabled} label="Notifications" />
      <Button variant="solid" type="submit">Sign up</Button>
    </form>
  );
}
```

---

## 🧩 Components

| Component | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`Button`](#button) | Clickable action with variants and sizes |
| [`IconButton`](#iconbutton) | Square button for a single icon, with a required accessible label |
| [`Input`](#input) | Text input with label, hint and error support |
| [`Textarea`](#textarea) | Multi-line text input with optional auto-resize |
| [`Checkbox`](#checkbox) | Binary or indeterminate checkbox |
| [`Radio`](#radio) | Radio group with arrow-key navigation |
| [`Switch`](#switch) | On/off toggle |
| [`Select`](#select) | Lightweight native-backed select |
| [`Badge`](#badge) | Small status or count label |
| [`Avatar`](#avatar) | User image with initials fallback |
| [`Tooltip`](#tooltip) | Hover and focus hint |
| [`Spinner`](#spinner) | Loading indicator |

---

### Button

```tsx
<Button>Default</Button>
<Button variant="solid" size="lg">Save</Button>
<Button variant="ghost" loading>Saving…</Button>
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `"solid" \| "outline" \| "ghost"` | `"outline"` |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` |

When `loading` is set, the button gets `aria-busy` and shows a `Spinner`.

### IconButton

```tsx
<IconButton label="Close dialog" icon={<XIcon />} />
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` (required) | — |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` | — |
| `variant` / `size` | Same as `Button` | — |

### Input

```tsx
<Input label="Username" hint="3–16 characters" />
<Input label="Email" error="That doesn't look like an email" />
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | — |
| `hint` | `string` | — |
| `error` | `string` | — |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` |

Hints and errors are wired up automatically via `aria-describedby`. Setting `error` also adds `aria-invalid`.

### Textarea

```tsx
<Textarea label="Bio" autoResize maxRows={8} />
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `autoResize` | `boolean` | `false` |
| `minRows` / `maxRows` | `number` | `3` / `—` |
| `label`, `hint`, `error` | Same as `Input` | — |

### Checkbox

```tsx
<Checkbox label="Accept terms" />
<Checkbox checked="indeterminate" label="Select all" />
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `checked` | `boolean \| "indeterminate"` | — |
| `defaultChecked` | `boolean` | `false` |
| `onCheckedChange` | `(checked: boolean) => void` | — |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | — |

### Radio

```tsx
<Radio.Group label="Plan" value={plan} onValueChange={setPlan}>
  <Radio value="free" label="Free" />
  <Radio value="pro" label="Pro" />
</Radio.Group>
```

| Prop (`Radio.Group`) | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value` / `defaultValue` | `string` | — |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | — |
| `orientation` | `"vertical" \| "horizontal"` | `"vertical"` |

### Switch

```tsx
<Switch label="Dark mode" checked={dark} onCheckedChange={setDark} />
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `checked` / `defaultChecked` | `boolean` | — |
| `onCheckedChange` | `(checked: boolean) => void` | — |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md"` | `"md"` |

Renders with `role="switch"` and `aria-checked`.

### Select

```tsx
<Select label="Country" placeholder="Choose one">
  <option value="ca">Canada</option>
  <option value="jp">Japan</option>
</Select>
```

`Select` wraps a native `<select>` for full mobile and screen reader support. It accepts all native props plus `label`, `hint`, `error` and `size`.

### Badge

```tsx
<Badge>New</Badge>
<Badge tone="success">Paid</Badge>
<Badge tone="danger" variant="solid">3</Badge>
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tone` | `"neutral" \| "info" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "danger"` | `"neutral"` |
| `variant` | `"soft" \| "solid" \| "outline"` | `"soft"` |

### Avatar

```tsx
<Avatar src="/me.jpg" name="Ada Lovelace" />
<Avatar name="Grace Hopper" size="lg" />  {/* Falls back to "GH" */}
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | `string` | — |
| `name` | `string` | — |
| `size` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` |
| `shape` | `"circle" \| "square"` | `"circle"` |

### Tooltip

```tsx
<Tooltip content="Copy to clipboard" side="top">
  <IconButton label="Copy" icon={<CopyIcon />} />
</Tooltip>
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `content` | `ReactNode` | — |
| `side` | `"top" \| "right" \| "bottom" \| "left"` | `"top"` |
| `delay` | `number` (ms) | `300` |

The tooltip opens on hover and focus, and closes on `Escape`.

### Spinner

```tsx
<Spinner />
<Spinner size="lg" label="Loading results" />
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` |
| `label` | `string` | `"Loading"` |

The spinner respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.

---

## 🎨 Theming

All visual tokens are CSS custom properties. Override them globally or within any scope:

```css
:root {
  --paw-color-accent: #7c3aed;
  --paw-color-accent-contrast: #ffffff;
  --paw-radius: 8px;
  --paw-font: "Inter", system-ui, sans-serif;
}

[data-theme="dark"] {
  --paw-color-bg: #0b0b0f;
  --paw-color-fg: #f4f4f5;
  --paw-color-border: #27272a;
}
```

See [`src/styles/tokens.css`](./src/styles/tokens.css) for the full list.

### Styling with Tailwind or your own CSS

Every component accepts `className` and exposes state through data attributes:

```tsx
<Switch className="data-[state=checked]:bg-emerald-500" />
```

---

## ♿ Accessibility

- All interactive components are fully keyboard operable.
- Labels, hints and errors are associated automatically.
- Focus rings use `:focus-visible`.
- Components are tested with axe-core, VoiceOver and NVDA.

Found an accessibility issue? Please [open an issue](../../issues). We treat these as bugs.

---

## 🌲 Tree-shaking

Import from the root and your bundler will drop unused components:

```tsx
import { Button } from "paw";
```

Deep imports are also available:

```tsx
import { Button } from "paw/button";
```

---

## 🛠 Development

```bash
git clone https://github.com/your-org/paw.git
cd paw
pnpm install

pnpm dev        # Storybook at http://localhost:6006
pnpm test       # Vitest + Testing Library
pnpm lint       # ESLint + Prettier
pnpm build      # Build ESM + CJS + types
```

### Project structure

```
paw/
├── src/
│   ├── components/
│   │   ├── button/
│   │   ├── checkbox/
│   │   └── ...
│   ├── styles/
│   │   └── tokens.css
│   └── index.ts
├── stories/
└── tests/
```

---

## 🤝 Contributing

Contributions are welcome! Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening a PR.

`paw` intentionally stays small. Before proposing a new component, please open a discussion so we can decide whether it fits.

---
