# 🐾 paw

**Small, accessible UI primitives for React.**

paw is a library of 12 unstyled-by-default, fully typed React components. Each one does a single job, ships with sensible accessibility behavior, and can be themed with CSS variables. You can use paw's default styles or replace them completely.

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/paw.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/paw)
[![bundle size](https://img.shields.io/bundlephobia/minzip/paw)](https://bundlephobia.com/package/paw)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/paw.svg)](./LICENSE)

---

## Features

- **Tiny.** The full library is about 9 kB gzipped, and it's tree-shakeable so you only ship what you import.
- **Accessible.** Components include WAI-ARIA roles, keyboard navigation and focus management.
- **Typed.** paw is written in TypeScript and exports all prop types.
- **Themeable.** Styling uses CSS custom properties, so paw has no CSS-in-JS runtime.
- **Composable.** Every component forwards refs, spreads native props and supports `asChild`.
- **SSR-safe.** paw works with Next.js, Remix and other server-rendering frameworks.

---

## Installation

```bash
npm install paw
# or
pnpm add paw
# or
yarn add paw
```

paw requires **React 18+** as a peer dependency.

To use the default theme, import the stylesheet once at your app root:

```tsx
import "paw/styles.css";
```

---

## Quick Start

```tsx
import { Button, Input, Stack, Toggle } from "paw";
import "paw/styles.css";

export function SignupForm() {
  const [newsletter, setNewsletter] = React.useState(true);

  return (
    <Stack gap="md">
      <Input label="Email" type="email" placeholder="you@example.com" />
      <Toggle
        checked={newsletter}
        onCheckedChange={setNewsletter}
        label="Subscribe to newsletter"
      />
      <Button variant="primary" type="submit">
        Sign up
      </Button>
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

---

## Components

| Component | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`Button`](#button) | Clickable action with variants and sizes |
| [`Input`](#input) | Text field with label, hint and error states |
| [`Checkbox`](#checkbox) | Binary or indeterminate selection |
| [`Toggle`](#toggle) | On/off switch |
| [`Radio`](#radio) | Single choice within a `RadioGroup` |
| [`Badge`](#badge) | Small status or count label |
| [`Avatar`](#avatar) | User image with initials fallback |
| [`Tooltip`](#tooltip) | Hover/focus hint for an element |
| [`Spinner`](#spinner) | Loading indicator |
| [`Divider`](#divider) | Horizontal or vertical separator |
| [`Stack`](#stack) | Flexbox layout helper |
| [`VisuallyHidden`](#visuallyhidden) | Content for screen readers only |

---

### Button

```tsx
<Button variant="primary" size="md" onClick={save}>Save</Button>
<Button variant="ghost" loading>Saving…</Button>
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `"primary" \| "secondary" \| "ghost" \| "danger"` | `"secondary"` |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` |
| `asChild` | `boolean` | `false` |

When `loading` is true, the button is disabled and shows a `Spinner`. It also sets `aria-busy`.

---

### Input

```tsx
<Input label="Username" hint="3–16 characters" error={errors.username} />
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | — |
| `hint` | `string` | — |
| `error` | `string` | — |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` |

paw links the label, hint and error to the input automatically using `aria-describedby`.

---

### Checkbox

```tsx
<Checkbox label="Accept terms" checked={accepted} onCheckedChange={setAccepted} />
<Checkbox label="Select all" checked="indeterminate" />
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `checked` | `boolean \| "indeterminate"` | — |
| `defaultChecked` | `boolean` | `false` |
| `onCheckedChange` | `(checked: boolean) => void` | — |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | — |

---

### Toggle

```tsx
<Toggle label="Dark mode" checked={dark} onCheckedChange={setDark} />
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `checked` | `boolean` | — |
| `defaultChecked` | `boolean` | `false` |
| `onCheckedChange` | `(checked: boolean) => void` | — |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | — |

Toggle renders with `role="switch"`. Users can switch it with Space or Enter.

---

### Radio

```tsx
<RadioGroup name="plan" value={plan} onValueChange={setPlan}>
  <Radio value="free" label="Free" />
  <Radio value="pro" label="Pro" />
</RadioGroup>
```

| Prop (`RadioGroup`) | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string` | — |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | — |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | — |
| `orientation` | `"vertical" \| "horizontal"` | `"vertical"` |

Users move between options with the arrow keys, following the roving tabindex pattern.

---

### Badge

```tsx
<Badge tone="success">Active</Badge>
<Badge tone="neutral" size="sm">12</Badge>
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tone` | `"neutral" \| "info" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "danger"` | `"neutral"` |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md"` | `"md"` |

---

### Avatar

```tsx
<Avatar src="/me.jpg" name="Ada Lovelace" size="lg" />
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | `string` | — |
| `name` | `string` | — |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` |
| `shape` | `"circle" \| "square"` | `"circle"` |

If the image is missing or fails to load, Avatar shows initials taken from `name` instead.

---

### Tooltip

```tsx
<Tooltip content="Copy to clipboard" side="top">
  <Button variant="ghost" aria-label="Copy">📋</Button>
</Tooltip>
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `content` | `ReactNode` | — |
| `side` | `"top" \| "right" \| "bottom" \| "left"` | `"top"` |
| `delay` | `number` (ms) | `300` |

Tooltip appears on hover and on focus, and it closes when the user presses Escape.

---

### Spinner

```tsx
<Spinner size="sm" label="Loading results" />
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` |
| `label` | `string` | `"Loading"` |

The animation respects the `prefers-reduced-motion` setting.

---

### Divider

```tsx
<Divider />
<Divider orientation="vertical" />
<Divider label="or" />
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `"horizontal"` |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | — |

---

### Stack

```tsx
<Stack direction="row" gap="sm" align="center" justify="between">
  <Avatar name="Ada" />
  <Badge>Admin</Badge>
</Stack>
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `direction` | `"row" \| "column"` | `"column"` |
| `gap` | `"none" \| "xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl"` | `"md"` |
| `align` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end" \| "stretch"` | `"stretch"` |
| `justify` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end" \| "between"` | `"start"` |
| `wrap` | `boolean` | `false` |

---

### VisuallyHidden

```tsx
<Button>
  <SearchIcon />
  <VisuallyHidden>Search</VisuallyHidden>
</Button>
```

VisuallyHidden hides content on screen while keeping it available to assistive technology.

---

## Theming

The default theme is built on CSS custom properties. To customize it, override any variable globally or within a specific scope:

```css
:root {
  --paw-color-primary: #6d28d9;
  --paw-color-primary-contrast: #ffffff;
  --paw-radius: 8px;
  --paw-font-family: "Inter", system-ui, sans-serif;
}

[data-theme="dark"] {
  --paw-color-bg: #0f0f12;
  --paw-color-fg: #f4f4f5;
}
```

See [`src/styles/tokens.css`](./src/styles/tokens.css) for the full list of tokens.

### Going unstyled

If you'd rather write all the styles yourself, skip `paw/styles.css`. Every component exposes stable `data-*` attributes you can target:

```css
[data-paw="button"][data-variant="primary"] { /* … */ }
[data-paw="toggle"][data-state="checked"] { /* … */ }
```

You can also use `className` and `style` as you normally would. paw works with Tailwind, CSS Modules, vanilla-extract and other styling approaches.

---

## Composition with `asChild`

Interactive components accept `asChild`. When it's set, paw merges its props and behavior onto your own element instead of rendering a default one:

```tsx
import Link from "next/link";

<Button asChild variant="primary">
  <Link href="/dashboard">Go to dashboard</Link>
</Button>
```

---

## TypeScript

All prop types are exported:

```ts
import type { ButtonProps, BadgeProps, StackProps } from "paw";
```

---

## Browser Support

paw supports the latest two versions of Chrome, Firefox, Safari and Edge.

---

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome. To get started:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/your-org/paw.git
cd paw
pnpm install
pnpm dev        # Storybook at localhost:6006
pnpm test       # Vitest + Testing Library
pnpm lint
```

Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening a PR. If you want to propose a new primitive, open an issue first. paw tries to stay small, so new components need a strong case.

---

## License

[MIT](./LICENSE) © paw contributors

# 🐾 paw

**Small, sharp UI primitives for React.**

paw is a lightweight React component library with 12 accessible, unstyled-by-default UI primitives. Each one does one job, has a small API, and stays out of your way.

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/paw.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/paw)
[![bundle size](https://img.shields.io/bundlephobia/minzip/paw)](https://bundlephobia.com/package/paw)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/paw.svg)](./LICENSE)

---

## Features

- **Tiny.** About 9 kB min+gzip for the whole library, and every component is tree-shakeable.
- **Accessible.** Components follow WAI-ARIA patterns and support full keyboard navigation.
- **Themeable.** Styling is driven by CSS variables. No CSS-in-JS runtime.
- **Typed.** Written in TypeScript with complete type definitions.
- **SSR-safe.** Works with Next.js, Remix, Astro, and Vite.
- **Zero dependencies.** React is the only peer dependency.

---

## Installation

```bash
npm install paw
# or
pnpm add paw
# or
yarn add paw
```

paw requires **React 18 or later**.

---

## Quick Start

```tsx
import { Button, Toggle, Tooltip } from 'paw';
import 'paw/styles.css'; // optional default theme

export function App() {
  return (
    <Tooltip content="Save your changes">
      <Button variant="solid" onClick={() => console.log('saved')}>
        Save
      </Button>
    </Tooltip>
  );
}
```

If you prefer to write your own styles, skip the stylesheet import. Every component renders sensible semantic HTML with `data-paw-*` attributes you can target.

---

## The 12 Primitives

| Component | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`Button`](#button) | Clickable action with variants and loading state |
| [`Toggle`](#toggle) | On/off switch |
| [`Checkbox`](#checkbox) | Checkbox with an indeterminate state |
| [`Radio`](#radio) | Radio group with arrow-key navigation |
| [`Input`](#input) | Text input with prefix and suffix slots |
| [`Badge`](#badge) | Small status label |
| [`Avatar`](#avatar) | Image with a fallback to initials |
| [`Tooltip`](#tooltip) | Hover or focus hint |
| [`Spinner`](#spinner) | Loading indicator |
| [`Divider`](#divider) | Horizontal or vertical separator |
| [`Kbd`](#kbd) | Keyboard shortcut display |
| [`VisuallyHidden`](#visuallyhidden) | Content hidden visually but available to screen readers |

---

### Button

```tsx
<Button variant="solid" size="md" loading={isSaving}>
  Save
</Button>
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `'solid' \| 'outline' \| 'ghost'` | `'solid'` |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` |

All native `<button>` attributes are also supported.

### Toggle

```tsx
const [on, setOn] = useState(false);

<Toggle checked={on} onCheckedChange={setOn} label="Dark mode" />
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `checked` | `boolean` | — |
| `defaultChecked` | `boolean` | `false` |
| `onCheckedChange` | `(checked: boolean) => void` | — |
| `label` | `string` | — |

The component renders with `role="switch"` and toggles with <kbd>Space</kbd>.

### Checkbox

```tsx
<Checkbox checked="indeterminate" onCheckedChange={setValue}>
  Select all
</Checkbox>
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `checked` | `boolean \| 'indeterminate'` | — |
| `onCheckedChange` | `(checked: boolean) => void` | — |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` |

### Radio

```tsx
<Radio.Group value={plan} onValueChange={setPlan} name="plan">
  <Radio value="free">Free</Radio>
  <Radio value="pro">Pro</Radio>
  <Radio value="team">Team</Radio>
</Radio.Group>
```

Arrow keys move the selection within the group, and the group uses a roving `tabindex`.

### Input

```tsx
<Input
  placeholder="Search…"
  prefix={<SearchIcon />}
  suffix={<Kbd>/</Kbd>}
  invalid={!!error}
/>
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prefix` | `ReactNode` | — |
| `suffix` | `ReactNode` | — |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` |

Setting `invalid` adds `aria-invalid` to the input.

### Badge

```tsx
<Badge tone="success">Active</Badge>
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tone` | `'neutral' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger' \| 'info'` | `'neutral'` |
| `variant` | `'soft' \| 'solid' \| 'outline'` | `'soft'` |

### Avatar

```tsx
<Avatar src="/me.jpg" name="Ada Lovelace" size="lg" />
```

If the image fails to load, the avatar shows the person's initials (`AL`).

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | `string` | — |
| `name` | `string` | — |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` |

### Tooltip

```tsx
<Tooltip content="Copy to clipboard" side="top" delay={300}>
  <Button variant="ghost">📋</Button>
</Tooltip>
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `content` | `ReactNode` | — |
| `side` | `'top' \| 'right' \| 'bottom' \| 'left'` | `'top'` |
| `delay` | `number` (ms) | `200` |

The tooltip opens on hover and focus, closes on <kbd>Esc</kbd>, and is linked to its trigger with `aria-describedby`.

### Spinner

```tsx
<Spinner size="sm" label="Loading results" />
```

The spinner renders with `role="status"`. The `label` is read by screen readers but not shown on screen.

### Divider

```tsx
<Divider />
<Divider orientation="vertical" />
<Divider label="or" />
```

### Kbd

```tsx
Press <Kbd>⌘</Kbd> + <Kbd>K</Kbd> to open search
```

### VisuallyHidden

```tsx
<button>
  <TrashIcon />
  <VisuallyHidden>Delete item</VisuallyHidden>
</button>
```

---

## Theming

paw's default theme is built on CSS custom properties. Override them globally or within any scope:

```css
:root {
  --paw-color-accent: #7c3aed;
  --paw-color-accent-contrast: #ffffff;
  --paw-color-border: #e5e7eb;
  --paw-color-text: #111827;
  --paw-radius: 8px;
  --paw-font: 'Inter', system-ui, sans-serif;
  --paw-focus-ring: 0 0 0 3px rgb(124 58 237 / 0.4);
}

[data-theme='dark'] {
  --paw-color-border: #374151;
  --paw-color-text: #f9fafb;
}
```

### Styling with Tailwind or plain CSS

Every component accepts `className` and exposes state through data attributes:

```css
[data-paw-button][data-variant='solid']:hover { filter: brightness(1.1); }
[data-paw-toggle][data-state='checked'] { background: var(--paw-color-accent); }
```

```tsx
<Button className="rounded-full px-6">Pill button</Button>
```

---

## Tree-shaking

Use named imports and your bundler will drop anything you don't use:

```tsx
import { Button } from 'paw';
```

You can also use per-component entry points:

```tsx
import { Button } from 'paw/button';
```

---

## Accessibility

Accessibility is a requirement for every paw component, not an add-on:

- Native elements are used wherever possible.
- Focus is always visible through `:focus-visible`.
- Each component is tested with axe, plus manual testing in VoiceOver and NVDA.
- All animations respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.

If you find an accessibility issue, please [open an issue](https://github.com/your-org/paw/issues). We treat these as bugs.

---

## Browser Support

paw supports the latest two versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and Safari.

---

## Contributing

```bash
git clone https://github.com/your-org/paw.git
cd paw
pnpm install
pnpm dev        # start the playground
pnpm test       # run unit and a11y tests
pnpm build      # build the library
```

Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening a pull request. paw deliberately stays small, so new primitives are proposed through an RFC issue before any code is written.

---

## License

MIT © paw contributors

# 🐾 paw

**Tiny, accessible React UI primitives.**

`paw` is a library of 12 small, unstyled-by-default UI primitives for React. Each one does one job, ships with sensible defaults, and stays out of your way when you want to customize it.

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/paw.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/paw)
[![bundle size](https://img.shields.io/bundlephobia/minzip/paw)](https://bundlephobia.com/package/paw)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/paw.svg)](./LICENSE)

---

## Features

- **Small.** About 6 kB min+gzip for the whole library. It is fully tree-shakeable, so you only ship what you import.
- **Accessible.** Components follow the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices and support keyboard navigation and screen readers.
- **Themeable.** Styling is driven by CSS variables. You can override a single token or replace the whole theme.
- **Typed.** Written in TypeScript with complete prop types.
- **Zero runtime dependencies.** The only peer dependency is React.
- **SSR-friendly.** Works with Next.js, Remix, Astro and other server-rendering frameworks.

---

## Installation

```bash
npm install paw
# or
yarn add paw
# or
pnpm add paw
```

**Requirements:** React 18 or later.

Import the base stylesheet once, at the root of your app:

```tsx
import "paw/styles.css";
```

---

## Quick start

```tsx
import { Button, Input, Switch } from "paw";
import "paw/styles.css";

export function App() {
  const [notify, setNotify] = React.useState(true);

  return (
    <form>
      <Input label="Email" type="email" placeholder="you@example.com" />
      <Switch
        label="Email notifications"
        checked={notify}
        onCheckedChange={setNotify}
      />
      <Button type="submit" variant="primary">
        Save
      </Button>
    </form>
  );
}
```

---

## Components

| Component | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`Button`](#button) | Clickable action with variants and sizes |
| [`Input`](#input) | Single-line text field with label and error support |
| [`Textarea`](#textarea) | Multi-line text field with optional auto-resize |
| [`Checkbox`](#checkbox) | Binary or indeterminate selection |
| [`Radio`](#radio) | Single choice within a `RadioGroup` |
| [`Switch`](#switch) | On/off toggle |
| [`Select`](#select) | Native-backed dropdown |
| [`Badge`](#badge) | Small status or count label |
| [`Avatar`](#avatar) | User image with initials fallback |
| [`Tooltip`](#tooltip) | Hover and focus hint |
| [`Spinner`](#spinner) | Loading indicator |
| [`Divider`](#divider) | Horizontal or vertical separator |

---

### Button

```tsx
<Button variant="primary" size="md" onClick={save}>
  Save
</Button>
<Button variant="ghost" loading>Saving…</Button>
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `"primary" \| "secondary" \| "ghost" \| "danger"` | `"secondary"` |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` |
| `asChild` | `boolean` (renders its child element instead of a `<button>`) | `false` |

---

### Input

```tsx
<Input
  label="Username"
  hint="Lowercase letters only"
  error={errors.username}
/>
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | — |
| `hint` | `string` | — |
| `error` | `string` | — |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` |

All native `<input>` props are also supported.

---

### Textarea

```tsx
<Textarea label="Bio" autoResize maxRows={8} />
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | — |
| `autoResize` | `boolean` | `false` |
| `minRows` / `maxRows` | `number` | `3` / `—` |
| `error` | `string` | — |

---

### Checkbox

```tsx
<Checkbox
  label="Accept terms"
  checked={accepted}
  onCheckedChange={setAccepted}
/>
<Checkbox label="Select all" checked="indeterminate" />
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `checked` | `boolean \| "indeterminate"` | — |
| `defaultChecked` | `boolean` | `false` |
| `onCheckedChange` | `(checked: boolean) => void` | — |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | — |

---

### Radio

```tsx
<RadioGroup value={plan} onValueChange={setPlan} label="Plan">
  <Radio value="free" label="Free" />
  <Radio value="pro" label="Pro" />
</RadioGroup>
```

| Prop (`RadioGroup`) | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value` / `defaultValue` | `string` | — |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | — |
| `orientation` | `"vertical" \| "horizontal"` | `"vertical"` |

Use the arrow keys to move between options.

---

### Switch

```tsx
<Switch label="Dark mode" checked={dark} onCheckedChange={setDark} />
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `checked` / `defaultChecked` | `boolean` | — |
| `onCheckedChange` | `(checked: boolean) => void` | — |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md"` | `"md"` |

---

### Select

```tsx
<Select label="Country" value={country} onValueChange={setCountry}>
  <option value="ca">Canada</option>
  <option value="jp">Japan</option>
</Select>
```

`Select` wraps a native `<select>`, so it works well on mobile and with assistive technology.

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | — |
| `placeholder` | `string` | — |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | — |
| `error` | `string` | — |

---

### Badge

```tsx
<Badge tone="success">Active</Badge>
<Badge tone="danger" variant="solid">3</Badge>
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tone` | `"neutral" \| "info" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "danger"` | `"neutral"` |
| `variant` | `"soft" \| "solid" \| "outline"` | `"soft"` |

---

### Avatar

```tsx
<Avatar src="/me.jpg" name="Ada Lovelace" size="lg" />
<Avatar name="Grace Hopper" /> {/* Renders "GH" */}
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | `string` | — |
| `name` | `string` (used for alt text and initials) | — |
| `size` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl"` | `"md"` |
| `shape` | `"circle" \| "square"` | `"circle"` |

---

### Tooltip

```tsx
<Tooltip content="Copy to clipboard" side="top">
  <Button aria-label="Copy">📋</Button>
</Tooltip>
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `content` | `ReactNode` | — |
| `side` | `"top" \| "right" \| "bottom" \| "left"` | `"top"` |
| `delay` | `number` (ms) | `300` |

The tooltip opens on hover and on focus, and closes on `Escape`.

---

### Spinner

```tsx
<Spinner size="sm" label="Loading results" />
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` |
| `label` | `string` (screen-reader text) | `"Loading"` |

The animation respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.

---

### Divider

```tsx
<Divider />

---

## Theming

All visual styles are controlled by CSS variables prefixed with `--paw-`. You can override them globally or within a scope:

```css
:root {

  --paw-color-primary-contrast: #ffffff;
  --paw-radius: 8px;
  --paw-font-family: "Inter", system-ui, sans-serif;
}

.compact {

}
```

`paw` reads the `data-theme` attribute on any ancestor element:

```html

To skip the default stylesheet entirely, don't import `paw/styles.css`. Every component exposes stable `data-*` attributes and a `className` prop you can target:

```css
[data-paw="button"][data-variant="primary"] { /* ... */ }

```

This also works with Tailwind:

```tsx

```

---

## Accessibility

Every component is tested with:

- Keyboard-only navigation
- VoiceOver (macOS and iOS) and NVDA (Windows)
- Automated checks using `axe-core`

Labels are associated with their controls automatically. Error messages are linked through `aria-describedby`.

---

## Refs and composition

All components forward refs to their underlying DOM element:

```tsx
const inputRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null);
<Input ref={inputRef} label="Search" />;

`Button` supports `asChild`, which lets it render a router link or another custom element:

```tsx
<Button asChild variant="primary">
  <Link to="/signup">Sign up</Link>

```

---

## Browser support

`paw` supports the last two versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and Safari. Internet Explorer is not supported.

---

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome. To get started:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/your-org/paw.git
cd paw
pnpm install
pnpm dev        # Start Storybook
pnpm test       # Run unit and a11y tests
pnpm build      # Build the library
```

Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening a PR. New components should stay small; if a component needs more than one job, it probably belongs in a separate package.

```markdown
# 🐾 paw

**Tiny, accessible UI primitives for React.**

paw is a lightweight component library of 12 small building blocks. Each one is unstyled by default, accessible out of the box, and easy to compose into your own design system.

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/paw.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/paw)
[![bundle size](https://img.shields.io/bundlephobia/minzip/paw)](https://bundlephobia.com/package/paw)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/paw.svg)](./LICENSE)

---

## Features

- **Small**: about 6 kB minified and gzipped for the whole library. It is tree-shakeable, so you only ship what you import.
- **Accessible**: follows WAI-ARIA patterns, with keyboard navigation and focus management built in.
- **Unstyled or styled**: use the optional default theme, or bring your own CSS, Tailwind, or CSS-in-JS.
- **TypeScript-first**: full type definitions, with props that extend native HTML element props.
- **Composable**: every component forwards refs and accepts `className`, `style`, and an `as` prop where it makes sense.
- **Zero dependencies**: only `react` and `react-dom` as peer dependencies.

---

## Installation

```bash
npm install paw
# or
yarn add paw
# or
pnpm add paw
```

paw requires **React 18 or later**.

---

## Quick Start

```tsx
import { Button, Badge, Tooltip } from 'paw';
import 'paw/styles.css'; // optional default theme

export default function App() {
  return (
    <Tooltip content="You have new messages">
      <Button variant="primary">
        Inbox <Badge>3</Badge>
      </Button>
    </Tooltip>
  );
}
```

---

## Components

| Component | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| [`Button`](#button) | Clickable action with variants and sizes |
| [`Input`](#input) | Text field with label and error support |
| [`Checkbox`](#checkbox) | Binary or indeterminate selection |
| [`Switch`](#switch) | On/off toggle |
| [`Radio`](#radio) | Single choice within a group |
| [`Badge`](#badge) | Small status or count indicator |
| [`Avatar`](#avatar) | User image with fallback initials |
| [`Tooltip`](#tooltip) | Contextual hint on hover or focus |
| [`Spinner`](#spinner) | Loading indicator |
| [`Divider`](#divider) | Horizontal or vertical separator |
| [`Tag`](#tag) | Removable label or chip |
| [`VisuallyHidden`](#visuallyhidden) | Content for screen readers only |

---

### Button

```tsx
import { Button } from 'paw';

<Button variant="primary" size="md" onClick={save}>
  Save
</Button>

<Button variant="ghost" loading>
  Submitting…
</Button>
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `variant` | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'ghost' \| 'danger'` | `'secondary'` | Visual style |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | Button size |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | Shows a spinner and disables interaction |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables the button |
| `as` | `ElementType` | `'button'` | Render as another element, such as `a` |

---

### Input

```tsx
import { Input } from 'paw';

<Input
  label="Email"
  type="email"
  placeholder="you@example.com"
  error={errors.email}
/>
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `label` | `string` | — | Accessible label, rendered visibly |
| `hint` | `string` | — | Helper text below the field |
| `error` | `string` | — | Error message; sets `aria-invalid` |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | Field size |

All native `<input>` props are supported.

---

### Checkbox

```tsx
import { Checkbox } from 'paw';

<Checkbox checked={agreed} onChange={setAgreed}>
  I agree to the terms
</Checkbox>

<Checkbox indeterminate>Select all</Checkbox>
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `checked` | `boolean` | — | Controlled state |
| `defaultChecked` | `boolean` | `false` | Uncontrolled initial state |
| `indeterminate` | `boolean` | `false` | Shows a mixed state |
| `onChange` | `(checked: boolean) => void` | — | Change handler |

---

### Switch

```tsx
import { Switch } from 'paw';

<Switch checked={darkMode} onChange={setDarkMode}>
  Dark mode
</Switch>
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `checked` | `boolean` | — | Controlled state |
| `defaultChecked` | `boolean` | `false` | Uncontrolled initial state |
| `onChange` | `(checked: boolean) => void` | — | Change handler |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md'` | `'md'` | Switch size |

Renders with `role="switch"` and `aria-checked`.

---

### Radio

```tsx
import { Radio } from 'paw';

<Radio.Group name="plan" value={plan} onChange={setPlan}>
  <Radio value="free">Free</Radio>
  <Radio value="pro">Pro</Radio>
  <Radio value="team" disabled>Team</Radio>
</Radio.Group>
```

| Prop (`Radio.Group`) | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `name` | `string` | — | Shared input name |
| `value` | `string` | — | Controlled selected value |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | — | Uncontrolled initial value |
| `onChange` | `(value: string) => void` | — | Change handler |
| `orientation` | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` | `'vertical'` | Layout and arrow-key direction |

---

### Badge

```tsx
import { Badge } from 'paw';

<Badge>New</Badge>
<Badge tone="success">Active</Badge>
<Badge tone="danger" dot />
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `tone` | `'neutral' \| 'info' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` | `'neutral'` | Color tone |
| `dot` | `boolean` | `false` | Renders as a small dot with no content |

---

### Avatar

```tsx
import { Avatar } from 'paw';

<Avatar src="/me.jpg" name="Ada Lovelace" />
<Avatar name="Grace Hopper" size="lg" /> {/* falls back to "GH" */}
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `src` | `string` | — | Image URL |
| `name` | `string` | — | Used for `alt` text and fallback initials |
| `size` | `'xs' \| 'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'xl'` | `'md'` | Avatar size |
| `shape` | `'circle' \| 'square'` | `'circle'` | Avatar shape |

---

### Tooltip

```tsx
import { Tooltip } from 'paw';

<Tooltip content="Copy to clipboard" placement="top">
  <Button aria-label="Copy">📋</Button>
</Tooltip>
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `content` | `ReactNode` | — | Tooltip content |
| `placement` | `'top' \| 'right' \| 'bottom' \| 'left'` | `'top'` | Preferred position |
| `delay` | `number` | `300` | Show delay in milliseconds |

The tooltip appears on hover and on focus, and closes on `Escape`. It is linked to its trigger with `aria-describedby`.

---

### Spinner

```tsx
import { Spinner } from 'paw';

<Spinner />
<Spinner size="lg" label="Loading results" />
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | Spinner size |
| `label` | `string` | `'Loading'` | Text announced to screen readers |

The animation respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.

---

### Divider

```tsx
import { Divider } from 'paw';

<Divider />
<Divider orientation="vertical" />
<Divider label="or" />
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|

# tiny-date

A tiny, dependency-free library that formats dates relative to now: `5 minutes ago`, `in 2 days`, `just now`.

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/tiny-date.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/tiny-date)
[![bundle size](https://img.shields.io/bundlephobia/minzip/tiny-date)](https://bundlephobia.com/package/tiny-date)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/tiny-date.svg)](LICENSE)

## Features

- **Tiny**: under 1 KB minified and gzipped
- **Zero dependencies**
- **Past and future** dates (`3 hours ago`, `in 3 hours`)
- **Localization** via the built-in `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`
- **TypeScript** types included
- Works in Node.js, browsers, Deno, and Bun

## Installation

```bash
npm install tiny-date
# or
yarn add tiny-date
# or
pnpm add tiny-date
```

## Quick Start

```js
import { timeAgo } from 'tiny-date';

timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000));
// => "5 minutes ago"

timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() + 2 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000));
// => "in 2 days"

timeAgo(Date.now() - 10 * 1000);
// => "just now"
```

CommonJS is supported too:

```js
const { timeAgo } = require('tiny-date');
```

## API

### `timeAgo(date, options?)`

Returns a human-readable string describing how far `date` is from now.

**Parameters**

| Name      | Type                       | Description                                          |
| --------- | -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `date`    | `Date \| number \| string` | A `Date`, a timestamp in milliseconds, or an ISO string |
| `options` | `Object`                   | Optional settings (see below)                        |

**Options**

| Option      | Type                               | Default    | Description                                                          |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `locale`    | `string`                           | `'en'`     | Any BCP 47 locale tag supported by `Intl`                            |
| `now`       | `Date \| number`                   | `Date.now()` | Reference time, useful for testing                                 |
| `numeric`   | `'always' \| 'auto'`               | `'always'` | Use `'auto'` for phrases like "yesterday" and "tomorrow"             |
| `style`     | `'long' \| 'short' \| 'narrow'`    | `'long'`   | Output style (`5 minutes ago` vs `5 min. ago`)                       |
| `threshold` | `number`                           | `45`       | Seconds under which `"just now"` is returned                         |

## Examples

### Localization

```js
timeAgo(Date.now() - 3600 * 1000, { locale: 'es' });
// => "hace 1 hora"

timeAgo(Date.now() - 3600 * 1000, { locale: 'ja' });
// => "1 時間前"
```

### Natural phrasing

```js
timeAgo(Date.now() - 86400 * 1000, { numeric: 'auto' });
// => "yesterday"
```

### Short style

```js
timeAgo(Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000, { style: 'short' });
// => "5 min. ago"
```

### Deterministic output for tests

```js
const now = new Date('2024-01-01T12:00:00Z');
timeAgo(new Date('2024-01-01T11:00:00Z'), { now });
// => "1 hour ago"
```

## Units

The largest fitting unit is chosen automatically:

| Difference        | Unit    |
| ----------------- | ------- |
| < 45 seconds      | just now |
| < 60 minutes      | minutes |
| < 24 hours        | hours   |
| < 30 days         | days    |
| < 12 months       | months  |
| otherwise         | years   |

## Error Handling

Invalid dates throw a `TypeError`:

```js
timeAgo('not a date');
// TypeError: tiny-date: invalid date
```

## Browser Support

Any environment that supports `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` (all modern browsers, Node.js 12+).

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome!

1. Fork the repo
2. Create a branch: `git checkout -b my-feature`
3. Install dependencies and run tests: `npm install && npm test`
4. Commit your changes and open a pull request

Please add tests for any new behavior.

[MIT](LICENSE)

# tiny-date

> Format dates relative to now: `5 minutes ago`, `in 2 hours`, `yesterday`.

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/tiny-date.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/tiny-date)
[![bundle size](https://img.shields.io/bundlephobia/minzip/tiny-date)](https://bundlephobia.com/package/tiny-date)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/tiny-date.svg)](LICENSE)

A small, dependency-free library for turning timestamps into human-friendly relative strings. Under 1 KB gzipped, fully typed, and built on `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` for localization.

## Features

- 🪶 Tiny, with zero dependencies
- 🌍 Localized output via the built-in `Intl` API
- 🔮 Handles past and future dates
- 🧩 Accepts `Date`, timestamps (ms), or ISO strings
- 🟦 TypeScript types included
- ⚡ Works in Node.js, browsers, Deno, and Bun

## Installation

```bash
npm install tiny-date
# or
yarn add tiny-date
# or
pnpm add tiny-date
```

## Usage

```js
import { timeAgo } from 'tiny-date';

timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000));
// => "5 minutes ago"

timeAgo(Date.now() + 2 * 60 * 60 * 1000);
// => "in 2 hours"

timeAgo('2024-01-01T12:00:00Z');
// => "1 year ago" (depending on the current date)
```

### CommonJS

```js
const { timeAgo } = require('tiny-date');
```

## API

### `timeAgo(date, options?)`

Returns a relative time string.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `date` | `Date \| number \| string` | The date to format. Numbers are treated as millisecond timestamps. |
| `options` | `Options` | Optional configuration (see below). |

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|--------|------|---------|-------------|
| `locale` | `string` | system locale | BCP 47 locale tag, e.g. `'es'`, `'ja'`. |
| `now` | `Date \| number` | `Date.now()` | Reference point to compare against. Useful for testing. |
| `numeric` | `'always' \| 'auto'` | `'auto'` | Use `'auto'` for phrases like "yesterday"; `'always'` for "1 day ago". |
| `style` | `'long' \| 'short' \| 'narrow'` | `'long'` | Output length: "5 minutes ago" vs "5 min. ago". |

### Examples

```js
// Localization
timeAgo(Date.now() - 3600 * 1000, { locale: 'es' });
// => "hace 1 hora"

// Numeric control
timeAgo(Date.now() - 86400 * 1000, { numeric: 'auto' });   // "yesterday"
timeAgo(Date.now() - 86400 * 1000, { numeric: 'always' }); // "1 day ago"

// Short style
timeAgo(Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000, { style: 'short' });
// => "5 min. ago"

// Fixed reference time (deterministic output)
timeAgo('2024-01-01', { now: '2024-01-08' });
// => "last week"
```

## Thresholds

The unit is chosen by the size of the difference:

| Difference | Unit |
|------------|------|
| < 45 seconds | seconds |
| < 45 minutes | minutes |
| < 22 hours | hours |
| < 6 days | days |
| < 4 weeks | weeks |
| < 11 months | months |
| otherwise | years |

## Error handling

Invalid dates throw a `TypeError`:

```js
timeAgo('not a date'); // TypeError: Invalid date
```

## Browser support

Any environment supporting `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` (all modern browsers, Node.js 12+). For older environments, use a [polyfill](https://github.com/formatjs/formatjs/tree/main/packages/intl-relativetimeformat).

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome!

1. Fork the repo
2. Create a branch: `git checkout -b my-feature`
3. Install dependencies: `npm install`
4. Make changes and add tests: `npm test`
5. Open a pull request

Please open an issue first for major changes.

// => "just now"

```js
const { timeAgo } = require('tiny-date');
```

### `timeAgo(date, options?)`

Returns a string describing how far `date` is from now.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `date` | `Date \| number \| string` | A `Date`, a timestamp in milliseconds, or an ISO 8601 string |

timeAgo('2024-01-01T12:00:00Z', { now: '2024-01-01T12:05:00Z' });

import { timeAgo } from 'tiny-date';

| `options` | `object` (optional)            | See below                                    |

| Option    | Type                          | Default              | Description                                                    |

| `maxUnit` | `"second" \| "minute" \| "hour" \| "day" \| "week" \| "month" \| "year"` | `"year"` | Largest unit to use. |

// Custom reference time
timeAgo('2024-01-01T12:00:00Z', { now: '2024-01-01T12:30:00Z' });

// Short style
timeAgo(Date.now() - 3600 * 1000, { style: 'short' });
// => "1 hr. ago"

// Other locales
timeAgo(Date.now() - 3 * 86400 * 1000, { locale: 'es' });

timeAgo(Date.now() - 90 * 86400 * 1000, { maxUnit: 'day' });

# tiny-date

> Format dates relative to now: "5 minutes ago", "in 2 days", "just now".

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/tiny-date.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/tiny-date)
[![bundle size](https://img.shields.io/bundlephobia/minzip/tiny-date)](https://bundlephobia.com/package/tiny-date)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/tiny-date.svg)](LICENSE)

`tiny-date` is a small, dependency-free library for turning timestamps into friendly, human-readable strings. It's under 1 KB gzipped, works in Node and the browser, and ships with TypeScript types.

## Features

- 🪶 Tiny, with zero dependencies
- 🔮 Handles past and future dates
- 🌍 Localization via `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`
- 🧩 Works with `Date`, timestamps, and ISO strings
- 📦 ESM and CommonJS builds, plus TypeScript types

## Installation

```bash
npm install tiny-date
```

```bash
yarn add tiny-date
pnpm add tiny-date
```

## Usage

```js
import { timeAgo } from 'tiny-date';

timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000));
// => "5 minutes ago"

timeAgo(Date.now() + 2 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000);
// => "in 2 days"

timeAgo('2020-01-01T00:00:00Z');
// => "5 years ago"

timeAgo(new Date());
// => "just now"
```

CommonJS:

```js
const { timeAgo } = require('tiny-date');
```

## API

### `timeAgo(date, options?)`

Returns a string describing how far `date` is from now.

| Parameter | Type                          | Description                      |
| --------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| `date`    | `Date \| number \| string`    | The date to format               |
| `options` | `Options` (optional)          | Configuration, described below   |

#### Options

| Option      | Type                                  | Default     | Description                                                   |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `locale`    | `string`                              | `"en"`      | BCP 47 locale tag, such as `"es"` or `"ja"`                   |
| `now`       | `Date \| number`                      | `Date.now()`| Reference point; useful for testing                           |
| `style`     | `"long" \| "short" \| "narrow"`       | `"long"`    | `"5 minutes ago"` / `"5 min. ago"` / `"5m ago"`              |
| `numeric`   | `"always" \| "auto"`                  | `"auto"`    | With `"auto"`, you get "yesterday" instead of "1 day ago"     |
| `threshold` | `number` (seconds)                    | `10`        | Differences smaller than this return `"just now"`             |

### Examples

```js
timeAgo(Date.now() - 86400000);
// => "yesterday"

timeAgo(Date.now() - 86400000, { numeric: 'always' });
// => "1 day ago"

timeAgo(Date.now() - 3 * 3600000, { locale: 'es' });
// => "hace 3 horas"

timeAgo(Date.now() - 3 * 3600000, { style: 'short' });
// => "3 hr. ago"

// Deterministic output for tests
timeAgo('2024-01-01', { now: '2024-01-08' });
// => "last week"
```

## Units

Output uses the largest sensible unit:

| Difference   | Unit    |
| ------------ | ------- |
| < 60 seconds | seconds |
| < 60 minutes | minutes |
| < 24 hours   | hours   |
| < 7 days     | days    |
| < 4 weeks    | weeks   |
| < 12 months  | months  |
| otherwise    | years   |

## Browser Support

`tiny-date` relies on `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`, supported in all modern browsers and Node 12+. For older environments, include a [polyfill](https://formatjs.io/docs/polyfills/intl-relativetimeformat/).

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome!

1. Fork the repo
2. Create a branch: `git checkout -b my-feature`
3. Install dependencies: `npm install`
4. Make your changes and add tests
5. Run `npm test`
6. Open a pull request

Please open an issue first for large changes.

# flak

A fast, configurable linter for YAML files.

flak catches syntax errors, style inconsistencies, and common configuration mistakes in your YAML before they reach production.

## Features

- **Syntax validation**: reports malformed YAML with exact line and column numbers
- **Style rules**: indentation, line length, trailing whitespace, quote style, and more
- **Duplicate key detection**: catches keys that silently overwrite each other
- **Auto-fix**: automatically corrects fixable issues with `--fix`
- **Multi-document support**: handles files with multiple `---` separated documents
- **CI-friendly**: machine-readable output formats and meaningful exit codes
- **Configurable**: enable, disable, or tune any rule per project or per file

## Installation

### Homebrew

```sh
brew install flak
```

### Cargo

```sh
cargo install flak
```

### Pre-built binaries

Download the latest release for your platform from the [Releases page](https://github.com/example/flak/releases) and place it on your `PATH`.

Verify the installation:

```sh
flak --version
```

## Quick Start

Lint a single file:

```sh
flak config.yaml
```

Lint a directory recursively:

```sh
flak .
```

Lint multiple paths and globs:

```sh
flak deploy/ "charts/**/*.yml" docker-compose.yaml
```

Read from stdin:

```sh
cat config.yaml | flak -
```

Example output:

```
config.yaml
  3:1   warning  trailing whitespace            trailing-spaces
  7:5   error    duplicate key "name"           key-duplicates
  12:81 warning  line too long (92 > 80)        line-length

✖ 3 problems (1 error, 2 warnings)
```

## Usage

```
flak [OPTIONS] <PATH>...
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-c, --config <FILE>` | Use a specific config file |
| `--fix` | Automatically fix problems where possible |
| `-f, --format <FORMAT>` | Output format: `text` (default), `json`, `github`, `junit` |
| `--select <RULES>` | Run only the listed rules (comma-separated) |
| `--ignore <RULES>` | Skip the listed rules (comma-separated) |
| `--max-warnings <N>` | Exit with an error if warnings exceed `N` |
| `--no-color` | Disable colored output |
| `-q, --quiet` | Only report errors |
| `-h, --help` | Show help |
| `-V, --version` | Show version |

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | No problems found (or only warnings, within the allowed limit) |
| `1` | One or more errors found |
| `2` | Invalid usage or configuration |

## Configuration

flak looks for a `.flak.yaml` file in the current directory and walks up through parent directories. Use `--config` to specify a different file.

```yaml
# .flak.yaml
extends: recommended

ignore:
  - vendor/
  - "**/generated/*.yaml"

rules:
  line-length:
    level: warning
    max: 120
  indentation:
    level: error
    spaces: 2
  quote-style:
    level: warning
    prefer: double
  document-start: disable
```

### Rule levels

Each rule can be set to `error`, `warning`, or `disable`.

### Inline directives

Disable rules with comments:

```yaml
# flak-disable-next-line line-length
description: "a very long string that would normally trigger the line-length rule..."

key: value  # flak-disable-line quote-style

# flak-disable key-duplicates
...
# flak-enable key-duplicates
```

## Rules

| Rule | Description | Fixable |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `syntax` | YAML must parse correctly | No |
| `key-duplicates` | Mapping keys must be unique | No |
| `indentation` | Consistent indentation width | Yes |
| `line-length` | Maximum line length | No |
| `trailing-spaces` | No trailing whitespace | Yes |
| `new-line-at-eof` | File ends with a newline | Yes |
| `quote-style` | Consistent string quoting | Yes |
| `truthy` | Avoid ambiguous values like `yes`/`no`/`on` | Yes |
| `document-start` | Require `---` at start of file | Yes |
| `empty-values` | Disallow keys with empty values | No |
| `key-ordering` | Keys sorted alphabetically | Yes |
| `comments` | Comment formatting (space after `#`) | Yes |

List all rules and their defaults:

```sh
flak --list-rules
```

## Integrations

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
- name: Lint YAML
  run: flak --format github .
```

### Pre-commit

```yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/example/flak
    rev: v1.0.0
    hooks:
      - id: flak
```

### Editor support

Run flak on save by pointing your editor's external linter at `flak --format json -`.

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome! To get started:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/example/flak
cd flak
cargo build
cargo test
```

Please open an issue before starting work on large changes. New rules should include tests and documentation.

## License

MIT © flak contributors

# flak

A fast, configurable linter for YAML files.

flak catches syntax errors, style inconsistencies, and common mistakes in your YAML before they reach production. It works on single files, directories, or piped input, and it integrates easily with CI pipelines and editors.

## Features

- **Syntax validation**: reports malformed YAML with line and column numbers
- **Style rules**: indentation, line length, trailing whitespace, quote style, and more
- **Safety checks**: duplicate keys, ambiguous values (e.g. `no`, `on`, `1e3`), and unquoted special strings
- **Auto-fix**: automatically corrects fixable issues with `--fix`
- **Configurable**: enable, disable, or tune rules via `.flak.yml`
- **Multiple output formats**: human-readable, JSON, JUnit, and SARIF
- **Multi-document support**: handles files containing several `---` documents

## Installation

### From a package manager

```sh
# npm
npm install -g flak

# Homebrew
brew install flak

# pip
pip install flak-cli
```

### From source

```sh
git clone https://github.com/example/flak.git
cd flak
make install
```

Verify the installation:

```sh
flak --version
```

## Quick Start

Lint a single file:

```sh
flak config.yml
```

Lint a directory recursively:

```sh
flak .
```

Lint from standard input:

```sh
cat config.yml | flak -
```

Example output:

```
config.yml
  3:1   error    duplicate key "name"            no-duplicate-keys
  7:15  warning  line too long (92 > 80)         line-length
  12:4  warning  wrong indentation: expected 2   indentation

✖ 3 problems (1 error, 2 warnings)
```

## Usage

```
flak [options] <file|dir|->...
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-c, --config <path>` | Path to a config file |
| `-f, --format <name>` | Output format: `text` (default), `json`, `junit`, `sarif` |
| `--fix` | Automatically fix problems where possible |
| `--rule <id>=<level>` | Override a rule level (`off`, `warn`, `error`) |
| `--ignore <glob>` | Ignore files matching a glob (repeatable) |
| `--max-warnings <n>` | Exit with an error if warnings exceed `n` |
| `-q, --quiet` | Report errors only |
| `--no-color` | Disable colored output |
| `-h, --help` | Show help |
| `-v, --version` | Show version |

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | No problems found (or only warnings within limits) |
| `1` | One or more errors found |
| `2` | Invalid configuration or usage error |

## Configuration

flak looks for a `.flak.yml` file in the current directory and walks up through parent directories. Use `--config` to specify a different file.

```yaml
# .flak.yml
extends: recommended

ignore:
  - vendor/**
  - "*.generated.yml"

rules:
  indentation:
    level: error
    spaces: 2
  line-length:
    level: warn
    max: 100
  quote-style:
    level: warn
    prefer: double
  no-duplicate-keys: error
  trailing-whitespace: off
```

### Inline directives

Disable rules using comments:

```yaml
# flak-disable-next-line line-length
description: "A very long string that would otherwise trigger the line length rule..."

# flak-disable rule-one rule-two
legacy:
    key:   value
# flak-enable rule-one rule-two
```

## Rules

| Rule | Description | Fixable |
| --- | --- | :---: |
| `no-duplicate-keys` | Disallow duplicate mapping keys | |
| `indentation` | Enforce consistent indentation | ✔ |
| `line-length` | Limit maximum line length | |
| `trailing-whitespace` | Disallow trailing spaces | ✔ |
| `quote-style` | Enforce single or double quotes | ✔ |
| `truthy-values` | Flag ambiguous booleans like `yes`/`no`/`on`/`off` | ✔ |
| `key-ordering` | Require keys in alphabetical order | |
| `document-start` | Require or forbid `---` | ✔ |
| `empty-values` | Disallow keys with empty values | |
| `final-newline` | Require a newline at end of file | ✔ |

Run `flak --list-rules` to see all available rules and their defaults.

## Integrations

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
name: Lint YAML
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  flak:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: npm install -g flak
      - run: flak --format sarif . > flak.sarif
```

### Pre-commit

```yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/example/flak
    rev: v1.0.0
    hooks:
      - id: flak
```

### Editors

Plugins are available for VS Code and Neovim. Any editor with LSP support can use `flak --lsp`.

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome!

1. Fork the repository
2. Create a branch: `git checkout -b my-feature`
3. Make your changes and add tests: `make test`
4. Open a pull request

Please open an issue first for large changes.

## License

MIT © flak contributors

Verify the installation:

```sh
flak --version
```

## Quick Start

Lint a single file:

```sh
flak config.yaml
```

Lint multiple files or whole directories (recursively finds `.yml` and `.yaml`):

```sh
flak deploy/ values.yaml docker-compose.yml
```

Read from stdin:

```sh
cat config.yaml | flak -
```

Example output:

```
config.yaml
  3:1   error    duplicate key "name"            no-duplicate-keys
  7:81  warning  line too long (92 > 80)         line-length
  12:5  warning  wrong indentation: expected 2   indentation
  15:10 error    trailing spaces                 trailing-spaces  (fixable)

✖ 4 problems (2 errors, 2 warnings)
```

```
flak [OPTIONS] <PATHS>...
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-c, --config <FILE>` | Path to a config file |
| `--fix` | Automatically fix fixable problems |
| `-f, --format <FORMAT>` | Output format: `text` (default), `json`, `github`, `junit` |
| `--select <RULES>` | Only run the listed rules (comma-separated) |
| `--ignore <RULES>` | Skip the listed rules (comma-separated) |
| `--max-warnings <N>` | Exit with failure if warnings exceed `N` |
| `--no-color` | Disable colored output |
| `-q, --quiet` | Report errors only, suppress warnings |
| `--list-rules` | Print all available rules and exit |
| `-h, --help` | Show help |
| `-V, --version` | Show version |

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | No problems found |
| `1` | One or more errors found (or warnings exceeded `--max-warnings`) |
| `2` | Invalid usage or configuration |

flak looks for a `.flak.yaml` file in the current directory, then walks up through parent directories. Use `--config` to specify a file explicitly.

```yaml
# .flak.yaml
extends: recommended

ignore:
  - vendor/
  - "**/generated/*.yaml"

rules:
  line-length:
    level: warning
    max: 120
  indentation:
    spaces: 2
    indent-sequences: true
  quote-style:
    level: off
  no-duplicate-keys: error
```

| Rule | Description | Fixable |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `syntax` | YAML must parse correctly | No |
| `no-duplicate-keys` | Mapping keys must be unique | No |
| `indentation` | Consistent indentation width | Yes |
| `line-length` | Maximum line length | No |
| `trailing-spaces` | No whitespace at end of lines | Yes |
| `final-newline` | Files end with a single newline | Yes |
| `quote-style` | Consistent string quoting | Yes |
| `truthy-values` | Avoid ambiguous booleans like `yes`/`on` | Yes |
| `unused-anchors` | Anchors must be referenced | No |
| `key-ordering` | Keys sorted alphabetically (opt-in) | No |

```yaml
# flak-disable-next-line line-length
description: "A very long string that would normally trigger the line length rule ..."

enabled: yes  # flak-disable-line truthy-values

# flak-disable indentation
legacy:
      weird: indent

Disable an entire file by placing this on the first line:

```yaml
# flak-disable-file
```

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
- name: Lint YAML
  run: flak --format github .
```

Problems appear as inline annotations on pull requests.

### Pre-commit

```yaml

  - repo: https://github.com/example/flak
    rev: v1.0.0
    hooks:
      - id: flak

```sh

```

```json
[

# flak

A fast, configurable linter for YAML files.

flak catches syntax errors, style inconsistencies, and common mistakes in your YAML before they reach production. It works on single files, directories, or piped input, and it fits easily into CI pipelines and pre-commit hooks.

## Features

- **Syntax validation**: catches malformed YAML with precise line and column reporting
- **Style rules**: indentation, line length, trailing whitespace, quoting, and more
- **Semantic checks**: duplicate keys, truthy value ambiguity (`yes`/`no`/`on`/`off`), empty values
- **Auto-fix**: automatically repairs many style issues with `--fix`
- **Multiple output formats**: human-readable, JSON, and SARIF
- **Configurable**: enable, disable, or tune rules per project or per file
- **Multi-document support**: handles files with several `---` separated documents

## Installation

```sh
# npm
npm install -g flak

# pip
pip install flak

# Homebrew
brew install flak
```

Verify the installation:

```sh
flak --version
```

## Quick Start

Lint a single file:

```sh
flak config.yaml
```

Lint a directory recursively:

```sh
flak .
```

Lint from standard input:

```sh
cat config.yaml | flak -
```

Example output:

```
config.yaml
  3:1    error    duplicate key "name"                  (no-duplicate-keys)
  7:81   warning  line too long (92 > 80 characters)    (line-length)
  12:14  warning  trailing whitespace                   (no-trailing-space)

✖ 3 problems (1 error, 2 warnings)
```

## Usage

```
flak [options] <file|directory|->...
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-c, --config <path>` | Path to a configuration file |
| `-f, --format <format>` | Output format: `text`, `json`, `sarif` (default: `text`) |
| `--fix` | Automatically fix fixable problems |
| `--select <rules>` | Only run the specified comma-separated rules |
| `--ignore <rules>` | Skip the specified comma-separated rules |
| `--max-warnings <n>` | Exit with an error if warnings exceed `n` |
| `--no-color` | Disable colored output |
| `-q, --quiet` | Report errors only, suppressing warnings |
| `-h, --help` | Show help |
| `-v, --version` | Show version |

### Exit Codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | No problems found (or only warnings within the allowed limit) |
| `1` | One or more errors found |
| `2` | Invalid configuration or usage error |

## Configuration

flak looks for a configuration file in the current directory, then in parent directories. Supported filenames:

- `.flak.yaml`
- `.flak.yml`
- `flak.config.yaml`

Example `.flak.yaml`:

```yaml
extends: recommended

ignore:
  - vendor/
  - "**/generated/*.yaml"

rules:
  line-length:
    severity: warning
    max: 120
  indentation:
    severity: error
    spaces: 2
  truthy:
    allowed-values: ["true", "false"]
  no-trailing-space: error
  document-start: off
```

### Rule Severity

Each rule can be set to `error`, `warning`, or `off`. Rules that accept options use the object form shown above.

### Inline Directives

Disable rules with comments:

```yaml
# flak-disable-next-line line-length
description: a very long line that would otherwise trigger a warning...

key: value  # flak-disable-line no-trailing-space

# flak-disable line-length
# ...many lines...
# flak-enable line-length
```

## Rules

| Rule | Description | Fixable |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `syntax` | YAML must parse correctly | No |
| `no-duplicate-keys` | Mapping keys must be unique | No |
| `indentation` | Consistent indentation width | Yes |
| `line-length` | Maximum line length | No |
| `no-trailing-space` | No trailing whitespace | Yes |
| `final-newline` | Files must end with a newline | Yes |
| `truthy` | Restrict ambiguous boolean values | Yes |
| `quote-style` | Enforce single or double quotes | Yes |
| `no-empty-values` | Disallow keys with empty values | No |
| `key-ordering` | Require alphabetically sorted keys | No |
| `document-start` | Require or forbid `---` | Yes |
| `comments` | Comment spacing and formatting | Yes |

List all rules and their options:

```sh
flak --list-rules
```

## Integrations

### Pre-commit

```yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/example/flak
    rev: v1.0.0
    hooks:
      - id: flak
```

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
- name: Lint YAML
  run: |
    npm install -g flak
    flak --format sarif . > flak.sarif

- uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3
  with:
    sarif_file: flak.sarif
```

### GitLab CI

```yaml
yaml-lint:
  image: node:20
  script:
    - npm install -g flak
    - flak --max-warnings 0 .
```

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome!

1. Fork the repository
2. Create a feature branch: `git checkout -b my-feature`
3. Make your changes and add tests
4. Run the test suite: `npm test`
5. Open a pull request

Please open an issue first for major changes so we can discuss the approach.

MIT © flak contributors

flak .

```sh

# pip

```

### From source

```sh
git clone https://github.com/example/flak.git
cd flak
make install
```

Verify the installation:

```sh

```

Lint a single file:

```sh

```

Lint a directory recursively:

```sh

```

Lint from standard input:

```sh

config.yaml
  3:1   error    duplicate key "name"            no-duplicate-keys
  7:81  warning  line too long (96 > 80)         line-length
  12:5  warning  wrong indentation: expected 2   indentation

```

| Option | Description |

| `--max-warnings <n>` | Exit with an error if warnings exceed `n` |
| `-q, --quiet` | Report errors only |
| `--no-color` | Disable colored output |
| `-h, --help` | Show help |

| Code | Meaning |

# flak

A fast, configurable linter for YAML files.

flak catches syntax errors, style inconsistencies, and common mistakes in your YAML before they reach production. It works on single files, directories, or piped input, and fits easily into CI pipelines and pre-commit hooks.

## Features

- Syntax validation with clear line and column error reporting
- Style checks for indentation, line length, trailing spaces, and quoting
- Detection of duplicate keys, truthy value pitfalls (`yes`/`no`/`on`/`off`), and empty values
- Configurable rules with per-rule severity (`error`, `warning`, `off`)
- Automatic fixing for safe, mechanical issues
- Multiple output formats: text, JSON, SARIF, and GitHub Actions annotations
- Inline comments to disable rules for specific lines or blocks

## Installation

**Using pip:**

```sh
pip install flak
```

**Using Homebrew:**

```sh
brew install flak
```

**Using Cargo:**

```sh
cargo install flak
```

Verify the installation:

```sh
flak --version
```

## Quick Start

Lint a single file:

```sh
flak config.yaml
```

Lint a directory recursively:

```sh
flak .
```

Lint from standard input:

```sh
cat config.yaml | flak -
```

Example output:

```
config.yaml
  4:3    error    duplicate key "name"            (key-duplicates)
  9:81   warning  line too long (96 > 80)         (line-length)
  12:1   warning  truthy value "yes" is ambiguous (truthy)

✖ 3 problems (1 error, 2 warnings)
```

## Usage

```
flak [OPTIONS] <PATH>...
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-c, --config <FILE>` | Path to a config file |
| `-f, --format <FORMAT>` | Output format: `text`, `json`, `sarif`, `github` (default: `text`) |
| `--fix` | Automatically fix fixable issues |
| `--select <RULES>` | Only run the listed rules (comma-separated) |
| `--ignore <RULES>` | Skip the listed rules (comma-separated) |
| `--strict` | Treat warnings as errors |
| `--max-warnings <N>` | Fail if warnings exceed N |
| `-q, --quiet` | Report errors only |
| `--no-color` | Disable colored output |
| `--list-rules` | Print all available rules and exit |
| `-h, --help` | Show help |
| `-v, --version` | Show version |

### Exit Codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | No problems found (or only warnings, without `--strict`) |
| `1` | One or more errors found |
| `2` | Invalid usage or configuration |

## Configuration

flak looks for a config file in the current directory, then in each parent directory, in this order: `.flak.yaml`, `.flak.yml`, `flak.toml`.

Example `.flak.yaml`:

```yaml
extends: recommended

ignore:
  - vendor/
  - "*.generated.yaml"

rules:
  indentation:
    level: error
    spaces: 2
  line-length:
    level: warning
    max: 120
  truthy:
    level: error
    allowed-values: ["true", "false"]
  trailing-spaces: off
```

### Built-in Rule Sets

- `recommended`: sensible defaults for most projects
- `strict`: all rules enabled at `error` level
- `minimal`: syntax errors and duplicate keys only

## Disabling Rules Inline

Disable a rule for a single line:

```yaml
key:   value  # flak-disable-line spacing
```

Disable a rule for the next line:

```yaml
# flak-disable-next-line line-length
description: a very long string that would normally trigger the line-length rule...
```

Disable rules for a block:

```yaml
# flak-disable indentation
list:
    - one
    - two
# flak-enable indentation
```

Disable all rules for a whole file by placing this on the first line:

```yaml
# flak-disable-file
```

## Rules

Run `flak --list-rules` for the full list. Common rules include:

| Rule | Description | Fixable |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `syntax` | YAML must parse correctly | No |
| `key-duplicates` | No duplicate keys in a mapping | No |
| `indentation` | Consistent indentation width | Yes |
| `line-length` | Maximum line length | No |
| `trailing-spaces` | No trailing whitespace | Yes |
| `truthy` | Avoid ambiguous boolean values | Yes |
| `quotes` | Consistent quote style | Yes |
| `empty-values` | Disallow implicit null values | No |
| `new-line-at-end` | File must end with a newline | Yes |
| `document-start` | Require or forbid `---` | Yes |

## Integrations

### Pre-commit

```yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/flak-lint/flak
    rev: v1.0.0
    hooks:
      - id: flak
```

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
- name: Lint YAML
  run: flak --format github .
```

### Docker

```sh
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/work" -w /work flak/flak .
```

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome. To get started:

1. Fork the repository and create a feature branch.
2. Make your changes and add tests.
3. Run the test suite with `make test`.
4. Open a pull request describing your change.

Please open an issue first for large changes or new rules.

# paw 🐾

A tiny React component library of 12 small, accessible UI primitives. Unstyled where it counts, tasteful by default, and easy to override.

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/paw-ui.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/paw-ui)
[![bundle size](https://img.shields.io/bundlephobia/minzip/paw-ui)](https://bundlephobia.com/package/paw-ui)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/paw-ui.svg)](./LICENSE)

## Features

- **12 focused primitives**: just the basics, nothing more
- **Accessible**: WAI-ARIA patterns and keyboard support built in
- **Tree-shakeable**: import only what you use
- **TypeScript-first**: full type definitions included
- **Themeable**: styled through CSS variables, no runtime CSS-in-JS
- **Lightweight**: zero dependencies besides React

## Installation

```bash
npm install paw-ui
# or
yarn add paw-ui
# or
pnpm add paw-ui
```

Requires `react` and `react-dom` >= 18.

## Quick Start

Import the stylesheet once at your app's entry point:

```jsx
import 'paw-ui/styles.css';
```

Then use the components:

```jsx
import { Button, Input, Badge } from 'paw-ui';

export default function App() {
  return (
    <form>
      <Input label="Email" type="email" placeholder="you@example.com" />
      <Button variant="primary">
        Subscribe <Badge>New</Badge>
      </Button>
    </form>
  );
}
```

## Components

| Component | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Button` | Clickable action with variants, sizes, and loading state |
| `Input` | Text field with label, hint, and error support |
| `Checkbox` | Binary toggle with indeterminate state |
| `Switch` | On/off toggle for settings |
| `Badge` | Small status or count indicator |
| `Avatar` | User image with initials fallback |
| `Tooltip` | Hover/focus hint attached to an element |
| `Modal` | Focus-trapped dialog with overlay |
| `Tabs` | Keyboard-navigable tabbed content |
| `Spinner` | Loading indicator |
| `Alert` | Inline message for info, success, warning, or error |
| `Card` | Simple content container |

## Usage Examples

### Button

```jsx
<Button variant="primary" size="md" onClick={save}>Save</Button>
<Button variant="ghost" loading>Saving…</Button>
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'ghost' \| 'danger'` | `'primary'` |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` |

### Modal

```jsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

<Modal open={open} onClose={() => setOpen(false)} title="Delete item?">
  This action cannot be undone.
</Modal>
```

### Tabs

```jsx
<Tabs defaultValue="account">
  <Tabs.List>
    <Tabs.Tab value="account">Account</Tabs.Tab>
    <Tabs.Tab value="billing">Billing</Tabs.Tab>
  </Tabs.List>
  <Tabs.Panel value="account">Account settings</Tabs.Panel>
  <Tabs.Panel value="billing">Billing details</Tabs.Panel>
</Tabs>
```

Each component accepts standard HTML attributes for its root element, plus `className` and `style`, and forwards refs.

## Theming

paw is styled with CSS variables. Override them globally or within any scope:

```css
:root {
  --paw-color-primary: #7c3aed;
  --paw-color-danger: #dc2626;
  --paw-radius: 8px;
  --paw-font: 'Inter', sans-serif;
  --paw-space: 0.5rem;
}

[data-theme='dark'] {
  --paw-color-bg: #111827;
  --paw-color-text: #f9fafb;
}
```

## Accessibility

- Full keyboard navigation (Tab, Arrow keys, Escape, Enter/Space)
- Visible focus rings
- Correct ARIA roles, states, and labels
- Respects `prefers-reduced-motion`

## Browser Support

Latest two versions of Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge.

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome!

1. Fork the repo
2. Create a branch: `git checkout -b feat/my-change`
3. Install dependencies: `npm install`
4. Run Storybook: `npm run storybook`
5. Run tests: `npm test`
6. Open a pull request

Please follow the existing code style and add tests for new behavior.

[MIT](./LICENSE) © paw contributors

# paw 🐾

A tiny React component library of 12 small, accessible, unopinionated UI primitives.

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/paw-ui.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/paw-ui)
[![bundle size](https://img.shields.io/bundlephobia/minzip/paw-ui)](https://bundlephobia.com/package/paw-ui)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/paw-ui.svg)](./LICENSE)

## Why paw?

- **Small**: each component is tree-shakeable, with no runtime dependencies besides React.
- **Accessible**: keyboard navigation, focus management, and ARIA attributes are built in.
- **Unopinionated**: minimal default styling, easy to override with CSS, CSS Modules, Tailwind, or CSS-in-JS.
- **Typed**: written in TypeScript, with full type definitions included.

## Installation

```bash
npm install paw-ui
# or
yarn add paw-ui
# or
pnpm add paw-ui
```

**Requirements:** React 17 or later.

## Quick Start

```jsx
import { Button, Input, Card } from 'paw-ui';
import 'paw-ui/styles.css'; // optional default styles

export default function App() {
  return (
    <Card>
      <Input label="Email" type="email" />
      <Button variant="primary">Subscribe</Button>
    </Card>
  );
}
```

## Components

| Component  | Description                                      |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `Button`   | Clickable action with variants and loading state |
| `Input`    | Text input with label, hint, and error support   |
| `Checkbox` | Binary toggle with indeterminate state           |
| `Switch`   | On/off toggle for settings                       |
| `Badge`    | Small status or count indicator                  |
| `Avatar`   | User image with initials fallback                |
| `Card`     | Container for grouped content                    |
| `Tooltip`  | Short hint shown on hover or focus               |
| `Modal`    | Dialog with focus trap and scroll lock           |
| `Spinner`  | Loading indicator                                |
| `Tabs`     | Keyboard-navigable tabbed content                |
| `Alert`    | Inline message for info, success, warning, error |

## Usage Examples

### Button

```jsx
<Button variant="primary" size="md" onClick={save}>Save</Button>
<Button variant="ghost" loading>Saving…</Button>
```

| Prop       | Type                                   | Default     |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| `variant`  | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'ghost'`  | `'primary'` |
| `size`     | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'`                 | `'md'`      |
| `loading`  | `boolean`                              | `false`     |
| `disabled` | `boolean`                              | `false`     |

### Modal

```jsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

<Modal open={open} onClose={() => setOpen(false)} title="Confirm">
  Are you sure?
</Modal>
```

### Tabs

```jsx
<Tabs defaultValue="one">
  <Tabs.List>
    <Tabs.Tab value="one">One</Tabs.Tab>
    <Tabs.Tab value="two">Two</Tabs.Tab>
  </Tabs.List>
  <Tabs.Panel value="one">First panel</Tabs.Panel>
  <Tabs.Panel value="two">Second panel</Tabs.Panel>
</Tabs>
```

### Tooltip

```jsx
<Tooltip content="Copy to clipboard">
  <Button>Copy</Button>
</Tooltip>
```

## Styling

paw ships with optional base styles. Every component accepts `className` and `style`, and exposes CSS custom properties for theming:

```css
:root {
  --paw-color-primary: #6d5dfc;
  --paw-color-text: #1a1a1a;
  --paw-radius: 6px;
  --paw-font-family: system-ui, sans-serif;
}
```

Skip the default stylesheet entirely if you prefer to style components yourself.

## Accessibility

- All interactive components are fully keyboard operable.
- `Modal` traps focus and restores it on close.
- `Tooltip` appears on both hover and focus, and is linked via `aria-describedby`.
- `Tabs` follow the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern (arrow keys, Home/End).

## Tree Shaking

Import from the root, or from individual paths:

```jsx
import { Button } from 'paw-ui';
import Button from 'paw-ui/Button';
```

## TypeScript

Types are included. Component props are exported for reuse:

```ts
import type { ButtonProps } from 'paw-ui';
```

## Browser Support

Latest versions of Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge.

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome!

1. Fork the repo and create a branch.
2. Install dependencies: `npm install`
3. Run the tests: `npm test`
4. Start Storybook: `npm run storybook`
5. Open a pull request describing your change.

Please follow the existing code style and add tests for new behavior.

## License

[MIT](./LICENSE) © paw contributors

# paw 🐾

A tiny React component library of 12 small, accessible, unopinionated UI primitives.

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/paw-ui.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/paw-ui)
[![bundle size](https://img.shields.io/bundlephobia/minzip/paw-ui)](https://bundlephobia.com/package/paw-ui)

## Why paw?

- **Small**: each component is tree-shakeable, and the whole library is under 6 kB gzipped.

```bash

# or

```

## Quick start

```jsx
import { Button, Input, Badge } from 'paw-ui';
import 'paw-ui/styles.css'; // optional default theme

  return (

        Subscribe <Badge>new</Badge>
      </Button>
    </form>
  );
}

| `Checkbox`   | Accessible checkbox with indeterminate state     |
| `Switch`     | On/off toggle                                    |
| `Badge`      | Small status or count indicator                  |
| `Avatar`     | Image with initials fallback                     |
| `Tooltip`    | Hover/focus hint attached to an element          |

| `Spinner`    | Loading indicator                                |
| `Alert`      | Inline message for info, success, warning, error |

```jsx
