# paw 🐾

A tiny React component library of 12 small, accessible UI primitives. Unstyled by default, easy to theme, and friendly to tree-shaking.

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/paw.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/paw)
[![bundle size](https://img.shields.io/bundlephobia/minzip/paw)](https://bundlephobia.com/package/paw)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/paw.svg)](./LICENSE)

## Features

- **12 focused primitives**, with no sprawling API surface
- **Accessible**: WAI-ARIA patterns, keyboard navigation, and focus management built in
- **Lightweight**: zero runtime dependencies, tree-shakeable ESM
- **Themeable**: styled through CSS variables and `className`, with no CSS-in-JS runtime
- **TypeScript-first**: full type definitions included
- **SSR-safe**: works with Next.js, Remix, and Vite

## Installation

```bash
npm install paw
# or
yarn add paw
# or
pnpm add paw
```

Requires `react` and `react-dom` ≥ 18.

## Quick Start

```jsx
import { Button, Input, Card } from 'paw';
import 'paw/styles.css'; // optional default theme

export default function App() {
  return (
    <Card>
      <Input label="Email" type="email" />
      <Button variant="primary">Subscribe</Button>
    </Card>
  );
}
```

## Components

| Component  | Description                                      |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `Button`   | Clickable action with variants and loading state |
| `Input`    | Text input with label, hint, and error support   |
| `Checkbox` | Checkbox with indeterminate state                |
| `Switch`   | On/off toggle                                    |
| `Select`   | Accessible dropdown select                       |
| `Badge`    | Small status or count indicator                  |
| `Avatar`   | User image with fallback initials                |
| `Card`     | Surface container with header/body/footer slots  |
| `Tooltip`  | Hover/focus hint attached to an element          |
| `Modal`    | Dialog with focus trap and scroll lock           |
| `Tabs`     | Keyboard-navigable tabbed interface              |
| `Spinner`  | Loading indicator                                |

## Usage Examples

### Button

```jsx
<Button variant="primary" size="md" onClick={save}>Save</Button>
<Button variant="ghost" loading>Saving…</Button>
```

| Prop       | Type                                  | Default     |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| `variant`  | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'ghost'` | `'primary'` |
| `size`     | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'`                | `'md'`      |
| `loading`  | `boolean`                             | `false`     |
| `disabled` | `boolean`                             | `false`     |

### Modal

```jsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

<Modal open={open} onClose={() => setOpen(false)} title="Delete item?">
  This action cannot be undone.
</Modal>
```

### Tabs

```jsx
<Tabs defaultValue="one">
  <Tabs.List>
    <Tabs.Tab value="one">One</Tabs.Tab>
    <Tabs.Tab value="two">Two</Tabs.Tab>
  </Tabs.List>
  <Tabs.Panel value="one">First panel</Tabs.Panel>
  <Tabs.Panel value="two">Second panel</Tabs.Panel>
</Tabs>
```

## Theming

paw uses CSS variables. Override them anywhere:

```css
:root {
  --paw-color-primary: #7c3aed;
  --paw-color-text: #1f2937;
  --paw-radius: 8px;
  --paw-font: system-ui, sans-serif;
  --paw-focus-ring: 0 0 0 3px rgba(124, 58, 237, 0.4);
}
```

Every component also accepts `className` and `style`, and forwards refs and native props to its root element.

## Importing Individually

For maximum tree-shaking:

```jsx
import { Button } from 'paw/button';
```

## Accessibility

- Full keyboard support (`Tab`, `Arrow` keys, `Esc`, `Enter`, `Space`)
- Correct ARIA roles, states, and labels
- Visible focus indicators
- Respects `prefers-reduced-motion`

## Browser Support

Latest two versions of Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge.

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome!

```bash
git clone https://github.com/your-org/paw.git
cd paw
npm install
npm run dev     # start the playground
npm test        # run tests
npm run lint    # lint the code
```

Please open an issue before starting work on large changes.

[MIT](./LICENSE) © paw contributors

# paw 🐾

A tiny React component library of 12 small, accessible UI primitives. Unstyled by default, themeable with CSS variables, and tree-shakeable.

![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/paw)
![bundle size](https://img.shields.io/bundlephobia/minzip/paw)
![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/paw)

## Features

- **Small**: each component is under 1 KB gzipped
- **Accessible**: WAI-ARIA compliant, keyboard friendly
- **Themeable**: styled through CSS custom properties
- **Typed**: written in TypeScript, ships with type definitions
- **Tree-shakeable**: import only what you use
- **Zero dependencies** beyond React

## Installation

```bash
npm install paw
# or
yarn add paw
# or
pnpm add paw
```

Requires React 17 or later.

## Quick Start

```jsx
import { Button, Input, Badge } from 'paw';
import 'paw/styles.css'; // optional default theme

export default function App() {
  return (
    <form>
      <Input label="Email" type="email" />
      <Button variant="primary">
        Subscribe <Badge>New</Badge>
      </Button>
    </form>
  );
}
```

## Components

| Component | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `Button` | Clickable action with variants and loading state |
| `Input` | Text input with label, hint, and error support |
| `Checkbox` | Checkbox with indeterminate state |
| `Switch` | On/off toggle |
| `Badge` | Small status or count indicator |
| `Avatar` | User image with initials fallback |
| `Tooltip` | Hover/focus popup label |
| `Spinner` | Loading indicator |
| `Progress` | Determinate and indeterminate progress bar |
| `Alert` | Inline message for info, success, warning, or error |
| `Tag` | Removable label or chip |
| `Divider` | Horizontal or vertical separator |

## Usage Examples

### Button

```jsx
<Button variant="primary" size="md" loading={false}>
  Save
</Button>
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
|------|------|---------|
| `variant` | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'ghost'` | `'primary'` |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` |

```jsx
const [on, setOn] = useState(false);
<Switch checked={on} onChange={setOn} label="Notifications" />
```

### Tooltip

```jsx
<Tooltip content="Copy to clipboard" placement="top">
  <Button>Copy</Button>
</Tooltip>
```

### Alert

```jsx
<Alert status="warning" title="Heads up">
  Your trial ends in 3 days.
</Alert>
```

## Theming

Override CSS variables at any scope:

```css
:root {
  --paw-color-primary: #6d28d9;
  --paw-color-text: #1f2937;
  --paw-radius: 6px;

- Proper roles, labels, and live regions (`Alert`, `Progress`, `Spinner`)
- Respects `prefers-reduced-motion`

Types are included. Props can be imported directly:

```ts
import type { ButtonProps } from 'paw';
```

Latest versions of Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge.

# paw

Twelve small React UI primitives for building interfaces without adopting a full design system. Use them on their own or compose them into forms, toolbars, and dialogs.

## Installation

```sh
npm install paw
```

## Quick start

```jsx
import { Button, Input, Label, Stack } from 'paw';

export default function NewsletterForm() {
  return (
    <form onSubmit={(event) => event.preventDefault()}>
      <Stack>
        <Label htmlFor="email">Email address</Label>
        <Input id="email" name="email" type="email" autoComplete="email" required />
        <Button type="submit">Subscribe</Button>
      </Stack>
    </form>
  );
}
```

This example demonstrates form composition. Replace the submit handler with your application’s subscription logic.

## Primitives

| Component | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| `Button` | Triggering an action or submitting a form. |
| `Input` | Collecting a single line of text, an email address, or a number. |
| `Textarea` | Collecting multiline text. |
| `Label` | Giving a form control a visible name. |
| `Checkbox` | Selecting an option independently of other options. |
| `Switch` | Turning a setting on or off. |
| `Select` | Choosing a value from a list of options. |
| `Badge` | Showing a short status or category. |
| `Separator` | Dividing related groups of content. |
| `Stack` | Arranging elements vertically with consistent spacing. |
| `Dialog` | Presenting a task or message in a modal. |
| `Tooltip` | Adding a brief hint to a control. Keep essential instructions visible. |

## Usage guidelines

- Pair form controls with visible labels. Match the label’s `htmlFor` to the control’s `id`.
- Use a button for an action and a link for navigation.
- Give icon-only buttons an accessible name; a tooltip alone is not a substitute.
- Test dialogs with a keyboard: check where focus lands when the dialog opens, how it closes, and where focus returns.

## Contributing

When proposing a change, include a small example that shows the problem or the intended behavior. For changes to interactive components, describe the expected keyboard and focus behavior.

# tiny-date

A lightweight, zero-dependency JavaScript library for formatting dates relative to now (e.g., `"5 minutes ago"`, `"in 2 days"`).

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/tiny-date.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/tiny-date)
[![bundle size](https://img.shields.io/bundlephobia/minzip/tiny-date)](https://bundlephobia.com/package/tiny-date)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/tiny-date.svg)](./LICENSE)

## Features

- **Tiny:** Less than 500 bytes minified and gzipped.
- **Zero Dependencies:** No bloat, just plain JavaScript.
- **Past & Future:** Handles both past (`"3 hours ago"`) and future (`"in 2 weeks"`) dates.
- **TypeScript Ready:** Includes built-in TypeScript definitions.

## Installation

Install via npm, yarn, or pnpm:

```bash
npm install tiny-date
```

```bash
yarn add tiny-date
```

```bash
pnpm add tiny-date
```

## Usage

```javascript
import tinyDate from 'tiny-date';

// Accepts Date objects, timestamps, or ISO date strings
tinyDate(Date.now() - 5000);                // "just now"
tinyDate(Date.now() - 60 * 1000 * 5);       // "5 minutes ago"
tinyDate(new Date('2023-01-01'));           // "1 year ago"

// Future dates
tinyDate(Date.now() + 60 * 1000 * 60 * 2);  // "in 2 hours"

# tiny-date

A lightweight, zero-dependency library for formatting dates relative to now (e.g., `"5 minutes ago"`, `"in 2 days"`).

## Features

- **Tiny:** Less than 1KB gzipped.
- **Zero dependencies:** Powered by the native `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` API.
- **TypeScript ready:** Includes built-in type definitions.
- **Internationalization:** Supports any locale supported by the browser or Node.js.

## Installation

```bash
npm install tiny-date
```

```bash
yarn add tiny-date
```

```bash
pnpm add tiny-date
```

## Quick Start

```javascript
import { formatRelative } from 'tiny-date';

const fiveMinutesAgo = new Date(Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000);
console.log(formatRelative(fiveMinutesAgo));
// => "5 minutes ago"

const inTwoDays = new Date(Date.now() + 2 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000);
console.log(formatRelative(inTwoDays));
// => "in 2 days"
```

## API

### `formatRelative(date, [options])`

Formats a date relative to the current time (or a custom base date).

#### Parameters

- **`date`** (`Date | number | string`): The target date to format. Accepts a `Date` object, a Unix timestamp (in milliseconds), or a date string.
- **`options`** (`Object`, optional): Configuration options.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `now` | `Date \| number` | `Date.now()` | The reference date to compare against. |
| `locale` | `string` | `'en'` | A BCP 47 language tag (e.g., `'es'`, `'fr'`, `'ja'`). |
| `style` | `'long' \| 'short' \| 'narrow'` | `'long'` | The length of the formatted output (e.g., `'in 1 month'` vs `'in 1 mo.'`). |

## Examples

### Localization

```javascript
import { formatRelative } from 'tiny-date';

const yesterday = Date.now() - 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;

formatRelative(yesterday, { locale: 'en' }); // => "yesterday"
formatRelative(yesterday, { locale: 'es' }); // => "ayer"
formatRelative(yesterday, { locale: 'fr' }); // => "hier"
```

### Short & Narrow Styles

```javascript
import { formatRelative } from 'tiny-date';

const threeHoursAgo = Date.now() - 3 * 60 * 60 * 1000;

formatRelative(threeHoursAgo, { style: 'long' });   // => "3 hours ago"
formatRelative(threeHoursAgo, { style: 'short' });  // => "3 hr. ago"
formatRelative(threeHoursAgo, { style: 'narrow' }); // => "3h ago"
```

### Custom Reference Date

```javascript
import { formatRelative } from 'tiny-date';

const target = new Date('2025-01-01');
const base = new Date('2025-01-10');

formatRelative(target, { now: base }); // => "9 days ago"
```

## Browser & Node.js Support

`tiny-date` relies on [`Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Intl/RelativeTimeFormat), which is supported in all modern browsers and Node.js 12+.

# flak

**A fast, opinionated YAML linter for humans and CI pipelines.**

`flak` catches syntax errors, formatting inconsistencies, and common YAML pitfalls before they break your deployments. It works out of the box with sensible defaults and can be tailored to your team's style guide.

---

## Features

- **Blazing fast**: Lints thousands of files in milliseconds.
- **Auto-fix**: Automatically resolve formatting issues with `--fix`.
- **Zero-config defaults**: Useful immediately, configurable when you need it.
- **Multiple output formats**: Human-readable, JSON, and SARIF (for GitHub Code Scanning).
- **Inline ignores**: Disable specific rules on a per-line or per-file basis.

---

## Installation

### Homebrew (macOS & Linux)
```bash
brew install flak
```

### Cargo (Rust)
```bash
cargo install flak-cli
```

### Pre-built Binaries
Download the latest release for your platform from the [Releases](https://github.com/your-org/flak/releases) page, or use the install script:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://flak.dev/install.sh | sh
```

---

## Usage

Lint a single file:
```bash
flak config.yaml
```

Lint an entire directory recursively:
```bash
flak ./k8s/
```

Automatically fix formatting issues:
```bash
flak --fix .
```

Output results as JSON:
```bash
flak --format json ./workflows/
```

### CLI Options

| Flag | Short | Description |
| :--- | :---: | :--- |
| `--fix` | `-f` | Automatically fix fixable lint errors |
| `--config <PATH>` | `-c` | Path to a custom configuration file |
| `--format <FMT>` | | Output format: `stylish` (default), `json`, `sarif`, `compact` |
| `--strict` | `-s` | Treat warnings as errors (non-zero exit code) |
| `--quiet` | `-q` | Only report errors, suppress warnings |
| `--version` | `-V` | Print version information |
| `--help` | `-h` | Print help information |

---

## Configuration

`flak` automatically looks for a `.flak.yaml` (or `.flak.yml`) file in the current directory or any parent directory.

### Example `.flak.yaml`

```yaml
extends: default

ignore:
  - "node_modules/**"
  - "vendor/**"
  - "*.generated.yaml"

rules:
  indentation:
    spaces: 2
    indent-sequences: true
  line-length:
    max: 100
    level: warning
  trailing-spaces: error
  truthy:
    allowed-values: ["true", "false"]
  key-duplicates: error
  empty-lines:
    max: 2
```

### Inline Disabling

You can disable rules for specific lines or blocks using comments:

```yaml
# flak:disable-next-line line-length
description: "This is a very long description that exceeds the configured maximum line length limit."

# flak:disable truthy
legacy_flag: yes
# flak:enable truthy
```

---

## CI/CD Integration

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
name: Lint YAML

on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  flak:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install flak
        run: curl -fsSL https://flak.dev/install.sh | sh
      - name: Run flak
        run: flak --strict .
```

---

## Exit Codes

- `0`: No errors found (warnings may be present unless `--strict` is used).
- `1`: One or more lint errors found.
- `2`: Invalid CLI arguments or configuration file error.

---

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome! Please read our [Contributing Guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) before submitting a pull request.

## License

MIT © [Your Name / Organization](LICENSE)

Lint all YAML files in the current directory:

flak .
```

Lint specific files or directories:

```

| Flag | Description |
| :--- | :--- |

Example `.flak.yaml`:

```yaml
ignore:

  - "vendor/**"

rules:
  indentation:
    spaces: 2
    indent-sequences: true
  line-length:
    max: 100
    level: warning
  trailing-spaces: error
  key-duplicates: error
  truthy:
    allowed-values: ["true", "false"]

```

Lint an entire directory recursively:

Options:
  -c, --config <FILE>    Path to a custom configuration file

  -q, --quiet            Only output errors, suppress warnings
  -h, --help             Print help
  -V, --version          Print version

`flak` works out of the box with sensible defaults. To customize its behavior, create a `.flak.yaml` file in your project root:

  - "dist/"

rules:

    level: error
    spaces: 2
  line-length:
    level: warn

  duplicate-keys: error
  trailing-spaces: error
  truthy-values:

  key-ordering: off
```

| Rule | Description | Auto-fixable |

Lint a single file:

flak config.yaml

Options:
  -c, --config <FILE>    Path to a custom configuration file
  -f, --format <FORMAT>  Output format [default: pretty] [possible values: pretty, compact, json, github]
      --fix              Automatically fix fixable issues
      --strict           Treat warnings as errors (exit code 1)
  -q, --quiet            Only output errors, suppress warnings
  -h, --help             Print help
  -V, --version          Print version
```

### Example Output

```text
config/deployment.yml
  12:5   error    Duplicate key "replicas" found                    key-duplicates
  18:81  warning  Line exceeds maximum length of 80 characters      line-length
  24:1   error    Expected indentation of 2 spaces, found 4         indentation

✖ 3 problems (2 errors, 1 warning)
  1 error potentially fixable with the `--fix` option.
```

## Configuration

`flak` automatically looks for a `.flak.yml` (or `.flak.yaml`) file in the current directory or any parent directory.

Example `.flak.yml`:

```yaml
# Paths to ignore (supports glob patterns)
ignore:
  - "node_modules/**"
  - "charts/**/templates/**"
  - "*.generated.yml"

# Rule configurations: "off", "warn", or "error"
rules:
  indentation:
    level: error
    spaces: 2

  line-length:
    level: warn
    max: 100

  key-duplicates: error
  trailing-spaces: error
  truthy:
    level: warn
    allowed-values: ["true", "false"]
```

## Built-in Rules

| Rule | Description | Fixable |
| :--- | :--- | :---: |
| `indentation` | Enforces consistent indentation spaces. | ✅ |
| `trailing-spaces` | Disallows trailing whitespace at the end of lines. | ✅ |
| `new-line-at-end-of-file` | Requires a single newline at the end of files. | ✅ |
| `key-duplicates` | Disallows duplicate keys within the same mapping. | ❌ |
| `line-length` | Enforces a maximum line length. | ❌ |
| `truthy` | Disallows ambiguous boolean values (e.g., `yes`, `no`, `on`, `off`). | ❌ |
| `empty-lines` | Limits consecutive empty lines. | ✅ |

## CI/CD Integration

### GitHub Actions

Use `--format github` to get inline annotations on your Pull Requests:

```yaml
name: Lint YAML

on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  flak:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install flak
        run: brew install flak
      - name: Run flak
        run: flak --format github .
```

# 🐾 paw

A lightweight, accessible React component library built around 12 essential UI primitives.

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/paw.svg?style=flat-square)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/paw)
[![bundle size](https://img.shields.io/bundlephobia/minzip/paw?style=flat-square)](https://bundlephobia.com/package/paw)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/paw.svg?style=flat-square)](./LICENSE)

**paw** gives you just enough structure to build clean interfaces without fighting a massive framework. No heavy runtime, no complex configuration—just 12 small, composable building blocks.

---

## ✨ Features

- **Tiny footprint:** Tree-shakeable and lightweight with zero external runtime dependencies.
- **Accessible by default:** Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with full keyboard navigation and focus management.
- **TypeScript-first:** Strictly typed props with exported interfaces for every primitive.
- **Easy to theme:** Styled with plain CSS custom properties—override variables or bring your own classes.

---

## 📦 Installation

```bash
npm install paw
# or
yarn add paw
# or
pnpm add paw
```

Import the base stylesheet once in your application's entry point (e.g., `main.tsx` or `_app.tsx`):

```tsx
import 'paw/styles.css';
```

---

## 🚀 Quick Start

```tsx
import { Stack, Avatar, Text, Badge, Button } from 'paw';

export function UserCard() {
  return (
    <Stack direction="row" align="center" gap="md">
      <Avatar src="/luna.jpg" alt="Luna" fallback="LU" />
      <Stack gap="xs">
        <Stack direction="row" align="center" gap="xs">
          <Text weight="bold">Luna</Text>
          <Badge variant="success">Online</Badge>
        </Stack>
        <Text size="sm" muted>
          Frontend Engineer
        </Text>
      </Stack>
      <Button variant="primary" size="sm" onClick={() => alert('Hi!')}>
        Message
      </Button>
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

---

## 🧩 The 12 Primitives

| Component | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| **`Box`** | A polymorphic layout container supporting spacing, display, and surface props. |
| **`Stack`** | Flexbox helper for arranging children horizontally or vertically with consistent gaps. |
| **`Divider`** | A horizontal or vertical hairline separator. |
| **`Text`** | Typographic primitive for headings, body copy, and captions with semantic `as` support. |
| **`Badge`** | Compact status indicator or label pill. |
| **`Avatar`** | User profile image with automatic initials fallback. |
| **`Button`** | Accessible button with variants (`primary`, `secondary`, `ghost`), sizes, and loading states. |
| **`Input`** | Styled text input supporting icons, error states, and native HTML attributes. |
| **`Checkbox`** | Accessible checkbox with support for checked, unchecked, and indeterminate states. |
| **`Switch`** | Toggle control for binary settings. |
| **`Spinner`** | Lightweight, CSS-animated loading indicator. |
| **`Tooltip`** | Floating label triggered on hover or keyboard focus. |

---

## 🎨 Theming

`paw` uses CSS custom properties for all design tokens. Override them in your own CSS to match your brand:

```css
:root {
  --paw-color-primary: #2563eb;
  --paw-color-primary-hover: #1d4ed8;
  --paw-radius-md: 8px;
  --paw-font-sans: 'Inter', system-ui, sans-serif;
}
```

Dark mode is supported out of the box via `[data-theme="dark"]` or `prefers-color-scheme: dark`.

---

## 🤝 Contributing

Contributions are welcome! Please read our [Contributing Guide](./CONTRIBUTING.md) before submitting a pull request.

```bash
# Clone the repo
git clone https://github.com/your-org/paw.git

# Install dependencies
pnpm install

# Start Storybook / dev server
pnpm dev

# Run tests
pnpm test
```

---

MIT © [paw contributors](./LICENSE)

# tiny-date

Tiny, dependency-free date formatting for humans.

```js
import { formatRelative } from "tiny-date";

formatRelative(new Date(Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000));
// "5 minutes ago"

formatRelative(new Date(Date.now() + 2 * 60 * 60 * 1000));
// "in 2 hours"
```

- Formats past and future dates relative to now
- Localized output using `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`
- Zero dependencies
- Works in modern browsers and Node.js
- Includes TypeScript definitions

## Installation

```sh
npm install tiny-date
```

## Usage

```js
import { formatRelative } from "tiny-date";

const fiveMinutesAgo = new Date(Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000);
const tomorrow = new Date(Date.now() + 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000);

formatRelative(fiveMinutesAgo); // "5 minutes ago"
formatRelative(tomorrow);       // "in 1 day"
```

Pass a locale for localized output:

```js
formatRelative(fiveMinutesAgo, { locale: "de" });
// "vor 5 Minuten"

formatRelative(tomorrow, { locale: "fr" });
// "dans 1 jour"
```

### Deterministic output

Provide `now` when rendering on a server, taking snapshots, or writing tests:

```js
const now = new Date("2025-01-01T12:00:00Z");

formatRelative("2025-01-01T11:55:00Z", { now });
// "5 minutes ago"
```

## API

### `formatRelative(date, options?)`

Returns a localized string describing `date` relative to the current time.

#### `date`

Accepts a `Date`, a Unix timestamp in milliseconds, or a date string supported by the JavaScript `Date` parser.

```js
formatRelative(Date.now() - 60_000); // "1 minute ago"
formatRelative("2025-01-01", { now: new Date("2025-01-02") }); // "yesterday"
```

An invalid date throws a `RangeError`.

#### Options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `now` | `Date \| number` | `Date.now()` | Reference time |
| `locale` | `string \| string[]` | Runtime locale | Locale passed to `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` |
| `numeric` | `"auto" \| "always"` | `"auto"` | Use phrases such as `"yesterday"` when available |

```js
formatRelative(yesterday, { numeric: "always" });
// "1 day ago"
```

### Ranges

tiny-date chooses the largest appropriate unit:

| Elapsed time | Example output |
| --- | --- |
| Less than 45 seconds | `just now` |
| Less than 45 minutes | `5 minutes ago` |
| Less than 22 hours | `3 hours ago` |
| Less than 26 days | `4 days ago` |
| Less than 11 months | `2 months ago` |
| Otherwise | `2 years ago` |

Future dates use the same ranges: `in 5 minutes`, `in 3 hours`, and so on.

## CommonJS

```js
const { formatRelative } = require("tiny-date");

console.log(formatRelative(Date.now() - 30_000));
// "just now"
```

## Requirements

A JavaScript runtime with support for `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`. No polyfills are included.

## Contributing

Issues and pull requests are welcome. Please include tests for bug fixes and new behavior.

```sh
npm install
npm test
```

## License

# tiny-date

Tiny, dependency-free relative date formatting for JavaScript.

Turn timestamps into human-friendly strings like **“5 minutes ago”**, **“in 2 hours”**, and **“yesterday”**.

## Features

- Past and future dates
- Seconds through years
- Automatic singular/plural handling
- Localization via `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`
- TypeScript types included
- No runtime dependencies

## Installation

```sh
npm install tiny-date
```

## Usage

```js
import { formatRelative } from 'tiny-date';

const now = Date.now();

formatRelative(now - 5 * 60 * 1000);
// "5 minutes ago"

formatRelative(now + 2 * 60 * 60 * 1000);
// "in 2 hours"

formatRelative(now - 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000);
// "yesterday"
```

Both `Date` objects and Unix timestamps in milliseconds are supported:

```js
formatRelative(new Date('2025-01-15T11:55:00Z'), {
  now: new Date('2025-01-15T12:00:00Z'),
});
// "5 minutes ago"
```

Passing `now` is especially useful for tests and server-side rendering.

## API

### `formatRelative(date, options?)`

Returns a localized string describing `date` relative to the current time.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `date` | `Date \| number` | The date to format. Numbers are milliseconds since the Unix epoch. |
| `options.now` | `Date \| number` | Reference time. Defaults to `Date.now()`. |
| `options.locale` | `string \| string[]` | Locale passed to `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`. Defaults to the runtime locale. |
| `options.numeric` | `'auto' \| 'always'` | Use `"yesterday"` when `'auto'`, or `"1 day ago"` when `'always'`. Defaults to `'auto'`. |

#### Examples

```js
formatRelative(date, { locale: 'fr' });
// "il y a 5 minutes"

formatRelative(now - 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000, { numeric: 'always' });
// "1 day ago"

formatRelative(now + 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000, { numeric: 'always' });
// "in 1 day"
```

An invalid date or timestamp throws a `TypeError`.

## Formatting behavior

`tiny-date` selects an appropriate unit based on the elapsed time:

| Difference | Example output |
| --- | --- |
| Seconds | `"30 seconds ago"` |
| Minutes | `"5 minutes ago"` |
| Hours | `"in 2 hours"` |
| Days | `"yesterday"` |
| Months | `"3 months ago"` |
| Years | `"in 2 years"` |

Relative calculations use timestamps, so elapsed time is not affected by time-zone display settings. Date-string parsing is intentionally left to the caller to avoid ambiguous input.

## Keeping timestamps updated

Formatted strings do not update automatically. Re-render them when needed—for example, once per minute in a UI:

```js
const timestamp = document.querySelector('[data-created-at]');
const createdAt = Number(timestamp.dataset.createdAt);

function update() {
  timestamp.textContent = formatRelative(createdAt);
}

update();
const interval = setInterval(update, 60_000);

// Call clearInterval(interval) when the component is removed.
```

## Requirements

`tiny-date` requires an environment with support for [`Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Intl/RelativeTimeFormat).

## Contributing

Issues and pull requests are welcome.

```sh
npm install
npm test
npm run build
```

Please include tests for bug fixes and new behavior.

## License

MIT

# flak

A fast, configurable CLI linter for YAML files. Use `flak` to catch syntax errors, enforce consistent formatting, and keep configuration files maintainable.

## Features

- Validate YAML syntax and detect duplicate keys
- Enforce indentation, line length, spacing, and document style
- Lint files, directories, glob patterns, or standard input
- Configure rules per project with `.flak.yaml`
- Automatically fix supported formatting issues
- Output results as human-readable text, JSON, or GitHub annotations
- Return CI-friendly exit codes

## Installation

`flak` requires Python 3.9 or later.

Install with [`pipx`](https://pipx.pypa.io/):

```sh
pipx install flak
```

Alternatively, install it in a virtual environment:

```sh
python -m pip install flak
```

Verify the installation:

```sh
flak --version
```

## Quick start

Lint a file:

```sh
flak deployment.yaml
```

Recursively lint a directory:

```sh
flak config/
```

Lint multiple paths or glob patterns:

```sh
flak deployment.yaml 'charts/**/*.yaml' .github/workflows/
```

Automatically fix supported formatting violations:

```sh
flak --fix config/
```

Example output:

```text
deployment.yaml
  4:5    error    Duplicate key "replicas"       duplicate-keys
  12:1   warning  Line exceeds 100 characters    line-length
  18:9   error    Expected 2 spaces, found 4     indentation

✖ 3 problems (2 errors, 1 warning)
```

## Usage

```text
flak [OPTIONS] [PATHS...]
```

If no paths are provided, `flak` lints the current directory. YAML files are identified by their `.yaml` or `.yml` extension.

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-c, --config PATH` | Use a specific configuration file |
| `-f, --format FORMAT` | Output format: `stylish`, `json`, or `github` |
| `-o, --output PATH` | Write results to a file instead of stdout |
| `--fix` | Fix supported formatting violations in place |
| `--no-ignore` | Lint files matched by ignore patterns |
| `--stdin-filename PATH` | Filename to use when reading from stdin |
| `-q, --quiet` | Suppress warnings; report errors only |
| `-h, --help` | Show help |
| `--version` | Show the installed version |

To lint standard input:

```sh
cat deployment.yaml | flak --stdin-filename deployment.yaml -
```

## Configuration

`flak` looks for `.flak.yaml` in the current directory and its parents. You can also specify a configuration file with `--config`.

```yaml
extends: recommended

rules:
  indentation:
    severity: error
    spaces: 2
  line-length:
    severity: warning
    max: 100
  trailing-spaces: error
  document-start: off

ignore:
  - .git/**
  - vendor/**
  - '**/templates/**'
```

Rule severities are `error`, `warning`, and `off`. Command-line options take precedence over configuration-file settings.

### Rules

The recommended configuration enables syntax validation and common correctness checks.

| Rule | Description | Fixable |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `duplicate-keys` | Disallow duplicate mapping keys | No |
| `empty-values` | Disallow empty values unless explicitly allowed | No |
| `indentation` | Enforce consistent indentation | Yes |
| `line-length` | Limit line length | No |
| `trailing-spaces` | Disallow trailing whitespace | Yes |
| `new-line-at-end-of-file` | Require a final newline | Yes |
| `document-start` | Require or forbid the `---` document marker | Yes |
| `quoted-strings` | Enforce the configured quoting style | No |
| `truthy` | Restrict ambiguous values such as `yes` and `on` | No |

YAML syntax errors are always reported and cannot be disabled.

### Inline suppression

Disable a rule for the current line:

```yaml
# flak:disable-line line-length
description: This intentionally long line contains generated content.
```

Disable a rule for the next line:

```yaml
# flak:disable-next-line empty-values
optional_value:
```

Disable and re-enable rules for a block:

```yaml
# flak:disable indentation
special_block:
    key: value
# flak:enable indentation
```

Suppressions should be used sparingly and include only the rules that need to be disabled.

## Continuous integration

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
name: Lint

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  yaml:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'
      - run: python -m pip install flak
      - run: flak --format github .
```

The `github` output format emits workflow annotations for supported violations.

### JSON output

```sh
flak --format json --output flak-results.json .
```

JSON output is useful for custom reporters and build-system integrations. `flak` writes diagnostics to the selected output destination and operational errors to stderr.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | No errors were found; warnings may still be present |
| `1` | Lint errors or invalid YAML were found |
| `2` | Invalid arguments, configuration, or another operational failure |

When `--fix` is used, the exit code reflects the violations remaining after fixes are applied.

## Development

# flak

`flak` is a small, configurable command-line linter for YAML files. It catches syntax errors, duplicate keys, and common formatting problems before they reach code review or CI.

## Features

- Validates YAML syntax
- Detects duplicate mapping keys
- Checks indentation, tabs, trailing whitespace, and final newlines
- Recursively lints `.yaml` and `.yml` files
- Supports stdin, custom configuration, and automatic style fixes
- Produces human-readable, JSON, or GitHub Actions output
- Respects `.gitignore` by default

## Installation

Download a prebuilt binary from the [releases page](https://github.com/flak-dev/flak/releases), or install with Go:

```sh
go install github.com/flak-dev/flak/cmd/flak@latest
```

Verify the installation:

```sh
flak --version
```

## Usage

```sh
flak [flags] [paths...]
```

Lint the current directory:

```sh
flak
```

Lint specific files or directories:

```sh
flak config.yaml deploy/ .github/workflows/
```

Read YAML from stdin:

```sh
cat config.yaml | flak -
```

Example output:

```text
config.yaml
  4:3   error    FLAK002  duplicate mapping key "port"
  8:17  warning  FLAK005  trailing whitespace

✖ 2 problems (1 error, 1 warning)
```

### Automatic fixes

Fix supported style violations in place:

```sh
flak --fix .
```

Only formatting issues are fixed automatically. Syntax errors and duplicate keys must be corrected manually.

### Output formats

```sh
flak --format stylish .
flak --format json .
flak --format github .
```

Use `--format github` in GitHub Actions to create inline annotations.

## Configuration

Create a default configuration file:

```sh
flak --init
```

`flak` searches for `.flak.yaml` in the current directory and then in parent directories. You can also specify a file explicitly:

```sh
flak --config path/to/flak.yaml .
```

Example `.flak.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  indentation:
    enabled: true
    spaces: 2
  line-length:
    enabled: true
    max: 100
  document-start:
    enabled: false

ignore:
  - vendor/**
  - "**/*.generated.yaml"
```

Command-line flags override configuration-file values. To lint without loading a configuration file, use `--no-config`.

## Rules

| Rule | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `syntax` | Error | Reports invalid YAML syntax |
| `duplicate-keys` | Error | Reports duplicate keys in a mapping |
| `indentation` | Error | Checks consistent space-based indentation |
| `tabs` | Error | Disallows tab characters used for indentation |
| `trailing-whitespace` | Warning | Reports whitespace at the end of lines |
| `final-newline` | Warning | Requires a newline at the end of each file |
| `line-length` | Disabled | Enforces a configurable maximum line length |
| `document-start` | Disabled | Requires `---` at the start of each document |

## Ignoring files and lines

Add patterns to the `ignore` list in `.flak.yaml`, or pass them directly:

```sh
flak --ignore 'vendor/**' --ignore '*.generated.yaml' .
```

Disable a rule for the next line:

```yaml
# flak-disable-next-line line-length
url: https://example.com/a/very/long/url/that/is/intentional
```

Disable rules for an entire file by placing a comment near the top:

```yaml
# flak-disable-file trailing-whitespace final-newline
```

## Command-line options

```text
--config PATH       Use a specific configuration file
--no-config         Do not load a configuration file
--format FORMAT     Output format: stylish, json, or github
--fix               Fix supported violations in place
--ignore PATTERN    Ignore matching paths; may be repeated
--no-gitignore      Do not respect .gitignore files
--strict            Treat warnings as errors
--init              Create a default .flak.yaml
-v, --verbose       Enable verbose output
-h, --help          Show help
--version           Show the installed version
```

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | No violations, or only warnings without `--strict` |
| `1` | Lint violations were found |
| `2` | Invalid arguments, configuration errors, or unreadable input |

## CI

Add `flak` to your build to prevent invalid YAML from being merged:

```sh
flak --format stylish --strict .
```

For GitHub Actions:

```yaml
- name: Lint YAML
  run: flak --format github --strict .
```

## Contributing

Bug reports, feature requests, and pull requests are welcome. Before submitting a change, run the test suite and lint the project:

```sh
go test ./...
flak .
```

## License

MIT
```

````markdown
# flak

**flak** is a fast, configurable command-line linter for YAML files. It catches syntax errors, duplicate keys, indentation problems, and common formatting issues before they reach production.

## Features

- Lints `.yaml` and `.yml` files, including multi-document streams
- Recursively scans directories while respecting `.gitignore`
- Supports human-readable, JSON, and GitHub Actions output
- Reads YAML from standard input
- Applies safe automatic fixes for whitespace issues
- Supports project configuration and inline rule suppression
- Preserves comments, key order, and scalar values

## Installation

Install with Cargo:

```sh
cargo install flak --locked
```

Alternatively, download a prebuilt binary for your platform from the releases page and place it somewhere on your `PATH`.

Verify the installation:

```sh
flak --version
```

## Quick start

Lint every YAML file in the current directory:

```sh
flak
```

Lint specific files or directories:

```sh
flak deployment.yaml charts/ .github/workflows/
```

Read from standard input:

```sh
cat deployment.yaml | flak -
```

Example output:

```text
charts/app/values.yaml
  18:9   error    mapping values are not allowed here       syntax
  42:1   warning  line is 137 characters long; maximum is 120  line-length

✖ 2 problems (1 error, 1 warning)
```

## Usage

```text
flak [OPTIONS] [PATH]...

Arguments:
  [PATH]...  Files or directories to lint, or "-" for stdin [default: .]

Options:
  -c, --config <FILE>       Use a specific configuration file
      --fix                 Apply safe fixes in place
  -f, --format <FORMAT>     Output format: stylish, json, or github
                            [default: stylish]
      --no-ignore           Do not respect .gitignore or configured excludes
      --max-warnings <N>    Fail when more than N warnings are reported
  -q, --quiet               Only report errors
  -h, --help                Print help
  -V, --version             Print version
```

Directories are searched recursively for files ending in `.yaml` or `.yml`.

## Configuration

flak searches the current directory and its parents for `.flak.yaml` or `.flak.yml`. Use `--config` to load a configuration file explicitly.

```yaml
# .flak.yaml
rules:
  duplicate-keys: error

  indentation:
    level: error
    spaces: 2

  line-length:
    level: warn
    max: 120

  trailing-spaces: error
  final-newline: error
  document-start: off

exclude:
  - "vendor/**"
  - "**/*.j2"
```

Exclude patterns are relative to the directory containing the configuration file. Command-line options take precedence over configuration values.

### Rules

Rules can be set to `off`, `warn`, or `error`. Rules with additional options accept a mapping containing `level`.

| Rule | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `syntax` | `error` | Reports invalid YAML. This rule cannot be disabled. |
| `duplicate-keys` | `error` | Reports duplicate keys within a mapping. |
| `no-tabs` | `error` | Disallows tab characters in indentation. |
| `indentation` | `error`, 2 spaces | Checks block indentation for consistency. |
| `line-length` | `off` | Limits line length; `max` defaults to 120 when enabled. |
| `trailing-spaces` | `error` | Disallows whitespace at the end of a line. Fixable. |
| `final-newline` | `error` | Requires a newline at the end of the file. Fixable. |
| `document-start` | `off` | Requires each YAML document to begin with `---`. |

## Inline suppression

Disable a rule for the next line:

```yaml
# flak:disable-next-line line-length
homepage: "https://example.com/a/very/long/path/that/does/not/need/to/be/wrapped"
```

Disable and re-enable a rule within a file:

```yaml
# flak:disable line-length
# Long generated values can go here.
# flak:enable line-length
```

To disable all non-syntax rules for a file, place this comment before the first document:

```yaml
# flak:disable-file
```

## Automatic fixes

Apply safe fixes in place:

```sh
flak --fix .
```

flak only fixes rules explicitly marked as fixable. It never reorders keys, rewrites values, normalizes unrelated formatting, or removes comments. Review changes with your version-control system before committing them.

## Continuous integration

Fail on errors or any warnings:

```sh
flak --max-warnings 0 .
```

For GitHub Actions annotations:

```yaml
- name: Lint YAML
  run: flak --format github --max-warnings 0 .
```

To generate a machine-readable report:

```sh
flak --format json . > flak-report.json
```

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | No errors were found, and the warning limit was not exceeded. |
| `1` | Lint errors were found, or the warning limit was exceeded. |
| `2` | flak could not run because of invalid arguments, configuration, or I/O errors. |

## Development

Build and test from source:

```sh
cargo build
cargo test
cargo run -- .
```

Before submitting a change, run:

```sh
cargo fmt --check
cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features
cargo test
```

## License

flak is available under the MIT License. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) for details.
````

# flak

A fast, configurable command-line linter for YAML files.

`flak` catches invalid syntax, duplicate keys, and common formatting problems before they reach CI or production. It works with files, directories, and standard input, and supports both human-readable and machine-readable output.

## Features

- Validates YAML syntax, including multi-document files
- Detects duplicate keys, invalid indentation, trailing whitespace, and long lines
- Recursively lints `.yaml` and `.yml` files
- Supports per-rule severity levels: `off`, `warning`, and `error`
- Reads configuration from `.flak.yaml`
- Excludes files using `.flakignore`
- Outputs `stylish`, `json`, or GitHub Actions annotations
- Never modifies your files

## Installation

Install with Cargo:

```sh
cargo install flak
```

Or install from a local checkout:

```sh
cargo install --path .
```

## Quick start

Create a default configuration file:

```sh
flak init
```

Lint the current directory:

```sh
flak .
```

Example output:

```text
deploy.yaml
  4:3    error    duplicate-keys   Key "replicas" is already defined
  18:101 warning  line-length      Line is 112 characters long; maximum is 100

✖ 2 problems (1 error, 1 warning)
```

## Usage

```text
flak [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...
```

If no paths are provided, `flak` lints the current directory.

```sh
# Lint specific files
flak deployment.yaml service.yml

# Lint a directory recursively
flak config/

# Treat warnings as errors
flak --strict .

# Produce JSON output
flak --format json .

# Produce GitHub Actions annotations
flak --format github .

# Read YAML from standard input
cat deployment.yaml | flak -

# Provide a filename for configuration and diagnostics
cat deployment.yaml | flak --stdin-filename deployment.yaml -
```

### Options

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-c, --config <FILE>` | Use a specific configuration file |
| `-f, --format <FORMAT>` | Output format: `stylish`, `json`, or `github` |
| `--strict` | Treat warnings as errors |
| `--stdin-filename <FILE>` | Filename to use when reading from standard input |
| `--no-ignore` | Include files excluded by ignore rules |
| `-q, --quiet` | Only print errors |
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose diagnostic output |
| `-h, --help` | Show help |
| `-V, --version` | Show the installed version |

## Configuration

`flak` searches for `.flak.yaml` in the current directory and its parent directories. Use `--config` to select a configuration file explicitly.

```yaml
version: 1

files:
  ignore:
    - vendor/**
    - "**/generated/*.yaml"

rules:
  duplicate-keys: error

  indentation:
    level: error
    spaces: 2

  line-length:
    level: warning
    max: 100

  trailing-spaces: error
  new-line-at-end-of-file: error
  document-start: off
  empty-values: off
```

Rules can use a severity shorthand:

```yaml
rules:
  trailing-spaces: warning
  document-start: off
```

Or an expanded form when additional settings are needed:

```yaml
rules:
  line-length:
    level: error
    max: 120
```

### Rules

| Rule | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `duplicate-keys` | `error` | Disallow duplicate keys in a mapping |
| `indentation` | `error` | Require consistent space-based indentation |
| `line-length` | `warning` | Limit line length; defaults to 100 characters |
| `trailing-spaces` | `error` | Disallow whitespace at the end of lines |
| `new-line-at-end-of-file` | `error` | Require a final newline |
| `document-start` | `off` | Require `---` at the start of each document |
| `empty-values` | `off` | Disallow mapping keys with empty values |

YAML syntax validation is always enabled.

## Ignoring files

Add patterns to `.flakignore` using gitignore-style syntax:

```gitignore
vendor/
.tmp/
**/generated/*.yaml
charts/**/templates/*.yaml
```

The `.git` directory is always ignored. Use `--no-ignore` to lint files that would otherwise be excluded.

## Continuous integration

`flak` returns a nonzero exit status when linting fails, making it suitable for CI pipelines.

Example GitHub Actions workflow:

```yaml
name: Lint

on:
  push:
  pull_request:

jobs:
  yaml:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - run: cargo install flak --locked
      - run: flak --format github --strict .
```

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | No errors; warnings are allowed unless `--strict` is used |
| `1` | Lint errors, invalid YAML, or warnings treated as errors |
| `2` | Invalid command-line arguments or configuration |

## Development

Build and test from source:

```sh
cargo build
cargo test
```

Run the development binary:

```sh
cargo run -- .
```

Contributions are welcome. Please include tests for new rules and keep diagnostics clear, actionable, and stable.

## License

Licensed under the MIT License. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) for details.
````

# flak

A fast, configurable YAML linter for people who would rather catch mistakes locally than in production.

`flak` checks YAML files for syntax errors, inconsistent formatting, and common configuration pitfalls. It works with individual files, directories, standard input, and CI pipelines.

## Features

- Validates YAML syntax
- Detects duplicate keys, invalid indentation, and ambiguous values
- Enforces configurable formatting rules
- Supports `.yaml` and `.yml` files
- Recursively lints directories while respecting `.gitignore`
- Provides human-readable, JSON, and GitHub Actions output
- Uses a single optional `.flak.yaml` configuration file
- Returns CI-friendly exit codes

## Installation

Install with Cargo:

```sh
cargo install flak
```

Or download a prebuilt binary from the [releases page](https://github.com/example/flak/releases) and place it somewhere on your `PATH`.

Verify the installation:

```sh
flak --version
```

## Usage

Lint specific files:

```sh
flak config.yaml deploy.yml
```

Recursively lint the current directory:

```sh
flak .
```

Lint multiple directories:

```sh
flak config/ manifests/
```

Read YAML from standard input:

```sh
cat config.yaml | flak -
```

When linting standard input, provide a filename so configuration and ignore rules can be resolved correctly:

```sh
cat config.yaml | flak --stdin-filename config.yaml -
```

### Command-line options

```text
Usage: flak [OPTIONS] <PATH>...

Arguments:
  <PATH>...  Files or directories to lint; use "-" for standard input

Options:
  -c, --config <FILE>       Use a specific configuration file
      --no-config           Disable configuration file discovery
      --format <FORMAT>     Output format: stylish, json, or github
                            [default: stylish]
      --deny-warnings       Treat warnings as errors
      --no-ignore           Do not respect ignore files
  -q, --quiet               Only print errors
  -v, --verbose             Print each file as it is checked
  -h, --help                Print help
  -V, --version             Print version
```

## Example output

```text
config.yaml
  4:7   error    duplicate-key  Key "replicas" is already defined
  9:1   warning  line-length    Line is 97 characters long; maximum is 80
  12:5  error    indentation    Expected 2 spaces, found 4

✖ 3 problems (2 errors, 1 warning)
```

## Configuration

`flak` searches the current directory and its parents for `.flak.yaml`. If no configuration file is found, it uses the default rules.

Example `.flak.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  indentation:
    level: error
    spaces: 2
  line-length:
    level: warning
    max: 100
  duplicate-keys: error
  trailing-spaces: error
  document-start: off
  truthy:
    level: warning
    allowed-values: ["true", "false"]
  empty-values: off

ignore:
  - vendor/**
  - "**/*.generated.yaml"
```

Use a configuration file from another location:

```sh
flak --config path/to/flak.yaml .
```

### Rules

| Rule | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `indentation` | `error` | Enforces consistent space-based indentation |
| `line-length` | `warning` | Limits line length; defaults to 80 characters |
| `duplicate-keys` | `error` | Reports keys defined more than once in a mapping |
| `trailing-spaces` | `error` | Disallows whitespace at the end of lines |
| `document-start` | `off` | Requires or forbids the `---` document marker |
| `truthy` | `warning` | Flags ambiguous values such as `yes`, `no`, `on`, and `off` |
| `empty-values` | `off` | Reports mapping values left empty |

Rules can be set to `off`, `warning`, or `error`:

```yaml
rules:
  line-length: off
  duplicate-keys: error
```

## Ignoring files

By default, `flak` respects `.gitignore` and patterns in the `ignore` section of `.flak.yaml`.

To lint files regardless of ignore rules:

```sh
flak --no-ignore .
```

To disable a rule for a single line, add an inline comment:

```yaml
password: "yes" # flak:disable-line truthy
```

To disable rules for the next line:

```yaml
# flak:disable-next-line line-length
description: "An intentionally long value that should not trigger the line-length rule."

name: Lint

  push:

```

The `github` format emits workflow annotations, allowing problems to appear directly on pull requests.

For machine-readable output in other systems:

```sh

```

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | No errors were found |
| `1` | Lint errors were found, or warnings were treated as errors |
| `2` | Invalid arguments, unreadable input, or another runtime failure |

```sh

cd flak

```

Run `flak` against its own YAML fixtures:

```sh
cargo run -- tests/fixtures
```

Bug reports, rule proposals, and pull requests are welcome. Please include a minimal YAML example when reporting a parsing or linting issue.

## License

Licensed under the [MIT License](LICENSE).

## Features

- Validate YAML syntax and detect duplicate keys
- Check indentation, trailing whitespace, line length, document markers, and empty values
- Lint individual files, directories, multiple YAML documents, or stdin
- Respect `.gitignore` and `.flakignore` files
- Apply safe formatting fixes with `--fix`
- Output results as text, JSON, or GitHub Actions annotations
- Configure rules and severity levels through `.flak.yaml`
- Return CI-friendly exit codes

## Installation

Install with Cargo:

```sh
cargo install flak
```

Or install from a source checkout:

```sh
cargo install --path .
```

Verify the installation:

```sh
flak --version
```

## Quick start

Lint a file:

```sh
flak deployment.yaml
```

Recursively lint all `.yaml` and `.yml` files in a directory:

```sh
flak config/
```

Lint the current project:

```sh
flak .
```

Example output:

```text
config/deployment.yaml
  12:5   error    indentation    expected 2 spaces, found 4
  28:1   warning  line-length    line is 113 characters; maximum is 100

```

```

Lint several paths:

```sh
flak charts/ .github/workflows/ docker-compose.yaml
```

Apply safe automatic fixes:

```sh
flak --fix .
```

Use a specific configuration file:

```sh
flak --config ci/flak.yaml .
```

Write JSON results to a file:

```sh
flak --format json . > flak-results.json
```

Read YAML from stdin:

```sh
cat deployment.yaml | flak --stdin-filename deployment.yaml -
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--config <FILE>` | Use a specific configuration file |
| `--format <FORMAT>` | Output format: `text`, `json`, or `github`; defaults to `text` |
| `--fix` | Apply safe fixes in place |
| `--no-ignore` | Do not respect `.gitignore` or `.flakignore` files |
| `--stdin-filename <FILE>` | Filename to use when reading from stdin |
| `-q`, `--quiet` | Suppress output when no violations are found |
| `-h`, `--help` | Show help |
| `-V`, `--version` | Show the installed version |

## Configuration

`flak` searches the current directory and its ancestors for `.flak.yaml`. If no configuration file is found, built-in defaults are used. Use `--config` to bypass configuration discovery.

Example `.flak.yaml`:

```yaml
ignore:
  - "vendor/**"
  - "**/*.j2"

rules:
  key-duplicates: error

  indentation:
    level: error
    spaces: 2

  trailing-spaces: error

  line-length:
    level: warning
    max: 100

  document-start: off
  empty-values: warning
```

| Rule | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `key-duplicates` | Report duplicate keys in the same mapping |
| `indentation` | Enforce a consistent number of indentation spaces |
| `trailing-spaces` | Report whitespace at the end of a line |
| `line-length` | Report lines longer than the configured maximum |
| `document-start` | Require or forbid the `---` document marker |
| `empty-values` | Report keys with an empty value |

Directory scans respect `.gitignore`. Additional patterns can be placed in `.flakignore`, with one glob per line:

**/generated/**

Blank lines and lines beginning with `#` are ignored.

`--fix` only applies changes that preserve the YAML document's meaning, such as correcting indentation or removing trailing whitespace.

```sh

  document-start:
    level: off

  key-duplicates:
    level: error

  empty-values:
    level: warning

  truthy:
    level: warning
    allowed:
      - "true"
      - "false"
```

Each rule can be disabled or assigned a severity:

```yaml
rules:
  line-length: off
  trailing-spaces: warning
  key-duplicates: error
```

## Rules

| Rule | Default severity | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `indentation` | `error` | Checks indentation width and rejects tab indentation |
| `line-length` | `warning` | Reports lines longer than the configured limit |
| `trailing-spaces` | `error` | Reports whitespace at the end of a line |
| `document-start` | `off` | Requires or forbids the `---` document marker |
| `key-duplicates` | `error` | Detects duplicate mapping keys |
| `empty-values` | `warning` | Reports keys with empty values |
| `truthy` | `warning` | Flags ambiguous boolean-like values such as `yes`, `no`, `on`, and `off` |

YAML syntax errors are always reported, regardless of rule configuration.

## Inline suppression

Disable a rule for the next line:

```yaml
# flak:disable-next-line line-length
description: This intentionally long value is kept on one line for compatibility.
```

Disable one or more rules for an entire file:

```yaml
# flak:disable-file line-length, empty-values
```

Suppressions should be used sparingly and include an explanation when the reason is not obvious.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | No errors were found |
| `1` | Lint errors were found, or warnings exceeded the configured policy |
| `2` | Invalid arguments, configuration errors, or unreadable input |

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
name: lint

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - run: python -m pip install flak
      - run: flak --format github .
```

The `github` format emits workflow annotations so findings appear directly on affected lines.

### Pre-commit

Add `flak` to `.pre-commit-config.yaml`:

```yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/example/flak
    rev: v0.1.0
    hooks:
      - id: flak
```

Then install and run the hooks:

```sh
pre-commit install
pre-commit run flak --all-files
```

## Development

Clone the repository and install development dependencies:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/example/flak.git
cd flak
python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"
```

Run the test suite:

```sh
pytest
```

Run formatting and static checks:

```sh
ruff format --check .
ruff check .
```

Bug reports and pull requests are welcome. Please include a minimal YAML example when reporting a parsing or linting issue.

- Supports configurable rules and per-file overrides
- Lints files, directories, or standard input
- Produces human-readable, JSON, or GitHub Actions output
- Respects `.gitignore` by default
- Uses exit codes suitable for scripts and CI pipelines
- Never modifies your files

## Installation

Download the latest binary for your platform from the [releases page](./releases), then place it somewhere on your `PATH`.

To build from source:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/example/flak.git
cd flak
make install
```

Verify the installation:

```sh
flak --version
```

## Quick start

Lint a file:

```sh
flak config.yaml
```

Lint every YAML file in the current directory:

```sh
flak .
```

Lint specific files and directories:

```sh
flak config.yaml deploy/ charts/
```

Read from standard input:

```sh
cat config.yaml | flak -
```

Example output:

```text
config.yaml:4:3  error  duplicate-keys  key "replicas" is already defined
config.yaml:8:1  warning  line-length    line is 124 characters; maximum is 100

2 problems (1 error, 1 warning)
```

## Usage

```text
flak [OPTIONS] [PATH...]
```

If no paths are provided, `flak` lints the current directory. Use `-` to read from standard input.

### Options

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-c, --config <FILE>` | Use a specific configuration file |
| `-f, --format <FORMAT>` | Output format: `stylish`, `json`, or `github` |
| `-q, --quiet` | Show errors only |
| `--no-ignore` | Do not respect `.gitignore` files |
| `--ext <EXTENSIONS>` | Comma-separated file extensions; default: `.yaml,.yml` |
| `--max-warnings <N>` | Fail when more than `N` warnings are reported |
| `--no-color` | Disable colored output |
| `-h, --help` | Show help |
| `-v, --version` | Show version information |

Examples:

```sh
# Produce machine-readable output
flak --format json .

# Treat more than three warnings as a failure
flak --max-warnings 3 .

# Include files that would normally be ignored
flak --no-ignore .
```

## Configuration

`flak` searches the current directory and its parents for `.flak.yaml` or `.flak.yml`. You can also specify a configuration file with `--config`.

```yaml
# .flak.yaml
ignore:
  - "vendor/**"
  - "**/generated/*.yaml"

rules:
  syntax: error
  duplicate-keys: error
  tabs: error
  trailing-spaces: warning

  indentation:
    level: error
    spaces: 2

  line-length:
    level: warning
    max: 100

  document-start: off
  empty-values: warning
  truthy:
    level: warning
    allowed: ["true", "false"]
```

Rules can be set to `error`, `warning`, or `off`. Rules with additional options accept a `level` property.

### Rules

| Rule | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `syntax` | `error` | Reports invalid YAML syntax |
| `duplicate-keys` | `error` | Disallows duplicate mapping keys |
| `tabs` | `error` | Disallows tab characters in indentation |
| `indentation` | `error` | Enforces consistent indentation |
| `trailing-spaces` | `warning` | Reports trailing whitespace |
| `line-length` | `warning` | Enforces a maximum line length |
| `document-start` | `off` | Requires `---` at the start of each document |
| `empty-values` | `warning` | Reports keys with empty values |
| `truthy` | `warning` | Reports ambiguous values such as `yes`, `no`, `on`, and `off` |

Disable a rule for the next line:

```yaml
# flak-disable-next-line line-length
description: This intentionally long value is allowed by the inline override.
```

Disable one or more rules for a section:

```yaml
# flak-disable empty-values
optional_value:
# flak-enable empty-values
```

To disable all rules, omit the rule names:

```yaml
# flak-disable
legacy_yaml: yes
# flak-enable
```

```yaml
name: Lint

on:

  pull_request:

jobs:

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

The `github` output format creates annotations for reported problems.

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | No errors were found, and the warning limit was not exceeded |

- Supports multi-document YAML files
- Recursively lints directories while respecting `.gitignore`
- Produces human-readable, JSON, GitHub Actions, and SARIF output
- Configurable per project, with per-rule severity levels
- Fails CI only when you want it to, with optional warning strictness

## Installation

### Homebrew

```sh
brew install flak
```

### Go

```sh
go install github.com/flak-dev/flak/cmd/flak@latest
```

### From source

```sh
git clone https://github.com/flak-dev/flak.git
cd flak
make install
```

Verify the installation:

```sh
flak --version
```

## Quick start

Lint a file:

```sh
flak deployment.yaml
```

Lint several files or an entire directory:

```sh
flak config.yaml charts/ manifests/
```

Lint standard input:

```sh
cat deployment.yaml | flak -
```

Example output:

```text
deployment.yaml
  8:5   error    duplicate-key      key "replicas" is already defined
  12:18 warning  truthy             use "true" or "false" instead of "yes"
  16:1   error    indentation        expected 2 spaces, found 4

✖ 3 problems (2 errors, 1 warning)
```

By default, warnings do not cause a nonzero exit status. Use `--strict` to treat warnings as failures:

```sh
flak --strict .
```

## Usage

```text
flak [options] [path ...]

Arguments:
  path                    Files or directories to lint. Use "-" for stdin.
                          Defaults to the current directory.

Options:
  -c, --config <file>     Use a specific configuration file
      --format <format>   Output format: stylish, json, github, or sarif
      --strict            Treat warnings as errors
      --no-ignore         Do not respect ignore files
      --quiet             Only report errors
      --color <mode>      Color output: auto, always, or never
  -h, --help              Show help
  -v, --version           Show version
```

Examples:

```sh
# Emit machine-readable diagnostics
flak --format json .

# Generate annotations in GitHub Actions
flak --format github .

# Use a configuration outside the current project
flak --config ci/flak.yaml manifests/

# Include files matched by ignore files
flak --no-ignore generated/
```

When linting directories, `flak` includes files ending in `.yaml` and `.yml`.

## Configuration

`flak` searches the current directory and its parents for one of:

- `.flak.yaml`
- `.flak.yml`
- `flak.yaml`
- `flak.yml`

You can also pass a configuration explicitly with `--config`.

Example `.flak.yaml`:

```yaml
extends: default

exclude:
  - vendor/**
  - .terraform/**
  - "**/*.generated.yaml"

rules:
  indentation:
    spaces: 2

  line-length:
    max: 100
    level: warning

  truthy:
    level: warning

  key-ordering: off
```

Command-line options take precedence over configuration files.

### Rules

| Rule | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `syntax` | Reports invalid YAML syntax | `error` |
| `duplicate-key` | Disallows duplicate mapping keys | `error` |
| `indentation` | Enforces consistent space-based indentation | `error`, 2 spaces |
| `line-length` | Limits line length | `warning`, 120 characters |
| `trailing-spaces` | Disallows whitespace at the end of lines | `error` |
| `final-newline` | Requires a newline at the end of each file | `error` |
| `truthy` | Warns about ambiguous values such as `yes` and `on` | `warning` |
| `empty-values` | Warns about keys with implicit null values | `off` |
| `key-ordering` | Requires mapping keys to be alphabetically ordered | `off` |

A rule can be configured with a severity:

```yaml
rules:
  line-length: off
  truthy: warning
  duplicate-key: error
```

Or with severity and rule-specific options:

```yaml
rules:
  indentation:
    level: error
    spaces: 4

  line-length:
    level: warning
    max: 80
```

Supported severity levels are `off`, `warning`, and `error`.

Add glob patterns to `.flakignore`:

```gitignore

dist/
**/*.generated.yaml
charts/**/templates/
```

Patterns are relative to the directory containing `.flakignore`. `flak` also respects `.gitignore` unless `--no-ignore` is supplied.

To suppress a rule for the next line, use an inline comment:

```yaml
# flak-disable-next-line line-length

```

To disable a rule for an entire file:

```yaml
# flak-disable truthy
enabled: yes

```yaml

  pull_request:

```yaml

```sh

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | No errors were found |
| `1` | Lint errors were found, or warnings were found with `--strict` |
| `2` | Invalid arguments, configuration errors, or file-reading failures |

Generate completions for your shell:

```sh

```

  8:5   error   duplicate-key    Key "replicas" is already defined
  14:9  warning truthy           Use an explicit boolean instead of "yes"
  22:1  warning line-length      Line is 143 characters; maximum is 120

✖ 3 problems (1 error, 2 warnings)
```

## Usage

```text
flak [flags] [paths...]
```

If no paths are provided, `flak` lints the current directory.

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-c, --config <file>` | Use a specific configuration file |
| `--fix` | Fix safe issues in place |
| `-f, --format <format>` | Output format: `text`, `json`, or `github` |
| `--severity <level>` | Report only issues at or above `warning` or `error` |
| `-q, --quiet` | Suppress output when no problems are found |
| `--no-color` | Disable colored output |
| `--list-rules` | List available rules and their default settings |
| `-h, --help` | Show help |
| `-v, --version` | Show the installed version |

### JSON output

```sh
flak --format json .
```

JSON output is stable and intended for editor integrations and other tooling.

### GitHub Actions annotations

```sh
flak --format github .
```

This emits workflow commands that display lint findings directly on the relevant lines in pull requests.

## Configuration

`flak` looks for `.flak.yaml` or `.flak.yml` in the current directory, then searches parent directories. Use `--config` to specify a file explicitly.

Example `.flak.yaml`:

```yaml
files:
  include:
    - "**/*.yaml"
    - "**/*.yml"
  exclude:
    - ".git/**"
    - "vendor/**"
    - "**/*.template.yaml"

rules:
  syntax: error
  duplicate-key: error
  indentation:
    severity: warning
    spaces: 2
  line-length:
    severity: warning
    max: 120
  trailing-spaces: warning
  truthy:
    severity: warning
    allowed:
      - "true"
      - "false"
  document-start:
    severity: off
```

A rule can be set to `error`, `warning`, or `off`. Rules with additional options use a mapping with a `severity` field.

## Rules

| Rule | Description | Fixable |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `syntax` | Reports invalid YAML | No |
| `duplicate-key` | Reports keys defined more than once in a mapping | No |
| `indentation` | Checks indentation width and rejects tab indentation | Yes |
| `line-length` | Checks maximum line length | No |
| `trailing-spaces` | Reports whitespace at the end of lines | Yes |
| `truthy` | Reports ambiguous values such as `yes`, `no`, `on`, and `off` | No |
| `document-start` | Checks for a leading `---` document marker | Yes |

Run `flak --list-rules` for the complete list supported by your installed version.

## Suppressing findings

Disable a rule for the next line:

```yaml
# flak-disable-next-line line-length
description: This is an intentionally long generated value that should not be wrapped.
```

Disable multiple rules:

```yaml
# flak-disable-next-line line-length, truthy
example: yes
```

Disable a rule for the remainder of a file:

```yaml
# flak-disable document-start
```

Suppression comments do not hide YAML syntax errors.

## Automatic fixes

```sh
flak --fix .
```

Only rules marked as fixable are changed. `flak` preserves comments and avoids semantic rewrites. Review changes with your version-control system before committing them.

To check formatting in CI, run without `--fix`.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | No findings at or above the requested severity |
| `1` | Lint findings were reported |
| `2` | Invalid arguments, configuration errors, or file I/O errors |

## CI example

```yaml
name: lint

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  yaml:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install flak
        run: go install github.com/flak-dev/flak/cmd/flak@latest
      - name: Lint YAML
        run: flak --format github .
```

## License

MIT

# flak

`flak` is a fast, configurable linter for YAML files. It catches syntax errors, duplicate keys, inconsistent formatting, and common configuration mistakes before they reach CI or production.

## Features

- Lint individual files, directories, or standard input
- Detect invalid YAML and duplicate mapping keys
- Enforce indentation, line length, whitespace, and document style
- Configure rules with `.flak.yaml`
- Exclude files using glob patterns
- Human-readable, JSON, and GitHub Actions output
- Respect `.gitignore` by default
- Return CI-friendly exit codes

## Installation

### Homebrew

```sh
brew install flak-cli/tap/flak
```

### Go

```sh
go install github.com/flak-cli/flak/cmd/flak@latest
```

### Binary releases

Download a prebuilt binary from the [releases page](https://github.com/flak-cli/flak/releases), then place it somewhere on your `PATH`.

Verify the installation:

```sh
flak --version
```

## Quick start

Lint the current directory recursively:

```sh
flak .
```

Lint specific files or directories:

```sh
flak config.yaml deploy/ .github/workflows/
```

Read YAML from standard input:

```sh
cat config.yaml | flak -
```

Example output:

```text
deploy.yaml:12:5: error: duplicate key "replicas" [key-duplicates]
deploy.yaml:18:101: warning: line is 104 characters long [line-length]

2 problems (1 error, 1 warning)
```

## Usage

```text
flak [flags] [paths...]
```

If no paths are provided, `flak` lints the current directory. Files ending in `.yaml` or `.yml` are checked automatically.

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-c, --config <path>` | Use a specific configuration file |
| `-f, --format <format>` | Output format: `text`, `json`, or `github` |
| `--strict` | Treat warnings as errors |
| `--no-ignore` | Do not respect `.gitignore` files |
| `-q, --quiet` | Print only diagnostics |
| `-v, --verbose` | Print linted files and configuration details |
| `-h, --help` | Show help |
| `--version` | Show the installed version |

### Output formats

Text output is intended for local development:

```sh
flak --format text .
```

JSON output is suitable for scripts and other tools:

```sh
flak --format json .
```

GitHub output creates workflow annotations:

```sh
flak --format github .
```

## Configuration

`flak` searches the current directory and its parents for `.flak.yaml` or `.flak.yml`. You can also specify a configuration file explicitly:

```sh
flak --config ci/flak.yaml .
```

Example `.flak.yaml`:

```yaml
version: 1

rules:
  key-duplicates: true
  indentation:
    spaces: 2
  line-length:
    max: 100
  trailing-spaces: true
  final-newline: true
  document-start: false
  truthy:
    allowed:
      - "true"
      - "false"

exclude:
  - vendor/**
  - .terraform/**
  - "**/*.j2"
```

Exclude patterns are relative to the configuration file's directory. Explicitly named files are linted even when they match an exclude pattern.

## Rules

Rules can be enabled with `true`, disabled with `false`, or configured with a mapping.

| Rule | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key-duplicates` | Enabled | Reports duplicate keys in the same mapping |
| `indentation` | 2 spaces | Enforces consistent space-based indentation |
| `line-length` | 100 characters | Reports lines longer than the configured maximum |
| `trailing-spaces` | Enabled | Reports whitespace at the end of lines |
| `final-newline` | Enabled | Requires a newline at the end of each file |
| `document-start` | Disabled | Requires or forbids the `---` document marker |
| `truthy` | Enabled | Reports ambiguous boolean-like values such as `yes` and `on` |

YAML syntax errors are always reported and cannot be disabled.

### Disable rules inline

Disable a rule for the current line:

```yaml
description: "A deliberately long value" # flak:disable-line line-length
```

Disable a rule for the next line:

```yaml
# flak:disable-next-line line-length
description: "A deliberately long value that would otherwise be reported"
```

Disable all rules for a file:

```yaml
# flak:disable-file
```

Multiple rules can be separated by commas:

```yaml
# flak:disable-next-line line-length, truthy
```

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | No errors were found |
| `1` | Lint errors were found, or warnings were found with `--strict` |
| `2` | `flak` could not run because of invalid arguments, configuration, or I/O errors |

## Continuous integration

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
name: lint

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  yaml:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: flak-cli/setup-flak@v1
      - run: flak --format github .
```

### Other CI systems

```sh
flak --strict .
```

A nonzero exit code fails the job when lint errors are found.

## Development

Clone the repository and run the test suite:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/flak-cli/flak.git
cd flak
go test ./...
```

Build the CLI locally:

```sh
go build -o flak ./cmd/flak
./flak --help
```

Contributions are welcome. Please include tests for new rules and update the documentation when changing CLI or configuration behavior.

`flak` is available under the [MIT License](LICENSE).
