# tiny-date

> A tiny, dependency-free library that formats dates relative to now — `"5 minutes ago"`, `"in 2 days"`, `"just now"`.

```
~700 bytes minified + gzipped
```

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/badge/npm-v1.0.0-blue)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/tiny-date)
[![bundle size](https://img.shields.io/badge/size-700%20B-brightgreen)](https://bundlephobia.com/package/tiny-date)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](./LICENSE)

---

## Why another date library?

`tiny-date` does one thing: turn a `Date` into human-friendly relative time. No parsing, no timezones, no formatting tokens, no 40 KB of locale data. If you need calendar math, use something else. If you need `"3 hours ago"` in your UI, this is it.

- **Tiny** — ~700 B gzipped, zero dependencies
- **Tree-shakeable** — ESM first, CJS still works
- **TypeScript** — ships with its own types
- **Locale-aware** — `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` under the hood, with a fast fallback
- **Testable** — inject your own `now` for deterministic snapshots

---

## Installation

```bash
npm install tiny-date
```

```bash
pnpm add tiny-date
```

```bash
yarn add tiny-date
```

---

## Quick start

```js
import { timeAgo } from 'tiny-date';

const fiveMinutesAgo = new Date(Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000);

timeAgo(fiveMinutesAgo);
// "5 minutes ago"

timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() + 2 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000));
// "in 2 days"

timeAgo(new Date());
// "just now"
```

---

## Usage

### Basic

```js
import { timeAgo } from 'tiny-date';

timeAgo('2024-01-01T12:00:00Z'); // accepts Date, string, or timestamp
timeAgo(1704110400000);
timeAgo(new Date(2024, 0, 1));
```

### Compact style

```js
timeAgo(date, { style: 'short' });
// "5 min ago"

timeAgo(date, { style: 'narrow' });
// "5m ago"
```

### Locales

```js
timeAgo(date, { locale: 'de' });
// "vor 5 Minuten"

timeAgo(date, { locale: 'ja' });
// "5 分前"
```

### Deterministic output (great for tests)

```js
const now = new Date('2024-06-01T12:00:00Z');

timeAgo('2024-06-01T11:55:00Z', { now });
// "5 minutes ago"
```

### Custom locale strings

```js
timeAgo(date, {
  locale: {
    past: '{value} ago',
    future: 'in {value}',
    now: 'just now',
    units: {
      minute: 'minute|minutes',
      hour: 'hour|hours',
      // ...
    },
  },
});
```

---

## API

### `timeAgo(input, options?)`

Formats `input` relative to `options.now` (defaults to `Date.now()`).

**Parameters**

| Name      | Type                          | Description                                              |
| --------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `input`   | `Date \| string \| number`    | The date to format. Invalid input throws a `TypeError`.  |
| `options` | `TimeAgoOptions`              | Optional configuration (see below).                      |

**Returns** `string`

### `TimeAgoOptions`

| Option     | Type                                | Default      | Description                                                                 |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------- | ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `now`      | `Date \| number`                    | `Date.now()` | Reference point. Useful for tests and server rendering.                     |
| `locale`   | `string \| LocaleDefinition`        | `'en'`       | BCP 47 tag (e.g. `'fr'`, `'pt-BR'`) or a custom locale object.              |
| `style`    | `'long' \| 'short' \| 'narrow'`     | `'long'`     | Output verbosity. Mirrors `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` styles.                 |
| `maxUnits` | `number`                            | `1`          | How many units to include. `2` gives `"1 hour 5 minutes ago"`.              |
| `rounding` | `'floor' \| 'round' \| 'ceil'`      | `'round'`    | Rounding strategy for the unit value.                                       |

### Thresholds

Units are chosen by the largest unit whose threshold is met:

| Range                    | Unit      | Example            |
| ------------------------ | --------- | ------------------ |
| < 45 seconds             | second    | `"30 seconds ago"` |
| < 90 seconds             | minute    | `"1 minute ago"`   |
| < 45 minutes             | minute    | `"20 minutes ago"` |
| < 90 minutes             | hour      | `"1 hour ago"`     |
| < 22 hours               | hour      | `"5 hours ago"`    |
| < 36 hours               | day       | `"1 day ago"`      |
| < 25 days                | day       | `"12 days ago"`    |
| < 45 days                | month     | `"1 month ago"`    |
| < 11 months              | month     | `"6 months ago"`   |
| < 18 months              | year      | `"1 year ago"`     |
| otherwise                | year      | `"3 years ago"`    |

Anything within ±5 seconds of `now` renders as the locale's `now` string (`"just now"` in English).

---

## Examples

### React

```jsx
import { timeAgo } from 'tiny-date';

function Timestamp({ date }) {
  return <time dateTime={date.toISOString()}>{timeAgo(date)}</time>;
}
```

### Live-updating list

```js
// Re-render every 30 seconds so relative times stay fresh
setInterval(() => renderList(), 30_000);
```

### Server-side rendering

Pass a fixed `now` so the server and client agree on the output:

```js
const now = new Date();
const html = items.map((i) => timeAgo(i.createdAt, { now })).join('');
```

---

## Browser & runtime support

Works anywhere `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` is available (all modern browsers, Node 14+). On older runtimes it falls back to a built-in English-only formatter, so you always get a string back.

- Chrome 71+
- Firefox 65+
- Safari 14+
- Edge 79+
- Node.js 14+

---

## TypeScript

Types are bundled — no `@types/tiny-date` needed.

```ts
import { timeAgo, type TimeAgoOptions } from 'tiny-date';

const opts: TimeAgoOptions = { style: 'short', locale: 'en-GB' };
const label: string = timeAgo(new Date(), opts);
```

---

## Contributing

Issues and PRs are welcome. A few ground rules:

1. Keep the bundle small. If a change adds more than ~100 B gzipped, open an issue first.
2. Add a test for anything you change. `npm test` runs the full suite.
3. Run `npm run size` before opening a PR.

```bash

cd tiny-date
npm install
npm test
```

---

| `now`        | `Date`     | `new Date()` | The reference "now" date. Useful for testing.         |
| `locale`     | `object`   | English   | Custom strings for localization (see [Localization](#localization)). |
| `rounding`   | `string`   | `'round'` | One of `'round'`, `'floor'`, or `'ceil'`.                |
| `maxUnit`    | `string`   | `'year'`  | Largest unit to use. One of `'second'`, `'minute'`, `'hour'`, `'day'`, `'week'`, `'month'`, `'year'`. |

**Returns:** `string`

**Examples**

```js
timeAgo(Date.now() - 10_000);              // "10 seconds ago"
timeAgo(Date.now() - 90_000);              // "2 minutes ago"
timeAgo(Date.now() - 3 * 60 * 60 * 1000);  // "3 hours ago"
timeAgo(Date.now() - 2 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000); // "2 days ago"
timeAgo('2020-01-01');                     // "4 years ago"
```

### `timeUntil(date, options?)`

Convenience wrapper that always returns future-facing strings.

```js
import { timeUntil } from 'tiny-date';

timeUntil(Date.now() + 60_000); // "in 1 minute"
```

---

## Localization

Pass a `locale` object to override any of the default strings. Unspecified keys fall back to English.

```js
timeAgo(Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000, {
  locale: {
    past: (value, unit) => `hace ${value} ${unit}`,
    future: (value, unit) => `en ${value} ${unit}`,
    units: {
      minute: 'minuto',
      minutes: 'minutos',
      // ...
    },
  },
});
// "hace 5 minutos"
```

See the [`locales`](./locales) directory for community-contributed translations.

---

## Supported Units

tiny-date picks the largest applicable unit for readability:

| Range             | Output example       |
| ----------------- | -------------------- |
| < 45 seconds      | `"just now"`         |
| < 90 seconds      | `"1 minute ago"`     |
| < 45 minutes      | `"N minutes ago"`    |
| < 90 minutes      | `"1 hour ago"`       |
| < 22 hours        | `"N hours ago"`      |
| < 36 hours        | `"1 day ago"`        |
| < 7 days          | `"N days ago"`       |
| < 4 weeks         | `"N weeks ago"`      |
| < 11 months       | `"N months ago"`     |
| otherwise         | `"N years ago"`      |

---

## Browser Support

tiny-date works in all modern browsers and Node.js 14+. It uses the built-in `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` where available, with a lightweight fallback for older environments.

---

## TypeScript

Type definitions are bundled with the package. No `@types/tiny-date` needed.

```ts
import { timeAgo } from 'tiny-date';

const label: string = timeAgo(new Date());
```

---

3. Commit your changes (`git commit -m 'feat: add my feature'`)

5. Open a Pull Request

runs.prompt: Write a README.md for a small open-source library called 'tiny-date' that formats dates relative to now (e.g., '5 minutes ago').
runs.output:
# tiny-date

> Format dates relative to now — `"5 minutes ago"`, `"in 2 days"` — in under 1 kB.

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/tiny-date.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/tiny-date)
[![bundle size](https://img.shields.io/bundlephobia/minzip/tiny-date)](https://bundlephobia.com/package/tiny-date)
[![build status](https://github.com/example/tiny-date/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/example/tiny-date/actions)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/tiny-date.svg)](./LICENSE)

`tiny-date` turns timestamps into human-readable relative strings. No dependencies, no `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` polyfills, no surprises.

```js
timeAgo(Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000); // "5 minutes ago"
timeAgo(Date.now() + 2 * 86400 * 1000); // "in 2 days"
```

---

## Features

- 🪶 **Tiny** — ~700 bytes minified + gzipped, tree-shakeable ESM
- 🧩 **Zero dependencies**
- 🌍 **Locale support** — ship only the locales you need
- 🔒 **TypeScript types** included
- 🧪 **Deterministic** — pass a `now` value for stable tests and SSR
- 🖥️ **Works everywhere** — Node 14+, all modern browsers, Deno, Bun

## Installation

```bash
npm install tiny-date
```

```bash
pnpm add tiny-date
# or
yarn add tiny-date
```

## Quick start

```js
import { timeAgo } from 'tiny-date';

timeAgo(new Date('2024-01-01T12:00:00Z'));
// => "3 years ago"
```

`timeAgo` accepts a `Date`, a timestamp (number), or an ISO 8601 string.

## Usage

### Relative to now

```js
import { timeAgo } from 'tiny-date';

timeAgo(Date.now() - 30 * 1000);       // "30 seconds ago"
timeAgo(Date.now() - 90 * 1000);       // "2 minutes ago"
timeAgo(Date.now() - 3 * 3600 * 1000); // "3 hours ago"
timeAgo(Date.now() - 10 * 86400 * 1000); // "last week"
```

### Future dates

Future dates are handled automatically and prefixed with `in`:

```js
timeAgo(Date.now() + 45 * 1000); // "in 45 seconds"
```

If you prefer an explicit API, use `timeUntil`, which is an alias with the same behavior:

```js
import { timeUntil } from 'tiny-date';

timeUntil(Date.now() + 86400 * 1000); // "in 1 day"
```

### Fixed reference point

Pass `now` to make output deterministic — useful for tests, snapshots, and server rendering:

```js
timeAgo('2024-03-01T00:00:00Z', { now: new Date('2024-03-01T00:05:00Z') });
// => "5 minutes ago"
```

### Thresholds

Control when the output switches from relative to absolute, and how coarse the rounding is:

```js
timeAgo(pastDate, {
  max: 'day',        // 'second' | 'minute' | 'hour' | 'day' | 'week' | 'month' | 'year'
  rounding: 'floor', // 'floor' | 'round' | 'ceil'
});
```

When a date exceeds `max`, `timeAgo` falls back to a short absolute format:

```js
timeAgo('2019-05-04T00:00:00Z', { max: 'week' });
// => "May 4, 2019"
```

Disable the fallback entirely with `fallback: false`, which returns the largest available unit (`"6 years ago"`).

## API

### `timeAgo(input, options?)`

Returns a relative time string for `input` compared to `options.now` (default: `Date.now()`).

| Option     | Type                                          | Default    | Description                                            |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `now`      | `Date \| number \| string`                    | `Date.now()` | Reference point to compare against.                  |
| `locale`   | `string \| Locale`                            | `'en'`     | Locale code or a locale object (see below).            |
| `max`      | `'second' \| 'minute' \| 'hour' \| 'day' \| 'week' \| 'month' \| 'year'` | `'year'` | Largest unit to express before falling back. |
| `rounding` | `'floor' \| 'round' \| 'ceil'`                | `'round'`  | How partial units are rounded.                         |
| `fallback` | `false \| (date: Date) => string`             | `undefined` | Custom absolute formatter, or `false` to disable.     |
| `numeric`  | `'always' \| 'auto'`                          | `'auto'`   | `'auto'` yields `"yesterday"`; `'always'` yields `"1 day ago"`. |

### `timeUntil(input, options?)`

Alias for `timeAgo` with identical behavior. Provided for readability at call sites.

### `registerLocale(code, locale)`

Register a custom locale globally.

```js
import { registerLocale, timeAgo } from 'tiny-date';

registerLocale('pirate', {
  units: {
    second: ['a blink ago', 'in a blink'],
    minute: ['%d min ago', 'in %d min'],
    hour: ['%d bells ago', 'in %d bells'],
    day: ['%d suns ago', 'in %d suns'],
    week: ['%d weeks ago', 'in %d weeks'],
    month: ['%d moons ago', 'in %d moons'],
    year: ['%d years ago', 'in %d years'],
  },
  now: 'just now',
  yesterday: 'yesterday',
  tomorrow: 'tomorrow',
});

timeAgo(Date.now() - 60000, { locale: 'pirate' }); // "1 min ago"
```

Each unit entry is a `[past, future]` pair. `%d` is replaced with the rounded count.

## Locales

English ships in the core bundle. Other locales are separate entry points so you only pay for what you import:

```js
import { timeAgo } from 'tiny-date';
import de from 'tiny-date/locales/de';

timeAgo(Date.now() - 3600 * 1000, { locale: de }); // "vor 1 Stunde"
```

Bundled locales: `de`, `es`, `fr`, `it`, `ja`, `ko`, `nl`, `pl`, `pt`, `ru`, `zh`.

Missing one? [Open a PR](#contributing) — locale files are ~20 lines each.

## TypeScript

Types are bundled; no `@types` package required.

```ts
import { timeAgo, type TimeAgoOptions } from 'tiny-date';

const opts: TimeAgoOptions = { max: 'day', rounding: 'floor' };
const label: string = timeAgo(Date.now() - 5000, opts);
```

## Browser (no bundler)

```html
<script type="module">
  import { timeAgo } from 'https://esm.sh/tiny-date';

  document.querySelectorAll('[data-timestamp]').forEach((el) => {
    el.textContent = timeAgo(el.dataset.timestamp);
  });
</script>
```

## Notes

- `timeAgo` is pure and synchronous. It does **not** update on its own — re-render on an interval if you need a live clock.
- Units use calendar-aware boundaries for months and years (a "month" is not a fixed 30 days).
- Inputs are parsed as UTC when given an ISO string without a timezone offset.

## Contributing

```bash
git clone https://github.com/example/tiny-date.git
cd tiny-date
npm install
npm test
```

Bug reports and locale additions are welcome. Please keep PRs focused — the whole point is that this stays tiny.

## License

[MIT](./LICENSE) © tiny-date contributors

# tiny-date

**A tiny (0.5kb), zero-dependency library to format dates as relative time strings (e.g., "5 minutes ago").**

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/tiny-date.svg?style=flat-square)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/tiny-date)
[![bundle size](https://img.shields.io/bundlephobia/minzip/tiny-date?style=flat-square)](https://bundlephobia.com/result?p=tiny-date)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/tiny-date.svg?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/yourusername/tiny-date/blob/main/LICENSE)

`tiny-date` takes the pain out of calculating time differences. Instead of showing a raw timestamp, give your users context with human-readable strings like "just now," "2 hours ago," or "in 3 days."

## Features

- 🪶 **Tiny:** Less than 0.5kb minified and gzipped.
- 🚫 **Zero Dependencies:** No bloat, just pure logic.
- ⏳ **Future & Past:** Handles both "ago" and "in" logic.
- 🌍 **Locale Friendly:** Basic customization for output strings.
- 📦 **Tree-shakeable:** Works with ESM and CommonJS.

## Installation

```bash
npm install tiny-date
# or
yarn add tiny-date
# or
pnpm add tiny-date
```

## Usage

### Basic Example

```javascript
import { timeAgo } from 'tiny-date';

const now = new Date();
const pastDate = new Date(now.getTime() - 5 * 60 * 1000); // 5 minutes ago

console.log(timeAgo(pastDate));
// Output: "5 minutes ago"

const futureDate = new Date(now.getTime() + 2 * 60 * 60 * 1000); // 2 hours in future

console.log(timeAgo(futureDate));
// Output: "in 2 hours"
```

### Custom Options

You can pass a configuration object as the second argument to customize the output.

```javascript
const date = new Date(Date.now() - 10000); // 10 seconds ago

// 1. Add a suffix/prefix manually (if you don't want default 'ago')
console.log(timeAgo(date, { suffix: true }));
// Output: "10 seconds ago"

// 2. Limit the granularity (round to nearest minute)
console.log(timeAgo(date, { round: 'minute' }));
// Output: "just now"
```

## API

### `timeAgo(date, [options])`

#### `date`
- **Type:** `Date` | `string` | `number`
- **Required:** Yes
- The date to format. Can be a Date object, an ISO string, or a timestamp.

#### `options` (Optional)

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `suffix` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether to append "ago" or prepend "in". |
| `round` | `'second' \| 'minute' \| 'hour'` | `'second'` | The smallest unit to display. |
| `locale` | `string` | `'en'` | Currently supports `'en'` (English) and `'es'` (Spanish). |

## Why tiny-date?

Many date libraries are massive and require complex immutable objects. `tiny-date` is designed for simple UI needs where you just need to show a label like "Updated 5 mins ago." It does one thing and does it well.

# tiny-date

> A tiny (less than 1KB) library to format dates as relative time strings like `"5 minutes ago"` or `"in 2 days"`.

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/tiny-date.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/tiny-date)
[![bundle size](https://img.shields.io/bundlephobia/minzip/tiny-date)](https://bundlephobia.com/package/tiny-date)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/tiny-date.svg)](https://github.com/yourusername/tiny-date/blob/main/LICENSE)
[![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-ready-blue)](https://www.typescriptlang.org/)

---

## Features

- 🪶 **Tiny** – less than 1KB gzipped, zero dependencies.
- 🌍 **Localizable** – built‑in English, easily add your own locale.
- ⏱️ **Smart** – handles both past and future dates (`"5 minutes ago"` / `"in 5 minutes"`).
- 🎛️ **Customizable** – tweak thresholds, rounding, and output format.
- 📦 **Tree‑shakable** – ESM and CJS builds, TypeScript types included.
- 🌐 **Works everywhere** – modern browsers, Node.js, Deno, Bun.

## Installation

```bash
npm install tiny-date
```

Or via CDN:

```html
<script type="module">
  import { timeAgo } from 'https://unpkg.com/tiny-date?module';
</script>
```

## Usage

```js
import { timeAgo } from 'tiny-date';

// Past
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000)); // "5 minutes ago"
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 3 * 60 * 60 * 1000)); // "3 hours ago"

// Future
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() + 2 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000)); // "in 2 days"

// With a custom "now"
timeAgo('2023-01-01', { now: new Date('2023-01-02') }); // "yesterday"
```

### Options

```js
timeAgo(date, {
  now: Date.now(),        // reference point (default: Date.now())
  locale: 'en',           // 'en' or a custom locale object (default: 'en')
  short: false,           // "5m ago" instead of "5 minutes ago" (default: false)
  round: 'round',         // 'floor' | 'ceil' | 'round' (default: 'round')
  thresholds: {           // custom thresholds (in seconds)
    minute: 60,
    hour: 3600,
    day: 86400,
    week: 604800,
    month: 2629800,       // 30.44 days
    year: 31557600,       // 365.25 days
  },
});
```

### Short format

```js
timeAgo(Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000, { short: true }); // "5m ago"
timeAgo(Date.now() + 2 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000, { short: true }); // "in 2d"
```

### Custom locale

```js
const fr = {
  past: (value, unit) => `il y a ${value} ${unit}`,
  future: (value, unit) => `dans ${value} ${unit}`,
  units: {
    second: 'seconde',
    minute: 'minute',
    hour: 'heure',
    day: 'jour',
    week: 'semaine',
    month: 'mois',
    year: 'année',
  },
  plural: (value, unit) => `${unit}s`, // optional pluralization
};

timeAgo(Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000, { locale: fr }); // "il y a 5 minutes"
```

## API

### `timeAgo(date, options?)`

Formats a date relative to `now`.

- **`date`** – `Date | string | number` – the date to format.
- **`options`** – optional object:
  - `now` – `Date | number` – reference point (default: `Date.now()`).
  - `locale` – `string | Locale` – locale code or custom locale object (default: `'en'`).
  - `short` – `boolean` – use short units like `"5m"` (default: `false`).
  - `round` – `'floor' | 'ceil' | 'round'` – rounding method (default: `'round'`).
  - `thresholds` – `object` – custom thresholds in seconds.

Returns a `string`.

## Browser Support

`tiny-date` uses `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` when available for automatic localization. For older browsers, it falls back to a built‑in English formatter. If you need to support very old environments (e.g. IE11), you can polyfill `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`.

runs.output:
# flak

> A fast, opinionated YAML linter for humans and CI pipelines.

`flak` catches syntax errors, style violations, and common footguns in your YAML files before they reach production. It's written in Rust, runs in milliseconds, and plays nicely with your existing tooling.

```
$ flak config/
config/deploy.yaml
  12:3   error    duplicate key "replicas"
  18:1   warning  trailing whitespace
  24:7   error    tab character in indentation

config/ci.yaml
   4:1   warning  document does not start with "---"
   9:5   error    inconsistent indentation (expected 2 spaces, found 4)

✖ 5 problems (3 errors, 2 warnings)
```

## Features

- **Syntax validation** — catches malformed YAML, duplicate keys, and invalid anchors/aliases
- **Style rules** — enforces consistent indentation, quoting, key ordering, and line endings
- **Schema validation** — validate against JSON Schema or a custom `.flak.yaml` schema
- **Fast** — parallel file traversal; lints thousands of files in under a second
- **Configurable** — per-project config with sensible defaults
- **CI-friendly** — machine-readable output, meaningful exit codes, GitHub Actions annotations
- **Zero config** — works out of the box with no setup

## Installation

### Homebrew (macOS / Linux)

```sh
brew install flak
```

### Cargo

```sh
cargo install flak
```

### Prebuilt binaries

Download the latest release for your platform from the [releases page](https://github.com/example/flak/releases).

### Docker

```sh
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/work" -w /work ghcr.io/example/flak:latest .
```

## Usage

```sh
flak [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...
```

Lint a single file:

```sh
flak config.yaml
```

Lint a directory recursively:

```sh
flak ./config
```

Lint everything in the current directory, respecting `.gitignore`:

```sh
flak .
```

Read from stdin:

```sh
cat config.yaml | flak -
```

### Common options

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-c, --config <FILE>` | Path to a config file (default: `.flak.yaml`) |
| `-f, --format <FMT>` | Output format: `pretty`, `json`, `sarif`, `github` (default: `pretty`) |
| `--fix` | Automatically fix fixable violations |
| `--no-ignore` | Do not respect `.gitignore` or `.flakignore` |
| `--max-warnings <N>` | Exit with an error if warnings exceed `N` |
| `-q, --quiet` | Only print errors |
| `-v, --verbose` | Print every file checked, including clean ones |
| `--stdin-filename <NAME>` | Filename to use when reading from stdin (for config matching) |

Run `flak --help` for the full list.

## Configuration

`flak` looks for a `.flak.yaml` file in the current directory, then walks up to the filesystem root. You can also point to a specific file with `--config`.

```yaml
# .flak.yaml
extends: flak:recommended

rules:
  indentation:
    spaces: 2
    style: consistent
  key-ordering:
    order: alphabetical
    ignore:
      - "on"
      - "jobs"
  line-length:
    max: 120
    severity: warning
  quoted-strings:
    quote-type: single
    required: only-when-needed
  trailing-whitespace: error
  document-start:
    present: true
  empty-values:
    forbid-in-block-mappings: true

ignore:
  - "vendor/**"
  - "**/generated/*.yaml"

overrides:
  - files: ["k8s/**/*.yaml"]
    rules:
      line-length: off
```

### Rule severities

Each rule can be set to one of:

- `off` — disable the rule
- `warning` — report but do not fail the run
- `error` — report and fail the run

### Inline suppression

Disable a rule for a single line or block:

```yaml
# flak:disable-next-line line-length
some_really_long_key: "and a really long value that would otherwise trip the linter"

# flak:disable quoted-strings
message: "this one is fine as-is"
# flak:enable quoted-strings
```

## Rules

`flak` ships with the following rules. See the [rules documentation](docs/rules.md) for details and examples.

| Rule | Default | Fixable |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `anchors` | error | no |
| `braces` | warning | yes |
| `brackets` | warning | yes |
| `colons` | warning | yes |
| `commas` | warning | yes |
| `comments` | warning | yes |
| `comments-indentation` | warning | yes |
| `document-end` | off | yes |
| `document-start` | warning | yes |
| `duplicate-keys` | error | no |
| `empty-lines` | warning | yes |
| `empty-values` | warning | no |
| `hyphens` | warning | yes |
| `indentation` | error | yes |
| `key-duplicates` | error | no |
| `key-ordering` | off | no |
| `line-length` | off | no |
| `new-line-at-end-of-file` | error | yes |
| `new-lines` | warning | yes |
| `octal-values` | error | no |
| `quoted-strings` | warning | yes |
| `schema` | off | no |
| `trailing-spaces` | warning | yes |
| `truthy` | warning | yes |

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | No errors (warnings may be present) |
| `1` | One or more errors found |
| `2` | Invalid usage or configuration error |
| `3` | Internal error |

## CI integration

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
- name: Lint YAML
  run: flak --format github .
```

The `github` format emits `::error` and `::warning` workflow commands, so violations appear inline on the pull request diff.

### GitLab CI

```yaml
lint:yaml:
  image: ghcr.io/example/flak:latest
  script:
    - flak --format json . > flak-report.json
  artifacts:
    when: always
    reports:
      codequality: flak-report.json
```

### Pre-commit

```yaml
# .pre-commit-config.yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/example/flak
    rev: v1.4.0
    hooks:
      - id: flak
```

## Auto-fixing

Many style rules can be fixed automatically:

```sh
flak --fix .
```

`flak` will rewrite files in place. Combine with `--dry-run` to preview changes:

```sh
flak --fix --dry-run .
```

## Performance

`flak` is designed to be fast enough to run on every save. On a 2023 MacBook Pro, linting the Kubernetes repository (~4,000 YAML files) takes roughly 180 ms with a warm cache.

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome. Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening a pull request.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/example/flak
cd flak
cargo test
cargo run -- tests/fixtures
```

## License

Licensed under either of [Apache License, Version 2.0](LICENSE-APACHE) or [MIT License](LICENSE-MIT) at your option.

```console
  9:1   warning  trailing whitespace                  no-trailing-spaces
  12:5  error    expected string, found integer       schema/type-mismatch
deploy/values.yaml
  ✓ clean

✗ 2 errors, 1 warning in 2 files (0.014s)
```

---

## Features

- **Syntax validation** — catches malformed indentation, unclosed quotes, tabs, and duplicate keys.
- **Style rules** — enforces consistent formatting (indentation width, line length, quoting, key ordering).
- **Schema validation** — validate against JSON Schema, Kubernetes CRDs, or custom rules.
- **Multi-document support** — handles `---` separated streams and anchors/aliases correctly.
- **Fast** — parallel file traversal; lints thousands of files in under a second.
- **CI-friendly** — machine-readable output, exit codes, and inline annotations for GitHub Actions and GitLab.
- **Configurable** — per-project `.flak.yaml` with rule overrides and ignore patterns.

---

## Installation

### Cargo

```sh
cargo install flak
```

### Homebrew

```sh
brew install flak
```

### Pre-built binaries

Download the latest release for your platform from the [releases page](https://github.com/example/flak/releases).

### Docker

```sh
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/work" ghcr.io/example/flak:latest /work
```

---

## Usage

```
flak [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...
```

Lint one or more files or directories. If no path is given, `flak` lints the current directory.

### Examples

Lint a single file:

```sh
flak config.yaml
```

Lint a directory recursively:

```sh
flak ./manifests
```

Read from stdin:

```sh
cat config.yaml | flak -
```

Validate against a JSON Schema:

```sh
flak --schema ./schemas/service.json deploy/service.yaml
```

Output as JSON for tooling:

```sh
flak --format json ./manifests
```

Auto-fix style issues in place:

```sh
flak --fix ./manifests
```

---

## Options

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-c, --config <FILE>` | Path to a config file (default: `.flak.yaml`). |
| `-f, --format <FMT>` | Output format: `pretty` (default), `json`, `sarif`, `github`. |
| `-s, --schema <FILE>` | JSON Schema to validate against. May be repeated. |
| `--fix` | Apply safe autofixes for style rules. |
| `--no-color` | Disable colored output. |
| `--strict` | Treat warnings as errors. |
| `--ignore <GLOB>` | Skip files matching the glob. May be repeated. |
| `-q, --quiet` | Only print errors. |
| `-v, --verbose` | Print per-file progress. |
| `-h, --help` | Show help. |
| `-V, --version` | Show version. |

---

## Configuration

`flak` looks for a `.flak.yaml` file in the current directory, then walks up to the repository root. A minimal example:

```yaml
# .flak.yaml
extends: flak:recommended

rules:
  indentation:
    spaces: 2
  line-length:
    max: 120
  no-duplicate-keys: error
  no-trailing-spaces: warn
  key-ordering:
    order: [apiVersion, kind, metadata, spec]

ignore:
  - "vendor/**"
  - "**/generated/*.yaml"

schemas:
  - match: "k8s/**/*.yaml"
    schema: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yannh/kubernetes-json-schema/master/v1.29.0-standalone-strict/all.json
```

### Rule severities

Each rule can be set to `off`, `warn`, or `error`:

```yaml
rules:
  no-tabs: error
  line-length: off
  trailing-newline: warn
```

### Inline suppression

Disable rules for a single line or block:

```yaml
# flak:disable-next-line line-length
description: This line is intentionally very long and would otherwise trigger a warning.

# flak:disable no-trailing-spaces
key: value
# flak:enable no-trailing-spaces
```

---

## Rules

| Rule | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `no-duplicate-keys` | error | Disallow duplicate mapping keys. |
| `no-tabs` | error | Disallow tab characters for indentation. |
| `indentation` | error | Enforce consistent indentation width. |
| `no-trailing-spaces` | warn | Disallow trailing whitespace. |
| `line-length` | warn | Enforce a maximum line length. |
| `trailing-newline` | warn | Require a newline at end of file. |
| `key-ordering` | off | Enforce a canonical key order. |
| `quotes` | off | Enforce single or double quotes for strings. |
| `empty-values` | off | Disallow empty values (`key:` with no value). |
| `document-start` | off | Require `---` at the start of each document. |

---

## CI Integration

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
- name: Lint YAML
  uses: example/flak-action@v1
  with:
    paths: ./manifests
    format: github
```

Or with the CLI directly:

```yaml
- run: cargo install flak
- run: flak --strict ./manifests
```

### GitLab CI

```yaml
lint:yaml:
  image: ghcr.io/example/flak:latest
  script:
    - flak --format json ./manifests > flak.json
  artifacts:
    reports:
      codequality: flak.json
```

### Pre-commit

```yaml
# .pre-commit-config.yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/example/flak
    rev: v0.4.2
    hooks:
      - id: flak
```

---

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | No errors found. |
| `1` | One or more errors found. |
| `2` | Invalid usage or configuration error. |

---

## Performance

`flak` parses YAML with [`saphyr`](https://github.com/saphyr-rs/saphyr) and parallelizes file traversal with [`rayon`](https://github.com/rayon-rs/rayon). On a 2023 MacBook Pro, linting the Kubernetes `manifests/` directory (~4,200 files) takes ~180 ms cold and ~40 ms warm.

---

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome. Please open an issue before starting work on a new rule so we can discuss the design.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/example/flak
cd flak
cargo test
cargo run -- ./testdata
```

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for details.

---

runs.output:
# flak

> A fast, configurable YAML linter.

`flak` is a command-line tool that checks YAML files for syntax errors, style inconsistencies, and schema violations. It is designed to be fast, extensible, and easy to integrate into your development workflow or CI pipeline.

## Features

- **Syntax validation** – Catch malformed YAML before it breaks your application.
- **Style enforcement** – Enforce consistent indentation, quoting, line length, and more.
- **Schema validation** – Validate against JSON Schema or custom schemas.
- **Custom rules** – Define your own rules using a simple configuration file.
- **Ignore files** – Exclude files or directories with `.flakignore`.
- **Multiple output formats** – Human-readable text, JSON, SARIF, and more.
- **Auto-fix** – Automatically fix certain style issues with `--fix`.
- **Fast** – Written in Rust, with parallel file processing.

## Installation

### Pre-built binaries

Download the latest release for your platform from the [releases page](https://github.com/yourname/flak/releases).

### Package managers

```bash
# Homebrew (macOS/Linux)
brew install flak

# Scoop (Windows)
scoop install flak

# Cargo (Rust)
cargo install flak

# npm (Node.js wrapper)
npm install -g flak
```

### From source

```bash
git clone https://github.com/yourname/flak.git
cd flak
cargo build --release
```

## Usage

```bash
flak [OPTIONS] [FILES...]
```

If no files are specified, `flak` reads from standard input.

### Options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-c, --config <FILE>` | Path to configuration file (default: `.flak.yaml`). |
| `-f, --format <FORMAT>` | Output format: `text` (default), `json`, `sarif`. |
| `--fix` | Automatically fix fixable issues. |
| `--strict` | Treat warnings as errors. |
| `--ignore <PATTERN>` | Ignore files matching the pattern (can be repeated). |
| `--no-color` | Disable colored output. |
| `-v, --verbose` | Increase verbosity. |
| `-q, --quiet` | Suppress non-error output. |
| `-h, --help` | Print help. |
| `-V, --version` | Print version. |

### Examples

Lint a single file:

```bash
flak config.yaml
```

Lint all YAML files in the current directory recursively:

```bash
flak .
```

Lint with a custom config and output JSON:

```bash
flak --config .flak.yaml --format json src/
```

Auto-fix issues:

```bash
flak --fix .
```

Read from stdin:

```bash
cat config.yaml | flak
```

## Configuration

`flak` looks for a `.flak.yaml` or `flak.yaml` file in the current directory or any parent directory. You can also specify a config file with `--config`.

Example `.flak.yaml`:

```yaml
# .flak.yaml
rules:
  indentation:
    spaces: 2
    indent-sequences: true
  line-length:
    max: 120
    allow-non-breakable-words: true
  quoted-strings:
    quote-type: single
    required: only-when-needed
  key-duplicates: true
  trailing-spaces: true
  empty-values:
    forbid-in-block-mappings: true
    forbid-in-flow-mappings: true
  schema:
    path: ./schemas/config.schema.json
    files:
      - "config/*.yaml"
```

### Ignoring files

Create a `.flakignore` file in your project root. It uses the same syntax as `.gitignore`.

```
# .flakignore
node_modules/
*.generated.yaml
```

## Rules

| Rule | Description | Fixable |
|------|-------------|---------|
| `syntax` | Validates YAML syntax. | No |
| `indentation` | Enforces consistent indentation. | Yes |
| `key-duplicates` | Disallows duplicate keys in mappings. | No |
| `trailing-spaces` | Disallows trailing whitespace. | Yes |
| `line-length` | Enforces a maximum line length. | No |
| `empty-values` | Disallows empty values in mappings. | No |
| `truthy` | Enforces consistent boolean values (`true`/`false`). | Yes |
| `quoted-strings` | Enforces consistent quoting style. | Yes |
| `schema` | Validates against a JSON Schema. | No |

Each rule can be configured with options. See the [documentation](https://github.com/yourname/flak/wiki/Rules) for details.

## Output formats

- **text** (default) – Colored, human-readable output.
- **json** – Machine-readable JSON.
- **sarif** – Static Analysis Results Interchange Format, for integration with GitHub Code Scanning.

Example JSON output:

```json
{
  "files": [
    {
      "path": "config.yaml",
      "errors": [
        {
          "line": 3,
          "column": 5,
          "rule": "indentation",
          "message": "Expected 2 spaces, found 4",
          "severity": "error"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| 0 | No issues found. |
| 1 | Lint errors found. |
| 2 | Usage error (invalid arguments, missing file, etc.). |
| 3 | Internal error. |

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome! Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for guidelines.

## License

This project is licensed under the MIT License. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) for details.

# flak

> A fast, opinionated YAML linter for humans and CI pipelines.

`flak` catches the YAML mistakes that cost you hours — duplicate keys, inconsistent indentation, trailing whitespace, unquoted booleans, and more — before they reach production.

```
$ flak config/
config/database.yml
  12:5   error    duplicate key "host" (previously defined at line 8)
  19:1   warning  trailing whitespace
  24:3   error    tab character used for indentation

config/ci.yml
   4:1   warning  document does not start with "---"
   7:9   error    unquoted boolean "yes" — did you mean the string "yes"?

✖ 5 problems (3 errors, 2 warnings)
```

---

## Features

- **Fast** — written in Rust, lints thousands of files in milliseconds.
- **Safe** — never modifies your files unless you pass `--fix`.
- **Configurable** — enable, disable, or re-tune every rule via `.flakrc`.
- **CI-friendly** — machine-readable output, meaningful exit codes, GitHub Actions annotations.
- **Multi-document aware** — handles `---` separated streams and anchors/aliases correctly.
- **Editor integration** — LSP mode for real-time diagnostics in your editor.

---

## Installation

### Homebrew (macOS / Linux)

```sh
brew install flak
```

### Cargo

```sh
cargo install flak
```

### npm

```sh
npm install --global @flak/cli
```

### Pre-built binaries

Download the latest release for your platform from the [releases page](https://github.com/example/flak/releases).

### Docker

```sh
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/work" -w /work ghcr.io/example/flak:latest .
```

---

## Usage

```
flak [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...
```

If no paths are given, `flak` reads from stdin.

### Common examples

Lint a single file:

```sh
flak config.yml
```

Lint every YAML file in a directory (recursively):

```sh
flak .
```

Lint from stdin:

```sh
cat config.yml | flak -
```

Auto-fix safe issues (trailing whitespace, missing document start, etc.):

```sh
flak --fix .
```

Emit JSON for tooling:

```sh
flak --format json . > report.json
```

Emit GitHub Actions annotations:

```sh
flak --format github .
```

Fail the build only on errors, not warnings:

```sh
flak --max-warnings 0 .
```

---

## Options

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-c, --config <FILE>` | Path to a config file. Defaults to `.flakrc` in the current directory. |
| `-f, --format <FORMAT>` | Output format: `pretty` (default), `json`, `github`, `sarif`. |
| `--fix` | Apply safe automatic fixes in place. |
| `--dry-run` | With `--fix`, show what would change without writing. |
| `--max-warnings <N>` | Exit non-zero if more than `N` warnings are found. Default: `-1` (unlimited). |
| `--ignore <GLOB>` | Skip files matching the glob. May be repeated. |
| `--no-ignore` | Do not respect `.gitignore` or `.flakignore`. |
| `--stdin-filename <NAME>` | Filename to use when reading from stdin (affects config resolution). |
| `--lsp` | Run as a Language Server over stdio. |
| `-q, --quiet` | Suppress output; rely on exit code only. |
| `-v, --verbose` | Print each file as it is checked. |
| `-h, --help` | Print help. |
| `-V, --version` | Print version. |

---

## Rules

`flak` ships with a curated set of rules. Each can be set to `off`, `warn`, or `error`.

| Rule | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `duplicate-key` | error | Two keys with the same name in one mapping. |
| `indentation` | error | Inconsistent or non-multiple-of-2 indentation. |
| `no-tabs` | error | Tab characters used for indentation. |
| `trailing-whitespace` | warn | Whitespace at the end of a line. |
| `document-start` | warn | File does not begin with `---`. |
| `document-end` | off | File does not end with `...`. |
| `key-ordering` | off | Keys are not in alphabetical order. |
| `quoted-strings` | off | Enforce a consistent string quoting style. |
| `truthy` | error | Unquoted `yes`/`no`/`on`/`off` that YAML 1.1 would coerce to a boolean. |
| `empty-values` | warn | A key with no value. |
| `line-length` | off | Lines exceed the configured maximum length. |
| `new-line-at-end-of-file` | warn | File does not end with a newline. |
| `anchors` | warn | Unused or undefined anchors/aliases. |
| `octal-values` | error | Values like `0755` that YAML 1.1 parses as octal. |

Run `flak --list-rules` to see the full list with descriptions.

---

## Configuration

`flak` looks for a `.flakrc` (YAML or JSON) in the current directory, then walks up to the filesystem root. You can also point at a specific file with `--config`.

```yaml
# .flakrc
extends: flak:recommended

rules:
  document-start: off
  line-length:
    level: warn
    max: 120
  key-ordering: error
  quoted-strings:
    level: error
    quote-type: double
    required: only-when-needed

ignore:
  - "vendor/**"
  - "**/generated/*.yml"

overrides:
  - files: ["k8s/**/*.yaml"]
    rules:
      document-start: error
```

### Ignoring files

Create a `.flakignore` file (same syntax as `.gitignore`) to exclude paths:

```
node_modules/
*.generated.yml
!important.generated.yml
```

---

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | No problems found (or only warnings, within `--max-warnings`). |
| `1` | One or more errors found. |
| `2` | Invalid usage or configuration error. |
| `3` | Internal error (please [file a bug](https://github.com/example/flak/issues)). |

---

## Editor integration

### VS Code

Install the [flak extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=example.flak) from the marketplace, or add to your `settings.json`:

```json
{
  "yaml.validate": false,
  "flak.enable": true,
  "flak.run": "onSave"
}
```

### Neovim (nvim-lspconfig)

```lua
require('lspconfig').flak.setup({})
```

### Any LSP client

```sh
flak --lsp
```

---

## CI

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
- name: Lint YAML
  run: flak --format github .
```

### GitLab CI

```yaml
lint:yaml:
  image: ghcr.io/example/flak:latest
  script:
    - flak --format json . | tee flak.json
  artifacts:
    reports:
      codequality: flak.json
```

### Pre-commit

```yaml
# .pre-commit-config.yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/example/flak
    rev: v1.4.0
    hooks:
      - id: flak
```

---

## Performance

`flak` is designed to be run on every save and every commit. On a 2020 MacBook Pro it lints the Kubernetes repository (~14,000 YAML files) in under 400 ms with all cores.

---

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome! Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening a pull request.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/example/flak
cd flak
cargo test
cargo run -- tests/fixtures
```

---

Unless you explicitly state otherwise, any contribution intentionally submitted for inclusion in this project by you, as defined in the Apache-2.0 license, shall be dual licensed as above, without any additional terms or conditions.

# flak

**Catch YAML flakes before they break your stack.**

`flak` is a fast, opinionated linter for YAML files. It validates syntax, enforces style rules, detects duplicate keys, and catches the subtle mistakes that slip past your editor and blow up in CI.

```
$ flak deploy/
deploy/service.yaml
  12:5   error    duplicate key 'ports' in mapping        (no-duplicate-keys)
  18:1   error    tab character found, YAML requires spaces  (no-tabs)
  24:9   warning  trailing whitespace                     (no-trailing-spaces)
  31:3   error    expected 2-space indentation, found 4   (indent)

deploy/config.yaml
   7:14  error    unquoted 'yes' parsed as boolean, did you mean "yes"?  (truthy-strings)

✖ 5 problems (4 errors, 1 warning)
```

---

## Why flak?

YAML is deceptively simple. A stray tab, an unquoted `no`, or a duplicated key can silently change behavior or crash a deploy. `flak` is designed to:

- **Fail fast** — parse errors are reported with precise line/column locations.
- **Catch the classics** — duplicate keys, tabs, truthy strings (`yes`/`no`/`on`/`off`), and inconsistent indentation.
- **Stay out of your way** — sensible defaults, zero config required, but fully configurable when you need it.
- **Play well with CI** — machine-readable output, meaningful exit codes, and a `--strict` mode.

---

## Installation

### Homebrew (macOS / Linux)

```sh
brew install flak
```

### npm

```sh
npm install -g flak
```

### Cargo

```sh
cargo install flak
```

### From source

```sh
git clone https://github.com/your-org/flak.git
cd flak
cargo build --release
# binary at ./target/release/flak
```

---

## Usage

```sh
flak [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...
```

Lint one or more files or directories. If no path is given, `flak` lints the current directory recursively.

### Examples

```sh
# Lint a single file
flak config.yaml

# Lint every YAML file under a directory
flak ./manifests

# Lint multiple paths
flak k8s/ .github/workflows/ docker-compose.yml

# Read from stdin
cat config.yaml | flak -

# Auto-fix what can be fixed
flak --fix ./manifests

# Strict mode: treat warnings as errors
flak --strict .

# Machine-readable output for CI
flak --format json .
```

### Common options

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-f, --format <fmt>` | Output format: `pretty` (default), `json`, `github`, `sarif`. |
| `--fix` | Automatically fix fixable issues (indentation, trailing whitespace, tabs). |
| `--strict` | Treat warnings as errors. |
| `--config <path>` | Path to a `.flakrc` config file. |
| `--ignore <glob>` | Ignore files matching a glob (repeatable). |
| `--no-color` | Disable colored output. |
| `-q, --quiet` | Only print errors, suppress warnings. |
| `-h, --help` | Show help. |
| `-V, --version` | Show version. |

---

## Rules

`flak` ships with a curated set of rules. Each can be set to `off`, `warn`, or `error`.

| Rule | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `parse-error` | error | File is not valid YAML. |
| `no-duplicate-keys` | error | Duplicate keys in the same mapping. |
| `no-tabs` | error | Tab characters used for indentation. |
| `indent` | error | Inconsistent indentation (default: 2 spaces). |
| `truthy-strings` | error | Unquoted `yes`, `no`, `on`, `off`, `y`, `n` that may be misparsed. |
| `no-trailing-spaces` | warn | Trailing whitespace at end of line. |
| `key-ordering` | off | Enforce alphabetical key ordering. |
| `line-length` | off | Enforce a maximum line length. |
| `document-start` | off | Require `---` at the start of each document. |
| `empty-values` | warn | Flag empty values (`key:` with nothing after). |
| `anchors-defined` | error | Aliases referencing undefined anchors. |

Run `flak --list-rules` to see the full list with descriptions.

---

## Configuration

`flak` looks for a `.flakrc`, `.flakrc.yaml`, or `.flakrc.json` file in the current directory or any parent. You can also point to one explicitly with `--config`.

```yaml
# .flakrc
rules:
  indent:
    level: error
    size: 2
  line-length:
    level: warn
    max: 120
  key-ordering: error
  document-start: off

ignore:
  - "vendor/**"
  - "**/generated/*.yaml"

overrides:
  - files: ["k8s/**/*.yaml"]
    rules:
      document-start: error
```

---

## CI Integration

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
- name: Lint YAML
  run: flak --format github .
```

The `github` formatter emits `::error` and `::warning` annotations that appear inline on pull requests.

### Pre-commit

```yaml
# .pre-commit-config.yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/your-org/flak
    rev: v1.2.0
    hooks:
      - id: flak
```

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | No problems found. |
| `1` | One or more errors found. |
| `2` | Invalid usage or configuration error. |

---

## Ignoring issues inline

```yaml
# flak-disable-next-line no-trailing-spaces
key: value   

# flak-disable truthy-strings
enabled: yes
# flak-enable truthy-strings
```

---

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome! Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening a pull request.

- Bug reports and feature requests: [open an issue](https://github.com/your-org/flak/issues).
- New rules: see [docs/writing-rules.md](docs/writing-rules.md).

```
$ flak config/
config/database.yml
  4:3   error    duplicate key "host"                no-duplicate-keys
  7:1   warning  trailing whitespace                 no-trailing-spaces
```

- **Fast** — written in Rust, lints thousands of files in milliseconds
- **Safe** — parses with a strict YAML 1.2 loader; never silently drops data
- **Configurable** — enable, disable, or tune every rule via `.flakrc`
- **CI-friendly** — machine-readable output, meaningful exit codes, GitHub Actions annotations
- **Editor integration** — LSP server for real-time diagnostics in any editor
- **Zero config** — sensible defaults that catch real bugs out of the box

---

## Installation

### Homebrew (macOS / Linux)

```sh
brew install flak
```

### Cargo

```sh
cargo install flak
```

### npm (for Node projects)

```sh
npm install --save-dev flak
```

### Prebuilt binaries

Download the latest release for your platform from the [releases page](https://github.com/example/flak/releases).

### Docker

```sh
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/work" ghcr.io/example/flak:latest /work
```

---

## Usage

```sh
flak [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...
```

Lint a single file:

```sh
flak config.yml
```

Lint a directory recursively:

```sh
flak .
```

Lint from stdin:

```sh
cat config.yml | flak -
```

### Common options

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-c, --config <FILE>` | Path to a config file (default: `.flakrc`) |
| `-f, --format <FORMAT>` | Output format: `pretty`, `json`, `github`, `sarif` |
| `--fix` | Automatically fix fixable issues |
| `--strict` | Treat warnings as errors |
| `--no-color` | Disable colored output |
| `--exclude <GLOB>` | Skip files matching a glob (repeatable) |
| `--rule <NAME>` | Run only the specified rule (repeatable) |
| `--ignore <NAME>` | Skip the specified rule (repeatable) |
| `-q, --quiet` | Only print errors |
| `-h, --help` | Print help |
| `-V, --version` | Print version |

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | No problems found |
| `1` | Lint errors found |
| `2` | Invalid usage or configuration error |
| `3` | Internal error |

---

## Rules

`flak` ships with the following rules. Each can be toggled or configured in `.flakrc`.

| Rule | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `no-duplicate-keys` | error | Disallow duplicate mapping keys |
| `indent-style` | error | Enforce spaces (default: 2) and forbid tabs |
| `no-trailing-spaces` | warning | Disallow trailing whitespace |
| `no-tabs` | error | Disallow tab characters anywhere |
| `quote-ambiguous` | warning | Require quotes around values that YAML 1.1 would parse as booleans (`yes`, `no`, `on`, `off`) |
| `key-ordering` | off | Enforce alphabetical key ordering |
| `line-length` | off | Enforce a maximum line length |
| `no-empty-values` | warning | Disallow empty values (`key:` with no value) |
| `document-start` | off | Require `---` at the start of every document |
| `document-end` | off | Require `...` at the end of every document |
| `final-newline` | warning | Require a newline at end of file |
| `no-anchors-aliases` | off | Disallow anchors and aliases |
| `max-nesting` | off | Limit nesting depth |

Run `flak --list-rules` to see the full list with descriptions.

---

## Configuration

`flak` looks for a `.flakrc` (or `.flakrc.yaml`, `.flakrc.yml`, or a `flak` key in `package.json`) in the current directory and walks up to the filesystem root.

```yaml
# .flakrc
extends: flak:recommended

rules:
  indent-style:
    level: error
    size: 4
  line-length:
    level: warning
    max: 120
  key-ordering: error
  no-anchors-aliases: off

ignore:
  - "vendor/**"
  - "**/generated/*.yml"

overrides:
  - files: ["ci/**/*.yml"]
    rules:
      document-start: off
```

### Presets

- `flak:recommended` — the default set of rules
- `flak:strict` — everything on, warnings promoted to errors
- `flak:off` — no rules; opt in explicitly

---

## CI integration

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
- name: Lint YAML
  run: flak --format github .
```

`--format github` emits `::error` and `::warning` workflow commands, so problems appear inline on the pull request diff.

### GitLab CI

```yaml
lint:yaml:
  image: ghcr.io/example/flak:latest
  script:
    - flak --format json . > flak.json
  artifacts:
    reports:
      codequality: flak.json
```

### Pre-commit

```yaml
# .pre-commit-config.yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/example/flak
    rev: v1.4.0
    hooks:
      - id: flak
```

---

## Editor integration

`flak` includes a built-in language server:

```sh
flak lsp
```

### VS Code

Install the [flak extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=example.flak) from the marketplace.

### Neovim (nvim-lspconfig)

```lua
require('lspconfig').flak.setup({})
```

### Helix

```toml
# languages.toml
[language-server.flak]
command = "flak"
args = ["lsp"]

[[language]]
name = "yaml"
language-servers = ["flak"]
```

---

## Auto-fixing

Some rules support automatic fixes:

```sh
flak --fix .
```

Fixable rules: `indent-style`, `no-trailing-spaces`, `final-newline`, `quote-ambiguous`.

Preview changes without writing:

```sh
flak --fix --dry-run .
```

---

## Performance

`flak` is designed to be run on every save and every commit. On a 2020 MacBook Pro:

| Corpus | Files | Time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Kubernetes manifests | 1,200 | 84 ms |
| GitHub Actions workflows | 400 | 22 ms |
| Ansible playbooks | 3,500 | 310 ms |

Files are linted in parallel across all available cores.

---

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome! Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening a pull request.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/example/flak
cd flak
cargo test
cargo run -- tests/fixtures
```

### Adding a rule

1. Create a new module under `src/rules/`.
2. Implement the `Rule` trait.
3. Register it in `src/rules/mod.rs`.
4. Add fixtures under `tests/fixtures/<rule-name>/`.
5. Document it in this README and in `docs/rules.md`.

---

runs.output:
# flak

A fast, opinionated YAML linter for people who are tired of indentation errors at 2 AM.

`flak` catches syntax errors, structural issues, and style violations in YAML files before they hit your CI pipeline — or worse, production.

```
$ flak deploy/
deploy/service.yaml
  12:5   error    inconsistent indentation (expected 2 spaces, found 4)
  18:1   error    duplicate key "replicas"
  24:9   warning  line exceeds 120 characters (found 143)
  31:3   error    unquoted string looks like a boolean: "yes"

deploy/config.yaml
  ✓ clean

✗ 4 problems in 2 files (3 errors, 1 warning)
```

## Features

- **Syntax checking** — parses every file and reports precise line/column locations
- **Duplicate key detection** — YAML silently accepts duplicates; `flak` doesn't
- **Style rules** — configurable indentation, line length, quoting, and key ordering
- **Anchor/alias validation** — catches broken anchors and circular references
- **Multi-document support** — handles `---` separated streams
- **Schema validation** — optionally validate against a JSON Schema
- **Fast** — parallel file processing, typically under 50ms for typical repos
- **Zero config by default** — sensible defaults, configurable when you need it

## Installation

### Homebrew (macOS / Linux)

```sh
brew install flak
```

### Cargo

```sh
cargo install flak
```

### npm

```sh
npm install -g flak-cli
```

### Pre-built binaries

Download from the [releases page](https://github.com/example/flak/releases).

## Usage

```sh
flak [OPTIONS] <PATH>...
```

Lint a single file:

```sh
flak config.yaml
```

Lint a directory recursively:

```sh
flak ./manifests
```

Lint everything changed since `main`:

```sh
git diff --name-only main...HEAD -- '*.yaml' '*.yml' | xargs flak
```

Read from stdin:

```sh
cat config.yaml | flak -
```

### Common flags

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--config <FILE>` | Use a specific config file |
| `--format <FMT>` | Output format: `text`, `json`, `sarif`, `github` (default: `text`) |
| `--quiet` | Only print errors, suppress warnings |
| `--max-warnings <N>` | Fail if warning count exceeds N |
| `--fix` | Auto-fix fixable issues (indentation, trailing whitespace, quoting) |
| `--stdin-filename <NAME>` | Filename to report when reading from stdin |
| `--no-ignore` | Don't respect `.gitignore` / `.flakignore` |
| `--jobs <N>` | Number of parallel workers (default: number of CPUs) |

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `0` | No problems found |
| `1` | Lint errors found |
| `2` | Invalid usage or configuration error |

## Configuration

`flak` looks for a config file in this order:

1. Path passed via `--config`
2. `.flakrc.yaml` / `.flakrc.yml` / `.flakrc.json` in the current directory
3. `flak` key in `package.json`
4. Defaults

### Example `.flakrc.yaml`

```yaml
# Files to lint and ignore
include:
  - "**/*.yaml"
  - "**/*.yml"
ignore:
  - "vendor/**"
  - "**/node_modules/**"
  - "**/generated/**"

# Rule configuration
rules:
  indentation: 2                 # spaces per indent level (or "off")
  max-line-length: 120
  duplicate-keys: error
  trailing-whitespace: error
  final-newline: require
  quote-strings: consistent      # "consistent" | "single" | "double" | "off"
  document-start: off            # require `---` at top of file
  truthy: error                  # disallow bare `yes`/`no`/`on`/`off` as booleans
  key-ordering: off              # enforce alphabetical keys
  empty-values: warn
  anchors-valid: error
  schema: ./schemas/config.json  # optional JSON Schema for validation

# Override rules for specific paths
overrides:
  - files: ["k8s/**/*.yaml"]
    rules:
      document-start: require
      key-ordering: [apiVersion, kind, metadata, spec]
  - files: ["**/*.test.yaml"]
    rules:
      max-line-length: off
```

### Inline suppression

Disable a rule for a single line or the next line:

```yaml
# flak-disable-next-line duplicate-keys
foo: 1
foo: 2

# flak-disable truthy
enabled: yes
# flak-enable truthy
```

## Output formats

### `text` (default)

Human-readable, with colors when writing to a TTY.

### `json`

```json
{
  "files": [
    {
      "path": "deploy/service.yaml",
      "problems": [
        {
          "line": 12,
          "column": 5,
          "severity": "error",
          "rule": "indentation",
          "message": "inconsistent indentation (expected 2 spaces, found 4)"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "summary": { "errors": 1, "warnings": 0, "files": 1 }
}
```

### `sarif`

Standard [SARIF](https://sarifweb.azurewebsites.net/) output for GitHub code scanning and other CI integrations.

### `github`

GitHub Actions workflow commands — annotates the diff view automatically.

## CI integration

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
- name: Lint YAML
  uses: example/flak-action@v1
  with:
    args: --format github .
```

### GitLab CI

```yaml
lint:yaml:
  image: ghcr.io/example/flak:latest
  script:
    - flak --format text .
```

### Pre-commit

Add to `.pre-commit-config.yaml`:

```yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/example/flak
    rev: v1.4.0
    hooks:
      - id: flak
```

## Editor support

- **VS Code** — [flak-vscode](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=example.flak-vscode)
- **Neovim** — via [null-ls](https://github.com/jose-elias-alvarez/null-ls.nvim) or `efm-langserver`
- **Helix** — built-in LSP integration via `flak --lsp`

`flak` ships an LSP mode for real-time diagnostics:

```sh
flak --lsp
```

## Rules reference

| Rule | Default | Fixable | Description |
|------|---------|:-------:|-------------|
| `indentation` | `2` | ✓ | Consistent indentation width |
| `max-line-length` | `120` | | Maximum line length |
| `duplicate-keys` | `error` | | Reject duplicate mapping keys |
| `trailing-whitespace` | `error` | ✓ | No trailing whitespace |
| `final-newline` | `require` | ✓ | File must end with a newline |
| `quote-strings` | `consistent` | ✓ | Quoting style for strings |
| `document-start` | `off` | ✓ | Require `---` at the top |
| `truthy` | `error` | | Disallow `yes`/`no`/`on`/`off` as booleans |
| `key-ordering` | `off` | ✓ | Enforce key order |
| `empty-values` | `warn` | | Flag empty mapping values |
| `anchors-valid` | `error` | | Anchors must resolve; no cycles |
| `schema` | — | | Validate against a JSON Schema |

## Why not `yamllint`?

`flak` is largely compatible with [`yamllint`](https://github.com/adrienverge/yamllint) config files and aims to be a drop-in replacement with:

- ~10× faster on large repositories (parallel + incremental parsing)
- Native LSP support
- SARIF and GitHub Actions output built in
- `--fix` for common style problems

If you're migrating, run:

```sh
flak --import-yamllint .yamllint
```

which converts your existing config to `.flakrc.yaml`.

## Contributing

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Bug reports and rule proposals are welcome — please include a minimal reproduction.

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

# flak

> A fast, opinionated YAML linter.

`flak` checks your YAML files for syntax errors, style violations, and schema mismatches — so your configs fail in CI instead of production.

```
$ flak deploy/
deploy/service.yaml
  12:3  error    duplicate key "image"                 no-duplicate-keys
  18:1  warning  expected 2-space indentation          indent
deploy/values.yaml
   7:9  error    value must be a string, got integer   schema(values.schema.json)

✖ 3 problems (2 errors, 1 warning)
```

## Features

- **Syntax validation** — catches malformed YAML before it reaches your app
- **Style rules** — configurable rules for indentation, quoting, key ordering, and more
- **Schema validation** — validate against JSON Schema
- **Multiple output formats** — human-readable, JSON, and SARIF (for GitHub code scanning)
- **Fast** — parallel file traversal, written in Rust
- **CI-friendly** — meaningful exit codes and annotations

## Installation

### Homebrew (macOS / Linux)

```sh
brew install flak
```

### Cargo

```sh
cargo install flak
```

### npm

```sh
npm install -g @flak/cli
```

### Prebuilt binaries

Download the latest release for your platform from the [releases page](https://github.com/example/flak/releases).

## Usage

```sh
flak [OPTIONS] <PATH>...
```

Lint one or more files or directories:

```sh
flak config.yaml
flak deploy/ manifests/ .github/
flak .                    # lints every *.yaml and *.yml in the tree
```

Read from stdin:

```sh
cat config.yaml | flak -
```

### Options

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-c, --config <FILE>` | Path to a config file (default: `flak.toml`) |
| `-f, --format <FORMAT>` | Output format: `pretty` (default), `json`, `sarif` |
| `-s, --schema <FILE>` | JSON Schema to validate against |
| `--fix` | Apply autofixes for fixable rules |
| `--rule <NAME>` | Run only the given rule (repeatable) |
| `--ignore <NAME>` | Skip the given rule (repeatable) |
| `--no-config` | Ignore any config file found on disk |
| `-q, --quiet` | Only print errors, suppress warnings |
| `--max-warnings <N>` | Exit non-zero if warnings exceed N |
| `-h, --help` | Print help |
| `-V, --version` | Print version |

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | No problems found |
| `1` | One or more errors (or warnings above `--max-warnings`) |
| `2` | Invalid usage or internal error |

## Configuration

`flak` looks for `flak.toml` in the current directory, then walks up to the filesystem root. You can override this with `--config`.

```toml
# flak.toml
files = ["**/*.yaml", "**/*.yml"]
ignore = ["vendor/**", "node_modules/**"]

[rules]
indent              = { spaces = 2 }
no-duplicate-keys   = "error"
no-trailing-spaces  = "error"
key-ordering        = { order = ["apiVersion", "kind", "metadata", "spec"] }
document-start      = "off"
line-length         = { max = 120, severity = "warning" }

[schema]
path = "schemas/config.schema.json"
```

Severity levels are `off`, `warning`, and `error`.

## Rules

| Rule | Fixable | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `indent` | ✅ | Enforce consistent indentation |
| `no-duplicate-keys` | | Disallow duplicate mapping keys |
| `no-tabs` | ✅ | Disallow tab characters |
| `no-trailing-spaces` | ✅ | Disallow trailing whitespace |
| `document-start` | ✅ | Require or forbid `---` |
| `document-end` | ✅ | Require or forbid `...` |
| `line-length` | | Enforce a maximum line length |
| `key-ordering` | ✅ | Enforce key order in mappings |
| `quoted-strings` | ✅ | Require or forbid quotes around strings |
| `empty-values` | | Control how empty values are represented |
| `truthy` | | Disallow `yes`/`no`/`on`/`off` as booleans |
| `comments` | | Require or forbid comments in specific contexts |

Run `flak --rule <name> --help` for rule-specific options.

## Schema validation

Pass a JSON Schema with `--schema`, or configure one in `flak.toml`:

```sh
flak --schema schemas/service.schema.json deploy/service.yaml
```

Schemas support `$ref`, `allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf`, and `additionalProperties`. Validation errors are reported at the offending line and column.

## Editor integration

### VS Code

Install the [`flak-vscode`](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=example.flak-vscode) extension for inline diagnostics and quick fixes.

### Neovim

With [`nvim-lint`](https://github.com/mfussenegger/nvim-lint):

```lua
require("lint").linters.flak = {
  cmd = "flak",
  stdin = false,
  args = { "--format", "json", "-" },
  stream = "stdout",
  parser = require("lint.parser").from_errorformat(
    "%f:%l:%c: %t: %m",
    { source = "flak" }
  ),
}
```

## CI

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
- uses: example/flak-action@v1
  with:
    args: "deploy/ --format sarif"
```

SARIF output is uploaded automatically to GitHub code scanning.

### GitLab CI

```yaml
lint-yaml:
  image: example/flak:latest
  script:
    - flak . --format json > flak.json
  artifacts:
    reports:
      codequality: flak.json
```

## Development

```sh
git clone https://github.com/example/flak
cd flak
cargo build --release
cargo test
```

Contributions are welcome — please open an issue before starting work on a new rule.

## License

MIT © the flak contributors.

# flak

> A fast, configurable linter for YAML files.

`flak` catches syntax errors, style inconsistencies, and common pitfalls in your YAML before they reach production. Whether you're managing Kubernetes manifests, CI configs, or application settings, `flak` helps you keep them clean and consistent.

## Features

- **Syntax validation** — Detects malformed YAML, duplicate keys, and invalid indentation
- **Style checks** — Enforces consistent formatting (indentation width, line length, quoting, trailing whitespace)
- **Schema-aware rules** — Optional strict mode for common YAML dialects (Kubernetes, GitHub Actions, Docker Compose)
- **Configurable** — Enable, disable, or tune rules via a `.flak.yml` config file
- **Fast** — Parallel file processing with sensible defaults
- **CI-friendly** — Machine-readable output (`json`, `sarif`) and non-zero exit codes on failure
- **Zero config to start** — Run `flak .` and it just works

## Installation

### Homebrew (macOS / Linux)

```bash
brew install flak
```

### npm

```bash
npm install -g flak-cli
```

### Go

```bash
go install github.com/flak-dev/flak@latest
```

### Binary releases

Download prebuilt binaries from the [releases page](https://github.com/flak-dev/flak/releases).

## Quick Start

Lint every YAML file in the current directory:

```bash
flak .
```

Lint specific files:

```bash
flak config.yaml deploy/*.yml
```

Example output:

```
deploy/service.yaml
  12:5   error    duplicate key "image"            no-duplicate-keys
  18:1   warning  line exceeds 120 characters      max-line-length
  24:3   error    inconsistent indentation (2 vs 4) consistent-indentation

✖ 3 problems (2 errors, 1 warning)
```

## Usage

```
flak [flags] [paths...]

Flags:
  -c, --config string     Path to config file (default ".flak.yml")
  -f, --format string     Output format: pretty, json, sarif (default "pretty")
      --fix               Automatically fix fixable issues
      --strict            Treat warnings as errors
      --no-color          Disable colored output
      --ignore string     Comma-separated glob patterns to ignore
  -q, --quiet             Only report errors
  -v, --version           Print version
  -h, --help              Show help
```

### Examples

**Lint a directory, ignoring vendor files:**

```bash
flak . --ignore 'vendor/**,node_modules/**'
```

**Auto-fix indentation and whitespace issues:**

```bash
flak --fix .
```

**Output JSON for CI pipelines:**

```bash
flak --format json . > report.json
```

**Enforce strict mode (warnings fail the build):**

```bash
flak --strict .
```

## Configuration

`flak` reads a `.flak.yml` (or `.flak.yaml`) file from the current directory or any parent. CLI flags override config values.

```yaml
# .flak.yml
extends: default

ignore:
  - "vendor/**"
  - "**/*.generated.yaml"

rules:
  indentation:
    enabled: true
    spaces: 2
  max-line-length:
    enabled: true
    max: 120
  no-duplicate-keys:
    enabled: true
  trailing-whitespace:
    enabled: true
  quoted-strings:
    enabled: true
    required: only-when-needed
  document-start:
    enabled: false
```

### Presets

Extend a built-in preset and override only what you need:

| Preset    | Description                                              |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `default` | Balanced ruleset suitable for most projects              |
| `strict`  | Everything in `default`, plus stricter style rules       |
| `k8s`     | Tailored for Kubernetes manifests                        |
| `gha`     | Tailored for GitHub Actions workflows                    |
| `relaxed` | Only catch real errors, no style opinions                |

```yaml
extends: k8s
```

## Rules

| Rule                    | Description                                       | Fixable |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | :-----: |
| `no-duplicate-keys`     | Detect duplicate mapping keys                     |         |
| `consistent-indentation`| Enforce uniform indentation width                 |    ✓    |
| `trailing-whitespace`   | Disallow trailing spaces and tabs                 |    ✓    |
| `max-line-length`       | Enforce a maximum line length                     |         |
| `document-start`        | Require or forbid `---` at document start         |    ✓    |
| `quoted-strings`        | Control when strings must be quoted               |    ✓    |
| `key-ordering`          | Enforce alphabetical key ordering                 |    ✓    |
| `no-empty-values`       | Flag empty values where one is expected           |         |
| `truthy`                | Discourage ambiguous booleans (`yes`, `no`, `on`) |    ✓    |
| `no-tabs`               | Disallow tab characters in indentation            |    ✓    |

See the [rules documentation](https://github.com/flak-dev/flak/blob/main/docs/rules.md) for details and options.

## CI Integration

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
- name: Lint YAML
  uses: flak-dev/action@v1
  with:
    args: "--strict ."
```

### GitLab CI

```yaml
lint:yaml:
  image: ghcr.io/flak-dev/flak:latest
  script:
    - flak --strict .
```

### Pre-commit hook

Add to your `.pre-commit-config.yaml`:

```yaml
- repo: https://github.com/flak-dev/flak
  rev: v1.4.0
  hooks:
    - id: flak
```

## Exit Codes

| Code | Meaning                             |
| ---- | ----------------------------------- |
| `0`  | No issues found                     |
| `1`  | Lint errors found                   |
| `2`  | Invalid usage or configuration      |
| `3`  | Internal error                      |

## Development

```bash
git clone https://github.com/flak-dev/flak.git
cd flak
make build     # compile
make test      # run tests
make lint      # lint the linter
```

Contributions are welcome — please open an issue before submitting large PRs.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE) © flak contributors
