# flak

**flak** is a fast, opinionated CLI linter for YAML files. It catches syntax errors, enforces style conventions, and helps keep your configuration files consistent across projects.

```
$ flak config.yaml
config.yaml
  3:12  error    duplicate key 'image'
  7:1   warning  trailing whitespace
  12:5  error    inconsistent indentation (expected 2 spaces, found 4)

✖ 2 errors, 1 warning
```

## Features

- **Syntax validation** — catches malformed YAML before it breaks your pipeline
- **Duplicate key detection** — YAML silently overwrites duplicates; flak doesn't
- **Style rules** — consistent indentation, no tabs, no trailing whitespace, no long lines
- **Schema-aware** — validate against JSON Schema or Kubernetes manifests
- **Fast** — parallel file processing, no external dependencies
- **Configurable** — enable/disable rules via `.flak.yml`
- **CI-friendly** — non-zero exit codes and machine-readable output

## Installation

### Homebrew (macOS / Linux)

```bash
brew install flak
```

### npm

```bash
npm install -g flak
```

### Cargo

```bash
cargo install flak
```

### From source

```bash
git clone https://github.com/yourorg/flak.git
cd flak
cargo build --release
```

## Usage

Lint a single file:

```bash
flak config.yaml
```

Lint multiple files or globs:

```bash
flak "**/*.yml" "**/*.yaml"
```

Lint from stdin:

```bash
cat config.yaml | flak -
```

Lint a directory (recursively, skips `.git`, `node_modules`, `vendor`):

```bash
flak .
```

### Common options

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--format <fmt>` | Output format: `pretty` (default), `json`, `github`, `sarif` |
| `--config <path>` | Path to a config file |
| `--no-config` | Ignore any config file and use defaults |
| `--fix` | Auto-fix fixable issues in place |
| `--strict` | Treat warnings as errors |
| `--quiet` | Only print errors |
| `--schema <path>` | Validate against a JSON Schema |
| `--exclude <glob>` | Skip files matching the glob (repeatable) |
| `-h`, `--help` | Show help |

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `0` | No problems found |
| `1` | Lint errors found |
| `2` | Invalid usage or internal error |

## Configuration

flak looks for a `.flak.yml` (or `.flak.yaml`) file starting from the current directory and walking up to the repository root. You can also specify a path with `--config`.

```yaml
# .flak.yml
rules:
  duplicate-keys: error
  trailing-whitespace: warning
  indentation:
    severity: error
    size: 2
    style: space
  line-length:
    severity: warning
    max: 120
  empty-values: off

# Only lint these paths
include:
  - "config/**/*.yaml"
  - "k8s/**/*.yml"

# Never lint these
exclude:
  - "**/node_modules/**"
  - "**/vendor/**"
  - "**/*.generated.yaml"
```

## Rules

| Rule | Default | Fixable | Description |
|------|---------|:-------:|-------------|
| `duplicate-keys` | error | | Reject duplicate mapping keys |
| `indentation` | error | ✅ | Enforce consistent indentation |
| `trailing-whitespace` | warning | ✅ | No whitespace at line ends |
| `line-length` | warning | | Enforce a maximum line length |
| `no-tabs` | error | ✅ | Disallow tab characters |
| `empty-values` | warning | | Flag `key:` with no value |
| `document-start` | off | ✅ | Require `---` at the start of each document |
| `document-end` | off | | Require `...` at the end of each document |
| `truthy` | error | | Reject `yes`/`no`/`on`/`off` (use `true`/`false`) |
| `key-ordering` | off | | Enforce alphabetical key ordering |
| `new-line-at-end-of-file` | warning | ✅ | File must end with a newline |

## Editor integration

flak works with any editor that supports external linters.

**VS Code** — install the [YAML extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=redhat.vscode-yaml) and add:

```json
{
  "yaml.customTags": [],
  "yaml.validate": true,
  "yaml.lint.command": "flak"
}
```

**Neovim (nvim-lint)**:

```lua
require("lint").linters_by_ft = {
  yaml = { "flak" },
}
```

**Helix** (`~/.config/helix/languages.toml`):

```toml
[[language]]
name = "yaml"
language-servers = ["flak-lsp"]
```

## CI integration

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
- name: Lint YAML
  run: flak --format github "**/*.yaml" "**/*.yml"
```

Using `--format github` produces inline annotations on pull requests.

### GitLab CI

```yaml
lint-yaml:
  image: yourorg/flak:latest
  script:
    - flak --strict .
```

### Pre-commit

Add to `.pre-commit-config.yaml`:

```yaml
- repo: https://github.com/yourorg/flak
  rev: v1.2.0
  hooks:
    - id: flak
```

## Examples

**Catch a duplicate key** — YAML silently drops the second `image`:

```yaml
services:
  web:
    image: nginx:1.25
    image: nginx:1.27   # ← flak: duplicate key 'image'
```

**Enforce 2-space indentation**:

```yaml
# .flak.yml
rules:
  indentation: { severity: error, size: 2, style: space }
```

**Auto-fix on save**:

```bash
flak --fix .
```

## Performance

flak is written in Rust and parses files in parallel. On a MacBook Pro M3:

| Files | Size | Time |
|-------|------|------|
| 1,000 | 12 MB | 0.4 s |
| 10,000 | 120 MB | 3.1 s |
| 100,000 | 1.2 GB | 28 s |

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome. Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening a pull request.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/yourorg/flak.git
cd flak
cargo test
cargo run -- tests/fixtures/
```

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE) for details.

## Acknowledgements

Inspired by [`yamllint`](https://github.com/adrienverge/yamllint), [`prettier`](https://prettier.io/), and the many YAML files broken by a single stray tab.

```markdown
# flak

> A fast, configurable linter for YAML files.

`flak` catches syntax errors, style violations, and structural problems in your
YAML before they reach production. It ships with sensible defaults, runs in
milliseconds, and integrates cleanly into CI pipelines.

```console
$ flak .
config/deploy.yaml
  12:3   error    duplicate key "image"            no-duplicate-keys
  18:1   warning  line exceeds 120 characters      max-line-length
  24:7   error    tab character in indentation     no-tabs

k8s/service.yaml
   1:1   error    missing document start "---"    document-start
   9:5   warning  truthy value should be boolean  truthy

✖ 5 problems (3 errors, 2 warnings)
```

---

## Features

- **Fast** — written in Rust, lints thousands of files in under a second.
- **Safe** — parses YAML 1.2 with full anchor, alias, and merge-key support.
- **Configurable** — enable, disable, or tune every rule from a single config file.
- **Context-aware** — built-in presets for Kubernetes, GitHub Actions, Docker Compose, and Ansible.
- **Fixable** — `--fix` automatically resolves formatting and style violations.
- **Editor-friendly** — machine-readable output for VS Code, Neovim, and CI annotations.

## Installation

### Homebrew (macOS / Linux)

```sh
brew install flak
```

### Cargo

```sh
cargo install flak
```

### npm

```sh
npm install --global @flak/cli
```

### Prebuilt binaries

Download the latest release for your platform from the
[releases page](https://github.com/flak-dev/flak/releases).

## Quick start

Lint every YAML file in the current directory:

```sh
flak
```

Lint specific files or directories:

```sh
flak config/ .github/workflows/ docker-compose.yml
```

Lint from stdin:

```sh
cat deploy.yaml | flak -
```

## Usage

```
flak [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...
```

### Options

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-c, --config <FILE>` | Path to a config file. |
| `-f, --format <FORMAT>` | Output format: `pretty`, `compact`, `json`, `sarif`, `github`. Default: `pretty`. |
| `--fix` | Apply safe fixes in place. |
| `--dry-run` | Show what `--fix` would change without writing. |
| `--preset <NAME>` | Apply a preset: `default`, `k8s`, `github`, `compose`, `ansible`, `strict`. |
| `--select <RULES>` | Run only the listed rules (comma-separated). |
| `--ignore <RULES>` | Skip the listed rules. |
| `--max-warnings <N>` | Fail if warnings exceed `N`. Default: `-1` (unlimited). |
| `--no-color` | Disable colored output. |
| `--quiet` | Suppress output; rely on the exit code. |
| `-h, --help` | Print help. |
| `-V, --version` | Print version. |

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | No errors or warnings found. |
| `1` | Lint errors found. |
| `2` | Invalid CLI usage or configuration error. |

## Configuration

`flak` looks for a config file in the following order:

1. Path passed to `--config`
2. `.flak.toml` in the current directory
3. `.flak.toml` in any parent directory
4. `flak` key inside `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

### Example `.flak.toml`

```toml
preset = "k8s"

# Files and directories to skip
exclude = [
  "vendor/**",
  "**/generated/*.yaml",
  "charts/**/templates/**",
]

# Fail the run if more than 10 warnings are reported
max-warnings = 10

[rules]
# Disable a rule entirely
document-start = "off"

# Downgrade to a warning
truthy = "warn"

# Upgrade to an error and tune its options
max-line-length = { level = "error", length = 100 }

# Rule-specific options
indentation = { level = "error", spaces = 2, indent-sequences = true }

[overrides."k8s/**/*.yaml"]
document-start = "off"

[overrides.".github/workflows/*.yml"]
truthy = "error"
```

### Inline directives

Silence a rule for a single line or an entire file:

```yaml
# flak:ignore truthy
enabled: yes

image: latest  # flak:ignore-line no-latest-tag

# flak:ignore-file
```

## Rules

### Syntax

| Rule | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `parse-error` | error | The file is not valid YAML. |
| `no-duplicate-keys` | error | A mapping contains the same key twice. |
| `no-tabs` | error | Tab characters used for indentation. |
| `no-trailing-spaces` | warn | Lines end with whitespace. |

### Style

| Rule | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `document-start` | warn | File should begin with `---`. |
| `document-end` | off | File should end with `...`. |
| `indentation` | error | Consistent indentation width. |
| `max-line-length` | warn | Lines longer than 120 characters. |
| `new-line-at-end-of-file` | warn | File must end with a newline. |
| `empty-values` | warn | Empty values should be `null` or `~`, not blank. |
| `key-ordering` | off | Mapping keys must be alphabetically sorted. |
| `quoted-strings` | off | Enforce a consistent string quoting style. |

### Semantics

| Rule | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `truthy` | warn | `yes`/`no`/`on`/`off` should be `true`/`false`. |
| `octal-values` | warn | Ambiguous octal literals such as `0755`. |
| `no-latest-tag` | warn | Container images should not use the `latest` tag. |
| `anchors-defined` | error | An alias refers to an undefined anchor. |
| `anchors-used` | warn | An anchor is defined but never aliased. |
| `merge-key-depth` | off | Limit nested merge-key (`<<`) usage. |

Run `flak --list-rules` for the full list, including rule-specific options.

## CI integration

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
name: lint
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  flak:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: flak-dev/action@v1
        with:
          args: "--format github ."
```

### GitLab CI

```yaml
lint-yaml:
  image: ghcr.io/flak-dev/flak:latest
  script:
    - flak --format sarif . > flak.sarif
  artifacts:
    reports:
      sast: flak.sarif
```

### Pre-commit

```yaml

repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/flak-dev/flak
    rev: v1.4.0
    hooks:
      - id: flak
        args: ["--fix"]
```

## Output formats

`flak` can emit machine-readable results for tooling:

```sh
flak --format json .      # JSON array of diagnostics
flak --format sarif .     # SARIF 2.1.0 for code scanning
flak --format github .    # GitHub Actions workflow commands
flak --format compact .   # one line per diagnostic
```

## Performance

`flak` parses files in parallel across all available cores and caches results
between runs. On a repository with 10,000 YAML files:

| Tool | Time |
| --- | --- |
| flak | 0.8 s |
| yamllint | 14.2 s |

Contributions are welcome. Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before

cd flak

# flak

> A fast, configurable YAML linter for humans and CI pipelines.

[![CI](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/example/flak/ci.yml?branch=main)](https://github.com/example/flak/actions)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-1.0.0-green.svg)](https://github.com/example/flak/releases)

`flak` catches YAML mistakes before they reach production — syntax errors, duplicate keys, style violations, and unsafe patterns — with clear, actionable messages and a machine-readable output mode for CI.

---

## Features

- **Blazing fast** — written in Rust, lints thousands of files in milliseconds.
- **Syntax validation** — reports precise line/column for parse errors.
- **40+ built-in rules** — covering correctness, style, and security.
- **Configurable** — enable/disable rules, set severities, and override per-path.
- **Multiple output formats** — `pretty`, `json`, `sarif`, `github`, `checkstyle`.
- **Autofix** — automatically resolves safe style violations with `--fix`.
- **Recursive** — scans directories, respects `.gitignore` and `.flakignore`.
- **Editor & CI friendly** — stable exit codes and GitHub Actions annotations.

---

## Installation

### Homebrew (macOS / Linux)

```sh
brew install flak
```

### Cargo

```sh
cargo install flak
```

### npm

```sh
npm install -g @example/flak
```

### Prebuilt binaries

Download the latest release for your platform from the [releases page](https://github.com/example/flak/releases).

### Docker

```sh
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/work" -w /work ghcr.io/example/flak:latest .
```

---

## Quick start

```sh
# Lint a single file
flak config.yaml

# Lint a directory recursively
flak ./manifests

# Lint everything in the current repo
flak .

# Auto-fix safe style issues
flak --fix .

# Machine-readable output for CI
flak --format json . > flak-report.json
```

Example output:

```
config.yaml
  3:1   error    duplicate-key          Duplicate key "image" in mapping (previous at 2:1)
  7:15  warning  trailing-spaces        Trailing whitespace
  9:5   error    syntax-error           Unexpected token "}" — expected ":" or "?"
  12:3  warning  key-order              Keys should be sorted alphabetically (a, b, c)

✖ 4 problems (2 errors, 2 warnings)
```

---

## Usage

```
flak [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...

Arguments:
  [PATHS]...  Files or directories to lint. Defaults to "." when omitted.

Options:
  -c, --config <FILE>       Path to a configuration file
      --no-config           Ignore configuration files
  -f, --format <FORMAT>     Output format [default: pretty]
                            [possible values: pretty, json, sarif, github, checkstyle]
      --fix                 Apply safe autofixes
      --dry-run             Show what --fix would change without writing
      --severity <LEVEL>    Minimum severity to report [default: warning]
                            [possible values: info, warning, error]
  -r, --rule <RULE>         Enable only the given rule (repeatable)
      --ignore <RULE>       Disable the given rule (repeatable)
      --ignore-path <GLOB>  Skip files matching the glob (repeatable)
      --stdin               Read YAML from stdin instead of files
      --no-color            Disable colored output
  -q, --quiet               Suppress non-error output
  -v, --verbose             Increase log verbosity
  -h, --help                Print help
  -V, --version             Print version
```

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning                                        |
|------|------------------------------------------------|
| `0`  | No problems found                              |
| `1`  | One or more errors found                       |
| `2`  | Invalid usage or configuration                 |
| `3`  | Internal error (please report)                 |

---

## Rules

Rules are grouped by category. Each rule has a stable ID and a default severity.

### Correctness

| Rule | Severity | Description |
|------|----------|-------------|
| `syntax-error` | error | Invalid YAML syntax |
| `duplicate-key` | error | Duplicate keys in a mapping |
| `unknown-tag` | error | Unknown or unsupported YAML tag |
| `anchor-undefined` | error | Reference to an undefined anchor |
| `circular-anchor` | error | Circular anchor reference |
| `empty-document` | warning | Document is empty |

### Style

| Rule | Severity | Description |
|------|----------|-------------|
| `indent` | warning | Inconsistent indentation (2 spaces expected) |
| `trailing-spaces` | warning | Trailing whitespace |
| `line-length` | warning | Line exceeds 120 characters |
| `key-order` | warning | Keys not sorted alphabetically |
| `empty-lines` | warning | More than one consecutive empty line |
| `document-start` | warning | Missing `---` document start marker |
| `document-end` | warning | Missing `...` document end marker |
| `quotes` | warning | Inconsistent quote style |
| `comments` | warning | Comment spacing (`# foo` not `#foo`) |

### Security

| Rule | Severity | Description |
|------|----------|-------------|
| `unsafe-tag` | error | Use of unsafe tags like `!!python/object` |
| `plain-secret` | warning | Likely secret in plain text (API keys, tokens) |
| `env-default` | warning | `${VAR:-default}` with hardcoded secret |

### Best practices

| Rule | Severity | Description |
|------|----------|-------------|
| `no-tabs` | error | Tabs used for indentation |
| `no-bom` | warning | File starts with a UTF-8 BOM |
| `final-newline` | warning | File does not end with a newline |
| `no-aliases` | info | Aliases discouraged in some configs |
| `deprecated-key` | warning | Deprecated key detected |

See the full rule reference in [docs/rules.md](docs/rules.md).

---

## Configuration

`flak` reads configuration from `.flak.yaml`, `.flak.yml`, or a `flak` key in `package.json`. Configuration is resolved from the nearest ancestor directory of each linted file.

```yaml
# .flak.yaml
extends: recommended

rules:
  indent:
    severity: error
    options:
      size: 2
      style: space

  line-length:
    severity: warning
    options:
      max: 100

  key-order: off
  no-aliases: error

ignore:
  - "vendor/**"
  - "**/*.generated.yaml"

overrides:
  - files: ["charts/**"]
    rules:
      line-length: off
```

### Presets

| Preset | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `recommended` | Balanced defaults — recommended for most projects |
| `strict` | All rules enabled at `error` |
| `style` | Style rules only |
| `security` | Security-focused rules only |
| `off` | No rules enabled |

### Inline suppression

```yaml
# flak: disable-next-line duplicate-key
foo: 1
foo: 2

# flak: disable key-order
b: 2
a: 1
```

---

## CI integration

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
- name: Lint YAML
  uses: example/flak-action@v1
  with:
    args: "."
```

Or use the CLI directly with `--format github` for inline annotations:

```yaml
- run: flak --format github .
```

### GitLab CI

```yaml
lint:yaml:
  image: ghcr.io/example/flak:latest
  script:
    - flak --format checkstyle . > report.xml
  artifacts:
    reports:
      codequality: report.xml
```

### Pre-commit

```yaml
# .pre-commit-config.yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/example/flak
    rev: v1.0.0
    hooks:
      - id: flak
```

---

## Editor integration

- **VS Code** — install [flak-vscode](https://github.com/example/flak-vscode)
- **Neovim** — via `nvim-lint` or `null-ls`
- **JetBrains** — plugin in development

---

## Comparison

| Tool | Speed | Rules | Autofix | Config |
|------|-------|-------|---------|--------|
| **flak** | ⚡⚡⚡ | 40+ | ✅ | YAML |
| yamllint | ⚡ | 20+ | ❌ | YAML |
| spectral | ⚡⚡ | 60+ | partial | YAML/JS |
| prettier | ⚡⚡ | style only | ✅ | JSON |

---

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome! Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening a pull request.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/example/flak
cd flak
cargo test
```

---

## License

MIT © The flak authors. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) for details.

runs.output:
# flak

> A fast, opinionated YAML linter.

`flak` catches the YAML mistakes that slip past your parser — duplicate keys, inconsistent indentation, trailing whitespace, dangerously permissive tags, and more. It runs in milliseconds, works on single files or whole directories, and plays nicely with your CI.

```
$ flak config/
config/deploy.yaml
  12:5   error    duplicate key "image"           no-duplicate-keys
  18:1   warning  trailing whitespace             no-trailing-whitespace
  24:9   error    tabs are not allowed            no-tabs
  31:3   warning  line exceeds 120 characters     max-line-length

✖ 4 problems (2 errors, 2 warnings)
```

## Features

- **Fast** — written in Rust; lints thousands of files in under a second.
- **Safe** — parses with a strict YAML 1.2 loader. No `!!python/object` surprises.
- **Configurable** — enable, disable, and tune rules per-project with `.flak.yaml`.
- **Editor-friendly** — machine-readable output formats for LSPs, editors, and CI.
- **Fix mode** — automatically repairs whitespace, indentation, and quoting issues.
- **Multi-document aware** — handles `---` separated streams and anchors/aliases correctly.

## Installation

### Homebrew

```sh
brew install flak
```

### Cargo

```sh
cargo install flak
```

### npm

```sh
npm install --global @flak/cli
```

### Pre-built binaries

Download the latest release for your platform from the [releases page](https://github.com/example/flak/releases).

## Usage

```
flak [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...
```

Lint a single file:

```sh
flak config.yaml
```

Lint everything under the current directory:

```sh
flak .
```

Lint from stdin:

```sh
cat config.yaml | flak -
```

### Options

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-c, --config <PATH>` | Path to a config file. Defaults to `.flak.yaml`. |
| `-f, --format <FORMAT>` | Output format: `pretty` (default), `json`, `github`, `sarif`, `quiet`. |
| `-q, --quiet` | Only print errors, suppress warnings. |
| `--fix` | Apply safe autofixes in place. |
| `--no-color` | Disable colored output. |
| `--stdin-filename <NAME>` | Filename to use when linting from stdin (for config resolution). |
| `-j, --jobs <N>` | Number of parallel workers. Defaults to the number of CPUs. |
| `-h, --help` | Print help. |
| `-V, --version` | Print version. |

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | No problems found. |
| `1` | One or more errors found. |
| `2` | Invalid usage or configuration error. |

Warnings alone do not cause a non-zero exit unless `--strict` is set.

## Configuration

`flak` looks for a `.flak.yaml` file in the current directory, then walks up to the filesystem root. You can also pass one explicitly with `--config`.

```yaml
# .flak.yaml
extends: flak:recommended

rules:
  no-duplicate-keys: error
  no-tabs: error
  no-trailing-whitespace: warning
  max-line-length:
    level: warning
    length: 100
  document-start:
    level: off

ignore:
  - "vendor/**"
  - "**/*.generated.yaml"

overrides:
  - files: ["charts/**/*.yaml"]
    rules:
      key-ordering: off
```

### Rule levels

Every rule accepts one of four levels:

- `error` — reported and fails the run.
- `warning` — reported but does not fail the run (unless `--strict`).
- `info` — reported only with `--verbose`.
- `off` — disabled.

## Rules

| Rule | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `no-duplicate-keys` | error | Disallow duplicate mapping keys. |
| `no-tabs` | error | Disallow tab characters for indentation. |
| `no-trailing-whitespace` | warning | Disallow trailing whitespace. |
| `no-empty-values` | warning | Disallow empty values (`key:` with no value). |
| `indentation` | error | Enforce consistent indentation (default: 2 spaces). |
| `max-line-length` | warning | Enforce a maximum line length (default: 120). |
| `document-start` | warning | Require `---` at the start of each document. |
| `document-end` | off | Require `...` at the end of each document. |
| `key-ordering` | off | Enforce alphabetical or custom key ordering. |
| `no-anchors` | off | Disallow anchors and aliases. |
| `no-custom-tags` | error | Disallow non-standard tags like `!!python/object`. |
| `quoted-strings` | off | Enforce quoting style for strings. |
| `truthy` | error | Disallow `yes`/`no`/`on`/`off` as booleans. |
| `new-line-at-end-of-file` | warning | Require a trailing newline. |
| `empty-document` | warning | Disallow empty documents. |

Run `flak --list-rules` to see the full list with descriptions and defaults.

## Autofix

`--fix` applies safe, non-destructive fixes:

```sh
flak --fix .
```

The following rules support autofix: `no-trailing-whitespace`, `indentation`, `new-line-at-end-of-file`, `document-start`, and `quoted-strings`.

Fixes are applied atomically — if a file cannot be fully fixed, it is left untouched.

## Editor integration

### VS Code

Install the [flak extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=example.flak) or configure your own:

```json
{
  "yaml.validate": false,
  "flak.enable": true,
  "flak.run": "onSave"
}
```

### Neovim (nvim-lint)

```lua
require("lint").linters.flak = {
  cmd = "flak",
  stdin = true,
  args = { "--format", "json", "-" },
  stream = "stdout",
  ignore_exitcode = true,
  parser = require("lint.parser").from_errorformat(
    "%f:%l:%c: %t%n %m",
    { source = "flak" }
  ),
}
```

## CI integration

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
- name: Lint YAML
  run: flak --format github .
```

The `github` format emits workflow commands so problems appear inline on the diff.

### pre-commit

```yaml
# .pre-commit-config.yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/example/flak
    rev: v1.4.0
    hooks:
      - id: flak
```

### GitLab CI

```yaml
lint:yaml:
  image: example/flak:latest
  script:
    - flak --format sarif . > flak.sarif
  artifacts:
    reports:
      sast: flak.sarif
```

## Ignoring problems

Suppress a single problem with a comment on the preceding line:

```yaml
# flak: ignore-next-line no-duplicate-keys
image: foo
image: bar
```

Suppress a whole file:

```yaml
# flak: ignore-file
```

## Comparison

| Tool | Language | Speed | Autofix | Config |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `flak` | Rust | ⚡⚡⚡ | ✅ | YAML |
| `yamllint` | Python | ⚡ | ❌ | YAML |
| `yaml-lint` | Node | ⚡⚡ | ❌ | JSON |

`flak` aims to be a drop-in replacement for `yamllint` for most projects. See [`MIGRATING.md`](./MIGRATING.md) for a rule-by-rule mapping.

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome. Please read [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](./CONTRIBUTING.md) and open an issue before starting work on a new rule.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/example/flak
cd flak
cargo test
cargo run -- tests/fixtures
```

## License

MIT — see [`LICENSE`](./LICENSE).

`flak` catches the YAML mistakes that break your CI at 3am — inconsistent indentation, duplicate keys, trailing whitespace, and the subtle type coercion bugs that turn `no` into `false` and `1.0` into `1`.

```
$ flak config/
config/deploy.yaml
  12:5   warning   trailing whitespace
  18:1   error     duplicate key "image"
  24:9   error     inconsistent indentation (expected 2 spaces, found 4)

config/services.yaml
  3:1    error     tab character in indentation

✖ 4 problems (3 errors, 1 warning)
```

## Features

- **Fast** — written in Go, lints thousands of files in milliseconds
- **Opinionated defaults** — sensible rules out of the box, zero config required
- **Auto-fix** — safely repairs formatting issues with `--fix`
- **CI-friendly** — exit codes, machine-readable output, and inline annotations
- **Extensible** — per-directory config, ignore files, and rule severity overrides

## Installation

### Homebrew (macOS / Linux)

```sh
brew install flak
```

### npm

```sh
npm install -g flak-cli
```

### Go

```sh
go install github.com/flakdev/flak@latest

Download the latest release for your platform from the [releases page](https://github.com/flakdev/flak/releases).

Lint a single file:

```sh
flak config.yaml
```

Lint a directory (recursively):

```sh
flak ./config
```

Lint everything tracked by Git:

```sh
flak $(git ls-files '*.yaml' '*.yml')
```

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--fix` | Automatically fix any issues that are safe to repair |
| `--format <fmt>` | Output format: `pretty` (default), `json`, `github`, `sarif` |
| `--config <path>` | Use a specific config file |
| `--ignore <glob>` | Skip files matching a glob (repeatable) |
| `--strict` | Treat warnings as errors |
| `--quiet` | Only print errors |
| `--version` | Print version and exit |

### Examples

Fix everything in place:

```sh
flak --fix ./config
```

Emit GitHub Actions annotations:

```sh
flak --format github ./config
```

Fail CI on any warning:

```sh
flak --strict ./config
```

`flak` looks for a `.flak.yaml` (or `.flak.yml`) file in the current directory, then walks up to the repository root. A minimal config:

```yaml
# .flak.yaml
rules:

  line-length:

| `empty-values` | `warning` | Flag empty values that may be unintentional |
| `anchors` | `warning` | Warn on unused anchors and aliases |

Set any rule to `off`, `warning`, or `error` to control its severity.

```

*.min.yaml
fixtures/**
```

### GitHub Actions

- name: Lint YAML

```

### GitLab CI

| `2` | Invalid usage or configuration error |

```sh

Read from stdin:

```

Arguments:

  -c, --config <FILE>      Path to a config file [default: .flak.yaml]
      --no-config          Ignore any config file
  -f, --format <FORMAT>    Output format: text, json, sarif, junit [default: text]
      --fix                Apply safe fixes in place
      --dry-run            With --fix, show changes without writing
      --schema <FILE>      Validate against a JSON Schema file
      --k8s                Validate against built-in Kubernetes schemas
      --exclude <GLOB>     Skip files matching a glob (repeatable)
      --max-warnings <N>   Exit non-zero if warnings exceed N
  -q, --quiet              Only print errors
  -v, --verbose            Print per-file progress
  -h, --help               Print help
  -V, --version            Print version
```

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning                                        |
| ---- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `0`  | No problems found                              |
| `1`  | One or more errors (or warnings over threshold)|
| `2`  | Invalid usage or configuration                 |
| `3`  | Internal error                                 |

---

## Configuration

`flak` looks for `.flak.yaml` in the current directory, then walks up to the filesystem root. Files may also declare inline overrides with a `# flak: disable` comment.

```yaml
# .flak.yaml
extends: flak:recommended

rules:
  line-length:
    max: 100
  indentation:
    spaces: 2
    style: consistent
  key-ordering:
    order: [apiVersion, kind, metadata, spec]
  quoted-strings:
    quote-type: double
    required: only-when-needed

overrides:
  - files: ["charts/**/*.yaml"]
    rules:
      line-length: off
  - files: ["**/*.json"]
    rules:
      document-start: off

exclude:
  - "**/vendor/**"
  - "**/.git/**"
```

### Inline directives

```yaml
# flak: disable-next-line line-length
some_really_long_key: and a really long value that would otherwise be flagged

# flak: disable indentation
weird:
   block: here
# flak: enable indentation
```

---

## Rules

`flak` ships with three rule sets. `flak:recommended` (the default) enables all rules marked ✅ below.

### Syntax

| Rule             | Default | Description                                        |
| ---------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `parse-error`    | ✅      | Rejects malformed YAML                             |
| `duplicate-key`  | ✅      | Flags duplicate keys in the same mapping           |
| `no-tabs`        | ✅      | Disallows tab characters for indentation           |
| `no-empty-values`| ✅      | Flags keys with no value                           |

### Style

| Rule              | Default | Description                                       |
| ----------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `indentation`     | ✅      | Consistent indentation width and style            |
| `line-length`     | ✅      | Maximum line length (default 120)                 |
| `trailing-spaces` | ✅      | No trailing whitespace                            |
| `document-start`  | ✅      | Require `---` at the top of each document         |
| `document-end`    |         | Require `...` at the end of each document         |
| `new-line-at-eof` | ✅      | Files must end with a newline                     |
| `quoted-strings`  | ✅      | Consistent quoting style                          |
| `key-ordering`    |         | Enforce a key order (e.g. Kubernetes manifests)   |
| `empty-lines`     | ✅      | No more than one consecutive blank line           |
| `comments`        | ✅      | Require a space after `#`                         |

### Semantic

| Rule             | Default | Description                                        |
| ---------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `schema`         |         | Validate against a JSON Schema (opt-in via `--schema` or `--k8s`) |
| `anchor-usage`   | ✅      | Unused or duplicate anchors                        |
| `alias-depth`    | ✅      | Reject deeply nested aliases (billion-laughs guard)|
| `truthy`         | ✅      | Reject `yes`/`no`/`on`/`off` as booleans (YAML 1.1 trap) |

Run `flak --list-rules` to see every rule with its full description and options.

---

## CI integration

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
- uses: example/flak-action@v1
  with:
    paths: .
    format: sarif
```

### GitLab CI

```yaml
lint:yaml:
  image: ghcr.io/example/flak:latest
  script:
    - flak --format junit --output flak.xml .
  artifacts:
    reports:
      junit: flak.xml
```

### pre-commit

```yaml
# .pre-commit-config.yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/example/flak
    rev: v1.4.0
    hooks:
      - id: flak
        args: [--fix]
```

---

## Editor support

- **VS Code** — [flak-vscode](https://github.com/example/flak-vscode) (uses the language server)
- **Neovim** — via `nvim-lint` or the built-in LSP client
- **JetBrains IDEs** — [flak-jetbrains](https://github.com/example/flak-jetbrains)

All integrations consume the same JSON output, so any editor that can run a command and parse JSON can use `flak`.

---

## Performance

Benchmarked on a 2021 MacBook Pro (M1 Pro), linting the [Kubernetes manifests repo](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes) (~14,000 YAML files):

| Tool    | Time   |
| ------- | ------ |
| `flak`  | 0.9 s  |
| `yamllint` | 11.4 s |

---

## Contributing

Bug reports and pull requests are welcome. Before opening a PR:

```sh
cargo test
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --check
```

Please add a test for any new rule and update `docs/rules.md`.

---

Unless you explicitly state otherwise, any contribution intentionally submitted for inclusion in this project shall be dual-licensed as above, without any additional terms or conditions.

# flak

A fast, opinionated linter for YAML files.

`flak` helps you catch syntax errors, style inconsistencies, and common pitfalls in your YAML before they hit production. Whether you're managing Kubernetes manifests, CI/CD pipelines, or configuration files, `flak` keeps your YAML clean and predictable.

---

## Features

- **Syntax validation** — Detects malformed YAML, tabs in indentation, and unclosed quotes.
- **Style enforcement** — Configurable rules for indentation, key ordering, line length, and trailing whitespace.
- **Duplicate key detection** — Catches silently-overwritten keys that YAML parsers happily accept.
- **Schema validation** — Optionally validate against JSON Schema or a custom ruleset.
- **Fast** — Written in Go, lints thousands of files in milliseconds.
- **CI-friendly** — Non-zero exit codes and machine-readable output (`--format=json`).

---

## Installation

### Homebrew (macOS / Linux)

```bash
brew install flak
```

### npm

```bash
npm install -g flak
```

### Go

```bash
go install github.com/yourorg/flak@latest
```

### Binary releases

Download a prebuilt binary from the [releases page](https://github.com/yourorg/flak/releases).

---

## Usage

Lint a single file:

```bash
flak config.yaml
```

Lint an entire directory (recursively):

```bash
flak ./manifests
```

Lint multiple paths and globs:

```bash
flak "config/*.yml" ".github/workflows/*.yaml"
```

Read from stdin:

```bash
cat config.yaml | flak -
```

### Example output

```
manifests/deployment.yaml
  12:3   error    duplicate key "image"          duplicate-key
  18:1   warning  line exceeds 100 characters    max-line-length
  24:5   error    tabs are not allowed in YAML   no-tabs

✖ 3 problems (2 errors, 1 warning)
```

---

## Common flags

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-c, --config <file>` | Path to a config file (default: `.flak.yml`) |
| `-f, --format <fmt>` | Output format: `pretty` (default), `json`, `github` |
| `--fix` | Automatically fix fixable issues (e.g., trailing whitespace) |
| `--ignore <glob>` | Ignore files matching a glob (repeatable) |
| `--strict` | Treat warnings as errors |
| `--quiet` | Only report errors, suppress warnings |
| `-h, --help` | Show help |
| `-v, --version` | Show version |

---

## Configuration

Create a `.flak.yml` file in your project root:

```yaml
# .flak.yml
rules:
  duplicate-key: error
  no-tabs: error
  trailing-whitespace: warning
  max-line-length:
    level: warning
    length: 120
  indentation:
    level: warning
    spaces: 2
  document-start: off
  key-ordering:
    level: warning
    order: [apiVersion, kind, metadata, spec]

ignore:
  - "vendor/**"
  - "**/generated/*.yaml"
```

### Rule levels

- `error` — Fails the lint run.
- `warning` — Reported but does not fail (unless `--strict`).
- `off` — Rule disabled.

---

## CI integration

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
- name: Lint YAML
  uses: yourorg/flak-action@v1
  with:
    args: "."
```

Or directly:

```yaml
- name: Lint YAML
  run: flak --format=github .
```

### Pre-commit hook

Add to `.pre-commit-config.yaml`:

```yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/yourorg/flak
    rev: v1.2.0
    hooks:
      - id: flak
```

---

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | No errors found |
| `1` | Lint errors found |
| `2` | Invalid usage or internal error |

---

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome! Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening a pull request.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/yourorg/flak
cd flak
make test
```

## License

[MIT](LICENSE) © Your Org

runs.output:
# flak

**A fast, opinionated YAML linter.**

`flak` catches the YAML mistakes that break your CI at 2am — duplicate keys, tabs where spaces belong, unquoted booleans, trailing whitespace, and a hundred other papercuts — before they ever leave your editor.

```console
$ flak deploy/
deploy/production.yaml
  12:3   error    duplicate key 'replicas'            no-duplicate-keys
  18:11  error    tab character in indentation        no-tabs
  24:7   warning  value 'yes' parses as boolean       quoted-booleans
  31:1   error    trailing whitespace                 no-trailing-spaces

✖ 4 problems (3 errors, 1 warning)
```

---

## Why flak?

- **Fast.** Written in Rust, parses in parallel, lints a 10,000-file monorepo in under a second.
- **Correct.** Uses a real YAML 1.2 parser — no regex hacks, no false positives on block scalars or anchors.
- **Opinionated by default, configurable when you need it.** Sensible rules out of the box, every one of them overridable.
- **Editor-friendly.** Machine-readable output for LSPs, SARIF, and CI annotations.
- **Zero config required.** Point it at a file or directory and it just works.

---

## Installation

### Homebrew (macOS / Linux)

```sh
brew install flak
```

### Cargo

```sh
cargo install flak-cli
```

### npm

```sh
npm install --global @flak/cli
```

### Pre-built binaries

Download the latest release for your platform from the [releases page](https://github.com/example/flak/releases).

---

## Quick start

```sh
# Lint a single file
flak config.yaml

# Lint everything under a directory
flak .

# Lint only files matching a glob
flak '**/*.yaml' '**/*.yml'

# Auto-fix what can be fixed
flak --fix .
```

`flak` exits with a non-zero status when it finds errors, so you can drop it straight into a pre-commit hook or CI pipeline.

---

## Usage

```
flak [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...
```

### Options

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-c, --config <FILE>` | Path to a config file. Defaults to `.flak.yaml` in the nearest ancestor directory. |
| `-f, --format <FORMAT>` | Output format: `pretty` (default), `json`, `sarif`, `github`, `quiet`. |
| `--fix` | Apply safe autofixes in place. |
| `--fix-dry-run` | Show what `--fix` would change without writing. |
| `--rule <RULE>` | Run only the given rule. Repeatable. |
| `--ignore <RULE>` | Skip the given rule. Repeatable. |
| `--severity <LEVEL>` | Minimum severity to report: `error`, `warning`, `info`. |
| `--stdin` | Read from stdin instead of files. |
| `--no-color` | Disable colored output. |
| `--max-warnings <N>` | Fail if more than `N` warnings are emitted. |
| `-q, --quiet` | Only print errors. |
| `-v, --verbose` | Print every file checked, including clean ones. |
| `-h, --help` | Print help. |
| `-V, --version` | Print version. |

### Examples

```sh
# Pipe from another tool
cat generated.yaml | flak --stdin

# Machine-readable output for a custom dashboard
flak --format json . > report.json

# Enforce zero warnings in CI
flak --max-warnings 0 .

# Run only the rules you care about
flak --rule no-duplicate-keys --rule no-tabs .
```

---

## Rules

`flak` ships with the following rules. Each is enabled by default unless noted.

### Errors

| Rule | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `no-duplicate-keys` | Two keys with the same name in one mapping. |
| `no-tabs` | Tab characters used for indentation. |
| `valid-syntax` | The file must parse as YAML 1.2. |
| `no-empty-document` | A document that is empty or contains only comments. |
| `consistent-indentation` | Mixed indentation widths within a file. |

### Warnings

| Rule | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `quoted-booleans` | `yes`, `no`, `on`, `off` used as bare scalars — they parse as booleans in YAML 1.1. |
| `quoted-numbers` | Numeric strings left unquoted, e.g. version `1.10` becoming `1.1`. |
| `no-trailing-spaces` | Whitespace at the end of a line. |
| `no-trailing-newline` | File does not end with exactly one newline. |
| `key-ordering` | Keys in a mapping are not alphabetically sorted. *(off by default)* |
| `line-length` | Lines longer than 120 characters. *(off by default)* |
| `no-anchors` | Anchors and aliases used. *(off by default)* |

### Info

| Rule | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `document-start` | File does not begin with `---`. *(off by default)* |
| `no-comments` | File contains comments. *(off by default)* |

Run `flak --list-rules` to see the full set with descriptions, or `flak --explain <rule>` for a detailed write-up with examples.

---

## Configuration

`flak` looks for a `.flak.yaml` file in the current directory, then walks up the tree until it finds one. You can also pass `--config <FILE>` explicitly.

```yaml
# .flak.yaml
extends: flak:recommended

rules:
  no-trailing-spaces: error
  line-length:
    severity: warning
    max: 100
  key-ordering: off
  no-comments: off

ignore:
  - "vendor/**"
  - "**/generated/*.yaml"

overrides:
  - files: ["k8s/**/*.yaml"]
    rules:
      document-start: error
      no-anchors: off
```

### Inline suppression

Disable a rule for a single line or file:

```yaml
# flak:disable-next-line no-trailing-spaces
key: value   

# flak:disable no-anchors
defaults: &defaults
  retries: 3
```

---

## Ignoring files

`flak` respects `.gitignore` by default. Add a `.flakignore` file for linter-specific exclusions:

```
vendor/
node_modules/
*.generated.yaml
```

---

## CI integration

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
- name: Lint YAML
  run: flak --format github .
```

The `github` format emits `::error` and `::warning` annotations that appear inline on the pull request diff.

### GitLab CI

```yaml
lint:yaml:
  image: ghcr.io/example/flak:latest
  script:
    - flak --format sarif . > flak.sarif
  artifacts:
    reports:
      sast: flak.sarif
```

### pre-commit

```yaml
# .pre-commit-config.yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/example/flak
    rev: v1.4.0
    hooks:
      - id: flak
```

---

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | No errors found. |
| `1` | One or more errors found. |
| `2` | Invalid usage or configuration. |
| `3` | Internal error (please [file a bug](https://github.com/example/flak/issues)). |

---

## Editor support

- **VS Code** — [`flak-vscode`](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=example.flak-vscode)
- **Neovim** — via [`nvim-lint`](https://github.com/mfussenegger/nvim-lint) or `null-ls`
- **Helix** — built-in LSP support, configure `flak lsp` as the language server

Any editor that speaks LSP can use `flak lsp`, which runs the linter on every keystroke and reports diagnostics in real time.

---

## Performance

On a 2019 MacBook Pro, linting the [Kubernetes manifests](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/cluster) (~8,400 YAML files):

| Tool | Time |
| --- | --- |
| `flak` | 0.7s |
| `yamllint` | 14.2s |

`flak` parses files in parallel across all cores and skips anything already cached by content hash.

---

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome. Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening a pull request.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/example/flak
cd flak
cargo test
cargo run -- tests/fixtures/
```

---

## License

MIT © The flak contributors. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) for details.

runs.output:
# 🐾 paw

> A tiny collection of 12 accessible, unstyled-by-default React UI primitives.
> Small enough to read in one sitting, composable enough to build on.

[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@paw/ui.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@paw/ui)
[![bundle size](https://img.shields.io/bundlephobia/minzip/@paw/ui)](https://bundlephobia.com/package/@paw/ui)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/@paw/ui.svg)](./LICENSE)

---

## Why paw?

Most component libraries want to own your design system. `paw` doesn't. It ships **12 small, focused primitives** with sensible defaults, full keyboard support, and WAI-ARIA compliance — but no opinions about your colors, spacing, or typography.

- 🪶 **Tiny** — ~6 kB gzipped for the whole library
- ♿ **Accessible** — keyboard navigation and ARIA attributes out of the box
- 🎨 **Themeable** — CSS variables + `className` passthrough on every component
- 🧩 **Composable** — compound components (`<Tabs.List>`, `<Card.Header>`) where it matters
- 📦 **Tree-shakeable** — ESM first, side-effect free
- 🧪 **Typed** — first-class TypeScript definitions

---

## Installation

```bash
npm install @paw/ui
# or
pnpm add @paw/ui
# or
yarn add @paw/ui
```

Peer dependencies: `react >= 18` and `react-dom >= 18`.

---

## Quick start

```tsx
import { Button, Card, Input, Badge } from '@paw/ui';
import '@paw/ui/styles.css';

export function Signup() {
  return (
    <Card>
      <Card.Header>
        <Card.Title>Join the pack</Card.Title>
        <Badge tone="success">New</Badge>
      </Card.Header>
      <Card.Body>
        <Input label="Email" type="email" placeholder="you@example.com" />
      </Card.Body>
      <Card.Footer>
        <Button variant="primary">Sign up</Button>
      </Card.Footer>
    </Card>
  );
}
```

---

## The 12 primitives

| # | Component  | What it does |
|---|------------|--------------|
| 1 | `<Button>`  | Clickable action with `variant`, `size`, `loading`, `icon` slots. |
| 2 | `<Input>`   | Single-line text field with label, hint, and error states. |
| 3 | `<Checkbox>`| Tri-state capable checkbox with indeterminate support. |
| 4 | `<Radio>`   | Radio button, works standalone or inside `<Radio.Group>`. |
| 5 | `<Switch>`  | On/off toggle with accessible `role="switch"` semantics. |
| 6 | `<Select>`  | Native-backed select with custom trigger styling. |
| 7 | `<Badge>`   | Small status label with `tone` and `dot` variants. |
| 8 | `<Avatar>`  | Image or initials fallback, with `<Avatar.Group>` stacking. |
| 9 | `<Card>`    | Compound container: `Header`, `Title`, `Body`, `Footer`. |
| 10 | `<Tooltip>`| Hover/focus tooltip, portals by default, delay configurable. |
| 11 | `<Modal>`  | Focus-trapped dialog with backdrop and escape-to-close. |
| 12 | `<Tabs>`   | Compound tab set: `List`, `Tab`, `Panel`, arrow-key nav. |

---

## Component examples

### Button

```tsx
<Button variant="primary" size="md" onClick={save}>
  Save changes
</Button>

<Button variant="ghost" loading>
  Saving…
</Button>

<Button variant="danger" iconLeft={<TrashIcon />}>
  Delete
</Button>
```

| Prop       | Type                                       | Default     |
|------------|--------------------------------------------|-------------|
| `variant`  | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'ghost' \| 'danger'` | `'secondary'` |
| `size`     | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'`                     | `'md'`      |
| `loading`  | `boolean`                                  | `false`     |
| `iconLeft` | `ReactNode`                                | —           |
| `iconRight`| `ReactNode`                                | —           |

### Input

```tsx
<Input
  label="Password"
  type="password"
  hint="At least 12 characters"
  error={errors.password}
  value={password}
  onChange={(e) => setPassword(e.target.value)}
/>
```

### Switch

```tsx
<Switch
  checked={enabled}
  onCheckedChange={setEnabled}
  label="Enable notifications"
/>
```

### Modal

```tsx
<Modal open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  <Modal.Content>
    <Modal.Title>Delete project?</Modal.Title>
    <Modal.Description>This action cannot be undone.</Modal.Description>
    <Modal.Actions>
      <Button variant="ghost" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Cancel</Button>
      <Button variant="danger" onClick={confirm}>Delete</Button>
    </Modal.Actions>
  </Modal.Content>
</Modal>
```

### Tabs

```tsx
<Tabs defaultValue="overview">
  <Tabs.List>
    <Tabs.Tab value="overview">Overview</Tabs.Tab>
    <Tabs.Tab value="activity">Activity</Tabs.Tab>
    <Tabs.Tab value="settings">Settings</Tabs.Tab>
  </Tabs.List>
  <Tabs.Panel value="overview">…</Tabs.Panel>
  <Tabs.Panel value="activity">…</Tabs.Panel>
  <Tabs.Panel value="settings">…</Tabs.Panel>
</Tabs>
```

---

## Theming

Every visual token is a CSS variable. Override them at `:root`, on a wrapper, or per-component:

```css
:root {
  --paw-color-accent: #4f46e5;
  --paw-color-accent-contrast: #ffffff;
  --paw-color-danger: #dc2626;
  --paw-color-surface: #ffffff;
  --paw-color-border: #e5e7eb;

  --paw-radius-sm: 4px;
  --paw-radius-md: 8px;
  --paw-radius-lg: 12px;

  --paw-focus-ring: 0 0 0 3px rgb(79 70 229 / 0.4);

Want to go further? Every component accepts `className` and `style`, and exposes stable `data-paw-*` attributes for targeting:

```css
[data-paw-button][data-variant='primary'] {
  background: linear-gradient(180deg, #6366f1, #4f46e5);
}
```

---

## Accessibility

`paw` aims for **WCAG 2.2 AA** by default:

- All interactive components are fully keyboard operable.
- Focus is trapped inside `<Modal>` and restored to the trigger on close.
- `<Tabs>` supports `ArrowLeft`, `ArrowRight`, `Home`, and `End`.
- `<Tooltip>` opens on hover **and** focus, and dismisses on `Escape`.
- Reduced-motion preferences are respected via `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Form controls use `aria-describedby` to wire hints and errors to inputs.

Found an a11y issue? Please [open an issue](https://github.com/paw-ui/paw/issues) — they're treated as bugs, not feature requests.

---

## Development

```bash
git clone https://github.com/paw-ui/paw.git
cd paw
pnpm install
pnpm dev        # Storybook on :6006
pnpm test       # Vitest + Testing Library
pnpm build      # tsup → dist/
pnpm lint       # ESLint + Prettier
```

The repo is a pnpm workspace:

```
packages/
  paw/          # the published library
  docs/         # docs site + Storybook
  playground/   # Vite sandbox for manual testing
```

---

## Browser support

Chrome / Edge 90+, Firefox 88+, Safari 14+. No IE.

# 🐾 paw

> A tiny collection of 12 unstyled-ish React UI primitives. Small API, zero dependencies, fully typed.

`paw` is a lightweight React component library built for people who want small, composable building blocks instead of a full design system. Every component is under 2KB gzipped, ships with TypeScript types, and works with any styling approach — CSS modules, Tailwind, styled-components, or plain CSS.

---

## ✨ Features

- 🪶 **Tiny** — 12 primitives, ~8KB gzipped total
- 🧩 **Composable** — every component forwards refs and spreads props
- 🎨 **Style-agnostic** — no CSS-in-JS runtime, no global styles injected
- ♿ **Accessible** — WAI-ARIA patterns baked in (focus traps, roles, keyboard nav)
- 🟦 **Typed** — first-class TypeScript definitions
- 🌳 **Tree-shakeable** — ESM + CJS builds, import only what you use
- ⚛️ **React 18+** — works with React 18 and 19, StrictMode-safe

---

## 📦 Installation

```bash
npm install @paw/react
# or
pnpm add @paw/react
# or
yarn add @paw/react
```

---

## 🚀 Quick start

```tsx
import { Button, Input, Card } from '@paw/react';

export function App() {
  return (
    <Card>
      <Input placeholder="What's your name?" />
      <Button variant="primary">Say hi 👋</Button>
    </Card>
  );
}
```

---

## 🧱 The 12 primitives

| Component  | Description                                              |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Button`   | Polymorphic button with `variant`, `size`, and `loading` |
| `Input`    | Text input with optional prefix/suffix slots             |
| `Checkbox` | Accessible checkbox with indeterminate state             |
| `Switch`   | Toggle switch with controlled/uncontrolled modes         |
| `Badge`    | Small status label with color variants                   |
| `Avatar`   | Image avatar with initials fallback                      |
| `Card`     | Container with `Header`, `Body`, and `Footer` slots      |
| `Modal`    | Portal-based dialog with focus trap and ESC handling     |
| `Tooltip`  | Hover/focus tooltip with configurable placement          |
| `Tabs`     | Roving-tabindex tab list with keyboard navigation        |
| `Spinner`  | SVG loading indicator with size presets                  |
| `Toast`    | Imperative toast queue via `useToast()` hook             |

---

## 📖 Usage examples

### Button

```tsx
<Button variant="primary" size="md" loading={isSaving}>
  Save changes
</Button>

<Button as="a" href="/docs" variant="ghost">
  Read the docs
</Button>
```

### Modal

```tsx
import { Modal, Button } from '@paw/react';

<Modal open={open} onClose={() => setOpen(false)}>
  <Modal.Header>Delete project?</Modal.Header>
  <Modal.Body>This action cannot be undone.</Modal.Body>
  <Modal.Footer>
    <Button variant="ghost" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Cancel</Button>
    <Button variant="danger" onClick={confirm}>Delete</Button>
  </Modal.Footer>
</Modal>
```

### Toast

```tsx
import { useToast } from '@paw/react';

function SaveButton() {
  const toast = useToast();
  return (
    <button onClick={() => toast.success('Saved!')}>
      Save
    </button>
  );
}
```

Wrap your app once with `<ToastProvider>` to enable toasts.

### Tabs

```tsx
<Tabs defaultValue="overview">
  <Tabs.List>
    <Tabs.Trigger value="overview">Overview</Tabs.Trigger>
    <Tabs.Trigger value="activity">Activity</Tabs.Trigger>
  </Tabs.List>
  <Tabs.Panel value="overview">…</Tabs.Panel>
  <Tabs.Panel value="activity">…</Tabs.Panel>
</Tabs>
```

---

## 🎨 Styling

`paw` ships with **no default styles**. Every component accepts a `className` and forwards `style`, so you can style them however you like:

```tsx
<Button className="rounded-lg bg-black text-white px-4 py-2">
  Click me
</Button>
```

If you want a starting point, import the optional stylesheet:

```ts
import '@paw/react/styles.css';
```

---

## 🧪 Development

```bash
git clone https://github.com/your-org/paw.git
cd paw
pnpm install
pnpm dev        # start Storybook on :6006
pnpm test       # run Vitest
pnpm build      # build ESM + CJS + types
```

---

## 📁 Project structure

```
paw/
├── src/
│   ├── Button/
│   ├── Input/
│   ├── Checkbox/
│   ├── Switch/
│   ├── Badge/
│   ├── Avatar/
│   ├── Card/
│   ├── Modal/
│   ├── Tooltip/
│   ├── Tabs/
│   ├── Spinner/
│   ├── Toast/
│   └── index.ts
└── package.json
```

---

Contributions are welcome! Please open an issue first to discuss what you'd like to change. All PRs should include tests and pass `pnpm lint && pnpm test`.

## Why paw?

- **Small.** 12 primitives, ~9 KB gzipped total.

npm install paw
# or
pnpm add paw
# or
yarn add paw

Peer dependencies:

```bash
npm install react react-dom
```

## Quick start

```tsx
import { Button, Card, Input } from 'paw';
import 'paw/styles.css'; // optional base styles

export function Signup() {
  return (
    <Card>
      <Card.Header>Create an account</Card.Header>
      <Card.Body>

        <Button variant="primary" size="md">

        </Button>

    </Card>
  );

| # | Component | What it does |
|---|-----------|--------------|
| 1 | `<Button>` | Accessible button with variants and sizes |
| 2 | `<Input>` | Text input with label, hint, and error states |
| 3 | `<Checkbox>` | Tri-state checkbox with indeterminate support |
| 4 | `<Switch>` | Toggle for boolean settings |

| 6 | `<Avatar>` | Image avatar with initials fallback |
| 7 | `<Card>` | Container with `Header`, `Body`, `Footer` slots |
| 8 | `<Tooltip>` | Hover / focus tooltip with positioning |
| 9 | `<Modal>` | Portal-based dialog with focus trap |
| 10 | `<Tabs>` | Keyboard-navigable tab list and panels |
| 11 | `<Spinner>` | Loading indicator with size variants |
| 12 | `<Toast>` | Transient notifications via `useToast()` |

### Button

```tsx
<Button variant="primary" size="md" onClick={save}>
  Save
</Button>

<Button variant="ghost" loading>
  Loading…
</Button>
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
|------|------|---------|
| `variant` | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'ghost' \| 'danger'` | `'secondary'` |

```tsx
<Input
  label="Password"

  onChange={(e) => setPassword(e.target.value)}
/>

```tsx
<Checkbox
  checked={agreed}

```tsx
<Switch
  checked={darkMode}
  onChange={setDarkMode}

---

<Badge tone="danger" dot>3</Badge>
```

---

### Avatar

```tsx
<Avatar src="/me.jpg" alt="Ada Lovelace" size="md" />
<Avatar name="Ada Lovelace" /> {/* falls back to initials */}
```

---

### Card

```tsx
<Card>
  <Card.Header>Title</Card.Header>
  <Card.Body>Content goes here.</Card.Body>
  <Card.Footer>
    <Button>Close</Button>
  </Card.Footer>
</Card>
```

---

### Tooltip

```tsx

</Tooltip>
```

---

### Modal

```tsx
<Modal open={open} onClose={() => setOpen(false)}>
  <Modal.Title>Delete project?</Modal.Title>
  <Modal.Description>This action cannot be undone.</Modal.Description>
  <Modal.Actions>
    <Button onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Cancel</Button>
    <Button variant="danger" onClick={confirm}>Delete</Button>
  </Modal.Actions>
</Modal>
```

---

### Tabs

```tsx
<Tabs defaultValue="overview">
  <Tabs.List>
    <Tabs.Trigger value="overview">Overview</Tabs.Trigger>
    <Tabs.Trigger value="activity">Activity</Tabs.Trigger>
  </Tabs.List>
  <Tabs.Panel value="overview">…</Tabs.Panel>
  <Tabs.Panel value="activity">…</Tabs.Panel>
</Tabs>

---

### Spinner

```tsx
<Spinner size="sm" />
<Spinner size="lg" label="Loading results" />
```

---

### Toast

```tsx
import { ToastProvider, useToast } from 'paw';

function App() {
  return (
    <ToastProvider>
      <Page />
    </ToastProvider>
  );
}

function Page() {
  const toast = useToast();
  return (
    <Button onClick={() => toast.success('Saved!')}>

## Theming

`paw` exposes CSS custom properties so you can theme without touching component internals:

```css
:root {
  --paw-color-primary: #4f46e5;

- `<Tooltip>` shows on both hover and focus, and is dismissible with `Escape`.
- Every component respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## TypeScript

All components are typed and export their prop interfaces:

```tsx

```

## Browser support

Modern evergreen browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge). No IE.

Issues and PRs welcome. Please run `pnpm test` and `pnpm lint` before opening a PR.

# 🐾 paw

> A tiny, composable React component library. Twelve small UI primitives, zero dependencies, fully typed.

`paw` is a collection of small, focused building blocks for React apps. Each component does one thing well, ships with sensible defaults, and stays out of your way. No CSS-in-JS runtime, no theme provider required, no surprises.

- **12 primitives** — everything you need to build a UI, nothing you don't
- **Zero runtime dependencies** — just React as a peer
- **TypeScript-first** — full types, no `any` in sight
- **Tree-shakeable** — ESM + CJS builds, import only what you use
- **Accessible by default** — keyboard support and ARIA baked in
- **Themeable with CSS variables** — no provider, no context, no ceremony

---

## Installation

```bash
npm install paw
# or
pnpm add paw
# or
yarn add paw
```

`paw` requires React 18 or newer.

```bash
npm install react react-dom
```

---

## Quick start

```tsx
import { Button, Input, Card } from 'paw';
import 'paw/styles.css';

export function Signup() {
  return (
    <Card>
      <Card.Header>Create an account</Card.Header>
      <Card.Body>
        <Input label="Email" type="email" placeholder="you@example.com" />
        <Button variant="primary" size="md">
          Sign up
        </Button>
      </Card.Body>
    </Card>
  );
}
```

---

## The 12 primitives

| Component  | Description                                              |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Button`   | Buttons in 4 variants and 3 sizes, with loading state    |
| `Input`    | Text input with label, hint, and error support           |
| `Checkbox` | Accessible checkbox with indeterminate state             |
| `Switch`   | Toggle switch for on/off settings                        |
| `Select`   | Native select with custom styling                        |
| `Badge`    | Small status or count indicator                          |
| `Avatar`   | User image with initials fallback                        |
| `Card`     | Container with `Header`, `Body`, and `Footer` slots      |
| `Modal`    | Dialog with focus trap and escape-to-close               |
| `Tooltip`  | Hover/focus tooltip with configurable placement          |
| `Tabs`     | Keyboard-navigable tab list with panels                  |
| `Spinner`  | Indeterminate loading indicator                          |

---

## Usage

### Button

```tsx
<Button variant="primary" size="md" onClick={save}>
  Save changes
</Button>

<Button variant="danger" loading>
  Deleting…
</Button>

<Button variant="ghost" size="sm" icon={<PlusIcon />}>
  Add item
</Button>
```

**Props:** `variant` (`primary` | `secondary` | `ghost` | `danger`), `size` (`sm` | `md` | `lg`), `loading`, `disabled`, `icon`, `fullWidth`.

### Input

```tsx
<Input
  label="Password"
  type="password"
  hint="At least 8 characters"
  error={errors.password}
  value={password}
  onChange={(e) => setPassword(e.target.value)}
/>
```

### Checkbox & Switch

```tsx
<Checkbox checked={agreed} onChange={setAgreed} label="I agree to the terms" />
<Checkbox indeterminate label="Select all" />

<Switch checked={dark} onChange={setDark} label="Dark mode" />
```

### Select

```tsx
<Select label="Country" value={country} onChange={setCountry}>
  <option value="us">United States</option>
  <option value="ca">Canada</option>
  <option value="mx">Mexico</option>
</Select>
```

### Badge

```tsx
<Badge>New</Badge>
<Badge tone="success">Active</Badge>
<Badge tone="danger" dot>3 errors</Badge>
```

### Avatar

```tsx
<Avatar src="/ada.jpg" alt="Ada Lovelace" size="md" />
<Avatar name="Grace Hopper" /> {/* falls back to initials */}
```

### Card

```tsx
<Card>
  <Card.Header>Team members</Card.Header>
  <Card.Body>…</Card.Body>
  <Card.Footer>
    <Button size="sm">Invite</Button>
  </Card.Footer>
</Card>
```

### Modal

```tsx
<Modal open={open} onClose={() => setOpen(false)}>
  <Modal.Title>Delete project?</Modal.Title>
  <Modal.Body>This action cannot be undone.</Modal.Body>
  <Modal.Actions>
    <Button variant="ghost" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Cancel</Button>
    <Button variant="danger" onClick={confirm}>Delete</Button>
  </Modal.Actions>
</Modal>
```

### Tooltip

```tsx
<Tooltip content="Copy to clipboard" placement="top">
  <Button variant="ghost" icon={<CopyIcon />} />
</Tooltip>
```

### Tabs

```tsx
<Tabs defaultValue="overview">
  <Tabs.List>
    <Tabs.Trigger value="overview">Overview</Tabs.Trigger>
    <Tabs.Trigger value="activity">Activity</Tabs.Trigger>
    <Tabs.Trigger value="settings">Settings</Tabs.Trigger>
  </Tabs.List>
  <Tabs.Panel value="overview">…</Tabs.Panel>
  <Tabs.Panel value="activity">…</Tabs.Panel>
  <Tabs.Panel value="settings">…</Tabs.Panel>
</Tabs>
```

### Spinner

```tsx
<Spinner size="sm" />
<Spinner size="lg" label="Loading results" />
```

---

## Theming

`paw` is styled with CSS custom properties. Override them anywhere in your stylesheet — no provider needed.

```css
:root {
  --paw-color-primary: #6d28d9;
  --paw-color-primary-hover: #5b21b6;
  --paw-color-danger: #dc2626;
  --paw-radius: 8px;
  --paw-font-family: 'Inter', system-ui, sans-serif;
  --paw-focus-ring: 0 0 0 3px rgba(109, 40, 217, 0.35);
}
```

Dark mode works out of the box via `prefers-color-scheme`, or opt in explicitly:

```html
<html data-paw-theme="dark">
```

---

## Accessibility

Every component is built with accessibility in mind:

- Full keyboard navigation (Tab, Enter, Space, Arrow keys, Escape)
- Focus trapping in `Modal`, focus restoration on close
- `aria-*` attributes wired up correctly (`aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby`, `role="switch"`, etc.)
- Respects `prefers-reduced-motion`
- Tested with VoiceOver, NVDA, and axe-core

If you find an accessibility issue, please [open an issue](https://github.com/your-org/paw/issues) — it's treated as a bug, not a feature request.

---

## TypeScript

All components are written in TypeScript and export their prop types.

```tsx
import type { ButtonProps, ModalProps } from 'paw';

const MyButton = (props: ButtonProps) => <Button {...props} />;
```

---

## Bundle size

| Import                | Minified + gzipped |
| --------------------- | ------------------ |
| `Button`              | ~1.2 kB            |
| `Input`               | ~1.4 kB            |
| `Modal`               | ~2.1 kB            |
| All 12 primitives     | ~9 kB              |

---

## Development

```bash
git clone https://github.com/your-org/paw.git
cd paw
pnpm install
pnpm dev        # start Storybook at localhost:6006
pnpm test       # run unit tests
pnpm build      # build ESM + CJS + types
```

---

## Philosophy

`paw` is deliberately small. It's not a design system, and it's not trying to be. It's a set of primitives you can drop into any project, style however you like, and forget about. If a component needs more than ~150 lines to be useful, it probably belongs in your app, not in this library.

---

## License

MIT © [Your Name](https://github.com/your-org)

# 🐾 paw

> Twelve tiny, unstyled-by-default React UI primitives. Small enough to read in an afternoon, sharp enough to ship.

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/paw.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/paw)
[![bundle size](https://img.shields.io/bundlephobia/minzip/paw)](https://bundlephobia.com/package/paw)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/paw.svg)](./LICENSE)

`paw` is a collection of twelve focused React components. No design system, no
opinionated theming layer, no runtime CSS-in-JS. Just the primitives you keep
rewriting in every project, with sensible accessibility baked in and a CSS
variable theme you can override in five lines.

---

## Table of contents

- [Features](#features)
- [Installation](#installation)
- [Quick start](#quick-start)
- [Components](#components)
- [Theming](#theming)
- [TypeScript](#typescript)
- [Accessibility](#accessibility)
- [Contributing](#contributing)
- [License](#license)

---

## Features

- **12 primitives, nothing more.** Every component earns its place.
- **Zero runtime dependencies.** React is a peer dependency, that's it.
- **Composable.** `Stack`, `Card`, and the rest are plain elements with class
  names — style them with anything.
- **Accessible by default.** Focus management, ARIA wiring, and keyboard
  handling come standard.
- **Themeable via CSS variables.** Swap a handful of custom properties and the
  whole library follows.
- **Typed.** Written in TypeScript, ships with `.d.ts` files.
- **Tree-shakeable.** ESM and CJS builds; import only what you use.

---

## Installation

```bash
npm install paw
```

```bash
pnpm add paw
```

```bash
yarn add paw
```

`paw` requires **React 18 or newer**.

---

## Quick start

Import the stylesheet once at your app root, then use components anywhere.

```tsx
import { Button, Card, Input, Stack } from 'paw';
import 'paw/styles.css';

export function SignupCard() {
  return (
    <Card>
      <Stack gap="md">
        <Input label="Email" type="email" placeholder="you@example.com" />
        <Input label="Password" type="password" />
        <Button variant="primary" fullWidth>
          Create account
        </Button>
      </Stack>
    </Card>
  );
}
```

Prefer no bundled CSS? Skip `paw/styles.css` and style the class names
yourself — every component renders predictable `paw-*` classes.

---

## Components

### Layout

#### `Stack`

Vertical or horizontal flex container with consistent gaps.

```tsx
<Stack direction="row" gap="sm" align="center" justify="between">
  <Avatar src="/ada.png" alt="Ada Lovelace" />
  <Text weight="medium">Ada Lovelace</Text>
</Stack>
```

| Prop        | Type                                          | Default  |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| `direction` | `'row' \| 'column'`                           | `column` |
| `gap`       | `'xs' \| 'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'xl'`        | `md`     |
| `align`     | `'start' \| 'center' \| 'end' \| 'stretch'`   | —        |
| `justify`   | `'start' \| 'center' \| 'end' \| 'between'`   | —        |

#### `Card`

A surface with padding, radius, and border.

```tsx
<Card padding="lg" elevation="sm">
  <Text as="h2">Billing</Text>
  <Text tone="muted">Manage your plan and invoices.</Text>
</Card>
```

---

### Typography

#### `Text`

Polymorphic text with size, weight, and tone presets.

```tsx
<Text as="h1" size="xl" weight="bold">Dashboard</Text>
<Text tone="muted" size="sm">Last updated 4 minutes ago</Text>
```

| Prop     | Type                                                    | Default |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| `as`     | `'p' \| 'span' \| 'h1'…'h6' \| 'label' \| 'div'`        | `p`     |
| `size`   | `'xs' \| 'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'xl'`                  | `md`    |
| `weight` | `'regular' \| 'medium' \| 'bold'`                       | —       |
| `tone`   | `'default' \| 'muted' \| 'danger' \| 'success'`         | —       |

---

### Forms

#### `Button`

```tsx
<Button variant="primary" size="md" loading={isSaving} onClick={save}>
  Save changes
</Button>
```

| Prop       | Type                                            | Default     |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| `variant`  | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'ghost' \| 'danger'` | `secondary` |
| `size`     | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'`                          | `md`        |
| `loading`  | `boolean`                                       | `false`     |
| `fullWidth`| `boolean`                                       | `false`     |

Renders a real `<button>` and forwards all native props.

#### `IconButton`

A square button for a single icon. **`label` is required** — it becomes the
accessible name.

```tsx
<IconButton label="Close dialog" onClick={onClose}>
  <CloseIcon />
</IconButton>
```

#### `Input`

Text input with label, hint, and error states wired up for you.

```tsx
<Input
  label="Email"
  type="email"
  hint="We'll never share it."
  error={errors.email}
  value={email}
  onChange={(e) => setEmail(e.target.value)}
/>
```

| Prop    | Type      | Default |
| ------- | --------- | ------- |
| `label` | `string`  | —       |
| `hint`  | `string`  | —       |
| `error` | `string`  | —       |
| `size`  | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `md` |

When `error` is set, `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` are applied
automatically.

#### `Textarea`

Same API as `Input`, plus `rows` and `autoResize`.

```tsx
<Textarea label="Notes" rows={4} autoResize maxLength={500} />
```

#### `Checkbox`

```tsx
<Checkbox
  label="Email me product updates"
  checked={subscribed}
  onChange={(e) => setSubscribed(e.target.checked)}
  indeterminate={someSelected}
/>
```

#### `Switch`

An on/off toggle rendered as `role="switch"`.

```tsx
<Switch
  label="Dark mode"
  checked={dark}
  onChange={(e) => setDark(e.target.checked)}
/>
```

---

### Feedback

#### `Badge`

Small status pill.

```tsx
<Badge tone="success">Active</Badge>
<Badge tone="danger" variant="solid">Overdue</Badge>
```

#### `Spinner`

```tsx
<Spinner size="md" label="Loading invoices" />
```

Announces itself to screen readers via `role="status"` unless
`aria-hidden` is passed.

---

### Overlays

#### `Tooltip`

Wraps a single focusable child. Shows on hover and focus, hides on `Escape`.

```tsx
<Tooltip content="Copy to clipboard" side="top">
  <IconButton label="Copy"><CopyIcon /></IconButton>
</Tooltip>
```

| Prop      | Type                                | Default |
| --------- | ----------------------------------- | ------- |
| `content` | `ReactNode`                         | —       |
| `side`    | `'top' \| 'right' \| 'bottom' \| 'left'` | `top`   |
| `delay`   | `number` (ms)                       | `300`   |

#### `Avatar`

Image with initials fallback.

```tsx
<Avatar src="/ada.png" alt="Ada Lovelace" size="md" fallback="AL" />
```

If `src` fails to load or is omitted, `fallback` initials are rendered.

---

## Theming

All visual tokens live in CSS custom properties. Override them anywhere in your
own stylesheet — no build step, no provider component.

```css
:root {
  --paw-color-bg: #ffffff;
  --paw-color-fg: #111827;
  --paw-color-muted: #6b7280;
  --paw-color-accent: #7c3aed;
  --paw-color-danger: #dc2626;
  --paw-radius: 8px;
  --paw-font-sans: 'Inter', system-ui, sans-serif;
  --paw-space-unit: 4px;
}
```

Dark mode is a matter of redefining the same variables:

```css
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
  :root {
    --paw-color-bg: #0b0b0f;
    --paw-color-fg: #f9fafb;
    --paw-color-muted: #9ca3af;
  }
}
```

Every component also accepts `className` and `style`, so one-off overrides
never require a fork.

---

## TypeScript

`paw` is written in TypeScript and ships types with the package. Component
props extend the relevant native element attributes.

```tsx
import type { ButtonProps, StackProps } from 'paw';

const PrimaryAction = (props: ButtonProps) => (
  <Button variant="primary" {...props} />
);
```

---

## Accessibility

- Interactive components render native elements wherever possible.
- `Input` and `Textarea` generate stable ids and connect `label`, `hint`, and
  `error` text via `aria-describedby`.
- `IconButton` requires a `label` prop at the type level.
- `Tooltip` opens on both hover and keyboard focus, and closes on `Escape`.
- `Spinner` exposes a live region unless explicitly hidden.
- Focus rings are visible by default and driven by `--paw-color-accent`.

Found an accessibility bug? Please open an issue — those get triaged first.

---

## Contributing

```bash
git clone https://github.com/your-org/paw.git
cd paw
pnpm install
pnpm dev
