# 🐾 paw

> Twelve tiny, composable React primitives. No dependencies. No bloat. Just paws.

`paw` is a small collection of accessible, unstyled-by-default UI primitives for React. Each component does one thing well, ships with sensible defaults, and gets out of your way when you want to customize.

- **12 primitives**, zero runtime dependencies (peer-depends on React 18+)
- **~4.2 kB** gzipped, tree-shakeable ESM + CJS builds
- **Accessible by default** — WAI-ARIA patterns, keyboard nav, focus management
- **TypeScript-first** — full types, generics where it matters
- **Themeable** — CSS variables, no build step required

---

## Installation

```bash
npm install paw
# or
pnpm add paw
# or
yarn add paw
```

Peer dependencies:

```bash
npm install react react-dom
```

---

## Quick start

```tsx
import { Button, Input, Card } from 'paw';
import 'paw/styles.css';

export function Login() {
  return (
    <Card>
      <Input label="Email" type="email" placeholder="you@example.com" />
      <Input label="Password" type="password" />
      <Button variant="primary">Sign in</Button>
    </Card>
  );
}
```

---

## The twelve primitives

| # | Component | What it does |
|---|-----------|--------------|
| 1 | [`Button`](#button) | Polymorphic button with variants & loading state |
| 2 | [`Input`](#input) | Text field with label, hint, and error slots |
| 3 | [`Checkbox`](#checkbox) | Tri-state checkbox with indeterminate support |
| 4 | [`Switch`](#switch) | Accessible on/off toggle |
| 5 | [`Badge`](#badge) | Tiny status pill |
| 6 | [`Avatar`](#avatar) | Image with initials fallback |
| 7 | [`Card`](#card) | Container with header/body/footer slots |
| 8 | [`Tooltip`](#tooltip) | Hover/focus tooltip with smart positioning |
| 9 | [`Modal`](#modal) | Dialog with focus trap & scroll lock |
| 10 | [`Tabs`](#tabs) | ARIA-compliant tab list |
| 11 | [`Spinner`](#spinner) | Indeterminate loading indicator |
| 12 | [`Toast`](#toast) | Imperative toast notifications |

---

## Usage

### Button

```tsx
<Button variant="primary" size="md" loading>
  Saving…
</Button>

<Button as="a" href="/docs" variant="ghost">
  Read the docs
</Button>
```

Props: `variant` (`primary` \| `secondary` \| `ghost` \| `danger`), `size` (`sm` \| `md` \| `lg`), `loading`, `as`, plus all native button/anchor attributes.

### Input

```tsx
<Input
  label="Username"
  hint="3–20 characters"
  error={errors.username}
  value={value}
  onChange={(e) => setValue(e.target.value)}
/>
```

### Checkbox

```tsx
<Checkbox
  checked={checked}
  indeterminate={someSelected}
  onChange={setChecked}
>
  Select all
</Checkbox>
```

### Switch

```tsx
<Switch checked={enabled} onChange={setEnabled} label="Dark mode" />
```

### Badge

```tsx
<Badge tone="success">Active</Badge>
<Badge tone="warning">Pending</Badge>
<Badge tone="danger">Failed</Badge>
```

### Avatar

```tsx
<Avatar src="/ada.png" name="Ada Lovelace" size={40} />
```

Falls back to initials when `src` is missing or fails to load.

### Card

```tsx
<Card>
  <Card.Header>Team</Card.Header>
  <Card.Body>…</Card.Body>
  <Card.Footer>
    <Button size="sm">Invite</Button>
  </Card.Footer>
</Card>
```

### Tooltip

```tsx
<Tooltip content="Copy to clipboard" side="top">
  <Button aria-label="Copy">📋</Button>
</Tooltip>
```

### Modal

```tsx
<Modal open={open} onClose={() => setOpen(false)}>
  <Modal.Title>Delete project?</Modal.Title>
  <Modal.Description>This action cannot be undone.</Modal.Description>
  <Modal.Actions>
    <Button variant="ghost" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Cancel</Button>
    <Button variant="danger" onClick={confirm}>Delete</Button>
  </Modal.Actions>
</Modal>
```

Traps focus, restores it on close, and locks body scroll.

### Tabs

```tsx
<Tabs defaultValue="overview">
  <Tabs.List>
    <Tabs.Tab value="overview">Overview</Tabs.Tab>
    <Tabs.Tab value="activity">Activity</Tabs.Tab>
  </Tabs.List>
  <Tabs.Panel value="overview">…</Tabs.Panel>
  <Tabs.Panel value="activity">…</Tabs.Panel>
</Tabs>
```

Arrow keys move between tabs; `Home`/`End` jump to the ends.

### Spinner

```tsx
<Spinner size="sm" label="Loading results" />
```

### Toast

```tsx
import { ToastProvider, useToast } from 'paw';

function App() {
  return (
    <ToastProvider>
      <Page />
    </ToastProvider>
  );
}

function Page() {
  const toast = useToast();
  return (
    <Button onClick={() => toast.success('Saved!')}>
      Save
    </Button>
  );
}
```

---

## Theming

Every component reads from CSS custom properties. Override them globally or per-scope:

```css
:root {
  --paw-color-primary: #6d28d9;
  --paw-color-danger:  #dc2626;
  --paw-radius:        8px;
  --paw-font-sans:     'Inter', system-ui, sans-serif;
  --paw-focus-ring:    0 0 0 3px rgba(109, 40, 217, 0.35);
}
```

Or style individual components with the `className` prop — no `!important` required.

---

## Accessibility

- All interactive primitives are keyboard reachable and follow WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices.
- Focus rings are visible and use `:focus-visible` so mouse users aren't bothered.
- `Modal` and `Tooltip` manage focus and `aria-*` wiring automatically.
- Motion respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.

If you find an a11y bug, please open an issue — it's treated as a bug, not a feature request.

---

## TypeScript

```tsx
import type { ButtonProps, ModalProps } from 'paw';
```

Components use `forwardRef` and expose their element types, so `ref` works as expected:

```tsx
const ref = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null);
<Button ref={ref}>Click</Button>
```

---

## Bundle size

| Import | Minified | Gzipped |
|--------|---------:|--------:|
| `Button` | 1.1 kB | 0.5 kB |
| `Modal` | 3.4 kB | 1.4 kB |
| All 12 | 9.8 kB | 4.2 kB |

Sizes measured with `size-limit`; run `pnpm size` locally.

---

## Development

```bash
git clone https://github.com/your-org/paw.git
cd paw
pnpm install
pnpm dev        # Storybook on :6006
pnpm test       # Vitest + Testing Library
pnpm build      # tsup → dist/
pnpm size       # bundle-size check
```

---

## Contributing

New primitives are welcome, but the bar is high: `paw` is intentionally small. Before opening a PR, please:

1. Open an issue describing the primitive and its use case.
2. Keep it dependency-free.
3. Add tests, a Storybook story, and a README entry.

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md).

---

runs.output:
# tiny-date

> Tiny, dependency-free date formatting — relative to now.

`tiny-date` turns a `Date` (or timestamp) into a human-readable string like `"5 minutes ago"`, `"in 3 days"`, or `"yesterday"`. No dependencies, no locale bloat, ~1.2 kB minified + gzipped.

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/tiny-date.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/tiny-date)
[![bundle size](https://img.shields.io/bundlephobia/minzip/tiny-date.svg)](https://bundlephobia.com/package/tiny-date)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![types](https://img.shields.io/npm/types/tiny-date.svg)](index.d.ts)

---

## Features

- 🪶 **~1.2 kB** minified + gzipped, **zero dependencies**
- 🌍 Ships with English, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Japanese, and Chinese
- 🧩 Pluggable locales — add your own in a few lines
- ⏱️ Works with past **and** future dates
- 🛠️ Full TypeScript types
- 🧪 100% test coverage

## Install

```bash
npm install tiny-date
```

```bash
pnpm add tiny-date
# or
yarn add tiny-date
```

## Quick start

```js
import { relative } from 'tiny-date'

const fiveMinutesAgo = new Date(Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000)

relative(fiveMinutesAgo)          // => '5 minutes ago'
relative(new Date())              // => 'just now'
relative(Date.now() + 3_600_000)  // => 'in 1 hour'
```

CommonJS and browser globals work too:

```js
const { relative } = require('tiny-date')
```

```html
<script src="https://unpkg.com/tiny-date/dist/tiny-date.global.js"></script>
<script>
  tinyDate.relative(new Date())
</script>
```

## Usage

### Past and future

```js
relative(new Date(Date.now() - 90 * 1000))       // => '2 minutes ago'
relative(new Date(Date.now() + 90 * 1000))       // => 'in 2 minutes'
relative(new Date(Date.now() - 2 * 86400000))    // => '2 days ago'
relative(new Date(Date.now() + 2 * 86400000))    // => 'in 2 days'
```

### Options

```js
relative(date, {
  locale: 'es',
  numeric: 'always',
  maxUnit: 'day',
})
```

### A fixed "now"

Useful in tests, snapshots, and server-rendered output:

```js
const now = new Date('2024-03-01T12:00:00Z')

relative(new Date('2024-02-28T12:00:00Z'), { now })  // => '2 days ago'
```

### Custom locales

```js
import { relative, registerLocale } from 'tiny-date'

registerLocale('pt-br', {
  past: 'faz {value}',
  future: 'em {value}',
  units: {
    second: 'segundo',
    minute: 'minuto',
    hour: 'hora',
    day: 'dia',
    week: 'semana',
    month: 'mês',
    year: 'ano',
  },
  // Optional overrides for the "just now" / "yesterday" / "tomorrow" cases.
  justNow: 'agora',
  yesterday: 'ontem',
  tomorrow: 'amanhã',
})

relative(new Date(Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000), { locale: 'pt-br' })
// => 'faz 5 minutos'
```

### Live updating

`tiny-date` is a pure function — it doesn't schedule timers. Pair it with whatever ticker you already have:

```js
const el = document.querySelector('#timestamp')

const tick = () => {
  el.textContent = relative(new Date(el.dataset.time))
}

tick()
setInterval(tick, 30_000)
```

## API

### `relative(date, options?) => string`

Formats `date` relative to `now`.

**`date`** — `Date | number | string`. A `Date` instance, a Unix timestamp in milliseconds, or an ISO 8601 string.

**`options`** — see below. All options are optional.

#### Options

| Option     | Type                                  | Default    | Description |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------- | ---------- | ----------- |
| `now`      | `Date \| number`                      | `Date.now()` | The reference point to compare against. |
| `locale`   | `string`                              | `'en'`     | Locale key. Must be registered (built-in or custom). |
| `numeric`  | `'auto' \| 'always'`                  | `'auto'`   | `'auto'` uses `"yesterday"` / `"tomorrow"` for ±1 day; `'always'` uses `"1 day ago"` / `"in 1 day"`. |
| `suffix`   | `boolean`                             | `true`     | Include the `"ago"` / `"in ..."` wrapper. Set to `false` for a bare duration (`"5 minutes"`). |
| `maxUnit`  | `'year' \| 'month' \| 'week' \| 'day' \| 'hour' \| 'minute' \| 'second'` | `'year'` | Largest unit to report. E.g. `maxUnit: 'day'` renders 3 weeks as `"21 days ago"`. |
| `minUnit`  | `'year' \| 'month' \| 'week' \| 'day' \| 'hour' \| 'minute' \| 'second'` | `'second'` | Smallest unit to report. E.g. `minUnit: 'minute'` renders 30 seconds as `"1 minute ago"`. |
| `round`    | `boolean`                             | `false`    | Round to the nearest unit instead of flooring. |
| `plural`   | `boolean`                             | `true`     | Use the plural form of a unit (`"2 days"` vs `"2 day"`). |

#### Throws

- `TypeError` if `date` is not a valid date.
- `RangeError` if `locale` is not registered.
- `RangeError` if `minUnit` is larger than `maxUnit`.

### `registerLocale(key, locale) => void`

Registers (or overwrites) a locale. See [Custom locales](#custom-locales) for the shape.

### `getLocale(key) => Locale | undefined`

Returns a registered locale object.

### `hasLocale(key) => boolean`

Returns `true` if a locale is registered under `key`.

### `locales() => string[]`

Returns the keys of all registered locales.

## Locales

| Key    | Language   | `5 minutes ago` | `in 2 hours` | `yesterday` |
| ------ | ---------- | --------------- | ------------ | ----------- |
| `en`   | English    | 5 minutes ago   | in 2 hours   | yesterday   |
| `es`   | Spanish    | hace 5 minutos  | en 2 horas   | ayer        |
| `fr`   | French     | il y a 5 minutes | dans 2 heures | hier      |
| `de`   | German     | vor 5 Minuten   | in 2 Stunden | gestern     |
| `pt`   | Portuguese | há 5 minutos    | em 2 horas   | ontem      |
| `ja`   | Japanese   | 5分前            | 2時間後      | 昨日        |
| `zh`   | Chinese    | 5分钟前          | 2小时后       | 昨天        |

## TypeScript

Types ship with the package — no `@types` install needed.

```ts
import { relative, type RelativeOptions, type Locale } from 'tiny-date'

const opts: RelativeOptions = { locale: 'fr', numeric: 'always' }

const label: string = relative(Date.now(), opts)
```

## Browser support

`tiny-date` targets ES2018 and works in any browser with `Intl`-free, `Date`-only support: Chrome 64+, Firefox 67+, Safari 12+, Edge 79+, and Node 12+.

## Why not Day.js / Moment / date-fns?

Those are excellent libraries — but they solve a much bigger problem. If all you need is *"how long ago was this?"*, `tiny-date` is roughly **1/20th the size** of `dayjs` with the relative-time plugin, and it has no dependencies to audit.

Use `dayjs` if you need parsing, timezones, or a plugin ecosystem. Use `tiny-date` if you need one function, fast.

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome! 🎉

```bash
git clone https://github.com/yourname/tiny-date.git
cd tiny-date
npm install
npm test
```

- 🐛 **Bug reports** — please include the input date, options, expected output, and actual output.
- 💡 **Feature requests** — open an issue first to discuss before writing code.
- 🌍 **New locales** — add them to `src/locales/`, and include a test.

Run the full check suite before opening a pull request:

```bash
npm run lint
npm run test
npm run build
```

## License

[MIT](./LICENSE) © [yourname](https://github.com/yourname)

---

<sub>Built with ☕️ and a very small amount of JavaScript.</sub>
</content></invoke>
</content></invoke>

# tiny-date

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/tiny-date.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/tiny-date)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

Format dates relative to now — `"5 minutes ago"`, `"in 3 days"`, `"just now"`.

Tiny on purpose: no dependencies, no locale bundles, no configuration file. One function, one job.

## Install

```sh
npm install tiny-date
```

## Usage

```js
const tinyDate = require('tiny-date');

tinyDate(new Date(Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000));
// => "5 minutes ago"

tinyDate(new Date(Date.now() + 3 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000));
// => "in 3 days"

tinyDate(new Date());
// => "just now"
```

ES modules and TypeScript are supported too:

```js
import tinyDate from 'tiny-date';
```

## API

### `tinyDate(date, options?)`

Returns a human-readable string describing `date` relative to the current time.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `date` | `Date \| number \| string` | The date to format. Numbers are treated as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds; strings are parsed with `new Date(string)`. |
| `options` | `object` | Optional. See below. |

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `relativeTo` | `Date \| number` | `Date.now()` | The point in time to compare against. Useful for testing. |
| `addSuffix` | `boolean` | `true` | Append `"ago"` / `"in ..."` to the result. Set to `false` for a bare duration like `"5 minutes"`. |
| `style` | `"long" \| "short"` | `"long"` | `"short"` abbreviates units: `"5m ago"`, `"in 3d"`. |
| `maxUnit` | `"year" \| "month" \| "week" \| "day" \| "hour" \| "minute" \| "second"` | `"year"` | The largest unit to report. Anything older is expressed in this unit. |
| `minUnit` | `"year" \| "month" \| "week" \| "day" \| "hour" \| "minute" \| "second"` | `"second"` | The smallest unit to report. Anything smaller is reported as `"just now"`. |

## Examples

```js
const tinyDate = require('tiny-date');

const now = Date.now();
const ago = (ms) => new Date(now - ms);

// Seconds and minutes
tinyDate(ago(30 * 1000));            // "30 seconds ago"
tinyDate(ago(5 * 60 * 1000));        // "5 minutes ago"

// Hours and days
tinyDate(ago(3 * 60 * 60 * 1000));   // "3 hours ago"
tinyDate(ago(2 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000)); // "2 days ago"

// Future dates
tinyDate(new Date(now + 60 * 60 * 1000)); // "in 1 hour"

// Options
tinyDate(ago(5 * 60 * 1000), { addSuffix: false }); // "5 minutes"
tinyDate(ago(5 * 60 * 1000), { style: "short" });   // "5m ago"
tinyDate(ago(400 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000), { maxUnit: "month" }); // "13 months ago"

// Deterministic output in tests
```

# tiny-date

> Human-friendly relative dates, in ~1.2 kB.

`tiny-date` turns a timestamp into a short, natural phrase — `"5 minutes ago"`, `"in 3 days"`, `"just now"` — with no dependencies and no surprises.

```js
import tinyDate from 'tiny-date'

tinyDate(Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000) // => "5 minutes ago"
```

---

## Features

- **Tiny** — 1.2 kB minified + gzipped, zero dependencies.
- **Correct** — handles future dates, DST, leap years, and month lengths.
- **Configurable** — pick the largest/smallest unit, add or drop suffixes, fall back to an absolute date.
- **Localizable** — ships with English and French, or bring your own strings.
- **Typed** — written in TypeScript, ships its own `.d.ts`.
- **Universal** — ESM, CJS, and a UMD build for `<script>` tags.

---

## Install

```sh
npm install tiny-date
```

```sh
pnpm add tiny-date
# or
yarn add tiny-date
```

CDN (UMD, exposes `window.tinyDate`):

```html
<script src="https://unpkg.com/tiny-date/dist/tiny-date.umd.js"></script>
<script>
  tinyDate(new Date(Date.now() - 3600_000)) // => "1 hour ago"
</script>
```

---

## Usage

```js
import tinyDate from 'tiny-date'

const now = Date.now()

tinyDate(now)                        // "just now"
tinyDate(now - 30_000)               // "30 seconds ago"
tinyDate(now - 5 * 60_000)           // "5 minutes ago"
tinyDate(now - 3 * 3_600_000)        // "3 hours ago"
tinyDate(now - 2 * 86_400_000)       // "2 days ago"
tinyDate(now + 3 * 86_400_000)       // "in 3 days"
tinyDate(now - 400 * 86_400_000)     // "on 12 Feb 2024"
```

Dates can be anything `Date` understands:

```js
tinyDate(new Date())                 // Date
tinyDate('2024-02-12T10:00:00Z')     // string
tinyDate(1707636000000)              // number (ms since epoch)
```

### Named exports

```js
import { formatRelative, formatAbsolute, parseRelative, isValid } from 'tiny-date'
```

| Export | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `formatRelative(date, options?)` | The main function. Same as the default export. |
| `formatAbsolute(date, options?)` | Always an absolute date, e.g. `"12 Feb 2024"`. |
| `parseRelative(text, options?)` | Turns `"5 minutes ago"` back into a `Date`. |
| `isValid(date)` | `true` if the input can be parsed as a date. |

---

## Options

```js
tinyDate(date, {
  now: Date.now(),
  maxUnit: 'year',
  minUnit: 'second',
  addSuffix: true,
  numeric: true,
  includeDate: true,
  locale: 'en',
  fallback: 'Invalid date',
})
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `now` | `Date \| number` | `Date.now()` | The reference point. Pass it in to make output deterministic (great for tests and SSR). |
| `maxUnit` | `'year' \| 'month' \| 'week' \| 'day' \| 'hour' \| 'minute' \| 'second'` | `'year'` | The largest unit that may be used. `"2 days ago"` becomes `"2 hours ago"` with `maxUnit: 'hour'`. |
| `minUnit` | same as `maxUnit` | `'second'` | The smallest unit that may be used. With `minUnit: 'minute'`, `"30 seconds ago"` becomes `"1 minute ago"`. |
| `addSuffix` | `boolean` | `true` | Append `"ago"` / `"in …"`. Set to `false` for a bare duration. |
| `numeric` | `boolean` | `true` | `false` uses word forms: `"yesterday"`, `"last week"`, `"next month"`. |
| `includeDate` | `boolean` | `true` | When the date is older than `maxUnit`, render an absolute date instead of a relative one. Set to `false` to always stay relative. |
| `locale` | `string \| object` | `'en'` | A built-in locale name or a custom locale object. |
| `fallback` | `string` | `'Invalid date'` | Returned when the input can't be parsed. |

### `maxUnit` and `minUnit`

```js
const date = Date.now() - 3 * 86_400_000

tinyDate(date, { maxUnit: 'hour' })  // "72 hours ago"
tinyDate(date, { maxUnit: 'day' })   // "3 days ago"
tinyDate(date, { maxUnit: 'week' })  // "last week"  (numeric: false)
```

### `numeric`

```js
const yesterday = Date.now() - 86_400_000

tinyDate(yesterday)                    // "1 day ago"
tinyDate(yesterday, { numeric: false }) // "yesterday"
```

### `includeDate`

```js
const old = new Date('2020-01-15T12:00:00Z')

tinyDate(old)                          // "on 15 Jan 2020"
tinyDate(old, { includeDate: false })  // "5 years ago"
```

### `addSuffix`

```js
tinyDate(Date.now() - 60_000, { addSuffix: false }) // "1 minute"
tinyDate(Date.now() + 60_000, { addSuffix: false }) // "1 minute"
```

---

## Locales

Built in: `en`, `fr`.

```js
tinyDate(Date.now() - 5 * 60_000, { locale: 'fr' }) // "il y a 5 minutes"
```

### Custom locales

A locale is a plain object — no pluralization library required.

```js
const de = {
  justNow: 'gerade eben',
  units: {
    second:  { one: 'Sekunde',  other: 'Sekunden' },
    minute:  { one: 'Minute',   other: 'Minuten' },
    hour:    { one: 'Stunde',   other: 'Stunden' },
    day:     { one: 'Tag',      other: 'Tage' },
    week:    { one: 'Woche',    other: 'Wochen' },
    month:   { one: 'Monat',    other: 'Monate' },
    year:    { one: 'Jahr',     other: 'Jahre' },
  },
  suffix: {
    past: 'vor',
    future: 'in',
  },
  word: {
    yesterday: 'gestern',
    lastWeek: 'letzte Woche',
    nextWeek: 'nächste Woche',
  },
  dateFormat: 'D MMM YYYY',
}

tinyDate(Date.now() - 86_400_000, { locale: de }) // "vor 1 Tag"
```

> Only `units`, `suffix`, and `justNow` are required. Missing `word` entries fall back to the numeric form, and missing `dateFormat` falls back to `D MMM YYYY`.

---

## TypeScript

Types ship with the package — no `@types/tiny-date` needed.

```ts
import tinyDate, { type TinyDateOptions, type Locale } from 'tiny-date'

const label: string = tinyDate(new Date(), { maxUnit: 'day' })
```

---

## API details

### `formatRelative(date, options?) => string`

Formats `date` relative to `options.now` (default: the current time).

### `formatAbsolute(date, options?) => string`

Formats `date` as an absolute date, e.g. `"12 Feb 2024"`. Accepts `locale` and `dateFormat`.

### `parseRelative(text, options?) => Date | null`

Parses a relative phrase produced by `formatRelative` back into a `Date`.

```js
parseRelative('5 minutes ago')  // => Date
parseRelative('in 3 days')      // => Date
parseRelative('nonsense')       // => null
```

### `isValid(date) => boolean`

```js
isValid('2024-02-30') // => false
isValid('2024-02-29') // => true
```

---

## How it works

1. The input is coerced to a `Date`. Invalid input returns `options.fallback`.
2. The difference from `now` is computed in milliseconds and split into calendar-aware units (months and years use actual calendar boundaries, not fixed 30/365-day spans).
3. The largest non-zero unit within `minUnit`…`maxUnit` is selected.
4. If the difference is under one `minUnit`, `"just now"` is returned.
5. If the date falls outside `maxUnit` and `includeDate` is `true`, an absolute date is returned instead.

---

## Browser support

Works in any environment with `Intl` and `Date` — all modern browsers, Node 18+, Deno, Bun, and edge runtimes. No polyfills required.

---

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome!

```sh
git clone https://github.com/yourname/tiny-date.git
cd tiny-date
npm install
npm test
```

Please keep the bundle under 2 kB gzipped — that's the whole point of the library.

| Script | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run build` | Build ESM, CJS, and UMD bundles. |
| `npm test` | Run the test suite. |
| `npm run test:watch` | Run tests in watch mode. |
| `npm run typecheck` | Check types. |
| `npm run lint` | Lint the source. |

---

## License

[MIT](./LICENSE) © yourname

---

<sub>Made with care, and with a very small bundle budget.</sub>

# tiny-date

> Format dates relative to now — `"5 minutes ago"`, `"in 3 days"`, `"yesterday"`.

Tiny (under 1 KB minified + gzipped), zero dependencies, tree-shakeable, and powered by the built-in `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` API for proper localization.

```js
tinyDate(new Date(Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000)); // → "5 minutes ago"
```

---

## Features

- 🪶 **Tiny** — ~600 bytes minified + gzipped, no dependencies
- 🌍 **Localized** — uses `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` out of the box (40+ locales)
- 🎯 **Precise** — configurable units, thresholds, and rounding
- 🧩 **Composable** — ESM + CJS + UMD builds, works in Node, browsers, Deno, Bun, and edge runtimes
- 🛠️ **Typed** — written in TypeScript, ships `.d.ts` declarations
- ✅ **Tested** — 100% coverage against the official `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` spec

---

## Installation

```bash
npm install tiny-date
```

```bash
pnpm add tiny-date
# or
yarn add tiny-date
# or
bun add tiny-date
```

### Browser (CDN)

```html
<script src="https://unpkg.com/tiny-date/dist/tiny-date.umd.js"></script>
<script>
  tinyDate(new Date(Date.now() - 90 * 1000)); // → "2 minutes ago"
</script>
```

---

## Quick start

```js
import { tinyDate } from 'tiny-date';

const now = Date.now();

tinyDate(now - 5 * 60 * 1000);        // "5 minutes ago"
tinyDate(now + 3 * 60 * 60 * 1000);   // "in 3 hours"
tinyDate(now - 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000);  // "yesterday"
tinyDate(now - 3 * 365 * 24 * 3600 * 1000); // "3 years ago"
```

`tinyDate` accepts anything `Date` can be constructed from:

```js
tinyDate('2024-03-01T10:00:00Z');
tinyDate(1709287200000);      // timestamp in ms
tinyDate(new Date());
```

---

## API

### `tinyDate(date, options?)`

Returns a human-readable string describing `date` relative to `now`.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type                | Default     | Description                                  |
| --------- | ------------------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `date`    | `Date \| number \| string` | —     | The date to format.                          |
| `options` | `TinyDateOptions`   | `{}`        | See [Options](#options).                     |

#### Returns

`string` — the formatted relative time.

#### Throws

`TypeError` if `date` is not a valid date.

---

### `tinyDate.distance(date, options?)`

Returns the raw difference between `date` and `now`, without formatting it. Useful for building your own strings or for testing.

```js
tinyDate.distance(Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000);
// → { value: -5, unit: 'minute' }
```

| Property | Type                                        | Description                        |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `value`  | `number`                                    | Signed amount (negative = past).   |
| `unit`   | `'year' \| 'month' \| 'week' \| 'day' \| 'hour' \| 'minute' \| 'second'` | The resolved unit. |

---

### `tinyDate.units`

An array of the supported units, ordered largest to smallest.

```js
tinyDate.units; // → ['year', 'month', 'week', 'day', 'hour', 'minute', 'second']
```

---

## Options

```ts
interface TinyDateOptions {
  now?: Date | number;
  maxUnit?: Unit;
  minUnit?: Unit;
  addSuffix?: boolean;
  numeric?: 'always' | 'auto';
  locale?: string | string[];
  rounding?: 'round' | 'floor' | 'ceil';
  fallback?: (date: Date, now: Date) => string;
}
```

### `now`

The reference point to compare against. Defaults to `Date.now()`.

```js
tinyDate('2024-01-01T00:00:00Z', { now: '2024-01-01T00:05:00Z' }); // "5 minutes ago"
```

### `maxUnit`

The largest unit to use. Defaults to `'year'`.

```js
tinyDate(Date.now() - 60 * 60 * 1000, { maxUnit: 'minute' }); // "60 minutes ago"
```

### `minUnit`

The smallest unit to use. Defaults to `'second'`.

```js
tinyDate(Date.now() - 500, { minUnit: 'minute' }); // "0 minutes ago"
```

### `addSuffix`

Whether to include `"ago"` / `"in …"`. Defaults to `true`.

```js
tinyDate(Date.now() - 60 * 1000, { addSuffix: false }); // "1 minute"
```

### `numeric`

- `'auto'` (default) — uses words like `"yesterday"` and `"tomorrow"` where the locale supports them.
- `'always'` — always uses a number, e.g. `"1 day ago"`.

```js
tinyDate(Date.now() - 86400000, { numeric: 'always' }); // "1 day ago"
tinyDate(Date.now() - 86400000, { numeric: 'auto' });   // "yesterday"
```

### `locale`

A BCP 47 language tag (or array of them) passed to `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`. Defaults to the runtime's locale.

```js
tinyDate(Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000, { locale: 'es' }); // "hace 5 minutos"
tinyDate(Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000, { locale: 'ja' }); // "5 分前"
```

### `rounding`

How to round fractional units. Defaults to `'round'`.

- `'round'` — nearest integer (`1.4` → `1`, `1.6` → `2`)
- `'floor'` — toward zero (`1.9` → `1`)
- `'ceil'` — away from zero (`1.1` → `2`)

### `fallback`

Called when the difference is too large to express with the available units (e.g. `maxUnit: 'day'` and the date is 3 years away). Defaults to an ISO-like absolute date.

```js
tinyDate('2001-01-01', {
  maxUnit: 'day',
  fallback: (date) => date.toISOString().slice(0, 10), // "2001-01-01"
});
```

---

## How units are chosen

`tinyDate` picks the **largest unit** whose absolute difference is at least `1`, then rounds the remainder.

| Difference        | Result         |
| ----------------- | -------------- |
| 45 seconds        | `45 seconds ago` |
| 90 seconds        | `2 minutes ago`  |
| 5 minutes         | `5 minutes ago`  |
| 2 hours           | `2 hours ago`    |
| 1 day             | `yesterday`      |
| 3 days            | `3 days ago`     |
| 5 weeks           | `1 month ago`    |
| 14 months         | `1 year ago`     |

Weeks are only used when the difference is at least 7 days and less than 30 days.

---

## TypeScript

Types are bundled — no `@types/tiny-date` needed.

```ts
import { tinyDate, type TinyDateOptions, type Unit } from 'tiny-date';

const label: string = tinyDate(new Date(), { locale: 'fr' });
```

---

## Browser support

`tiny-date` requires `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`, available in:

- Chrome 71+, Edge 79+, Firefox 65+, Safari 14+
- Node.js 13+ (full ICU), Deno, Bun, Cloudflare Workers, Vercel Edge

If `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` is unavailable, `tiny-date` falls back to a small built-in English formatter so it never throws.

---

## Development

```bash
git clone https://github.com/yourname/tiny-date.git
cd tiny-date
npm install
```

| Script              | Description                        |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `npm run dev`       | Start the watch build              |
| `npm run build`     | Build ESM, CJS, and UMD bundles    |
| `npm test`          | Run the test suite                 |
| `npm run test:watch`| Run tests in watch mode            |
| `npm run lint`      | Lint and type-check                |
| `npm run size`      | Print bundle sizes                 |

---

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome! Please open an issue first to discuss any large changes.

1. Fork the repository
2. Create a branch: `git checkout -b feat/my-feature`
3. Make your changes and add tests
4. Run `npm test && npm run lint`
5. Open a pull request

---

## License

[MIT](./LICENSE) © yourname

---

<sub>Built with ❤️ — if `tiny-date` saves you a dependency, consider starring the repo.</sub>

# tiny-date

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/tiny-date.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/tiny-date)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

Format dates relative to now — `"5 minutes ago"`, `"in 3 days"`, `"just now"`.

Tiny on purpose: no dependencies, no locale bundles, no configuration file. One function, one job.

## Install

```sh
npm install tiny-date
```

## Usage

```js
const tinyDate = require('tiny-date');

tinyDate(new Date(Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000));
// => "5 minutes ago"

tinyDate(new Date(Date.now() + 3 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000));
// => "in 3 days"

tinyDate(new Date());
// => "just now"
```

ES modules and TypeScript are supported too:

```js
import tinyDate from 'tiny-date';
```

## API

### `tinyDate(date, options?)`

Returns a human-readable string describing `date` relative to the current time.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `date` | `Date \| number \| string` | The date to format. Numbers are treated as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds; strings are parsed with `new Date(string)`. |
| `options` | `object` | Optional. See below. |

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `relativeTo` | `Date \| number` | `Date.now()` | The point in time to compare against. Useful for testing. |
| `addSuffix` | `boolean` | `true` | Append `"ago"` / `"in ..."` to the result. Set to `false` for a bare duration like `"5 minutes"`. |
| `style` | `"long" \| "short"` | `"long"` | `"short"` uses abbreviated units (`"5m ago"`, `"in 3d"`). |
| `maxUnit` | `"second" \| "minute" \| "hour" \| "day" \| "week" \| "month" \| "year"` | `"year"` | The largest unit to report. Anything beyond it is expressed in this unit. |
| `minUnit` | same as `maxUnit` | `"second"` | The smallest unit to report. Anything smaller is rounded down to it. |

## Examples

```js
const now = Date.now();
const minute = 60 * 1000;
const hour = 60 * minute;
const day = 24 * hour;

tinyDate(now - 45 * 1000);            // "just now"
tinyDate(now - 5 * minute);           // "5 minutes ago"
tinyDate(now - 2 * hour);             // "2 hours ago"
tinyDate(now - 3 * day);              // "3 days ago"
tinyDate(now + 30 * minute);          // "in 30 minutes"
tinyDate(now - 90 * minute);          // "in 1 hour"  (rounded to the nearest unit)

tinyDate(now - 5 * minute, { style: 'short' });        // "5m ago"
tinyDate(now - 5 * minute, { addSuffix: false });      // "5 minutes"
tinyDate(now - 5 * minute, { relativeTo: now });       // "just now"
```

### Testing with a fixed reference point

```js
const reference = new Date('2024-01-01T00:00:00Z');

tinyDate(new Date('2023-12-31T23:55:00Z'), { relativeTo: reference });
// => "5 minutes ago"
```

## Behavior notes

- Units are chosen by magnitude: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, years.
- A difference of less than one second (in either direction) is reported as `"just now"`.
- Future dates are phrased as `"in <duration>"`, past dates as `"<duration> ago"`.
- Month and year lengths are approximated (a month is 30 days, a year is 365 days) to keep the implementation small and predictable.
- Invalid dates throw a `TypeError`.

## Why another date library?

Because most of the time you don't need 200 kB of locale data to print `"5 minutes ago"`. `tiny-date` is a single file with no dependencies, so it drops into any bundle without ceremony.

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome! Please open an issue first to discuss any larger changes.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/yourname/tiny-date.git
cd tiny-date
npm install
npm test
```

Please keep the library dependency-free and the source readable — the whole point is that it's tiny.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

# tiny-date

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/tiny-date.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/tiny-date)
[![bundle size](https://img.shields.io/bundlephobia/minzip/tiny-date.svg)](https://bundlephobia.com/package/tiny-date)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

> Format dates relative to now — `"5 minutes ago"`, `"in 3 hours"`, `"2 days ago"`.

**tiny-date** is a tiny, dependency-free helper for rendering human-friendly relative timestamps. It handles the awkward parts — thresholds, pluralization, and future dates — so you don't have to.

- 🪶 **~600 bytes** minified + gzipped
- 🚫 **Zero dependencies**
- 🌳 **Tree-shakeable** ESM + CommonJS builds
- 🌍 **Localized** out of the box (English, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Japanese)
- 🧪 **Fully unit tested**

---

## Installation

```bash
npm install tiny-date
```

```bash
yarn add tiny-date
```

```bash
pnpm add tiny-date
```

---

## Quick start

```js
import { relativeTime } from 'tiny-date';

const fiveMinutesAgo = new Date(Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000);

relativeTime(fiveMinutesAgo); // => "5 minutes ago"
```

Or use the default export:

```js
import tinyDate from 'tiny-date';

tinyDate(new Date()); // => "just now"
```

### In the browser

```html
<script type="module">
  import { relativeTime } from 'https://esm.sh/tiny-date';

  document.querySelector('#timestamp').textContent = relativeTime(
    new Date('2024-03-01T12:00:00Z')
  );
</script>
```

---

## API

### `relativeTime(date, options?)`

Formats `date` relative to a reference point in time.

**Parameters**

| Name   | Type              | Description                                        |
| ------ | ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `date` | `Date \| number \| string` | The date to format. Invalid input returns `""`. |
| `options` | `Options`     | Optional configuration. See below.                 |

**Returns**

`string` — the formatted relative time, or `""` if `date` is invalid.

### `Options`

| Option      | Type                          | Default     | Description                                                                 |
| ----------- | ----------------------------- | ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `now`       | `Date \| number`              | `Date.now()` | The reference point. Useful for testing or rendering relative to a fixed time. |
| `addSuffix` | `boolean`                     | `true`      | When `false`, returns only the duration (e.g. `"5 minutes"`).               |
| `locale`    | `string`                      | `"en"`      | Locale code. See [Supported locales](#supported-locales).                   |
| `fallback`  | `string`                      | `""`        | Returned when the date is invalid.                                           |

---

## Examples

```js
import { relativeTime } from 'tiny-date';

const now = Date.now();
const ago = (ms) => new Date(now - ms);
const ahead = (ms) => new Date(now + ms);

relativeTime(ago(30 * 1000));            // "just now"
relativeTime(ago(60 * 1000));            // "a minute ago"
relativeTime(ago(5 * 60 * 1000));        // "5 minutes ago"
relativeTime(ago(2 * 60 * 60 * 1000));   // "2 hours ago"
relativeTime(ago(3 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000)); // "3 days ago"
relativeTime(ago(60 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000)); // "2 months ago"

relativeTime(ahead(3 * 60 * 60 * 1000)); // "in 3 hours"
relativeTime(ahead(2 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000)); // "in 2 days"
```

### Without suffixes

```js
relativeTime(new Date(Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000), { addSuffix: false });
// => "5 minutes"
```

### Relative to a fixed point

```js
const reference = new Date('2024-01-01T00:00:00Z');

relativeTime(new Date('2023-12-31T23:00:00Z'), { now: reference });
// => "an hour ago"
```

### Other locales

```js
relativeTime(new Date(Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000), { locale: 'es' });
// => "hace 5 minutos"

relativeTime(new Date(Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000), { locale: 'fr' });
// => "il y a 5 minutes"
```

### Invalid dates

```js
relativeTime('not a date');            // => ""
relativeTime('not a date', { fallback: 'unknown' }); // => "unknown"
```

---

## Supported locales

| Code   | Language    |
| ------ | ----------- |
| `en`   | English     |
| `es`   | Spanish     |
| `fr`   | French      |
| `de`   | German      |
| `pt`   | Portuguese  |
| `ja`   | Japanese    |

Missing a language? [Open an issue](https://github.com/yourname/tiny-date/issues) — adding one is usually a single object in `src/locales/`.

---

## How thresholds work

tiny-date uses natural-language thresholds rather than naive division, so results read the way a human would say them:

| Time difference      | Output        |
| -------------------- | ------------- |
| `< 45 seconds`       | `just now`    |
| `< 90 seconds`       | `a minute`    |
| `< 45 minutes`       | `N minutes`   |
| `< 90 minutes`       | `an hour`     |
| `< 22 hours`         | `N hours`     |
| `< 36 hours`         | `a day`       |
| `< 26 days`          | `N days`      |
| `< 45 days`          | `a month`     |
| `< 320 days`         | `N months`    |
| `< 548 days`         | `a year`      |
| `>= 548 days`        | `N years`     |

---

## TypeScript

Types ship with the package — no `@types` install needed.

```ts
import { relativeTime, type Options, type Locale } from 'tiny-date';

const opts: Options = { locale: 'de', addSuffix: false };
```

---

## Browser support

Works in any environment with `Intl` support: all modern browsers, Node.js 14+, Deno, Bun, and edge runtimes.

---

2. Create a branch: `git checkout -b feature/my-change`
3. Make your changes
4. Run the tests: `npm test`
5. Commit and open a pull request

Please open an issue first for larger changes so we can discuss the approach.

# tiny-date > Human-friendly relative dates, in ~1 kB. `tiny-date` turns a timestamp into a string people actually understand — `"5 minutes ago"`, `"in 3 days"`, `"just now"` — with no dependencies, no locale bundles, and no surprises. ```js import { relative } from 'tiny-date' relative(Date.now() - 5 * 60_000) // → "5 minutes ago" ``` --- ## Contents - [Why tiny-date?](#why-tiny-date) - [Install](#install) - [Quick start](#quick-start) - [API](#api) - [`relative(date, options?)`](#relativedate-options) - [`relativeParts(date, options?)`](#relativepartsdate-options) - [`parseRelative(text, options?)`](#parserelativetext-options) - [`isRelative(text)`](#isrelativetext) - [Options](#options) - [Thresholds](#thresholds) - [Localization](#localization) - [Time zones](#time-zones) - [Edge cases](#edge-cases) - [TypeScript](#typescript) - [Browser support](#browser-support) - [Contributing](#contributing) - [License](#license) --- ## Why tiny-date? Most "time ago" helpers fall into one of two camps: 1. **Big ones** — `dayjs`, `date-fns`, `moment` — that ship a locale file per language and a formatting engine you don't need for a single string. 2. **Tiny ones** — a `switch` statement in a `utils.js` that nobody can configure, localize, or test. `tiny-date` is the middle ground: one function, one options object, one optional locale, and a hard rule that **the output is never wrong by more than a rounding error**. - 🪶 **~1.1 kB** minified + gzipped, zero dependencies - 🌍 **Any locale** via the built-in `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` (no locale files to import) - 🧪 **100% test coverage**, deterministic clock injection - 🧩 **Tree-shakeable** — import only what you use - 📦 **ESM + CJS + a single-file UMD build** --- ## Install ```sh npm install tiny-date ``` ```sh pnpm add tiny-date # or yarn add tiny-date ``` Or drop it straight into a page: ```html ``` --- ## Quick start ```js import { relative } from 'tiny-date' const now = Date.now() relative(now - 30_000) // "just now" relative(now - 5 * 60_000) // "5 minutes ago" relative(now - 3 * 3_600_000) // "3 hours ago" relative(now - 2 * 86_400_000) // "2 days ago" relative(now + 45 * 60_000) // "in 45 minutes" ``` With a reference point: ```js relative('2024-03-01T12:00:00Z', { base: new Date('2024-03-01T12:00:00Z') }) // → "just now" ``` In a template: ```js const post = { title: 'Hello', createdAt: 1717171717000 } `

${post.title}

${relative(post.createdAt)}
` ``` --- ## API ### `relative(date, options?)` Returns a human-readable string describing `date` relative to `base` (default: the current time). ```js relative(date: Date | number | string, options?: Options): string ``` | Argument | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `date` | `Date \| number \| string` | The moment to describe. Numbers are treated as epoch milliseconds; strings are parsed with `new Date(...)`. | | `options` | `Options` | See [Options](#options). | ```js relative(new Date()) // "just now" relative(Date.now() - 86_400_000) // "yesterday" relative(Date.now() - 86_400_000 * 400) // "1 year ago" ``` ### `relativeParts(date, options?)` Same as `relative`, but returns the pieces instead of a finished string — useful for custom rendering or for wrapping parts in markup. ```js relativeParts(Date.now() - 5 * 60_000) // → { value: 5, unit: 'minute', past: true } ``` ```js relativeParts(Date.now() - 5 * 60_000) // → { value: -5, unit: 'minute', past: false } ``` The returned object is always shaped like: ```ts { value: number // signed: negative = past, positive = future unit: 'second' | 'minute' | 'hour' | 'day' | 'month' | 'year' past: boolean } ``` ### `parseRelative(text, options?)` The inverse of `relative`: turns `"5 minutes ago"` back into a `Date`. ```js parseRelative('5 minutes ago') // → Date (5 minutes before now) parseRelative('in 3 days') // → Date (3 days after now) parseRelative('just now') // → Date (now) parseRelative('nonsense') // → null ``` | Option | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `base` | `Date \| number` | `Date.now()` | The reference point the text is relative to. | | `locale` | `string` | `'en'` | Locale whose phrasing should be recognized. | > Parsing is intentionally forgiving but **not** a general-purpose NLP date parser. It understands the exact phrasings `tiny-date` itself produces, plus a handful of common aliases (`"yesterday"`, `"tomorrow"`, `"a minute ago"`). ### `isRelative(text)` A cheap type guard for the above. ```js isRelative('5 minutes ago') // true isRelative('March 3rd') // false ``` --- ## Options All options are optional. | Option | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `base` | `Date \| number` | `Date.now()` | The reference point. | | `locale` | `string` | `'en'` | BCP 47 locale tag, e.g. `'en'`, `'de'`, `'pt-BR'`, `'ja'`. | | `numeric` | `'auto' \| 'always'` | `'auto'` | `'auto'` renders `"yesterday"` / `"last week"`; `'always'` renders `"1 day ago"`. | | `style` | `'long' \| 'short' \| 'narrow'` | `'long'` | Passed through to `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`. | | `justNow` | `string \| false` | `'just now'` | Text for differences under 45 seconds. Pass `false` to disable and fall through to `"0 seconds ago"`. | | `maxUnit` | `'second' \| 'minute' \| 'hour' \| 'day' \| 'month' \| 'year'` | `'year'` | The largest unit to report. Anything bigger is clamped to this unit. | | `fallback` | `string \| ((date: Date) => string)` | `date.toISOString()` | Used when the input can't be parsed into a valid date. | ```js relative(Date.now() - 86_400_000, { numeric: 'always' }) // → "1 day ago" relative(Date.now() - 86_400_000, { style: 'short' }) // → "1 day ago" (short style drops the word "ago" in some locales) relative(Date.now() - 86_400_000, { locale: 'de' }) // → "vor 1 Tag" relative(Date.now() - 86_400_000, { justNow: false }) // → "1 day ago" (unaffected — only applies under 45s) ``` --- ## Thresholds Rounding is where most relative-time libraries get weird. `tiny-date` uses a fixed, documented table so that `"59 minutes ago"` never becomes `"1 hour ago"` and `"23 hours ago"` never becomes `"yesterday"`. | Difference | Output (`en`) | | --- | --- | | `< 45 seconds` | `just now` | | `45s – 89s` | `1 minute ago` | | `90s – 44m` | `N minutes ago` | | `45m – 89m` | `1 hour ago` | | `90m – 21h` | `N hours ago` | | `22h – 35h` | `1 day ago` | | `36h – 25d` | `N days ago` | | `26d – 44d` | `1 month ago` | | `45d – 319d` | `N months ago` | | `320d – 547d` | `1 year ago` | | `≥ 548d` | `N years ago` | Months are approximated as **30.44 days** (the mean Gregorian month) and years as **365.25 days**, so drift stays under a day across a decade. --- ## Localization `tiny-date` uses the platform's [`Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Intl/RelativeTimeFormat) — no locale files are bundled, and adding a language is a one-word change. ```js relative(Date.now() - 3 * 3_600_000, { locale: 'fr' }) // "il y a 3 heures" relative(Date.now() - 3 * 3_600_000, { locale: 'es' }) // "hace 3 horas" relative(Date.now() - 3 * 3_600_000, { locale: 'ja' }) // "3 時間前" relative(Date.now() - 3 * 3_600_000, { locale: 'ar' }) // "قبل 3 ساعات" ``` If the runtime doesn't support `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`, `tiny-date` falls back to a small built-in English formatter so it never throws. --- ## Time zones `tiny-date` compares **absolute instants**, so it behaves correctly across time zones and DST boundaries without any configuration. ```js // A timestamp is a timestamp — the user's clock zone is irrelevant. relative(1717171717000) // "5 minutes ago" (wherever you are) ``` If you need *calendar-aware* output ("yesterday" meaning the previous calendar day, not the previous 24 hours), pass a `base` and use `maxUnit: 'day'` with `numeric: 'auto'` — or reach for `Intl.DateTimeFormat` directly. --- ## Edge cases ```js relative(new Date('nope')) // → "Invalid Date" (or your `fallback`) relative(Date.now() - 5 * 60_000, { fallback: () => '—' }) // → "—" relative(Date.now() + 10 * 365 * 86_400_000, { maxUnit: 'month' }) // → "in 120 months" relative(Date.now(), { justNow: false }) // → "0 seconds ago" ``` - `NaN` and `Invalid Date` inputs never throw. - Future dates are always phrased in the future tense (`"in 5 minutes"`). - `base` in the future is supported: `relative(past, { base: futureDate })` yields `"in 5 minutes"`. --- ## TypeScript Types ship with the package. ```ts import { relative, type Options, type RelativeParts } from 'tiny-date' const opts: Options = { locale: 'en-GB', numeric: 'always' } const parts: RelativeParts = relativeParts(Date.now(), opts) ``` --- ## Browser support | Browser | Support | | --- | --- | | Chrome 71+ | ✅ | | Firefox 65+ | ✅ | | Safari 14.1+ | ✅ | | Edge 79+ | ✅ | | Node 16+ | ✅ | | IE 11 | ❌ (use the UMD build with a polyfill) | --- ## Contributing Contributions are welcome and appreciated! 🎉 ```sh git clone https://github.com/yourname/tiny-date.git cd tiny-date npm install npm test ``` Before opening a pull request: 1. Run `npm run lint` and `npm run format`. 2. Add tests for any behavior change — the suite aims for 100% coverage. 3. Update the README if you change or add an option. 4. Keep it small. If a feature would add more than ~200 bytes gzipped, it probably belongs in a different package. **Good first issues** are tagged [`good first issue`](https://github.com/yourname/tiny-date/labels/good%20first%20issue). --- ## License [MIT](./LICENSE) © [Your Name](https://github.com/yourname) --- Built with ☕️ and a stubborn insistence on small bundles.

```sh
npm install tiny-date
```

```sh
pnpm add tiny-date
# or
yarn add tiny-date
```

## Usage

```js
import { formatRelative } from 'tiny-date';

formatRelative(new Date(Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000));
// => "5 minutes ago"

formatRelative(new Date(Date.now() + 3 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000));
// => "in 3 days"

formatRelative(new Date());
// => "just now"
```

CommonJS:

```js
const { formatRelative } = require('tiny-date');
```

### Default export

```js
import tinyDate from 'tiny-date';

tinyDate(new Date(Date.now() - 90 * 1000));
// => "2 minutes ago"
```

### `formatRelative(date, options?)`

Returns a human-readable string describing `date` relative to the current time.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `relativeTo` | `Date \| number \| string` | `Date.now()` | The reference point to compare against. |
| `locale` | `string \| string[]` | `undefined` | BCP 47 locale tag(s), e.g. `"es"`. Falls back to the runtime default. |
| `numeric` | `"auto" \| "always"` | `"auto"` | `"auto"` renders `"yesterday"` / `"last week"`; `"always"` renders `"1 day ago"`. |
| `style` | `"long" \| "short" \| "narrow"` | `"long"` | Passed through to `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`. |
| `maxUnit` | `"second" \| "minute" \| "hour" \| "day" \| "week" \| "month" \| "year"` | `"year"` | Largest unit to report. Anything beyond is clamped to this unit. |

```js
formatRelative(new Date(Date.now() - 60 * 60 * 1000), { style: 'short' });
// => "1 hr. ago"

formatRelative(new Date(Date.now() - 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000), { numeric: 'always' });
// => "1 day ago"

formatRelative(new Date(Date.now() - 400 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000), { maxUnit: 'month' });
// => "13 months ago"
```

### `formatRelativeParts(date, options?)`

Same as `formatRelative`, but returns structured data — handy if you want to style the number and the unit separately.

```js
formatRelativeParts(new Date(Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000));
// => { value: -5, unit: 'minute', text: '5 minutes ago' }
```

- Dates in the future are prefixed with `"in "`; past dates are suffixed with `" ago"`.

- Invalid dates throw a `TypeError`.

```js
// => "5 minutes ago"

formatRelative(new Date(Date.now() + 3 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000))
// => "in 3 days"
```

CommonJS:

```js
const { formatRelative } = require('tiny-date')
```

### Shorthand

The default export is `formatRelative`, so you can import it directly:

```js
import formatRelative from 'tiny-date'

formatRelative(Date.now() - 3600000) // => "1 hour ago"
```

## API

### `formatRelative(date, options?)`

Returns a string describing `date` relative to `now`.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `date` | `Date \| number \| string` | The date to format. Numbers are treated as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds; strings are parsed with `new Date(string)`. |
| `options` | `object` | See below. |

#### Options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `now` | `Date \| number` | `Date.now()` | The reference point for "now". Useful for testing. |
| `locale` | `string` | `"en"` | Locale code, e.g. `"en"`, `"es"`. |
| `style` | `"long" \| "short"` | `"long"` | `"short"` abbreviates units (`"5m ago"`). |
| `addSuffix` | `boolean` | `true` | Set to `false` to omit `"ago"` / `"in ..."`. |
| `maxUnit` | `"second" \| "minute" \| "hour" \| "day" \| "week" \| "month" \| "year"` | `"year"` | The largest unit to report. Anything beyond it is expressed in this unit. |

### `formatDistance(date, date2, options?)`

Formats the distance between two dates, without a suffix.

```js
import { formatDistance } from 'tiny-date'

formatDistance(new Date('2024-01-01'), new Date('2024-01-08'))
// => "7 days"
```

## Examples

```js
import { formatRelative } from 'tiny-date'

const now = Date.now()

formatRelative(now - 30 * 1000)          // => "just now"
formatRelative(now - 45 * 1000)          // => "45 seconds ago"
formatRelative(now - 5 * 60 * 1000)      // => "5 minutes ago"
formatRelative(now - 90 * 60 * 1000)     // => "1 hour ago"
formatRelative(now - 3 * 86400000)       // => "3 days ago"
formatRelative(now - 14 * 86400000)      // => "2 weeks ago"
formatRelative(now - 60 * 86400000)      // => "2 months ago"
formatRelative(now - 730 * 86400000)     // => "2 years ago"
```

### Future dates

```js
formatRelative(Date.now() + 60 * 1000)    // => "in 1 minute"
```

### Short style

```js
formatRelative(Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000, { style: 'short' })
// => "5m ago"
```

### Without a suffix

```js
formatRelative(Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000, { addSuffix: false })
// => "5 minutes"
```

### Localized

```js
formatRelative(Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000, { locale: 'es' })
// => "hace 5 minutos"
```

### Testing with a fixed `now`

```js
const now = new Date('2024-06-01T12:00:00Z')

formatRelative(new Date('2024-06-01T11:55:00Z'), { now })
// => "5 minutes ago"
```

## Locales

| Locale | Code |
| --- | --- |
| English | `en` |
| Spanish | `es` |

Missing a language? Contributions are welcome — see [Contributing](./CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Browser support

`tiny-date` targets modern browsers and Node.js 18+. It ships as ESM and UMD builds.

```html
<script src="https://unpkg.com/tiny-date/dist/tiny-date.min.js"></script>
<script>
  tinyDate.formatRelative(Date.now() - 300000) // => "5 minutes ago"
</script>
```

## Why not Day.js / date-fns?

Those libraries are great — but if all you need is `"5 minutes ago"`, pulling in a full date library is overkill. `tiny-date` does one thing, weighs about as much as a tweet, and gets out of your way.

# tiny-date

> Format dates relative to now — `"5 minutes ago"`, `"in 2 hours"`, `"just now"`.

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/tiny-date.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/tiny-date)
[![bundle size](https://img.shields.io/bundlephobia/minzip/tiny-date.svg)](https://bundlephobia.com/package/tiny-date)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%3E%3D14-brightgreen.svg)](https://nodejs.org)

**tiny-date** is a tiny, dependency-free helper that turns a `Date` (or timestamp) into a
human-readable string relative to the current moment. It ships with sensible English
defaults, an optional short style, and a pluggable `now` so it's easy to test.

- 🪶 **~1.2 kB minified + gzipped**, zero dependencies
- 🕰️ Handles both past and future
- 🧪 100% test coverage
- 🌐 Works in Node, Bun, Deno, and the browser
- 🇬🇧 Built-in English locale, extensible for your own

---

## Installation

```bash
npm install tiny-date
```

```bash
pnpm add tiny-date
# or
yarn add tiny-date
```

---

## Quick start

```js
import { relative } from 'tiny-date'

relative(new Date(Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000))
// => '5 minutes ago'

relative(new Date(Date.now() + 2 * 60 * 60 * 1000))
// => 'in 2 hours'

relative(new Date())
// => 'just now'
```

CommonJS works too:

```js
const { relative } = require('tiny-date')
```

---

## API

### `relative(date, options?)`

Returns a string describing how far `date` is from now.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `date` | `Date \| number \| string` | The date to describe. Numbers are treated as Unix timestamps (ms); strings are parsed with `new Date(...)`. |
| `options` | `object` | Optional. See [Options](#options). |

**Returns:** `string`

### `format(date, options?)`

Alias of `relative`, for people who prefer the verb "format".

```js
import { format } from 'tiny-date'

format(Date.now() - 1000) // => 'just now'
```

---

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `now` | `Date \| number` | `Date.now()` | The reference point. Pass a fixed value to get deterministic output (handy in tests). |
| `style` | `'long' \| 'short'` | `'long'` | `'long'` → `"5 minutes ago"`, `'short'` → `"5m ago"`. |
| `suffix` | `boolean` | `true` | Set to `false` to omit `"ago"` / `"in"`. |
| `fallback` | `string` | `'just now'` | Used for invalid dates. |

```js
relative(date, { style: 'short' })      // => '5m ago'
relative(date, { suffix: false })       // => '5 minutes'
relative(date, { now: new Date(0) })    // => uses Jan 1 1970 as "now"
relative(date, { fallback: 'unknown' }) // => 'unknown' for invalid input
```

---

## Output reference

Given a date in the past:

| Difference | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 0 – 44 seconds | `just now` |
| 45 – 89 seconds | `a minute ago` |
| 90 seconds – 44 minutes | `N minutes ago` |
| 45 – 89 minutes | `an hour ago` |
| 90 minutes – 21 hours | `N hours ago` |
| 22 – 35 hours | `a day ago` |
| 36 hours – 24 days | `N days ago` |
| 25 – 44 days | `a month ago` |
| 45 – 319 days | `N months ago` |
| 320 – 547 days | `a year ago` |
| 548+ days | `N years ago` |

Future dates mirror this table with a leading `"in "` (`"in 5 minutes"`, `"in a day"`).

### Short style

| Difference | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 0 – 44 seconds | `now` |
| 45 – 89 seconds | `1m ago` |
| 90 seconds – 44 minutes | `5m ago` |
| 45 – 89 minutes | `1h ago` |
| 90 minutes – 21 hours | `3h ago` |
| 22 – 35 hours | `1d ago` |
| 36 hours – 24 days | `12d ago` |
| 25 – 44 days | `1mo ago` |
| 45 – 319 days | `7mo ago` |
| 320 – 547 days | `1y ago` |
| 548+ days | `3y ago` |

---

## Advanced usage

### Deterministic output in tests

```js
import { relative } from 'tiny-date'

const now = new Date('2024-03-01T12:00:00Z')

relative(new Date('2024-03-01T11:55:00Z'), { now })
// => '5 minutes ago'
```

### Rendering a list

```js
const posts = [
  { title: 'Hello world', createdAt: Date.now() - 60_000 },
  { title: 'Shipping it', createdAt: Date.now() - 3 * 86_400_000 },
]

posts.map(p => `${p.title} — ${relative(p.createdAt)}`)
// => ['Hello world — a minute ago', 'Shipping it — 3 days ago']
```

### Live updating

```js
import { relative } from 'tiny-date'

const el = document.querySelector('#updated')

const tick = () => {
  el.textContent = relative(el.dataset.updatedAt)
}

tick()
setInterval(tick, 30_000)
```

### Custom locales

The internal formatter is exported so you can build your own locale on top of it:

```js
import { createFormatter } from 'tiny-date'

const fr = createFormatter({
  units: {
    minute: { one: 'une minute', other: '%d minutes' },
    hour: { one: 'une heure', other: '%d heures' },
  },
  past: 'il y a %s',
  future: 'dans %s',
})

fr(new Date(Date.now() - 5 * 60_000))
// => 'il y a 5 minutes'
```

---

## Browser usage

tiny-date is ESM-first and ships a browser-ready ESM build:

```html
<script type="module">
  import { relative } from 'https://esm.sh/tiny-date'

  document.body.textContent = relative(Date.now() - 60_000)
</script>
```

For bundlers, the package exposes `"exports"` with `import` and `require` conditions, so
`import { relative } from 'tiny-date'` and `const { relative } = require('tiny-date')`
both work without a config change.

---

## Requirements

- Node.js 14+ (uses `Intl`-free, plain JS — no polyfills needed)
- Any modern browser

---

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome! Please:

1. Open an issue first to discuss larger changes.
2. Fork the repo and create a feature branch.
3. Run the checks before opening a pull request:

```bash
npm install
npm test          # unit tests
npm run lint      # eslint + prettier
npm run build     # bundle + size check
```

Please include tests for any new behaviour — the project aims for 100% coverage.

---

## License

[MIT](./LICENSE) © tiny-date contributors

# tiny-date

> Human-friendly relative dates, in ~1 kB. Zero dependencies.

`tiny-date` turns a `Date` (or timestamp) into a string people actually understand — `"5 minutes ago"`, `"in 3 hours"`, `"yesterday"` — without pulling in a 70 kB date library.

```js
import { formatRelative } from 'tiny-date'

formatRelative(Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000)
//=> "5 minutes ago"

formatRelative(Date.now() + 3 * 60 * 60 * 1000)
//=> "in 3 hours"
```

---

## Contents

- [Why tiny-date?](#why-tiny-date)
- [Install](#install)
- [Quick start](#quick-start)
- [API](#api)
  - [`formatRelative(date, options?)`](#formatrelativedate-options)
  - [`formatDistance(date, base?, options?)`](#formatdistancedate-base-options)
  - [`toRelativeParts(date, options?)`](#torerelativepartsdate-options)
- [Options](#options)
- [Formatting rules](#formatting-rules)
- [Styles](#styles)
- [Localization](#localization)
- [TypeScript](#typescript)
- [Testing with a fixed "now"](#testing-with-a-fixed-now)
- [Browser support](#browser-support)
- [FAQ](#faq)
- [Contributing](#contributing)
- [License](#license)

---

## Why tiny-date?

Most "relative time" helpers ship a full calendar engine, timezone database, and locale bundles. If all you need is *"how long ago was that?"*, that's overkill.

**tiny-date is:**

- 🪶 **~1.2 kB** minified + gzipped
- 🚫 **Zero dependencies**
- 🌍 **Localized** via the built-in `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` (40+ locales, no bundle cost)
- 🧩 **Tree-shakeable** — import only the function you use
- 🧪 **Deterministic** — pass your own `now` for tests
- 📦 **ESM + CJS** + TypeScript declarations

---

## Install

```bash
npm install tiny-date
```

```bash
pnpm add tiny-date
# or
yarn add tiny-date
```

```html
<!-- UMD / global build -->
<script src="https://unpkg.com/tiny-date/dist/tiny-date.umd.js"></script>
<script>tinyDate.formatRelative(new Date())</script>
```

---

## Quick start

```js
import { formatRelative } from 'tiny-date'

const post = new Date('2024-03-01T10:00:00Z')

formatRelative(post)                    // "2 months ago"
formatRelative(post, { style: 'short' }) // "2mo ago"
formatRelative(post, { locale: 'es' })  // "hace 2 meses"
formatRelative(post, { numeric: 'always' }) // "2 months ago"
```

Future dates work too — the suffix flips automatically:

```js
formatRelative(Date.now() + 90 * 1000)        // "in a minute"
formatRelative(Date.now() + 2 * 86400_000)    // "in 2 days"
```

---

## API

### `formatRelative(date, options?)`

Returns a human-readable string describing how far `date` is from `now`.

```js
formatRelative(date: Date | number | string, options?: Options): string
```

```js
formatRelative(new Date())                     // "just now"
formatRelative(Date.now() - 3600_000)          // "an hour ago"
formatRelative(Date.now() - 86400_000)         // "yesterday"
formatRelative(Date.now() - 7 * 86400_000)     // "last week" → "7 days ago"
```

Throws a `TypeError` if `date` is not a valid date.

### `formatDistance(date, base?, options?)`

Like `formatRelative`, but **without** the `"ago"` / `"in"` prefix. Useful for durations, timestamps, and log lines.

```js
formatDistance(date: Date | number | string, base?: Date | number, options?: Options): string
```

```js
formatDistance(Date.now() - 5 * 60_000)   // "5 minutes"
formatDistance(a, b)                      // "3 hours"
formatDistance(a, b, { style: 'short' })  // "3h"
```

### `toRelativeParts(date, options?)`

Returns the underlying structured result — handy if you want to render the number and unit separately (e.g. to add a tooltip or a live-updating counter).

```js
toRelativeParts(date: Date | number | string, options?: Options): {
  value: number
  unit: Intl.RelativeTimeFormatUnit
  direction: 'past' | 'future' | 'none'
  label: string
}
```

```js
toRelativeParts(Date.now() - 5 * 60_000)
//=> { value: -5, unit: 'minute', direction: 'past', label: '5 minutes ago' }
```

---

## Options

All options are optional and every function accepts the same object.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `locale` | `string \| string[]` | `'en'` | BCP 47 locale tag, or a list of tags for fallback. |
| `style` | `'long' \| 'short' \| 'narrow'` | `'long'` | `long`: `"5 minutes ago"` · `short`: `"5m ago"` · `narrow`: `"5m ago"`. |
| `numeric` | `'auto' \| 'always'` | `'auto'` | `auto` uses `"yesterday"` / `"tomorrow"`; `always` uses `"1 day ago"` / `"in 1 day"`. |
| `now` | `Date \| number` | `Date.now()` | Reference point for the comparison. |
| `maxUnit` | `Unit \| null` | `null` | Coarsest unit to report. Anything larger falls back to `fallback`. |
| `minUnit` | `Unit` | `'second'` | Finest unit to report. |
| `fallback` | `string \| ((date: Date) => string)` | `null` | Rendered when the difference exceeds `maxUnit`. Defaults to an absolute date (`"Mar 1, 2024"`). |
| `rounding` | `'round' \| 'floor' \| 'ceil'` | `'round'` | How fractional units are reduced. |
| `includeSeconds` | `boolean` | `false` | Report `"12 seconds ago"` instead of `"just now"`. |

```js
formatRelative(date, {
  locale: 'fr',
  style: 'long',
  numeric: 'always',
  maxUnit: 'day',
  fallback: (d) => d.toISOString().slice(0, 10),
})
```

---

## Formatting rules

Differences are rounded to the nearest sensible unit, following a set of human-friendly thresholds:

| Difference | Output (`numeric: 'auto'`) | Output (`numeric: 'always'`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| < 45 seconds | `just now` | `0 seconds ago` / `in 0 seconds` |
| 45 s – 90 s | `a minute ago` | `1 minute ago` |
| 90 s – 45 min | `N minutes ago` | `N minutes ago` |
| 45 min – 90 min | `an hour ago` | `1 hour ago` |
| 90 min – 22 h | `N hours ago` | `N hours ago` |
| 22 h – 36 h | `yesterday` / `tomorrow` | `1 day ago` / `in 1 day` |
| 36 h – 25 d | `N days ago` | `N days ago` |
| 25 d – 45 d | `a month ago` | `1 month ago` |
| 45 d – 320 d | `N months ago` | `N months ago` |
| 320 d – 548 d | `a year ago` | `1 year ago` |
| ≥ 548 d | `N years ago` | `N years ago` |

Units are: `second`, `minute`, `hour`, `day`, `week`, `month`, `year`.

---

## Styles

```js
const date = Date.now() - 3 * 60 * 60 * 1000

formatRelative(date, { style: 'long' })   // "3 hours ago"
formatRelative(date, { style: 'short' })  // "3h ago"
formatRelative(date, { style: 'narrow' }) // "3h ago"
```

Short style abbreviates the unit and drops the space before the suffix: `"3h ago"`, `"in 2d"`, `"yesterday"`.

---

## Localization

`tiny-date` delegates wording and pluralization to the platform's [`Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Intl/RelativeTimeFormat), so most locales work with no extra setup:

```js
formatRelative(date, { locale: 'de' })  // "vor 5 Minuten"
formatRelative(date, { locale: 'ja' })  // "5分前"
formatRelative(date, { locale: 'ar' })  // "قبل 5 دقائق"
```

Fallback chain:

```js
formatRelative(date, { locale: ['pt-BR', 'pt', 'en'] })
```

### Custom locale

Override the wording for a locale without shipping a full dictionary:

```js
import { formatRelative, defineLocale } from 'tiny-date'

defineLocale('xx', {
  units: {
    minute: { one: 'minüt', other: 'minüt' },
    hour:   { one: 'stund', other: 'stund' },
  },
  past: (n, unit) => `${n} ${unit} her`,
  future: (n, unit) => `in ${n} ${unit}`,
  now: 'just now',
})

formatRelative(Date.now() - 60_000, { locale: 'xx' }) // "1 minüt her"
```

> **Note:** when a custom locale is registered for the requested tag, `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` is bypassed for that tag only.

---

## TypeScript

Types ship with the package — no `@types` install needed.

```ts
import { formatRelative, type Options, type Unit } from 'tiny-date'

const opts: Options = { locale: 'en', style: 'short', maxUnit: 'day' }
const label: string = formatRelative(new Date(), opts)
```

---

## Testing with a fixed "now"

Pass `now` to make output deterministic:

```js
import { formatRelative } from 'tiny-date'

const now = new Date('2024-06-01T12:00:00Z')

formatRelative(new Date('2024-06-01T11:55:00Z'), { now })
//=> "5 minutes ago"
```

Or freeze it globally for a test file:

```js
import { setNow } from 'tiny-date'

beforeEach(() => setNow(new Date('2024-06-01T12:00:00Z')))
afterEach(() => setNow(null)) // back to Date.now()
```

---

## Browser support

| Browser | Support |
| --- | --- |
| Chrome / Edge | 80+ |
| Firefox | 79+ |
| Safari | 14.1+ |
| Node.js | 18+ |

`Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` is required for non-`en` locales; a built-in English fallback is used if it's missing.

---

## FAQ

**Does it handle timezones?**
Relative differences are computed in absolute time (UTC-based), so they're timezone-independent. Only the `fallback` absolute date is rendered in the local timezone.

**What about DST transitions?**
Because differences are absolute, a day across a DST boundary may read `"23 hours ago"` rather than `"yesterday"`. Use `numeric: 'always'` if you prefer raw arithmetic.

**Can I use it in React?**
Yes — but call it inside a component body (or `useMemo`) so it re-renders as time passes:

```jsx
function TimeAgo({ date }) {
  const label = useMemo(() => formatRelative(date), [date])
  return <time dateTime={new Date(date).toISOString()}>{label}</time>
}
```

**How do I refresh labels automatically?**
`tiny-date` doesn't schedule timers. Re-render on an interval, or use the exported `createTicker(intervalMs)` helper:

```js
import { createTicker } from 'tiny-date'

const stop = createTicker(() => setLabel(formatRelative(date)), 30_000)
```

**Is the output stable across versions?**
The thresholds table above is part of the public contract. Changes to it are released as a **minor** version and listed in the changelog.

---

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome!

```bash
git clone https://github.com/yourname/tiny-date.git
cd tiny-date
npm install
npm test
```

- 🐛 **Bug reports** — please include the expected vs. actual output and your locale.
- 💡 **Feature requests** — open an issue first to discuss scope.
- ✅ **PRs** — add tests, keep the bundle under 2 kB gzipped, and run `npm run lint`.

---

## License

MIT © [yourname](https://github.com/yourname)

---

# tiny-date

> Tiny, dependency-free date formatting for humans. "5 minutes ago", "in 3 hours", "2 days ago" — and nothing else.

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/tiny-date.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/tiny-date)
[![bundle size](https://img.shields.io/bundlephobia/minzip/tiny-date.svg)](https://bundlephobia.com/package/tiny-date)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/tiny-date.svg)](./LICENSE)

---

## Why?

Most "time ago" libraries ship Intl-sized machinery for a job that takes 40 lines. `tiny-date` does one thing — describe the distance between a date and now — with zero dependencies and a footprint small enough to paste into a bundle without thinking twice.

- 🪶 **~1.2 kB minified + gzipped**
- 🚫 **Zero dependencies**
- 🌍 **Locale-aware** (English included, more welcome)
- 🧩 **Tree-shakeable** ESM + CommonJS builds
- 🧪 **100% test coverage**

## Install

```bash
npm install tiny-date
```

```bash
yarn add tiny-date
```

```bash
pnpm add tiny-date
```

## Usage

```js
import { relative } from 'tiny-date'

relative(new Date(Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000))
// => '5 minutes ago'

relative(new Date(Date.now() + 3 * 60 * 60 * 1000))
// => 'in 3 hours'

relative(new Date('2024-01-01'))
// => '2 months ago'
```

Or via the default export:

```js
import tinyDate from 'tiny-date'

tinyDate(new Date())
// => 'just now'
```

### CommonJS

```js
const { relative } = require('tiny-date')
```

### In the browser

```html
<script type="module">
  import { relative } from 'https://esm.sh/tiny-date'

  document.querySelector('#time').textContent = relative(new Date('2024-06-01'))
</script>
```

## API

### `relative(date, options?)`

Returns a human-readable string describing how far `date` is from now.

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type               | Default | Description                                |
| -------- | ------------------ | ------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `date`   | `Date \| number \| string` | — | The date to describe. Invalid dates throw a `RangeError`. |
| `options` | `Options`        | `{}`    | See below.                                |

**Options**

| Option      | Type                                       | Default    | Description |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------ | ---------- | ----------- |
| `locale`    | `string`                                   | `'en'`     | Locale code. Only `'en'` is bundled today. |
| `style`     | `'long' \| 'short'`                        | `'long'`   | `'long'` → `"5 minutes ago"`, `'short'` → `"5m ago"`. |
| `maxUnit`   | `'year' \| 'month' \| 'week' \| 'day' \| 'hour' \| 'minute' \| 'second'` | `'year'` | The largest unit to use. `'day'` turns "3 months ago" into "92 days ago". |
| `minUnit`   | `'day' \| 'hour' \| 'minute' \| 'second'`  | `'second'` | The smallest unit to use. `'minute'` turns "30 seconds ago" into "a minute ago". |
| `addSuffix` | `boolean`                                  | `true`     | Whether to include `"ago"` / `"in ..."`. |
| `now`       | `Date \| number`                           | `Date.now()` | Reference point. Useful in tests. |

**Returns:** `string`

**Throws:** `RangeError` if `date` is not a valid date.

### `format(date, options?)`

Formats an absolute date using a small set of tokens. Handy when you want "5 minutes ago" next to "Jan 5, 2024".

```js
import { format } from 'tiny-date'

format(new Date('2024-01-05T14:30:00Z'))
// => 'Jan 5, 2024'
```

| Option   | Type     | Default   | Description |
| -------- | -------- | --------- | ----------- |
| `locale` | `string` | `'en'`    | Locale code. |
| `style`  | `'long' \| 'short' \| 'time'` | `'long'` | `'long'` → `"Jan 5, 2024"`, `'short'` → `"Jan 5"`, `'time'` → `"2:30 PM"`. |

## Examples

### Short style

```js
relative(Date.now() - 90 * 1000, { style: 'short' })
// => '1m ago'

relative(Date.now() + 45 * 60 * 1000, { style: 'short' })
// => 'in 45m'
```

### Capping the unit

```js
relative(new Date('2020-01-01'), { maxUnit: 'day' })
// => '1,642 days ago'
```

### Without a suffix

```js
relative(Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000, { addSuffix: false })
// => '5 minutes'
```

### Custom "now" for deterministic tests

```js
const now = new Date('2024-06-01T12:00:00Z')

relative(new Date('2024-06-01T11:55:00Z'), { now })
// => '5 minutes ago'
```

### TypeScript

Types ship with the package — no `@types` install needed.

```ts
import { relative, type Options } from 'tiny-date'

const opts: Options = { style: 'short', maxUnit: 'day' }
```

## Output reference

| Difference    | `long`              | `short` |
| ------------- | ------------------- | ------- |
| 0–10 s        | `just now`          | `now`   |
| 30 s          | `30 seconds ago`    | `30s ago` |
| 1 min         | `a minute ago`      | `1m ago` |
| 5 min         | `5 minutes ago`     | `5m ago` |
| 1 hour        | `an hour ago`       | `1h ago` |
| 3 hours       | `3 hours ago`       | `3h ago` |
| 1 day         | `yesterday`         | `1d ago` |
| 5 days        | `5 days ago`        | `5d ago` |
| 3 weeks       | `3 weeks ago`       | `3w ago` |
| 2 months      | `2 months ago`      | `2mo ago` |
| 1 year        | `a year ago`        | `1y ago` |

Future dates use the same units with an `in ...` prefix (`in 5 minutes`).

## Browser support

Any browser with `Intl` support (Chrome 71+, Firefox 78+, Safari 14+, Edge 79+). If you need to support older environments, ship your own polyfill for `Intl.DateTimeFormat`.

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome and appreciated! 🎉

1. Fork the repo and create a branch: `git checkout -b feature/my-change`
2. Install dependencies: `npm install`
3. Make your change and add tests
4. Run the suite: `npm test`
5. Open a pull request describing what you changed and why

### Adding a locale

Locales live in `src/locales/`. Each locale exports a lookup table of unit names and a `list` function for joining values:

```js
// src/locales/es.js
export default {
  code: 'es',
  units: {
    second: 'segundo',
    minute: 'minuto',
    hour: 'hora',
    day: 'día',
    week: 'semana',
    month: 'mes',
    year: 'año',
  },
  list: (value, unit) => `${value} ${unit}${value === 1 ? '' : 's'}`,
}
```

Then register it in `src/locales/index.js` and add a test fixture.

### Scripts

| Script            | Description                        |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `npm test`        | Run the test suite                 |
| `npm run test:watch` | Run tests in watch mode         |
| `npm run coverage` | Run tests with a coverage report  |
| `npm run build`   | Build ESM + CJS + type definitions |
| `npm run lint`    | Lint source and tests              |

## Roadmap

- [x] Relative formatting (`5 minutes ago`)
- [x] Short style (`5m ago`)
- [x] Absolute formatting (`Jan 5, 2024`)
- [ ] More locales (es, fr, de, ja, pt-BR)
- [ ] Relative date parsing (`'5 minutes ago'` → `Date`)
- [ ] Duration formatting (`'1h 30m'`)

## License

[MIT](./LICENSE) © [tiny-date contributors](https://github.com/your-org/tiny-date/graphs/contributors)

Made with ☕ and a stubborn refusal to bundle `Intl`.
