# flak

[![CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/CI-passing-brightgreen)](https://github.com/example/flak/actions)
[![Crates.io](https://img.shields.io/badge/crates.io-flak-orange)](https://crates.io/crates/flak)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE)

**flak** is a fast, opinionated linter for YAML files. It catches the small mistakes that break pipelines — duplicate keys, stray tabs, inconsistent indentation, missing document markers — before they reach production.

```
$ flak k8s/
k8s/deployment.yaml:12:3  warning  FLK004  key "replicas" should be quoted (it parses as a number)
k8s/deployment.yaml:31:1  error    FLK001  duplicate key "name" in mapping
k8s/service.yaml:4:1       error    FLK002  tab character used for indentation

3 problems (2 errors, 1 warning)
```

---

## Table of Contents

- [Features](#features)
- [Installation](#installation)
- [Usage](#usage)
- [Rules](#rules)
- [Configuration](#configuration)
- [Output formats](#output-formats)
- [Exit codes](#exit-codes)
- [Autofix](#autofix)
- [Ignoring files and lines](#ignoring-files-and-lines)
- [Editor integration](#editor-integration)
- [Pre-commit hook](#pre-commit-hook)
- [CI usage](#ci-usage)
- [How it compares](#how-it-compares)
- [Contributing](#contributing)
- [License](#license)

---

## Features

- **Single static binary** — no runtime dependencies, no Python, no Node.
- **Fast** — lints ~10,000 files/second on a single core; streams files instead of loading them into memory.
- **Streaming parser** — reports errors at the exact line and column, even in deeply nested documents.
- **50+ built-in rules** covering style, correctness, and Kubernetes/Docker Compose conventions.
- **Configurable** — enable, disable, and tune rules per project in `flak.yaml`.
- **Autofix** — `--fix` rewrites files in place for the rules that can be fixed safely.
- **Machine-readable output** — JSON, JUnit XML, SARIF, and GitHub Actions annotations.
- **Editor integration** — a Language Server Protocol server (`flak lsp`) for real-time diagnostics.

## Installation

### Cargo

```bash
cargo install flak
```

### Homebrew

```bash
brew install flak
```

### Prebuilt binaries

Download the latest release for your platform:

```bash
# Linux (x86_64)
curl -sSL https://github.com/example/flak/releases/latest/download/flak-linux-x86_64.tar.gz \
  | tar -xz flak
sudo mv flak /usr/local/bin/

# macOS (Apple Silicon)
curl -sSL https://github.com/example/flak/releases/latest/download/flak-macos-aarch64.tar.gz \
  | tar -xz flak
sudo mv flak /usr/local/bin/
```

### Docker

```bash
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/work" ghcr.io/example/flak:latest lint .
```

## Usage

```bash
flak lint [PATH]...        # lint files (default command)
flak check [PATH]...       # alias for `lint`
flak fix [PATH]...         # lint and apply safe fixes
flak rules                 # list all rules
flak config                # print the resolved configuration
flak lsp                   # run the language server
```

Common flags:

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-c, --config <FILE>` | Path to the config file (default: nearest `flak.yaml`) |
| `--format <FORMAT>` | `stylish` (default), `compact`, `json`, `github`, `junit`, `sarif` |
| `--enable <RULES>` | Comma-separated rule IDs to enable (overrides config) |
| `--disable <RULES>` | Comma-separated rule IDs to disable |
| `--severity <LEVEL>` | Minimum severity to report: `error`, `warning`, `info` |
| `--fix` | Apply safe fixes in place |
| `--diff` | Print a diff of the fixes that `--fix` would apply, without writing |
| `--no-color` | Disable ANSI colors |
| `--quiet` | Print only the summary line |
| `--stdin` | Read a single YAML document from stdin and lint it |
| `--stdin-filename <NAME>` | Filename to report for `--stdin` (affects rule matching) |
| `--threads <N>` | Number of worker threads (default: CPU count) |
| `--watch` | Re-lint on file changes (experimental) |

Examples:

```bash
# Lint the current directory recursively
flak lint .

# Only errors, as JSON, for a CI step
flak lint . --severity error --format json

# Check a single file with a specific rule turned off
flak lint docker-compose.yml --disable FLK012

# Lint YAML piped in from another tool
kubectl get -o yaml pod/my-pod | flak --stdin --stdin-filename pod.yaml
```

## Rules

Rules are grouped by category. Each rule has a stable ID; you can enable or disable them individually.

### Correctness

| ID | Name | Description | Fixable |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FLK001 | `duplicate-key` | A mapping contains the same key twice | No |
| FLK002 | `tab-indent` | A tab character is used for indentation | Yes |
| FLK003 | `unclosed-quote` | A quoted scalar is never closed | No |
| FLK004 | `ambiguous-scalar` | A value looks like a number/bool but is meant to be a string | No |
| FLK005 | `invalid-anchor` | An anchor is referenced but never defined | No |
| FLK006 | `duplicate-anchor` | The same anchor name is defined twice | No |
| FLK007 | `merge-conflict` | A merge key (`<<`) conflicts with an explicit key | No |
| FLK008 | `bad-alias` | An alias (`*name`) points to a non-scalar anchor | No |
| FLK009 | `empty-document` | The file contains no document | No |
| FLK010 | `multiple-documents` | A file contains more than one `---` document | No |

### Style

| ID | Name | Description | Fixable |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FLK011 | `trailing-whitespace` | Line ends with spaces or tabs | Yes |
| FLK012 | `missing-doc-start` | File does not begin with `---` | Yes |
| FLK013 | `line-length` | Line exceeds the configured maximum (default 120) | No |
| FLK014 | `indentation-width` | Indentation is not a multiple of the configured width (default 2) | Yes |
| FLK015 | `trailing-newline` | File does not end with a newline | Yes |
| FLK016 | `key-order` | Mapping keys are not in the configured order | No |
| FLK017 | `quoted-key` | A key is quoted unnecessarily | Yes |
| FLK018 | `redundant-quotes` | A scalar is quoted but does not need to be | Yes |
| FLK019 | `empty-value` | A key has an empty value (`key:`) | No |
| FLK020 | `comment-spacing` | A comment is missing a space after `#` | Yes |
| FLK021 | `comment-position` | A comment is not on its own line or preceded by a space | No |
| FLK022 | `truthy-value` | A value is `yes`/`no`/`on`/`off` instead of `true`/`false` | Yes |
| FLK023 | `null-value` | A value is `null`/`~` instead of an empty value | Yes |
| FLK024 | `key-case` | A key does not follow the configured casing convention | No |
| FLK025 | `trailing-colon` | A mapping key ends with a colon | No |

### Kubernetes

| ID | Name | Description | Fixable |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FLK030 | `k8s-missing-api-version` | A resource has no `apiVersion` | No |
| FLK031 | `k8s-missing-kind` | A resource has no `kind` | No |
| FLK032 | `k8s-missing-metadata-name` | A resource has no `metadata.name` | No |
| FLK033 | `k8s-latest-tag` | A container image uses the `:latest` tag | No |
| FLK034 | `k8s-missing-resource-limits` | A container has no CPU/memory limits | No |
| FLK035 | `k8s-missing-liveness-probe` | A container has no liveness probe | No |
| FLK036 | `k8s-host-network` | `hostNetwork: true` is set | No |
| FLK037 | `k8s-privileged` | A container runs as privileged | No |
| FLK038 | `k8s-non-root` | A container does not set `runAsNonRoot: true` | No |

### Docker Compose

| ID | Name | Description | Fixable |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FLK040 | `compose-missing-version` | The `version` key is missing (obsolete in Compose v2) | No |
| FLK041 | `compose-unpinned-image` | An image has no tag or digest | No |
| FLK042 | `compose-build-no-context` | A `build` key has no `context` | No |
| FLK043 | `compose-ports-range` | A port range is not quoted | Yes |

### GitHub Actions

| ID | Name | Description | Fixable |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FLK050 | `gha-missing-on` | A workflow has no `on:` trigger | No |
| FLK051 | `gha-unpinned-action` | An action is referenced by tag or branch instead of SHA | No |
| FLK052 | `gha-permissive-permissions` | `permissions` is not set at the workflow or job level | No |
| FLK053 | `gha-missing-timeout` | A job has no `timeout-minutes` | No |

Run `flak rules` for the full list with descriptions and default severities.

## Configuration

flak looks for a `flak.yaml` (or `flak.yml`, or `.flak.yaml`) in the current directory and walks up the tree to the project root. The nearest file wins.

```yaml
# flak.yaml
extends: default

rules:
  # Turn a rule off entirely.
  FLK013:
    enabled: false

  # Change a rule's severity.
  FLK033:
    severity: error

  # Configure a rule's options.
  FLK014:
    indent: 4
  FLK024:
    case: snake_case
  FLK016:
    order:
      - apiVersion
      - kind
      - metadata
      - spec

# Files and directories to skip.
exclude:
  - "**/node_modules/**"
  - "**/vendor/**"
  - "*.generated.yaml"

# Only lint files matching these globs.
include:
  - "**/*.yaml"
  - "**/*.yml"

# Rules that only apply to certain paths.
overrides:
  - files: ["k8s/**"]
    rules:
      FLK035:
        enabled: false
  - files: [".github/workflows/**"]
    rules:
      FLK050:
        enabled: false
```

### Inline configuration

Add a comment directive to a file to change its behavior:

```yaml
# flak:disable FLK013
# flak:enable FLK024
# flak:off
# flak:on
```

## Output formats

**`stylish`** (default) — grouped by file, human-readable:

```
k8s/deployment.yaml
  12:3   warning  FLK004  key "replicas" should be quoted (it parses as a number)
  31:1   error    FLK001  duplicate key "name" in mapping

✖ 2 problems (1 error, 1 warning)
```

**`compact`** — one line per problem, easy to grep:

```
k8s/deployment.yaml:12:3: warning: FLK004 key "replicas" should be quoted (it parses as a number)
k8s/deployment.yaml:31:1: error: FLK001 duplicate key "name" in mapping
```

**`json`** — for tooling:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "problems": [
    {
      "file": "k8s/deployment.yaml",
      "line": 31,
      "column": 1,
      "severity": "error",
      "rule": "FLK001",
      "message": "duplicate key \"name\" in mapping",
      "snippet": "  name: my-app"
    }
  ],
  "summary": { "errors": 1, "warnings": 1, "infos": 0, "files": 1 }
}
```

**`github`** — GitHub Actions annotations:

```
::error file=k8s/deployment.yaml,line=31,col=1,title=FLK001::duplicate key "name" in mapping
```

**`junit`** and **`sarif`** are also available for CI dashboards and code scanning.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | No problems found (or only problems below `--severity`) |
| `1` | Problems were found |
| `2` | flak failed to run (bad config, unreadable file, internal error) |

## Autofix

```bash
flak fix .            # apply fixes in place
flak fix . --diff     # show what would change, write nothing
```

Only rules marked *Fixable* in the tables above are applied. flak never changes the semantic meaning of a document: it will not reorder keys, rewrap long lines, or remove quotes that could alter a value's type. Fixes are applied atomically — if a file cannot be parsed, it is left untouched.

## Ignoring files and lines

**`.flakignore`** — gitignore-style patterns:

```gitignore
# Generated files
**/*.generated.yaml
charts/
```

**Inline** — suppress a single problem on a single line:

```yaml
replicas: 3  # flak:ignore FLK004
```

**Block** — suppress everything in a range:

```yaml
# flak:off
legacy:
  weird:    formatting
# flak:on
```

## Editor integration

flak ships a language server. Point your editor at it to get live diagnostics:

```bash
flak lsp --stdio
```

### Neovim (built-in LSP)

```lua
vim.lsp.config('flak', {
  cmd = { 'flak', 'lsp', '--stdio' },
  filetypes = { 'yaml' },
  root_markers = { 'flak.yaml', '.git' },
})
vim.lsp.enable('flak')
```

### VS Code

Install the [flak VS Code extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=example.flak), or use the generic LSP client:

```json
{
  "yaml.servers": {
    "flak": {
      "command": "flak",
      "args": ["lsp", "--stdio"]
    }
  }
}
```

## Pre-commit hook

Add to `.pre-commit-config.yaml`:

```yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/example/flak
    rev: v1.4.0
    hooks:
      - id: flak
        args: ["--severity", "error"]
```

Or install the git hook directly:

```bash
flak install-hooks
```

## CI usage

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
name: lint-yaml
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  flak:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: example/flak-action@v1
        with:
          severity: error
```

### Generic

```bash
flak lint . --format github --severity error
```

## How it compares

| Tool | Focus | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `yamllint` | Style | Python; the de-facto standard, but slow on large trees |
| `kubeconform` | Schema | Validates against Kubernetes JSON schemas only |
| `actionlint` | Workflows | GitHub Actions only |
| **flak** | Style + correctness + conventions | Single binary, streaming, autofix, multi-format output |

flak is not a schema validator. For Kubernetes resource schemas, use `kubeconform` alongside it.

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome!

```bash
git clone https://github.com/example/flak
cd flak
cargo build --release
cargo test
```

### Adding a rule

1. Create `src/rules/<category>/<rule_name>.rs` implementing the `Rule` trait.
2. Register it in `src/rules/<category>/mod.rs`.
3. Add a test fixture under `tests/fixtures/<rule_name>/`.
4. Run `cargo test` and `cargo fmt --check`.

Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening a pull request.

## License

flak is distributed under the [MIT License](LICENSE).

# flak

[![Go](https://img.shields.io/badge/go-1.22%2B-blue)](https://go.dev)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green)](LICENSE)
[![CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/build-passing-brightgreen)](https://github.com/you/flak/actions)

**flak** is a fast, opinionated linter for YAML files. It catches the small mistakes that break CI pipelines, confuse humans, and slip into production configs — duplicate keys, tabs, trailing whitespace, unquoted `yes`/`no`, and more.

```
$ flak config/
config/app.yaml:12:3  warning  FLAK011  truthy value "yes" should be quoted
config/app.yaml:24:1  error    FLAK002  duplicate key "replicas" (first defined at line 18)
config/db.yaml:1:1   info     FLAK005  missing document start marker "---"

3 problems in 2 files (1 error, 1 warning, 1 info)
```

---

## Table of Contents

- [Features](#features)
- [Installation](#installation)
- [Quick Start](#quick-start)
- [Usage](#usage)
  - [Command-line flags](#command-line-flags)
  - [Exit codes](#exit-codes)
  - [Output formats](#output-formats)
- [Rules](#rules)
- [Configuration](#configuration)
  - [Config file](#config-file)

  - [Editors](#editors)
- [Using flak as a library](#using-flak-as-a-library)
- [Contributing](#contributing)
- [License](#license)

---

## Features

- **Zero-config** — sensible defaults that work on any YAML file.
- **Fast** — parses files in parallel; lints a 10k-file tree in under a second.
- **Configurable** — enable, disable, tune, and re-level any rule.
- **Multi-document aware** — handles `---` separated streams and anchors/aliases.
- **Auto-fix** — `--fix` rewrites files in place for the rules that can be fixed safely.
- **Machine-readable output** — JSON, GitHub annotations, Checkstyle, and JUnit XML.
- **Editor friendly** — inline `# flak:ignore` comments and a `--stdin` mode for LSP integrations.
- **Single static binary** — no runtime dependencies.

---

## Installation

### Go

```bash
go install github.com/you/flak/cmd/flak@latest
```

### Homebrew

```bash
brew install flak
```

### Prebuilt binaries

Download the latest release for your platform from the [releases page](https://github.com/you/flak/releases):

```bash
# Linux (amd64)
curl -sSL https://github.com/you/flak/releases/latest/download/flak_linux_amd64.tar.gz \
  | tar -xz -C /usr/local/bin flak
```

### From source

```bash
git clone https://github.com/you/flak.git
cd flak
make build
./bin/flak --version
```

---

## Quick Start

Lint every YAML file in the current directory:

```bash
flak .
```

Lint specific files or globs:

```bash
flak config/app.yaml 'services/**/*.yaml'
```

Lint from stdin (useful for editor integrations):

```bash
cat config/app.yaml | flak --stdin --filename config/app.yaml
```

Generate a default config file:

```bash
flak --init          # writes .flak.yml
```

---

## Usage

```
flak [flags] [path ...]
```

Paths may be files or directories. Directories are walked recursively; only files matching `*.yaml`, `*.yml`, or `*.yaml.tpl` are linted.

### Command-line flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-c, --config <path>` | auto-discovered | Path to a config file. |
| `-f, --format <format>` | `stylish` | Output format: `stylish`, `compact`, `json`, `github`, `checkstyle`, `junit`. |
| `--severity <level>` | `all` | Minimum severity to report: `error`, `warning`, `info`, `all`. |
| `--enable <rules>` | — | Comma-separated rule IDs to enable (overrides config). |
| `--disable <rules>` | — | Comma-separated rule IDs to disable (overrides config). |
| `--stdin` | `false` | Read a single YAML document from stdin. |
| `--filename <name>` | `<stdin>` | Filename to report for stdin input. |
| `--fix` | `false` | Auto-fix fixable issues in place. |
| `--init` | `false` | Write a default `.flak.yml` and exit. |
| `--list-rules` | `false` | Print all rules and exit. |
| `--no-color` | auto | Disable colored output. |
| `--quiet` / `-q` | `false` | Print only the summary line. |
| `--verbose` / `-v` | `false` | Print additional diagnostics. |
| `--version` | — | Print version and exit. |
| `--help` / `-h` | — | Print help and exit. |

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | No issues found (or only issues below `--severity`). |
| `1` | Issues were found. |
| `2` | flak failed to run (bad config, unreadable file, internal error). |

### Output formats

**`stylish`** (default) — grouped by file, human-friendly.

```
config/app.yaml
  12:3   warning  FLAK011  truthy value "yes" should be quoted
  24:1   error    FLAK002  duplicate key "replicas" (first defined at line 18)

2 problems in 1 file (1 error, 1 warning)
```

**`compact`** — one line per issue, easy to `grep`.

```
config/app.yaml:12:3: warning: FLAK011 truthy value "yes" should be quoted
```

**`json`** — stable schema, for tooling.

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "files": [
    {
      "path": "config/app.yaml",
      "issues": [
        {
          "rule": "FLAK011",
          "severity": "warning",
          "message": "truthy value \"yes\" should be quoted",
          "line": 12,
          "column": 3,
          "fixable": true
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "summary": { "errors": 1, "warnings": 1, "infos": 0, "files": 1 }
}
```

**`github`** — GitHub Actions workflow commands.

```
::warning file=config/app.yaml,line=12,col=3::FLAK011 truthy value "yes" should be quoted
```

**`checkstyle`** and **`junit`** — for CI dashboards that ingest those formats.

---

## Rules

| ID | Rule | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FLAK001` | `syntax-error` | error | The file is not valid YAML. |
| `FLAK002` | `duplicate-key` | error | The same key is defined twice in one mapping. |
| `FLAK003` | `trailing-whitespace` | warning | A line ends with spaces or tabs. |
| `FLAK004` | `tab-indentation` | error | A line is indented with a tab character. |
| `FLAK005` | `missing-document-start` | info | The file does not begin with `---`. |
| `FLAK006` | `missing-final-newline` | warning | The file does not end with a newline. |
| `FLAK007` | `line-too-long` | warning | A line exceeds the configured maximum length. |
| `FLAK008` | `empty-document` | warning | The file (or a document in it) is empty. |
| `FLAK009` | `trailing-blank-lines` | info | The file ends with more than one blank line. |
| `FLAK010` | `key-spacing` | warning | A mapping key is not followed by exactly one space before `:`. |
| `FLAK011` | `truthy-value` | warning | A scalar is `yes`, `no`, `on`, `off`, `y`, or `n` and should be quoted. |
| `FLAK012` | `empty-value` | info | A key has no value. |
| `FLAK013` | `invalid-anchor-name` | error | An anchor or alias name contains invalid characters. |
| `FLAK014` | `multiple-documents` | info | The file contains more than one `---` document. |

Run `flak --list-rules` for the authoritative, up-to-date list.

---

## Configuration

flak looks for a config file in the current directory and walks up the tree, in this order:

1. `.flak.yml`
2. `.flak.yaml`
3. `flak.yml`
4. `flak.yaml`

Use `--config` to point at a specific file.

### Config file

```yaml
# .flak.yml
version: "1"

# Enable/disable rules. Omitted rules use their default severity.
rules:
  line-too-long:
    max: 120
  missing-document-start: false
  truthy-value: error
  duplicate-key: error

# Override severity per rule.
severity:
  trailing-whitespace: info
  empty-value: false

# Files and directories to skip (glob patterns, gitignore-style).
exclude:
  - "vendor/**"
  - "**/*.generated.yaml"
  - "charts/**/templates/**"

# Files to always include, even if excluded above.
include:
  - "charts/**/templates/deployment.yaml"
```

### Rule options

| Rule | Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `line-too-long` | `max` | `120` | Maximum allowed line length. |
| `trailing-blank-lines` | `max` | `1` | Maximum allowed blank lines at end of file. |
| `key-spacing` | `before` / `after` | `0` / `1` | Spaces allowed before/after `:` in a mapping. |
| `truthy-value` | `values` | `[yes, no, on, off, y, n]` | Scalars treated as ambiguous booleans. |
| `multiple-documents` | `max` | `1` | Maximum allowed documents per file. |

### Severity

Each rule has a severity of `error`, `warning`, or `info`. Set a rule to `false` to disable it, or to a severity string to re-level it:

```yaml
rules:
  trailing-whitespace: info
  empty-value: false
```

### Excluding files

In addition to `exclude` in the config, flak honors a `.flakignore` file at the project root using gitignore-style syntax:

```
# .flakignore
node_modules/
*.lock.yaml
fixtures/legacy/
```

### Inline suppressions

Disable a rule for the next line:

```yaml
replicas: 3  # flak:ignore FLAK011
```

Disable a rule for the whole file (must be on the first line):

```yaml
# flak:ignore-file FLAK005
---
name: app
```

Disable all rules for a line:

```yaml
replicas: 3  # flak:ignore
```

---

## Auto-fixing

Some rules can be fixed automatically:

```bash
flak --fix .
```

Fixable rules: `trailing-whitespace`, `tab-indentation`, `missing-final-newline`, `trailing-blank-lines`, `key-spacing`, `truthy-value`, `missing-document-start`.

`--fix` rewrites files in place and prints a summary of what changed:

```
Fixed 5 problems in 3 files
```

> **Note:** `flak --fix` is safe by default, but always review the diff before committing.

---

## Editor & CI integration

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
name: lint-yaml
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  flak:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version: "1.22"
      - run: go install github.com/you/flak/cmd/flak@latest
      - run: flak --format github .
```

### GitLab CI

```yaml
yaml-lint:
  image: golang:1.22
  script:
    - go install github.com/you/flak/cmd/flak@latest
    - flak --format junit . | tee flak-report.xml
  artifacts:
    when: always
    paths: [flak-report.xml]
```

### pre-commit

```yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/you/flak
    rev: v1.4.0
    hooks:
      - id: flak
        args: ["--fix"]
```

### Editors

**Neovim** (with `nvim-lint`):

```lua
require('lint').linters_by_ft = {
  yaml = { 'flak' },
}
```

**VS Code** — use the [flak-vscode](https://github.com/you/flak-vscode) extension, or wire up a generic task:

```json
{
  "type": "shell",
  "command": "flak --stdin --filename ${file}",
  "group": { "kind": "test", "isDefault": true }
}
```

---

## Using flak as a library

```go
package main

import (
    "fmt"
    "os"

    "github.com/you/flak/pkg/lint"
)

func main() {
    cfg, err := lint.DefaultConfig()
    if err != nil {
        panic(err)
    }

    result, err := lint.LintFile(cfg, "config/app.yaml")
    if err != nil {
        panic(err)
    }

    for _, issue := range result.Issues {
        fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "%s:%d:%d %s %s\n",
            issue.Path, issue.Line, issue.Column, issue.Rule, issue.Message)
    }
}
```

---

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome!

1. Fork the repository and create a branch.
2. Run the test suite: `make test`.
3. Format your code: `make fmt`.
4. Open a pull request describing the change.

New rules should:

- Be prefixed `FLAK` and assigned the next available ID.
- Be documented in the [Rules](#rules) table and in `docs/rules/`.
- Include unit tests and at least one example fixture under `testdata/`.
- Be opt-in or non-breaking by default — changing a default severity is a minor version bump.

---

## License

flak is released under the [MIT License](LICENSE).

runs.output:
# flak

**A fast, opinionated linter for YAML files.**

`flak` catches the YAML problems that don't break your parser but break your pipeline: duplicate keys, tabs masquerading as indentation, unquoted `yes`/`no`/`on`/`off` strings, missing document markers, trailing whitespace, and more. It parses with a real YAML 1.2 parser, so it understands anchors, aliases, merge keys, multi-document streams, and block scalars — and it never rewrites your file unless you ask it to.

```
$ flak config/
config/app.yaml
  2:10  warning  FLAK010  unquoted value "yes" parses as boolean
  7:1   error    FLAK005  duplicate key "replicas" (first seen at line 4)
  14:1  warning  FLAK001  trailing whitespace

2 errors, 1 warning  ·  1 file checked  ·  12ms
```

---

## Table of contents

- [Why flak](#why-flak)
- [Installation](#installation)
- [Usage](#usage)
- [Rules](#rules)
- [Configuration](#configuration)
- [Output formats](#output-formats)
- [Exit codes](#exit-codes)
- [Ignoring files](#ignoring-files)
- [Autofix](#autofix)
- [Editor integration](#editor-integration)
- [CI usage](#ci-usage)
- [How it works](#how-it-works)
- [Contributing](#contributing)
- [License](#license)

---

## Why flak

YAML is a superset of JSON and a superset of a dozen other things too. That flexibility is why it's everywhere — and why it's easy to write YAML that means something different from what you intended:

```yaml
# What you wrote
replicas: yes
timeout: 30

# What your app read
replicas: true
timeout: 30
```

`flak` exists to make those ambiguities loud. It is:

- **Correct.** Built on a spec-compliant YAML 1.2 parser, not on regexes. It knows the difference between a key and a value, a comment and a string, and a block scalar from a folded one.
- **Fast.** A single-pass AST walk with a rule registry. Linting a 5,000-line Kubernetes manifest takes milliseconds.
- **Configurable.** Every rule can be enabled, disabled, or re-graded. Severity is yours to decide.
- **Composable.** Human-readable output for terminals, JSON and JUnit for CI, SARIF for code scanning.

---

## Installation

### npm (recommended)

```bash
npm install --save-dev flak
npx flak .
```

### Homebrew

```bash
brew install flak
```

### Standalone binary

Download a release for your platform and drop it on your `PATH`:

```bash
# macOS (Apple silicon)
curl -fsSL https://github.com/flak-lint/flak/releases/latest/download/flak-darwin-arm64 -o /usr/local/bin/flak
chmod +x /usr/local/bin/flak
```

Linux (`amd64`, `arm64`) and Windows (`x64`) builds are available under the same release tag.

### Docker

```bash
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/work" ghcr.io/flak-lint/flak:latest .
```

---

## Usage

```bash
flak                          # lint every YAML file in the current directory
flak config/ deploy/          # lint specific paths
flak "**/*.yaml"              # lint a glob
flak -                        # lint YAML from stdin
```

By default `flak` recursively walks the given paths and inspects files matching:

```
*.yaml  *.yml  .flakrc.yaml  .github/workflows/*.yaml
```

### Common commands

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `flak lint [paths...]` | Lint files (the default when no subcommand is given) |
| `flak rules` | List all rules with their default severity |
| `flak explain FLAK005` | Show the rationale and examples for one rule |
| `flak init` | Write a starter `.flakrc.yaml` to the current directory |
| `flak --version` | Print the version |

### Options

```
Usage: flak [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...

Arguments:
  [PATHS]...  Files or directories to lint. Use "-" for stdin.

Options:
  -c, --config <FILE>        Path to a config file (default: nearest .flakrc.yaml)
      --no-config            Ignore config files entirely
  -f, --format <FORMAT>      Output format: stylish, compact, json, junit, github, sarif
      --select <RULES>       Only run these rules (comma-separated, e.g. FLAK001,FLAK005)
      --ignore <RULES>       Skip these rules (comma-separated)
      --ruleset <FILE>       Load additional custom rules from a file
      --severity <LEVEL>     Minimum severity to report: error, warning, info
      --max-warnings <N>     Exit non-zero if more than N warnings are found
      --fix                  Apply safe automatic fixes in place
      --fix-dry-run          Print a diff of the fixes that --fix would apply
      --stdin-filename <NAME> Filename to report for stdin input
      --no-color             Disable colored output
      --quiet                Print nothing; use the exit code
  -w, --watch                Re-lint on file change
  -h, --help                 Print help
  -V, --version              Print version
```

---

## Rules

Every rule has a stable ID. IDs never change meaning across minor versions — if a rule's behaviour changes, a new ID is added and the old one is deprecated.

### Errors

| ID | Name | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FLAK001` | `duplicate-key` | A mapping contains the same key twice. Later values silently overwrite earlier ones in most parsers. |
| `FLAK002` | `invalid-yaml` | The file could not be parsed as YAML. |
| `FLAK003` | `tab-indentation` | A tab character is used for indentation. YAML forbids tabs in indentation. |
| `FLAK004` | `undefined-alias` | An alias (`*ref`) refers to an anchor that was never defined. |
| `FLAK005` | `duplicate-anchor` | An anchor name is defined more than once in the same document. |
| `FLAK006` | `merge-key-conflict` | A merge key (`<<`) is used where the target is not a mapping, or a key is both merged and defined. |
| `FLAK007` | `unclosed-quote` | A quoted scalar is never terminated. |
| `FLAK008` | `empty-file` | The file contains no document. |

### Warnings

| ID | Name | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FLAK010` | `implicit-boolean` | An unquoted value like `yes`, `no`, `on`, `off` may be parsed as a boolean. Quote it. |
| `FLAK011` | `implicit-number` | An unquoted value like `0123`, `1_000`, or `1:30` may be parsed as a number. Quote it. |
| `FLAK012` | `missing-document-start` | A multi-document stream does not begin with `---`. |
| `FLAK013` | `missing-document-end` | A multi-document stream does not end with `...`. |
| `FLAK014` | `inconsistent-indent` | Indentation width changes within the same block. |
| `FLAK015` | `trailing-whitespace` | A line ends with spaces or tabs. |
| `FLAK016` | `missing-final-newline` | The file does not end with a newline. |
| `FLAK017` | `line-too-long` | A line exceeds the configured maximum length. |
| `FLAK018` | `empty-value` | A key has no value (`key:` with nothing after it). Often a typo. |
| `FLAK019` | `redundant-document-marker` | A `---` appears where a single-document file does not need one. |
| `FLAK020` | `comment-spacing` | A comment is not separated from the preceding token by a space. |
| `FLAK021` | `key-order` | Keys are not in the configured order (opt-in; off by default). |
| `FLAK022` | `deprecated-merge` | The `<<` merge key is used; explicit `extends` is preferred in some schemas. |

### Info

| ID | Name | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FLAK030` | `unused-anchor` | An anchor is defined but never referenced. |
| `FLAK031` | `long-file` | The file exceeds the configured line count and may be worth splitting. |

Run `flak rules` for the live list, or `flak explain FLAK010` for rationale, examples, and a suggested fix.

---

## Configuration

`flak` looks for a `.flakrc.yaml` in the current directory and walks up to the filesystem root, using the nearest one it finds. A `flak` key in `package.json` is also supported.

```yaml
# .flakrc.yaml
extends: default

rules:
  FLAK001:
    severity: error
  FLAK010:
    severity: warning
  FLAK017:
    severity: info
    max-line-length: 120
  FLAK021:
    severity: off
    order: [apiVersion, kind, metadata, spec]

ignore:
  - "**/node_modules/**"
  - "**/*.generated.yaml"

options:
  indent: 2
  allow-duplicate-keys: false
  check-empty-values: true
```

### Rule options

| Rule | Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FLAK010` | `allow` | `[]` | Values to permit unquoted (e.g. `["yes", "no"]`). |
| `FLAK011` | `allow` | `[]` | Values to permit unquoted. |
| `FLAK017` | `max-line-length` | `100` | Maximum line length before reporting. |
| `FLAK021` | `order` | `[]` | Required key order. |
| `FLAK031` | `max-lines` | `1000` | Line count above which the file is flagged. |

### Selecting rules

```bash
flak --select FLAK001,FLAK010 config/     # only these two
flak --ignore FLAK017,FLAK021 config/     # everything except these two
```

`--select` and `--ignore` are applied on top of the config file, so a rule disabled in `.flakrc.yaml` stays disabled unless you explicitly re-enable it with `--select`.

### Custom rules

Point `--ruleset` at a YAML file to add your own checks. Custom rules are matched against the parsed document and run alongside the built-ins.

```yaml
# .flak-rules.yaml
rules:
  - id: ORG001
    name: require-owner
    severity: warning
    description: Every mapping must have an `owner` key.
    match: mapping
    require-keys: [owner]
```

---

## Output formats

```bash
flak --format stylish config/     # default: grouped by file, colored
flak --format compact config/     # one line per problem
flak --format json config/        # machine-readable
flak --format junit config/       # JUnit XML for CI test reporters
flak --format github config/      # GitHub Actions annotations
flak --format sarif config/       # SARIF for code scanning
```

### JSON

```json
{
  "version": "1.0",
  "files": [
    {
      "path": "config/app.yaml",
      "problems": [
        {
          "rule": "FLAK005",
          "severity": "error",
          "message": "duplicate key \"replicas\" (first seen at line 4)",
          "line": 7,
          "column": 1,
          "endLine": 7,
          "endColumn": 12,
          "fixable": false
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "summary": {
    "files": 1,
    "errors": 1,
    "warnings": 1,
    "infos": 0,
    "fixable": 0
  }
}
```

### GitHub Actions

With `--format github`, problems are emitted as workflow annotations and shown inline on the pull request diff:

```
config/app.yaml:7:1: error: duplicate key "replicas" (first seen at line 4) [FLAK005]
```

---

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | No problems found (or only problems below `--severity`). |
| `1` | Problems were found. |
| `2` | Usage error, unreadable config, or a file that could not be read. |
| `3` | An internal error. Please file a bug report. |

`--max-warnings N` turns a warning-only run into exit code `1` once the warning count exceeds `N`.

---

## Ignoring files

Create a `.flakignore` in your project root. It uses gitignore-style syntax:

```gitignore
# Generated manifests
**/chart.lock.yaml
**/*.helm.yaml

# Vendored configs
vendor/**
```

Files matched by `.flakignore` are skipped entirely. To suppress a rule for a single line, use a directive comment:

```yaml
replicas: yes # flak:disable FLAK010
```

To disable all rules for a file:

```yaml
# flak:disable
```

---

## Autofix

Some rules can be fixed automatically:

```bash
flak --fix config/          # rewrite files in place
flak --fix-dry-run config/  # show a diff without writing
```

```diff
--- a/config/app.yaml
+++ b/config/app.yaml
@@ -2,1 +2,1 @@
-replicas: yes
+replicas: "yes"
```

Currently fixable: `FLAK010`, `FLAK011`, `FLAK015`, `FLAK016`, `FLAK020`, `FLAK012`, `FLAK013`.

`--fix` is conservative: it never reorders keys, never changes quoting style beyond what's needed, and never touches block scalars. Files are written atomically, and a backup is not kept — run `flak --fix-dry-run` first if you're unsure.

---

## Editor integration

### VS Code

Install the [flak VS Code extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=flak-lint.flak) for in-editor diagnostics, or use the generic YAML extension with `flak` as the linter:

```json
{
  "yaml.validateWithFlak": true,
  "flak.configPath": "${workspaceFolder}/.flakrc.yaml"
}
```

### Neovim

With [nvim-lint](https://github.com/mfussenegger/nvim-lint):

```lua
require('lint').linters_by_ft = {
  yaml = { { 'flak', '--format', 'compact' } },
}
```

### Other editors

Any editor that can run an external command and parse `compact` or `json` output will work. `compact` prints `path:line:col: severity: message [RULE]`, which is the format most LSP bridges expect.

---

## CI usage

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
name: lint-yaml
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  flak:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
      - run: npm install --save-dev flak
      - run: npx flak --format github --max-warnings 0 .
```

### GitLab CI

```yaml
yaml-lint:
  image: node:20
  script:
    - npm ci
    - npx flak --format junit --output report.xml .
  artifacts:
    when: always
    paths: [report.xml]
```

### Pre-commit

```yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/flak-lint/flak
    rev: v1.4.0
    hooks:
      - id: flak
        files: \.ya?ml$
```

---

## How it works

1. **Parse.** The file is read and parsed into an AST using a YAML 1.2 core-schema parser. Parse errors are reported as `FLAK002` with the offending line and column.
2. **Walk.** The AST is traversed once, and each node is tested against the enabled rules. Rules are pure functions from a node to zero or more problems.
3. **Report.** Problems are sorted by file, then line, then column, and rendered in the requested format.

`flak` never executes or evaluates your YAML. Anchors and aliases are resolved for analysis only; no custom tags are instantiated, so a malicious `!!python/object` tag is inert.

---

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/flak-lint/flak
cd flak
npm install
npm run build
npm test
```

### Adding a rule

1. Create `src/rules/<name>.ts` exporting a rule object with an `id`, `severity`, `check(node, context)` function, and a `meta` block containing `description` and `examples`.
2. Register it in `src/rules/index.ts`.
3. Add a fixture under `tests/fixtures/<name>/` with a `valid.yaml` and an `invalid.yaml`.
4. Run `npm test` — the harness generates a snapshot of expected output.

Rule IDs are permanent. If you need to change a rule's behaviour in a breaking way, add a new ID and deprecate the old one.

### Reporting bugs

Please include the YAML that triggered the problem (or a minimal reproduction), the output you got, and the output you expected. A failing fixture is the fastest possible bug report.

---

## License

MIT © flak contributors

---

*`flak` is not affiliated with any YAML specification working group. It aims to be boring, fast, and correct — in that order.*

runs.output:
# flak

A fast, opinionated linter for YAML files.

`flak` parses your YAML, reports syntax errors and style violations with precise line/column locations, and can automatically fix the mechanical issues it finds. It ships with sensible defaults, is fully configurable, and integrates cleanly with CI.

```console
$ flak .
config.yaml
  12:1   warning  YAML101  trailing whitespace
  18:1   error    YAML113  duplicate key "replicas"
  24:1   info     YAML105  line too long (142 > 120)

✖ 3 issues in 1 file (1 error, 1 warning, 1 info)
```

---

## Table of Contents

- [Features](#features)
- [Installation](#installation)
- [Quick start](#quick-start)
- [Usage](#usage)
- [Rules](#rules)
- [Configuration](#configuration)
- [Ignoring files and lines](#ignoring-files-and-lines)
- [Output formats](#output-formats)
- [Exit codes](#exit-codes)
- [Auto-fixing](#auto-fixing)
- [CI integration](#ci-integration)
- [Editor integration](#editor-integration)
- [How it works](#how-it-works)
- [Contributing](#contributing)
- [License](#license)

---

## Features

- **Syntax validation** — catches malformed YAML before your pipeline does.
- **~30 built-in rules** covering whitespace, formatting, and semantic issues.
- **Precise diagnostics** — every issue reports file, line, column, and a human-readable message.
- **Configurable** — enable, disable, and tune rules via `.flak.yml`.
- **Auto-fix** — `--fix` rewrites files in place for the rules that can be fixed safely.
- **Multiple output formats** — human-readable, JSON, JUnit, Checkstyle, GitHub Actions, and SARIF.
- **Fast** — written in Go, parallel across files, and streams results as they are found.
- **Zero runtime dependencies** — a single static binary.

---

## Installation

### Go

```console
go install github.com/flak-lint/flak@latest
```

### Homebrew

```console
brew install flak
```

### Prebuilt binary

Download the latest release for your platform and drop the `flak` binary on your `PATH`:

```console
curl -sSL https://github.com/flak-lint/flak/releases/latest/download/flak_linux_amd64 -o /usr/local/bin/flak
chmod +x /usr/local/bin/flak
```

### Docker

```console
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/work" -w /work ghcr.io/flak-lint/flak:latest .
```

---

## Quick start

Lint every YAML file in the current directory:

```console
flak .
```

Lint specific files or globs:

```console
flak config.yaml .github/workflows/*.yml
```

Check whether files are clean (useful in CI):

```console
flak --check .
```

Read from standard input:

```console
cat config.yaml | flak --stdin --filename config.yaml
```

---

## Usage

```console
flak [flags] [path...]
```

If no path is given, `flak` lints the current directory.

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-c, --config <file>` | auto-discovered | Path to the configuration file. |
| `-f, --format <format>` | `stylish` | Output format: `stylish`, `compact`, `json`, `json-lines`, `junit`, `checkstyle`, `github`, `sarif`. |
| `-o, --output <file>` | stdout | Write the report to a file instead of stdout. |
| `--enable <rules>` | — | Enable rules by ID or tag (e.g. `--enable style,security`). |
| `--disable <rules>` | — | Disable rules by ID or tag. |
| `--rules` | — | List all available rules and exit. |
| `--fix` | `false` | Apply safe automatic fixes in place. |
| `--fix-only` | `false` | Apply fixes and report nothing. |
| `--check` | `false` | Exit non-zero if any issue is found; do not write a report. |
| `--stdin` | `false` | Read a single YAML document from stdin. |
| `--filename <name>` | `<stdin>` | Filename to report for stdin input. |
| `--no-color` | auto | Disable colored output. |
| `--color` | auto | Force colored output. |
| `--quiet` | `false` | Only print the summary line. |
| `--verbose` | `false` | Print additional diagnostics. |
| `--jobs <n>` | CPU count | Number of files to lint in parallel. |
| `--timeout <duration>` | `30s` | Per-file parse timeout. |
| `-v, --version` | — | Print the version and exit. |
| `-h, --help` | — | Print help and exit. |

### Examples

```console
# Only run the security rules
flak --enable security .

# Run everything except the noisy formatting rules
flak --disable style,formatting .

# Produce a SARIF report for code scanning
flak --format sarif --output flak.sarif .

# Fix what can be fixed, then report what remains
flak --fix .
```

---

## Rules

Rules are identified by a stable ID and a tag. Use `flak --rules` to print the full list with descriptions.

### Syntax

| ID | Tag | Severity | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `YAML001` | `syntax` | error | The file could not be parsed as valid YAML. |
| `YAML002` | `syntax` | error | The file contains a tab character used for indentation. |
| `YAML003` | `syntax` | error | The file contains an invalid escape sequence in a quoted scalar. |
| `YAML004` | `syntax` | error | A mapping key is not unique within its mapping. |

### Whitespace

| ID | Tag | Severity | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `YAML101` | `whitespace` | warning | Trailing whitespace at end of line. |
| `YAML102` | `whitespace` | warning | Line contains a tab character. |
| `YAML103` | `whitespace` | warning | File uses CRLF line endings. |
| `YAML104` | `whitespace` | warning | File does not end with a newline. |
| `YAML105` | `whitespace` | warning | File contains more than one consecutive blank line. |
| `YAML106` | `whitespace` | warning | File ends with one or more blank lines. |

### Formatting

| ID | Tag | Severity | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `YAML201` | `formatting` | warning | Line exceeds the maximum allowed length. |
| `YAML202` | `formatting` | warning | Mapping key is not followed by a single space. |
| `YAML203` | `formatting` | warning | Indentation is inconsistent with the surrounding block. |
| `YAML204` | `formatting` | info | Document does not start with `---`. |
| `YAML205` | `formatting` | info | File is empty. |
| `YAML206` | `formatting` | info | Sequence item uses a dash that is not followed by a space. |
| `YAML207` | `formatting` | info | Quoted scalar does not need to be quoted. |

### Semantics

| ID | Tag | Severity | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `YAML301` | `semantics` | warning | Value uses a YAML 1.1 boolean literal (`yes`, `no`, `on`, `off`). |
| `YAML302` | `semantics` | warning | Value looks like a number but is quoted as a string. |
| `YAML303` | `semantics` | warning | Value looks like a string but is unquoted. |
| `YAML304` | `semantics` | info | Anchor is defined but never referenced. |
| `YAML305` | `semantics` | info | Alias references an anchor that is never defined. |
| `YAML306` | `semantics` | warning | Merge key (`<<`) is used. |

### Security

| ID | Tag | Severity | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `YAML401` | `security` | error | Secret-like key has a hard-coded value. |
| `YAML402` | `security` | warning | File contains a private key block. |
| `YAML403` | `security` | warning | File is world-readable and contains secret-like keys. |

---

## Configuration

`flak` looks for a configuration file in the current directory and walks up the tree. Supported names:

```
.flak.yml
.flak.yaml
.flak.toml
```

### Example

```yaml
# .flak.yml
extends: default

rules:
  YAML101:
    enabled: true
  YAML201:
    enabled: true
    max-line-length: 100
  YAML301:
    enabled: false
  YAML401:
    enabled: true
    patterns:
      - "password"
      - "api[_-]?key"
      - "token"

ignore:
  - "vendor/**"
  - "**/*.generated.yml"

severity-overrides:
  YAML205: ignore
```

### Options

| Key | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `extends` | string | Base configuration to inherit from (`default` or a path). |
| `rules` | map | Per-rule settings. `enabled` toggles a rule; other keys are rule-specific. |
| `ignore` | list | Glob patterns of files to skip. |
| `include` | list | Glob patterns to restrict linting to. |
| `severity-overrides` | map | Force a rule's severity to `error`, `warning`, `info`, or `ignore`. |
| `exclude-dirs` | list | Directory names to skip entirely (default: `.git`, `node_modules`, `vendor`). |

### Per-rule options

| Rule | Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `YAML201` | `max-line-length` | `120` | Maximum allowed line length. |
| `YAML203` | `indent` | `2` | Expected indentation width. |
| `YAML205` | `allow-empty` | `false` | Whether empty files are acceptable. |
| `YAML301` | `allowed` | `[]` | Additional literals to permit. |
| `YAML401` | `patterns` | see above | Regex patterns matched against key names. |
| `YAML401` | `allow-placeholder` | `true` | Ignore values that look like placeholders (`${...}`, `changeme`, `***`). |

---

## Ignoring files and lines

### `.flakignore`

Create a `.flakignore` file in your project root. It uses gitignore-style syntax:

```gitignore
# Generated files
*.generated.yml
charts/**/values-*.yaml

# Third-party
vendor/
```

### Inline suppression

Suppress a rule on a specific line:

```yaml
replicas: 3 # flak:ignore YAML201
```

Suppress all rules on a line:

```yaml
replicas: 3 # flak:ignore
```

Suppress a rule for a whole file by placing the directive at the top:

```yaml
# flak:file-ignore YAML401
```

---

## Output formats

### `stylish` (default)

```
config.yaml
  12:1   warning  YAML101  trailing whitespace
  18:1   error    YAML113  duplicate key "replicas"
  24:1   info     YAML105  line too long (142 > 120)

✖ 3 issues in 1 file (1 error, 1 warning, 1 info)
```

### `compact`

```
config.yaml:12:1: warning: YAML101 trailing whitespace
config.yaml:18:1: error: YAML113 duplicate key "replicas"
```

### `json`

```json
{
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "files": [
    {
      "path": "config.yaml",
      "issues": [
        {
          "rule": "YAML101",
          "severity": "warning",
          "message": "trailing whitespace",
          "line": 12,
          "column": 1,
          "fixable": true
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "summary": {
    "files": 1,
    "issues": 3,
    "errors": 1,
    "warnings": 1,
    "infos": 1
  }
}
```

### `github`

```
::warning file=config.yaml,line=12,col=1::YAML101 trailing whitespace
::error file=config.yaml,line=18,col=1::YAML113 duplicate key "replicas"
```

### `junit`, `checkstyle`, `sarif`

Machine-readable reports for CI dashboards, code quality tools, and GitHub code scanning.

---

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | No issues found. |
| `1` | Issues were found. |
| `2` | An error occurred (bad configuration, unreadable file, invalid flag). |
| `3` | Issues were found **and** `--fix` was requested but some issues remain unfixed. |

---

## Auto-fixing

```console
flak --fix .
```

`flak` only applies fixes it considers safe and unambiguous. The following rules are currently fixable:

- `YAML101` — remove trailing whitespace
- `YAML102` — convert tabs to spaces
- `YAML103` — normalize CRLF to LF
- `YAML104` — add a trailing newline
- `YAML105` — collapse consecutive blank lines
- `YAML106` — remove trailing blank lines
- `YAML202` — insert a space after the mapping colon
- `YAML206` — insert a space after a sequence dash

Fixes are applied in memory, re-parsed, and re-linted before being written, so a file is never left in a broken state. If re-linting fails, the original file is restored and the error is reported.

---

## CI integration

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
name: Lint YAML

on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  flak:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version: stable
      - run: go install github.com/flak-lint/flak@latest
      - name: Lint YAML files
        run: flak --format github --check .
```

### GitLab CI

```yaml
yaml-lint:
  image: golang:1.22
  script:
    - go install github.com/flak-lint/flak@latest
    - flak --format junit --output flak.xml .
  artifacts:
    reports:
      junit: flak.xml
```

### Pre-commit

```yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/flak-lint/flak
    rev: v1.4.0
    hooks:
      - id: flak
        files: \.ya?ml$
```

---

## Editor integration

### VS Code

Add a task in `.vscode/tasks.json`:

```json
{
  "version": "2.0.0",
  "tasks": [
    {
      "label": "flak: lint",
      "type": "shell",
      "command": "flak --format json .",
      "problemMatcher": {
        "owner": "flak",
        "fileLocation": ["absolute"],
        "pattern": {
          "regexp": "^(.*):$",
          "file": 1
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

### Neovim

```lua
vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("BufWritePost", {
  pattern = { "*.yml", "*.yaml" },
  command = { "flak", "--fix", "%" },
})
```

---

## How it works

1. **Discovery** — `flak` expands the given paths into a list of YAML files, honoring `.flakignore` and the `ignore`/`include` configuration.
2. **Parsing** — each file is parsed with a YAML 1.2-compatible parser. Parse failures are reported as `YAML001` with the location of the offending token.
3. **Analysis** — the parsed document is walked by each enabled rule. Rules that need raw text (line length, trailing whitespace) receive the original source alongside the AST.
4. **Reporting** — diagnostics are collected, sorted by file and position, and rendered in the requested format.

`flak` never modifies a file unless `--fix` or `--fix-only` is passed.

---

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome!

```console
git clone https://github.com/flak-lint/flak.git
cd flak
make build
make test
```

### Adding a rule

1. Create a new file in `internal/rules/` implementing the `Rule` interface.
2. Register it in `internal/rules/registry.go` with a unique ID, tag, and default severity.
3. Add a test fixture under `testdata/rules/<rule-id>/`.
4. Run `make test` and `make lint`.

Please open an issue before starting on a large change so we can discuss the design.

---

## License

`flak` is released under the MIT License. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) for details.

# flak

[![CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/CI-passing-brightgreen)](https://github.com/yourname/flak/actions)
[![npm](https://img.shields.io/badge/npm-flak-blue)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/flak)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green)](./LICENSE)

A fast, opinionated linter for YAML files.

`flak` parses your YAML and reports the mistakes that are easy to miss by eye and annoying to debug in production — duplicate keys, tabs, trailing whitespace, unquoted risky scalars, inconsistent indentation — with a clear rule name, a line number, and an autofix where one exists.

```
$ flak config.yaml

config.yaml
  12:1   warning  yaml/duplicate-key    Duplicate key "name" (first seen on line 4)
  18:1   error    yaml/tab-indent       Tab character used for indentation
  24:5   warning  yaml/unquoted-yes      Value "yes" parses as a boolean
  31:1   error    yaml/trailing-space    Trailing whitespace

✖ 4 problems (2 errors, 2 warnings)
```

---

## Contents

## Why flak?

YAML is a superset of JSON and a superset of a lot of things people wish weren't. That flexibility means a typo in a config file can silently change its meaning instead of failing loudly.

- **Duplicate keys** are silently discarded by most parsers. The second `image:` in a CI config just wins.
- **Tabs** are illegal for indentation in YAML, but many editors insert them anyway.
- **Unquoted `yes`, `no`, `on`, `off`** parse as booleans in YAML 1.1, and as strings in YAML 1.2 — a classic source of "it works on my machine".
- **Trailing whitespace** creates noisy diffs.

`flak` is a single binary with no runtime dependencies, written in Rust. It lints a 5,000-line manifest in under 10 ms.

## Installation

### npm (recommended)

```sh
npm install --save-dev flak
npx flak .
```

### Cargo

```sh
cargo install flak
```

### Homebrew

```sh
brew install flak
```

### Prebuilt binary

Download the latest release for your platform and drop it on your `PATH`:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://github.com/yourname/flak/releases/latest/download/flak-linux-x86_64 -o /usr/local/bin/flak
chmod +x /usr/local/bin/flak
```

Requires flak v1.0+ on Node 18 or later.

## Usage

```sh
# Lint everything in the current directory
flak .

# Lint specific files
flak config.yaml docker-compose.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml

# Lint stdin, printing to stdout
cat config.yaml | flak --stdin-filename config.yaml

# Auto-fix what can be fixed, then re-lint
flak . --fix

# Show only errors, or only a specific rule
flak . --severity error
flak . --rule yaml/duplicate-key

# List the rules
flak --list-rules
```

### CLI options

| Flag | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-c, --config <path>` | Path to a config file | auto-discovered |
| `--no-config` | Ignore config files entirely | `false` |
| `--fix` | Apply safe autofixes in place | `false` |
| `--fix-only` | Apply autofixes and exit without reporting | `false` |
| `--format <fmt>` | `pretty`, `compact`, `json`, `github`, `checkstyle`, `junit` | `pretty` |
| `--output <file>` | Write results to a file instead of stdout | stdout |
| `--severity <level>` | Minimum severity to report: `error`, `warning`, `info` | `info` |
| `--rule <id>` | Only run this rule (repeatable) | — |
| `--ignore <pattern>` | Additional glob to ignore (repeatable) | — |
| `--stdin-filename <name>` | Filename to use when linting stdin | `<stdin>` |
| `--no-color` | Disable colored output | auto |
| `--quiet` | Suppress output; rely on exit code | `false` |
| `--list-rules` | Print the rule catalogue and exit | — |
| `--explain <rule>` | Explain a single rule and exit | — |
| `--version` | Print version and exit | — |
| `--help` | Print help and exit | — |

## Rules

| Rule | Severity | Fixable | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `yaml/duplicate-key` | error | no | A mapping key appears more than once in the same mapping. |
| `yaml/tab-indent` | error | yes | A tab character is used for indentation. |
| `yaml/trailing-space` | warning | yes | A line ends with whitespace. |
| `yaml/trailing-newline` | warning | yes | The file does not end with a newline. |
| `yaml/line-length` | warning | no | A line exceeds the configured maximum length. |
| `yaml/unquoted-yes` | warning | yes | A value that may parse as a boolean is unquoted. |
| `yaml/unquoted-number` | warning | yes | A numeric-looking value is unquoted and may change type. |
| `yaml/unquoted-date` | warning | yes | A date-like value is unquoted and may parse as a timestamp. |
| `yaml/missing-doc-start` | info | yes | The document does not begin with `---`. |
| `yaml/empty-document` | warning | no | The file contains no YAML document. |
| `yaml/inconsistent-indent` | warning | no | Indentation is not a multiple of the configured step. |
| `yaml/merge-key` | info | no | A `<<` merge key is used; some tools do not support it. |
| `yaml/anchored-orphan` | warning | no | An anchor is defined but never referenced. |
| `yaml/alias-undefined` | error | no | An alias references an anchor that does not exist. |
| `yaml/duplicate-anchor` | error | no | The same anchor name is defined twice. |
| `yaml/multiple-docs` | info | no | The file contains more than one document. |
| `yaml/implicit-string-key` | warning | yes | A key that looks like a number or boolean is unquoted. |
| `yaml/flow-mapping` | info | no | A flow mapping (`{...}`) is used where a block mapping would be clearer. |
| `yaml/flow-sequence` | info | no | A flow sequence (`[...]`) is used where a block sequence would be clearer. |
| `yaml/comment-spacing` | warning | yes | A comment is missing a space after `#`. |
| `yaml/comment-block` | info | no | A `#` comment contains a TODO/FIXME marker. |
| `yaml/bom` | warning | yes | The file starts with a UTF-8 byte order mark. |
| `yaml/non-printable` | error | no | The file contains a non-printable control character. |

Run `flak --list-rules` for the full, authoritative list, or `flak --explain yaml/duplicate-key` for details, examples, and rationale.

## Configuration

`flak` looks for a config file in the current directory and walks up the tree, using the first one it finds:

- `flak.yaml`
- `flak.yml`
- `.flak.yaml`
- `.flak.yml`
- `flak.json`
- a `flak` key in `package.json`

```yaml
# flak.yaml
extends: recommended

rules:
  yaml/line-length:
    severity: warning
    max: 120
  yaml/unquoted-yes: error
  yaml/comment-block: off

ignore:
  - "vendor/**"
  - "**/*.min.yaml"
  - "fixtures/legacy/**"

include:
  - "**/*.yaml"
  - "**/*.yml"

options:
  indent: 2
  allow_duplicate_keys: false
  check_utf8_bom: true
  yaml_version: "1.2"
```

### Presets

| Preset | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `recommended` | The default: sensible rules for general-purpose YAML. |
| `strict` | `recommended` plus every optional warning turned into an error. |
| `minimal` | Only errors that change how a file parses. |
| `kubernetes` | Tuned for Kubernetes manifests. |
| `github-actions` | Tuned for GitHub Actions workflows. |
| `docker-compose` | Tuned for Compose files. |

```yaml
extends: kubernetes
```

## Ignoring files and lines

**Glob patterns** in the `ignore` list exclude files entirely:

```yaml
ignore:
  - "**/node_modules/**"
  - "**/generated/**"
```

**Inline comments** suppress a rule for the next line:

```yaml
image: nginx:latest # flak:disable yaml/unquoted-number
```

**Block comments** suppress rules for a region:

```yaml
# flak:disable yaml/line-length
metadata:
  annotations:
    a-very-long-key-name: "a very long value that goes on and on and on"
# flak:enable yaml/line-length
```

**`# flak:disable` (no rule list)** disables all rules on that line or in that region.

## Autofix

```sh
flak . --fix
```

Fixable rules are rewritten in place; everything else is reported for a human to resolve. `--fix` is safe by default — it never changes the parsed meaning of a document. To see what would change without touching your files:

```sh
flak . --fix --diff
```

Fixes are applied per file, and the file is re-parsed afterwards to confirm it still parses. If a fix would produce an invalid document, it is rolled back and reported as an unfixable diagnostic.

## Output formats

```sh
flak . --format json
```

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "diagnostics": [
    {
      "file": "config.yaml",
      "line": 12,
      "column": 1,
      "severity": "error",
      "code": "yaml/duplicate-key",
      "message": "Duplicate key \"name\" (first seen on line 4)",
      "fix": null
    }
  ],
  "summary": { "errors": 1, "warnings": 1, "infos": 0, "files": 1 }
}
```

| Format | Use case |
| --- | --- |
| `pretty` | Human-readable terminal output (default). |
| `compact` | One line per diagnostic, for grepping. |
| `json` | Machine-readable, for scripts and editors. |
| `github` | GitHub Actions annotations. |
| `checkstyle` | Checkstyle XML, for IDEs and CI viewers. |
| `junit` | JUnit XML, for CI test reporters. |

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | No problems found. |
| `1` | Problems were found. |
| `2` | Invalid command-line usage or config file. |
| `3` | A file could not be read or parsed as YAML. |

## Editor integration

### VS Code

Install the [flak VS Code extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=flak.flak) for in-editor diagnostics and quick fixes.

### Neovim

With [`nvim-lint`](https://github.com/mfussenegger/nvim-lint):

```lua
require('lint').linters_by_ft = {

```

### Other editors

Any editor that can run a command-line linter and parse JSON works:

```sh

```

## CI integration

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
name: lint
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  flak:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: yourname/flak-action@v1
```

Or run it directly:

```yaml
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
      - run: npm install --save-dev flak
      - run: npx flak . --format github
```

### GitLab CI

```yaml
flak:
  image: node:20
  script:
    - npm ci
    - npx flak . --format junit --output flak-report.xml
  artifacts:
    when: always
    paths: [flak-report.xml]
```

### Pre-commit

```yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/yourname/flak
    rev: v1.2.0
    hooks:
      - id: flak
        files: \.(ya?ml)$
```

## Library API

```js
import { lint, lintText, format } from 'flak';

const result = lint(['config.yaml'], { config: { extends: 'recommended' } });

for (const d of result.diagnostics) {
  console.log(`${d.file}:${d.line}:${d.column} ${d.code} ${d.message}`);
}

console.log(format(result, 'json'));
```

```js
import { lintText } from 'flak';

const { diagnostics } = lintText('a: 1\na: 2\n', { filename: 'inline.yaml' });
// diagnostics[0].code === 'yaml/duplicate-key'
```

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome — bug reports, new rules, documentation.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/yourname/flak
cd flak
cargo build
cargo test
```

### Adding a rule

1. Create `src/rules/<rule_name>.rs` implementing the `Rule` trait.
2. Register it in `src/rules/mod.rs` with a default severity and whether it is fixable.
3. Add tests in `tests/rules/<rule_name>.rs` covering valid and invalid fixtures.
4. Document it in `docs/rules/<rule_name>.md` and add a row to the rules table in this README.
5. Run `cargo fmt && cargo clippy -- -D warnings && cargo test`.

New rules must include at least one negative fixture (valid YAML that must not be reported) and one positive fixture.

# flak

[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/flak)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/flak)
[![CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/build-passing-brightgreen)](https://github.com/you/flak/actions)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](./LICENSE)

A fast, opinionated linter for YAML files.

`flak` parses your YAML, checks it against a set of configurable rules, and reports problems with file, line, and column information — the same format editors and CI tools already understand.

```console
$ flak
src/k8s/deployment.yaml:12:3  error  key "replicas" is missing from mapping  @flak/required-keys
src/k8s/deployment.yaml:19:5  warning  value "always" is not quoted  @flak/quotes
src/config/app.yaml:1:1  error  document is empty  @flak/empty-document

✖ 3 problems (2 errors, 1 warning)
```

---

## Features

- **Zero config.** Sensible defaults for the most common YAML mistakes.
- **Rule-based.** Every check is a named rule you can enable, disable, or tune.
- **Editor-friendly.** Machine-readable output (`--format json`, `--format github`, `--format checkstyle`) for CI and `problem matchers`.
- **Fast.** A single-pass parser; lints a 1,000-file tree in well under a second.
- **No dependencies on your runtime.** Works on YAML 1.1 and 1.2 documents, including multi-document streams (`---`).

---

## Installation

```console
npm install --save-dev flak
```

Or run it without installing:

```console
npx flak ./config
```

Requires Node.js 18 or newer.

---

## Usage

```console
flak [options] [file-or-directory...]
```

By default `flak` lints every `.yaml` and `.yml` file in the current directory, recursively.

```console
# Lint the current directory
flak

# Lint specific paths
flak ./config ./k8s/deployment.yaml

# Lint stdin (useful for pre-commit hooks)
cat openapi.yaml | flak --stdin-filename openapi.yaml

# Only report errors, ignore warnings
flak --quiet

# Auto-fix what can be fixed safely
flak --fix
```

### Options

| Option | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-c, --config <path>` | Path to a configuration file. | Auto-discovered |
| `--no-config` | Ignore all configuration files. | `false` |
| `--format <fmt>` | Output format: `stylish`, `json`, `github`, `checkstyle`, `compact`, `tap`. | `stylish` |
| `--fix` | Apply safe automatic fixes in place. | `false` |
| `--quiet` | Report errors only; suppress warnings and info. | `false` |
| `--max-warnings <n>` | Exit non-zero if there are more than `n` warnings. | `-1` (unlimited) |
| `--stdin-filename <path>` | Filename to report for content piped on stdin. | `<stdin>` |
| `--ignore-pattern <glob>` | Additional glob to ignore. Repeatable. | — |
| `--no-ignore` | Lint files that would otherwise be ignored. | `false` |
| `--rule <rule>` | Toggle a rule: `--rule no-required-keys` to disable, `--rule quotes:error` to set severity. Repeatable. | — |
| `--list-rules` | Print all available rules and exit. | `false` |
| `-v, --version` | Print the version and exit. | — |
| `-h, --help` | Print help and exit. | — |

---

## Rules

| Rule | Description | Fixable | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@flak/empty-document` | A document contains no content. | | error |
| `@flak/duplicate-keys` | The same key appears twice in a mapping. | | error |
| `@flak/tab-indent` | Lines are indented with tab characters. | ✔ | error |
| `@flak/trailing-spaces` | Lines contain trailing whitespace. | ✔ | warning |
| `@flak/line-length` | A line exceeds the configured maximum length. | | warning |
| `@flak/missing-document-start` | A multi-document file should begin with `---`. | | warning |
| `@flak/required-keys` | A mapping is missing a required key. | | error |
| `@flak/unknown-keys` | A mapping contains a key not in the known schema. | | error |
| `@flak/quotes` | Strings that could be misinterpreted should be quoted. | | warning |
| `@flak/anchors` | Anchors and aliases are used; they hurt readability. | | warning |
| `@flak/merge-keys` | The `<<` merge key is used. | | warning |
| `@flak/implicit-typos` | A value looks like a typo of a common boolean (`tru`, `flase`). | ✔ | error |
| `@flak/consistent-indent` | Indentation is inconsistent within a document. | | error |
| `@flak/key-order` | Mapping keys are not in a consistent, alphabetical order. | ✔ | warning |
| `@flak/no-empty-value` | A key is present with an empty value. | | warning |

Run `flak --list-rules` for the full, up-to-date list with descriptions.

---

## Configuration

`flak` looks for a configuration file in the current working directory, walking up toward the filesystem root:

1. `flak.config.js`
2. `flak.config.mjs`
3. `flak.config.cjs`
4. `.flakrc.json`
5. `.flakrc.yaml`
6. `flak.config.yaml`
7. `package.json` (a `"flak"` field)

The first one found wins.

### `flak.config.js`

```js
export default {
  rules: {
    '@flak/duplicate-keys': 'error',
    '@flak/quotes': 'warn',
    '@flak/line-length': ['warn', { max: 100 }],
    '@flak/required-keys': 'off',
    '@flak/unknown-keys': ['error', { schema: './schemas/service.schema.json' }],
  },
  ignore: ['**/vendor/**', '**/*.generated.yaml'],
  env: {
    node: true,
    ci: true,
  },
};
```

### `.flakrc.yaml`

```yaml
rules:
  '@flak/duplicate-keys': error
  '@flak/line-length':
    - warn
    - max: 100
  '@flak/required-keys': off
ignore:
  - '**/vendor/**'
```

### Rule severities

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `'error'` | Reported as an error; fails the run. |
| `'warn'` | Reported as a warning; does not fail the run. |
| `'info'` | Reported as information; does not fail the run. |
| `'off'` | The rule is disabled. |

### Inline directives

Disable a rule for a single file or a block:

```yaml
# flak:disable @flak/line-length
description: A very long line that would otherwise trigger the rule...
# flak:enable @flak/line-length
```

Disable a rule for the rest of the file:

```yaml
# flak:disable-next-line @flak/quotes
pattern: "*.yaml"
```

---

## Ignoring files

Files are ignored when they match any of:

- A `.flakignore` file in the project root (one glob per line, `#` for comments).
- The `ignore` array in your configuration file.
- The default patterns: `**/node_modules/**`, `**/.git/**`, `**/dist/**`, `**/build/**`, `**/coverage/**`, `**/.venv/**`, `**/vendor/**`.

```gitignore
# .flakignore
**/fixtures/**
**/*.min.yaml
```

---

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | No problems found. |
| `1` | One or more errors were reported. |
| `2` | A configuration or CLI error occurred. |

---

## CI integration

`flak` produces GitHub Actions annotations directly:

```yaml
name: lint
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  flak:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx flak --format github --max-warnings 0
```

Other formats:

```console
flak --format json       # JSON array of problems
flak --format compact    # one line per problem
flak --format checkstyle # XML, for Jenkins and similar
flak --format tap        # TAP, for test harnesses
```

### Pre-commit

```yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/you/flak
    rev: v1.4.0
    hooks:
      - id: flak
        files: \.ya?ml$
```

## Editor integration

`flak --format json` is understood by most YAML LSPs and by the popular "problems" panel in VS Code, Neovim, and IntelliJ. A minimal VS Code task:

```json
{
  "version": "2.0.0",
  "tasks": [
    {
      "label": "flak",
      "type": "shell",
      "command": "npx flak --format json",
      "problemMatcher": {
        "owner": "flak",
        "fileLocation": ["absolute"],
        "pattern": {
          "regexp": "^(.*):(\\d+):(\\d+)\\s+(.*)$",
          "file": 1,
          "line": 2,
          "column": 3,
          "message": 4
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

## Programmatic API

```js
import { lint, lintText } from 'flak';

const result = await lint(['./config']);

for (const problem of result.problems) {
  console.log(problem.file, problem.line, problem.column, problem.message, problem.rule);
}

const single = await lintText('a: 1\na: 2\n', { filename: 'example.yaml' });
console.log(single.problems.length); // 1
```

## Features

- **Fast.** Single-pass parsing, parallel across files. Lints a 1,000-file repository in well under a second.
- **Strict parsing.** Duplicate keys, bad indentation, and malformed anchors are *errors*, not warnings — because they silently change meaning in most YAML parsers.
- **50+ built-in rules**, covering formatting, style, correctness, and security.
- **Configurable.** Every rule can be enabled, disabled, reconfigured, or turned into a custom check via `custom-rules`.
- **Autofix.** Most formatting rules support `--fix`, applying safe, minimal edits in place.
- **Multiple output formats:** human-readable, `json`, `junit`, `github`, `sarif`, `tap`, `checkstyle`.
- **Schema validation** against JSON Schema for YAML documents.
- **Editor and CI integration** out of the box.

## Installation

### Prebuilt binaries

```bash
# macOS (Homebrew)
brew install flak

# Linux (Debian/Ubuntu)
curl -fsSL https://github.com/example/flak/releases/latest/download/flak-linux-x86_64.tar.gz \
  | tar -xz -C /usr/local/bin

# Windows (Scoop)
scoop install flak

# Any platform via npm
npm install -g flak
```

### From source

```bash
git clone https://github.com/example/flak.git
cd flak
cargo install --path .
```
